entityDescription:
Phase One is a Danish company that specializes in the development and manufacturing of high-end digital medium format cameras and imaging systems. The company was founded in 1993 and has since become a leading provider of aerial and industrial imaging solutions.
In the SPACE industry, Phase One has developed the iXM-SP150 camera system, which is a radiation robust, 150MP camera modele designed to be used on satellites. This camera system features a large-format image sensor with flexible telescope interface and advanced software tools for image processing and analysis. It is designed to provide accurate and detailed imagery for applications such as Earth Observation and Space Situational Awareness. Phase One provides the world’s highest image quality in terms of resolution, dynamic range, color fidelity and geometric accuracy. It is headquartered in Denmark, with regional offices across the world.

Multiverse Computing is an innovative company that emerged as a spin-off from the Donostia International Physics Center (DIPC), affiliated with the University of the Basque Country. Our primary objective is the development of quantum and quantum-inspired algorithms. Starting with a Proof of Concept (PoC) on Portfolio Optimization, we have progressed to collaborating with multinational corporations on a diverse range of challenges.
Today, Multiverse stands as the leading company in Europe for quantum and quantum-inspired software, and we are proud to receive support from the European Commission through the European Innovation Council. Our team comprises 80+ talented individuals representing 23 nationalities, and we have established offices in Germany, Canada, France and UK.
Being a knowledge-driven enterprise, we have a prolific publication record with our papers amassing over 9000 citations. However, to remain competitive on a global scale, we recognize the importance of safeguarding our generated knowledge. Over the past two years, we have diligently filed more than 50 patent applications.

description: AcrossLimits (AL) is a technology company that also offers specialist consultancy services, with its roots firmly derived from the innovation and ICT sectors. It works throughout Europe and is based in Malta. The company was established in June 2001 as a limited liability company and has been participating in EU funded projects ever since. Our technical expertise covers many sectors, from technology and innovation research projects to development, digitisation, elearning, eHealth and mobile applications amongst others. Since its inception, AL has been involved in over 80 EU-funded projects. As EU project partners we have built our experience as technical partners, designing and developing digital platforms and/or elearning platforms mostly in the areas of eHealth, eCommerce, eGovernment, etc, as well as being the dissemination leads for various projects. As consultants, we provide our clients with support to access opportunities in Europe, such as training, accessing funding, networking, and taking research results to the market. Since 2004 the company has also been operating a private training centre under the brand name TrainingMalta which is licensed under the Malta Further and Higher Education Agency. We specialise in the delivery of practical and experiential training in a variety of industries including maritime, robotics, education and health, and also focusing on entrepreneurial and soft skills development. Further information can be found on www.trainingmalta.com. Our training centre is ISO9001:2015 certified. Here we have experience delivering in-person, virtual, and blended training courses but due to COVID, we had to shift almost entirely to our online training platform, although in-person learning is now picking back up. AL is also actively involved in research and here focuses its efforts on the creation of innovative ICT solutions, we are experts in the configuration and programming of cross-platform systems, notably in the area of Green ICT. At the European level, we are very active in various research programs covering diverse areas of interest which include: eLearning, environmental monitoring, Green ICT, telecare, e-Government, digital culture and in the promotion of gender equality. AcrossLimits maintains strong links with the equality-based groups in Europe and beyond and assists in the creation and sustainability of representative bodies. The closest to home is the Federation of Women Entrepreneurs, which is fully supported by AcrossLimits as a charitable trust. Our training wing is a registered college and is also fully supported by AcrossLimits to deliver personal and social development for disadvantaged individuals and technical skills development those working in education. The number of paid staff in our core team is around 15 people, however, we have over 50 international experts of various industries in our network based all throughout Europe, ready to provide their expertise on a contract basis.

entityDescription: Asana Cat UG is focused on enhancing the harmony between humans, pets, and wildlife within our shared living spaces. Recognizing the threats that high-traffic areas and natural preserves pose to cats, and the dangers cats can present to local ecosystems, the company has developed the CatSla Galileo-Tracker. This advanced tracking and training device utilizes modern technology, behavioral sciences, and automatic danger zone detection to keep cats safe and protected while alleviating the concerns of cat owners. Offering real-time monitoring, customizable virtual fences, and a user-friendly web interface, the CatSla-Tracker is designed to actively keep pets away from danger zones, rather than merely alerting the owner. Emphasizing eco-friendliness and sustainability, Asana Cat's innovative approach not only ensures pet safety but also promotes responsible pet ownership and contributes to the preservation of biodiversity.

BINC INDUSTRIES, owns and exclusively supplies the innovative finishing process namedMMP technology®. Its selective removal of roughness enables to obtain and control the super-finishes of surfaces at a level of homogeneity and reproducibility never reached before.
MMPTECHNOLOGY®,is a mechanical-physical-catalyst surface treatment applied to items placed inside a treatment tank. It can provide highly accurate selective surface finishes. The roughness level achieved by MMP TECHNOLOGY® can provide mechanical, physical, flow, chemical…. properties to the parts.
MMPTECHNOLOGY®begins with a detailed analysis of the surface state of the item to be treated. The processing parameters required to meet the customer’s objectives are then determined with a degree of precision that is unique on the market
 
The Micro Machining Process (MMPTECHNOLOGY®) is a surface finishing technology based upon selective filtration of wavelength ranges of roughness, allowing for the production of very precise and selective surface states.
The results are both uniform and reproducible:MMPTECHNOLOGY®is an industrial process that ensures total traceability and industrial-grade control of all parameters right up to the final finish.
MMPTECHNOLOGY®is highly effective on almost every alloy, regardless of hardness.MMPTECHNOLOGY®can efficiently treat parts made from any manufacturing method, including forging, casting, machining, EDM/ECM, and additive layer methods (DMLS, SLM, etc.).

entityDescription:
The main goal of C-biotech is to provide sustainable solutions for the building sector, cities and society as a whole. We use industrial hemp as a biorefinery to produce biomass that can be used in isolation materials, hempwood, cladding as well as in engineered solutions such as charging stations and traffic poles. Biobased construction materials are the key in reducing carbon emissions from the construction sector, which currently contributes 40% to the global emissions. By producing the required biomass locally, one can significantly reduce supply chains and transport energy. We hereby promote circularity and provide a means to cities to work on their ESG profile. We can literally grow traffic signs of the city IN the city. Can’t get more circular than that. There is a reason why the EU green deal mentions “Improving energy efficiency in the building sector will play a key role in achieving carbon-neutrality by 2050, a goal set out in the European Green Deal. Hemp can play a significant role in reaching this objective.” And there is more. With hemp, C-biotech remediates historical contaminated soils (e.g. PFOS, heavy metals) in an ecological and natural way. Thanks to our bio-based materials, we also try to ensure that remediation also pays off for the farmer that cannot use contaminated land for harvesting crops.

entityDescription: Founded in 2017, Dessia carries a simple vision: Tomorrow's engineering will see human engineers and AI applications collaborate. This solution integrates with existing 3D/PLM environments to ensure 'continuous engineering'. The technological specificity of the AI employed by Dessia is that it is based on deterministic models (explainable AI), and therefore ensures the transparency and reliability of the results produced. Dessia's symbiosis with the aeronautics industry is therefore a natural one, since the application of such intelligent technologies is already underway, and deterministic models will be preferred for reasons of transparency and certification.

The technological specificity of the AI employed by Dessia is that it is based on deterministic models (explainable AI), and therefore ensures the transparency and reliability of the results produced. Dessia's symbiosis with the aeronautics industry is therefore a natural one, since the application of such intelligent technologies is already underway, and deterministic models will be preferred for reasons of transparency and certification.

entityDescription:
Snowcap's ambition is to revolutionize the estimation of water reserves stored as seasonal snow in the mountains. This critical information can be used to optimize hydro-power operations, assist with flood forecasting, estimate fresh water resources and to help plan water utilization from local to regional scales.
We utilize state-of-the-art Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) based methodology to capture the variability in snow depth at high spatial resolution, across vast mountain ranges with an unprecedented sub-weekly temporal revisit frequency. The satellite SAR-based snow depth estimates over mountains are further combined with snow model simulations and radiometer-based observations of snow water equivalent over non-mountainous regions to allow for daily water resources analysis from local to continental scales.

entityDescription:
ANT-X designs and builds custom drone solutions tailored to specific industrial applications.

Based on the experience gathered as a university laboratory in the research area of guidance, navigation and control of UAVs, ANT-X has the competences needed to carry out the entire process of design, prototyping, integration and flight testing of custom UAV platforms.

ANT-X is able to:

_Design drone solutions tailored to the specific application, based on the user’s requirements.
_Identify and integrate a suitable sensor payload to the user’s particular application.
_Cover the entire development process of the UAV, including design, integration and prototyping.
_Assist the user in operations, in particular providing assistance to guarantee compliance to regulations.

ANT-X can leverage the experience as a research laboratory in the field of aerospace guidance and control, and propose innovative configurations beyond classical coplanar multi-rotor UAVs. The ANT-X solutions employ state-of-the-art open-source software running onboard the drone, which allows for easy integration with payload and existing infrastructure.

Moreover, ANT-X provides laboratory solutions for research and education in flight robotics and UAV control.

ANT-X is a spin-off company of Politecnico di Milano university.

description:
yuri is a space biotech company that uses the microgravity environment of space to develop and manufacture superior biotech products. The team of 30+ space engineers and biologists has worked on 20+ payloads for the International Space Station in collaboration with organizations like NASA, ESA, GSK, Charité Berlin. 
yuri products and services 
yuri develops modular bioreactors and incubators for cell cultures, protein crystals or plants and launches them for scientists around the world to the ISS and other spacecraft. They also sell and rent devices to simulate microgravity on Earth. Since 2022 they develop their own pipeline of biotech products that are either triggered by or manufactured in microgravity. 
Team and history 
yuri was founded by the ex-Airbus engineers Maria Birlem and Christian Bruderrek together with serial entrepreneur Mark Kugel in 2019. Maria and Christian have worked on countless ISS payloads during their time at Airbus and saw the huge potential of microgravity for the life sciences beyond just government funded research. Since then the team has grown to 30+ team members in their headquarters in Southern Germany and their engineering hub in Luxembourg. They combine several decades of experience in human spaceflight engineering and space biology. In 2022, Daniela Bezdan joined as Chief Scientific Officer (CSO). She brings in experience from Weill-Cornell Medicine New York, CRG Barcelona, Max-Planck, NASA Genelabs and Poppy Health, where she until recently was co-founder and CSO. Daniela leads the development of yuri’s own biotech product pipeline. 
Key facts
- Founding date: June 2019 
- Employees: 30+ 
- Offices: Meckenbeuren, Germany (Headquarter) | Esch-sur-Alzette, Luxembourg 
- Customers: NASA, ESA, DLR, UCLA, UCSD, Charité Berlin, NYU Abu Dhabi, Technion Israel, UTS Sydney, NUS Singapore

entityDescription:
The Institute of Engineering Thermodynamics at the German Aerospace Center (Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt -DLR) in Stuttgart, with further research facilities in Cologne, Ulm, Oldenburg and Hamburg, does research in the field of efficient energy storage systems that conserve natural resources, and next generation energy conversion technologies with a staff of 180 scientific and technical employees, engineers and doctoral candidates. The spectrum of activities ranges from theoretical studies to laboratory work for basic research and to the operation of pilot plants. These experimental and theoretical studies are accompanied by systems analysis studies to analyse the associated technological, environmental and economic potential and situate it in a larger overall context of the energy economy by means of scenarios.
A tight network with the University of Stuttgart -especially with the Institute of Energy Storage- and with the Helmholtz Institute Ulm at the University of Ulm is existing.

As the challenge of orbital debris or “space junk” is set to grow, there is an urgent need to address the question of debris management, ensure the safety of the current working satellites, and innovate for the production and monitoring of future satellites. 
The Space Sustainability Rating (SSR) is an initiative seeking to foster voluntary actions by satellite operators to reduce the risks related to space debris and on-orbit collisions providing: 
A rating system informed by transparent, data-based assessments of the level of sustainability of space missions 
Practical guidance on how to improve sustainability performance & practices 
A platform for action-focused collaboration centered on the rating system to support research and leverage best practices 
The SSR supports space actors, such as governments, space agencies, and commercial companies, in understanding the impact of their activities on the space environment, identifying opportunities to minimize those impacts and taking an active role in making space safer and more sustainable, for all.

entityDescription:
TETMET was born from the observation that metallic structures could be optimized in three dimensions in particular: the quantity of material used, the quantity of energy used in the production process and the logistic effort required to transport finished goods over long distances. 
TETMET opens lattice structures to many industries, including luxury, design and architecture as well as construction, space, naval and aeronautic. 
 
The traditional topological optimisation approach consists in removing material where it is not needed, in order to gain mass. The production of optimized structures via a subtractive approach result in a massive energy consumption and a large amount of waste. 3D printing (WAAM for metal or lit-powder) consists in adding material only where needed require a considerable amount of energy to keep the material at the liquid state, or to atomize the raw material to make it a powder. 
Lattice structures only use the strict necessary quantity of material, without later addition or subtraction. They are produced by assembling metallic rods through laser welding, a process using very little energy. 
 
In other words, TETMET enables the additive manufacturing of large size objects with 40% less material and 90% less energy than 3D printing. 
 
TETMET’s flexible toolchain allows decentralized production. The machines producing the pieces may be located anywhere and are actioned by a service hosted in the cloud. It is therefore possible to produce closer to the object’s final destination and therefore avoid the complexity and the cost of transporting large items. 
 
Finally, it goes without saying that the savings on the three dimensions have a significant impact on the carbon footprint of the final products. 
 
 
 
TETMET’ toolchain encompasses: 
- The digital generation of optimized lattice structures
- A beam steering system
- A robotic arm, on which the laser is mounted
- The machine-learning and constant improvement

entityDescription:
For the recerationnal boating, the accidental grounding (when a ship hits the bottom of the sea) is the 2nd cause of SAR (Search and rescue) interventions at sea, the 1st expenditure budget for insurances companies with an average of 8000€ repair cost per accident.
Some solutions have been around for many years, but have not evolved much. They fail to adress the need to improve safety at sea for a ever growing population of sailors, who are also less and less savvy on the water: As a result, we see a x3 growth in grounding over the last 10 years (source: Insurance companies).
To achieve this, we've designed the following solution:RS Nautic 360 is a smart solution presenting itself as an electronic applicance, mounted on the boat dashboard. Using an embedded GPS module, it helps to calculate with accuracy the water level available above the sea bed ahaed of the boat. It triggers an alarm up to 180 seconds before an anticipated impact.

R Systems was founded in november 2019 to developp a project - RS AERO - aimed at securing helicopters flights in hazardous areas where powerlines are posing a threat to the aircraft.
During our incubation at DECA BFC, there was a compelling incentive to leverage our technology and target another market: RS Nautic was born from this initiative.

entityDescription:
The core business of Wave S.r.l. is the development of radiofrequency and microwave electronic circuits targeted to the space, telecommunication and defence markets.
Wave S.r.l. was born in 2005, in Rome, Italy. During 18 years Wave has developed specific competences both in the design of Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC) and Hybrid Integrated Microwave Modules (HMIC). Wave know-how and experience spans from UHF to 60GHz. Since 2007 the company manufacture and sells wireless devices for telecommunication network in urban and rural scenarios.
Company competences spans through different sectors, the most significant are:
- Solid State Power Amplifier (SSPA) for space, defence, radar and telecommunication applications
- Datalink (UAV, Defence, Mobile) RF modules, channel emulators, 5G, IoT and ISM applications
- Microwave Modules: Low Noise Amplifiers, Synthesizers, Mixer ecc.. dedicated to: automatic test equipment (ATE), SATCOM, 5G, IoT
- SATCOM Applications: Receivers, LNAs, BUC and SSPAs for fixed and mobile terminals
- GaN and GaAs MMICs for space, defence and telecommunication markets

Wave is fully equipped with a manufacturing and testing microwave facility. The Facility is composed by two main working centers: precision mecanics CNC and microelectrics/RF PCB qualified for production, reworking, testing and tuning of complex microwave modules operating in space and defence markets.
Since 2018 Wave has been ISO9001:2015 qualified for both mechanics and electronics design and manufacturing.

MediaTek is a fabless semiconductor company, which is another way of saying we design chips for electronic devices that our partners manufacture.
We design cutting-edge system-on-chip (SoC) solutions for cellular handsets and tablet devices; fixed and wireless connectivity; high-definition TV; optical storage and DVD and Blu-ray products.
MediaTek is headquartered in Taiwan and has sales and research subsidiaries in mainland China, Singapore, India, U.S., Japan, South Korea, Denmark, the UK, Sweden and Dubai. Our R&D centre in Cambourne (near Cambridge) develops smartphone SW and cellular system technology, and our R&D centre in Kent develops RF technology. MTK Wireless Ltd is the UK operation of MediaTek Inc. In the UK, we have two R&D centers – both working on technology for our future SoC wireless chipsets. Our R&D centre in Cambourne (near Cambridge) develops SW and system technology, and our R&D centre in Kent develops RF technology

MediaTek'sWirelessProducts
MediaTek has cumulatively shipped well over 2.5Bn cellular chipsets since entering the cellular market segment less than a decade ago. MediaTek’s “total solution” turnkey approach, and insatiable appetite for excellence in modem solutions, has enabled our customers to successfully deploy MediaTek powered handsets in over 150 countries worldwide. Most recently, our 3G chipsets have been at the forefront of enabling the democratization of smartphones for the mass market. In addition to cellular chipsets, MediaTek has developed leading edge wireless connectivity technology, including Wi-Fi, BT GPS and NFC.
MediaTekin the UK
MediaTek has two sites in the UK contributing to the companies development of wireless handset technology -
- The R&D site in Cambourne: the Cambridge team focuses on Protocol Stack and Multimedia software development and systems-level development and test.
- The R&D site in West Malling, Kent: the Kent team develop RF technology, including multimode cellular transceivers.

entityDescription:
I am a freelance user experience designer working in collaboration with technology companies in the development of applications for mobile devices. With more than 20 years of experience in the digital communication and journalism sector.

The lack of projects led me to work as a day labourer in the olive harvest in Cordoba (Spain) in the 2022-2023 campaign. There I discovered what agricultural work is like and how alien it is to new technologies, as it is an almost virgin sector in this sense, at least in the area where I worked.

But I also discovered that agriculture and farmers can improve their working conditions, make tasks more efficient and sustainable and increase the yield of their farms if they take advantage of the benefits offered by new technologies and, of course, satellite communications.

entityDescription:
Obortech’s Smart Hub provides all actors in the supply chain with an ecosystem in which they can operate in a fair, transparent, secure, flexible, and cost-efficient environment. Obortech offers its clients IoT sensors and blockchain-based peer-to-peer data verification. The Smart Hub is like a social network, allowing all participants to keep track of the delivered goods at any given moment using measurements taken from IoT sensors and peer-to-peer verified data uploaded in real-time to the hub and secured via blockchain technology, preventing any tampering of the information. Obortech’s Smart Hub is making supply chains visible for consumers and distributors, offering consumers detailed insights on their purchases, allowing them to make information-based choices on their food purchases. By using blockchain and IoT technology, Obortech will enable a reduction in food waste in supply chains, contributing to the EU’s action plan for 2030. Through constant monitoring of data, that is gathered by the IoT sensors and recorded on the blockchain, actors in the supply chain can receive information on faults in the supply chain (e.g., temperature change, sealing break, etc.) and react in real-time, thus preventing food waste.
The Smart Hub intro: https://youtu.be/mybaRPxLi7A
The Smart Hub demo: https://www.obortech.io/smart-hub
The Obortech’s pitch deck: https://bit.ly/3BRKobl
Obortech has collaborated with several food companies to test its technology in a fully operational environment. In collaboration with a logistic company in Mongolia (Mongolian Express LLC) and apple farms in Germany (Elbe-Obst), Obortech has beta tested its technology for delivering apples from Germany to Mongolia. The results gathered from the tests provided relevant feedback for further development. Obortech has also won the Polish Startup program, the Poland Prize, and received �‎50K grant for a soft landing in the Polish market. Furthermore, the company has collaborated with several companies in Poland, Germany, and Mongolia to test its technology in the meat and mining supply chains, validating the company’s technology through numerous use cases. The Smart Hub use cases: https://blog.obortech.io. Obortech has 10 awards & recognitions from multinational organizations such as Microsoft, Amazon, PwC, World Bank, MIT Accelerator & Poland Prize, Fruit Logistica, Berlin Partner, etc. See the full award and partner list: https://bit.ly/3HIjVhy

entityDescription:
Developing magnetic principle-based propulsion systems (engines) for all mobility applications. These propulsion devices do not require any mechanical moving components and are maintenance free. They are powered by renewable electric energy.

TOMO has invented and developed propulsion systems that operate in the field of magnetic physics. An array of electrically generated magnetic fields interact with each other and interact with the momentum of inertia of the generator (Test-Object) itself. By doing so, a scalable force (measured in Newton) acts on the generator and pushes it forwards or backwards.

The magnetic propulsion systems from TOMO will be attached to the object that has to be moved (satellite, plane, ship, car, drone …). There are no mechanical moving parts involved (no gearboxes, no rotating transmission shafts, etc).
Working technology demonstrators exist at TOMO and drive/move objects that float on water, are suspended in air, or roll on wheels. As this is a scalable technology, the lightest generator TOMO has built weights less than 150 grams, while larger generators weigh 5 kg and more.

entityDescription:
SmartIR was founded to develop a commercial pathway for a patented graphene technology for adaptive emissivity and absorption of infrared (IR) and visible light.
SmartIR Ltd is currently developing a flexible, lightweight, and switchable graphene-based tile system for coating surfaces to control infrared emissivity and visible colour across a broad spectrum. Tiles enable control of thermal radiation on demand and can be connected together to cover large surfaces and controlled on a tile-by-tile basis.

Applications exist across the aerospace and space sectors with a primary market opportunity surrounding supporting thermal management solutions in the growing sector of NanoSat and MircoSat deployments.
There is a strong market pull for lightweight, flexible, thermal control systems for integration into nano- and microSatellites. This technology can be used for space suits to regulate the body temperature in the harsh environment of outer space.
In addition to aerospace, adaptive thermal tile (ATT) also has applications into thermal signature management for increased survivability and force protection against set-and-forget style weapons systems which target heat emissions for course guidance.

In addition to aerospace, adaptive thermal tile (ATT) also has applications into thermal signature management for increased survivability and force protection against set-and-forget style weapons systems which target heat emissions for course guidance.

entityDescription:
GRUPO ONCE has been a benchmark company in Spain, specializing in the management of solutions for companies that outsource the management of their services. Alentis with more than 25 years of experience and specialized in large areas of activity -Cleaning-Environment, Security, Outsourcing, Fire-Driving, Integral Maintenance and Facility Services-, formed part of a multi-brand architecture with other companies such as Confortel, ServiMedia, Travel 2000, etc.

Today, all these companies have merged under a single brand, ILUNION, the new ONCE commitment to unite in the same direction and capitalize on the social value of all its companies that today operated through Fundosa and Ceosa. ILUNION materializes in the business sphere the social initiative of ONCE and its Foundation, with a pioneering and innovative model, which maintains the balance between its economic and social values. Thus, ILUNION is a benchmark in the creation of quality employment for people with disabilities in Spain and in which more than 36.770 people currently work, 43% of them with disabilities. It is a socially responsible business project that develops its activity in five divisions and 50 business lines with criteria of economic and social profitability.

Thus, under this objective, the company Ilunion Limpieza y Medio Ambiente, S.A. was born within ILUNION. that gathers and brings together all the experience of GRUPO ALENTIS in the management of Cleaning services through the company PILSA. Therefore, Ilunion maintains the contracts, as well as the technical and operational staff, and the material resources of PILSA, thus, it has more than 25 years of experience, being leaders in inclusion.

Ilunion offers integral cleaning solutions throughout the national geography. It has more than 9,000 professionals and offers a wide range of solutions in the following areas: Commercial Cleaning, Landscaping and Gardening, Pest Control, Waste Management and Building Maintenance.

entityDescription:
Wetlands and coastal ecosystems such as mangroves provide climate, biodiversity and social impacts, however typical restoration approaches are limited in scale and lack finance. On the other hand, larger corporations are looking for ways not just to become climate neutral but nature positive, with the recent Science Based Targets Network and the TNFD providing frameworks for this transition. With recent controversies around carbon credits, there is a demand for highly credible and meaningful impact data from contributions, not only on carbon but also biodiversity. We form a bridge between local wetland restoration projects and corporate ESG contributions through high quality data.
We do this through custom built tools such as specialised attachments for drones, which empower local groups to collect meaningful and holistic data streams on carbon, biodiversity and even social impacts. We help to fund the restoration and conservation efforts of these local groups, providing them the tools needed to collect the data at a quality that meets the demands of corporate contributors. This data is then disaggregated into specific 3x3 parcels of land which customers support through a subscription model, subscribing to impact and these meaningful data streams.

entityDescription:
CloudNet is an Internet Service provider that provide a number of services for both residential, commercial and Public Sectors (such as NHS Orkney, Orkney Islands Council and Marine Services). Our services seek to be proactive with a high degree of flexibility, whereby we work with companies to develop solutions to meet their needs. We understand that not one size fits all therefore we adapt our solutions accordingly.
Our deployed network stretches from Caithness (Mainland Scotland) – and serve the Castle of Mey, the Queen Mothers old residence (now looked after in trust overseen by Prince Charles) to the very north of Orkney, North Ronaldsay, with potential support and growth into Shetland.
We have been operating since 2011 providing services which include
• Private Wireless Networks
• Private Fibre Networks
• Internet Services to remote and rural areas
• Residential Service
• Business Circuits
• Internet of Things – IoT (partnering with North/IoT Scotland) and our networks
• Wi-Fi Coverage Access Nodes
• Marine Wi-Fi (Ferry Connectivity/Cruise Ships/Sea Farms)
Ship-to-Shore Communications
• Public Sector (NHS Orkney, Orkney Islands Council) Private and managed services
Alongside our mainstream work, we are also involved in projects to develop new and innovative solutions partnering alongside organisations and companies such as Orkney Islands Council, University of Strathclyde, CISCO Systems, BAE Naval Systems, Scottish Sea Farms, UK Government (DCMS) and Scottish Government (Scottish Futures Trust, 5G Centre for Scotland, CENSIS). We have working alongside such organisations since 2014 and have been classed as a Northern Centre of Innovation. We understand and innovate around problems and have a very good knowledge and understanding of the challenges faced due to rural/remote terrain. Weather alone has helped us to help others deliver, trial, and test their equipment/solutions to see how well their technologies cope in such environments. Not only this but we proudly we too have influenced Government policy on remote working and rural connectivity.

entityDescription:
Circe - Smart Navigation Solutions S.L. is a company oriented to the development of security solutions for geolocation systems.
Commercial satellite navigation signals are not secure, and this makes GNSS receivers vulnerable. Most of the modern devices and systems that use GNSS are not protected, and on the other hand, there are few solutions on the market, and most are oriented to the defense sector.

entityDescription:
Some of the hardest problems decision-makers face involve understanding large, complex systems such as economies, infrastructure, biological processes and human behaviour. Such systems, and the interrelationships and interdependencies between them, display emergent complexity and cannot therefore be fully understood through analysing past data or machine learning alone. To truly understand these problems we must recreate them through large scale simulations of the real world. 
Improbable’s Skyral platform technology and approach enables simulations of an unprecedented­ scale, empowering decision makers to answer “what if?” questions. These simulations are able to display emergent behaviour, leading to unexpected events and multi­order consequences that had previously been impossible to explore. This can be combined with live operational data to both improve model performance, provide a recognised ground picture within the joint operations area, provide support to battlespace management and drive after action review.

Improbable’s mission is to transform the way governments plan, execute and assess critical aspects of their nations’ governance, safety and security. Improbable provides a technology which is entirely unique in the market and the solution provides the means to improve situational awareness and decision-making processes, whilst enabling insight into the cascading consequences of actions and, in doing so, help decision makers to thrive in complexity in a way that cannot be adequately represented with existing capabilities. This will enable better appreciation of consequences intended and unintended; represent the complexity of the contemporary multi-domain operating environment; support the ability to plan against sub-threshold threats and enable interoperability by design.

entityDescription:
The TreeMap, is a geospatial company established in 2020. With headquarters in France and a significant presence in Jakarta, we are a passionate team of conservationists and scientists committed to preserving tropical forests. Our approach combines scientific investigations and advanced monitoring solutions utilizing satellite technology. We aim to uncover the underlying causes of deforestation and forest fires, evaluate the effectiveness of conservation projects and regulations, and advocate for sustainable practices in agriculture, timber, and mining industries. Transparency is at the core of our philosophy, and we make our scientific products and monitoring platform, the Nusantara Atlas: https://nusantara-atlas.org/ open access. It serves as a comprehensive resource for tracking deforestation and fires related to the palm oil and pulp-and-paper industries in Indonesia and Malaysia.
While Nusantara Atlas is open source, we recognize the need to address our client's specific requirements, including the integration of confidential data that they may prefer to keep private. We are dedicated to continuously enhancing the platform with new functionalities to meet evolving needs. To sustain and support these extended features, we offer an annual subscription model. Clients subscribing to Nusantara Atlas gain access to its enhanced capabilities, empowering them to fully leverage the platform for their projects and initiatives. In addition to the platform, we provide valuable services to companies, NGOs, governments, and research centres. These include API development, offering direct access to our deforestation data through application programming interfaces, with a corresponding subscription fee. We also provide technical consulting services, drawing upon our expertise in deforestation, forest fire mapping and interpretation, protected area and conservation project performance, and predictive deforestation models. Furthermore, we engage in research and development activities, constantly pushing the boundaries in forest and fire mapping, crop mapping, and their implications for forests. Please feel free to explore our list of publications for further information: https://thetreemap.com/publications

entityDescription:
SCHOTT:
SCHOTT is a leading international technology group that specializes in the manufacturing of high-quality materials and components for various industries, including the aerospace and semiconductor sector. Here's a brief overview of SCHOTT's background in space, SpacePV (Space Photovoltaics), semiconductors, and its expertise in glass-related technologies:
Background in Space:
SCHOTT has a strong presence in the aerospace and space exploration industry. The company has been providing innovative glass and materials solutions for space applications, ranging from optical components for telescopes and sensors to thermal protection systems for re-entry vehicles. SCHOTT's materials are engineered to withstand the extreme conditions of space, including high radiation, temperature variations, and vacuum environments.
SpacePV (Space Photovoltaics):
SCHOTT is a notable player in the private SpacePV sector, which involves the development and manufacturing of SpacePV Cover glass. SCHOTT's expertise in specialized glass contributes to the efficiency and reliability of these solar power solutions in the challenging space environment.
Glass and Relevant Experience:
SCHOTT has a rich history and expertise in glass manufacturing and related technologies. The company's advanced glass solutions are used in a wide range of industries, including optics, electronics, healthcare, and energy. SCHOTT's glass innovations cover areas such as optical fibers, display glass, pharmaceutical packaging, and specialty glass for extreme conditions.
 
SCHOTT, is a leader in glass manufacturing, has already established advanced Ultra-Thin Glass (UTG) production capabilities. In addition to this, SCHOTT AG holds the position of being the market leader in manufacturing ultra-thin glass, offering unrivaled solutions for large-scale glass sheets as thin as 30 µm. This breakthrough in glass technology is not only revolutionizing the creation of ultra-thin Space PV Cover Glass but also contributing significantly to the optimization of solar panel designs in terms of size, weight, and cost-effectiveness.
SCHOTT's UTG technology, designed for a wide range of applications, is particularly suited for space applications, promising efficient and lightweight solar energy solutions for spacecraft. Furthermore, this development extends its benefits to support the establishment of new Space PV applications.
Overall, SCHOTT's background and expertise in space, SpacePV, semiconductor materials, and glass technologies position it as a key player in providing cutting-edge solutions for demanding industries, including those that require materials to perform exceptionally well in space conditions.

entityDescription:
Recognizing the pressing need to answer an increasing demand to put small payloads into orbit (up to 1000kg), and mitigate environmental impact of space activities to ensure a sustainable future, ISP has been founded in 2022 and strives to develop rocket launcher solutions that combines affordable launch solutions with a long term vision of sustainability, both on Earth and in Space. 
Our project focuses on multiple key aspects. Firstly, it emphasizes the use of an innovative propulsion system (hybrid propulsion), aiming to increase reliability, and safety while offering lower complexity and costs. 
Moreover, we consider reusability as a cornerstone of sustainability and cost competitiveness. Indeed, by designing the rocket launcher with reusable stages and components, ISP seeks to significantly reduce costs and ressources consumption associated with each launch. 
Regarding space sustainability, our long term vision is to globally reduce the orbital footprint of space activities by incorporating directly into the design compatibilies with deorbitation and servicing activities. 
Within our global development roadmap, 2025 rhymes with the development of our micro rocket launcher able to put 150kg payload into LEO, 500kg in 2028 and 1000 kg in 2032.
Let's be part of the journey to a more Sustainable Space!

entityDescription:
Lupovis provisions agile deception environments that enhance cyber protection frameworks. Artificial Intelligence (“AI”)-implemented solutions provide pro-active and offence-centric deception strategies for cyber-attackers that have mastered traditional perimeter defences. The solution provides contextual threat intelligence when deployed outside of organisational infrastructures; and manages threats that have penetrated the network, enticing attackers through a rich engagement environment and guiding their evolution paths through the infrastructure using adaptive manipulation techniques, in so doing extending the time window for Security Operation Centre (SOC) operators to respond with the most effective countermeasures to arrest the breach whilst maintaining operational integrity and business continuity. 

Lupovis currently offers two products founded on the core platform and the capabilities described previously;
- SNARE, providing pro-active security through contextual threat intelligence and high-fidelity alerts. The Lupovis algorithms characterise adversaries and cyber-attacks in real-time to infer context such as; Who, What, Where, How and When. Amongst key actionable information – one of the featured enabled by SMART: SCOTLAND funding - Lupovis will be the only company providing an Indicator-of-Intelligence (IoI), differentiating if an attacker is a human or not through the ability to characterise the skills and methodologies of an attacker in real time.
- PROWL, an intelligence platform that eliminates the noise and filters irrelevant threats through AI-driven, prioritising effort on managing meaningful attacks. PROWL acquires data on threats that not only guides the focus of security and Security Operations Centre (SOC) teams, but also informs the development of Lupovis SNARE, in combination enriching the provision of actionable information.

entityDescription:
SPIE ICS, tous les services ICT, la proximité en plus !

Filiale du groupe SPIE, SPIE ICS est une Entreprise de Services Numériques, spécialisée dans les infrastructures ICT*, depuis l’Environnement Utilisateurs jusqu’au Data Center. Sa vocation est de contribuer à la transformation numérique des métiers de ses clients en tant que vecteur de croissance et de développement tout en diminuant la complexité technologique des systèmes d’information et en simplifiant l’usage pour les utilisateurs.

L’activité de SPIE ICS est de concevoir, mettre en œuvre et maintenir des infrastructures innovantes au travers d’une offre de services globale : conseil & ingénierie, projets & intégration, infogérance & maintenance, services opérés & cloud.

Grâce à l’expertise de ses 3 000 salariés et à son réseau d’implantation avec 60 agences en France elle accompagne ses clients dans leurs évolutions numériques, en privilégiant, sur le terrain, la proximité, la performance et la responsabilité, tout en garantissant la sécurité des collaborateurs.

Elle dispose de 5 domaines d'expertises technologiques :

Communications Unifiées & Collaboration (vidéoconférence, mobilité/nomadisme, relation clients…)
Infrastructures IP & Sécurité (Réseaux Locaux et étendus d’entreprise, réseaux opérés & la sécurité globale du système d’information)
Data Center (LAN Data Center, serveurs, virtualisation, stockage/archivage/sauvegarde, client léger)
Environnement Utilisateurs (postes de travail/BYOD, bureautique/périphériques)
Bâtiment Intelligent (infrastructures, vidéo protection/contrôle d’accès sur IP...)
 

L’activité de SPIE ICS se répartie, d’une part à hauteur de 55% auprès des Entreprises de Taille Intermédiaire et des collectivités territoriales, et d’autre part, de 45% auprès des grands comptes nationaux et internationaux.

Elle pilote le comité digital du groupe SPIE regroupant toutes ses filiales ICT pour garantir à ses clients une couverture homogène des services sur différents pays : Belgique, Pays-Bas, Suisse, Allemagne. Elle est membre actif de l’alliance GWA (Global Workspace Alliance), qui concentre un réseau mondial de prestataires de services sur les 5 continents pour traiter des projets à forte dimension internationale.

TheLIST3N(Computer Science and Digital Society) laboratory develops efficient approaches (concepts, models, methods and tools) to deal with the entire data processing chain, from sensors to uses, through data analysis and optimization.

This research unit project is the result of a reconfiguration of four existing research teams: ERA, LOSI, M2S and Tech-CICO. The new structure includes76 permanent researchersfor a total staff of165 people.

The UR's scientific project is based on the design of an integrated processing chain. The primary objective of this integrated approach is to promote the design of new methods and methodological advances in the disciplines by taking into account the specificities of the different links in the chain. Each link contributes to the performance of the overall chain while evolving in a constrained space imposed by its connection to the other links in the chain.

· Compute—Our Compute portfolio offers both general purpose servers for multi-workload computing and workload optimized servers which offer the best performance and value for demanding applications. · HPC & AI—Our HPC & AI business offers standard and custom hardware and software solutions designed to support specific use cases. entityDescription:
Agricolus is a dynamic and innovative product company founded in 2017, based in Italy, springing out from the synergy of the combined competences of a group of skilled professionals supported by two firms: TeamDev Srl and Aedit Srl. Their knowledge is based on ten-year of international experiences in research, analysis, advice and development of useful applications for agricultural management. Agricolus has a strong focus on technological innovation. Adopting this approach, the company has started to enlarge the client portfolio including SMEs, government, and large companies.
In 2013 Agricolus group started using drones for survey operations and carrying out researches in agriculture with multi-spectral analysis to optimize the use of fertilizers and pesticides. On October 11th, 2014 the first laboratory of Precision Farming in Italy was born, thanks to the collaboration with the Agricultural Institute of Todi. Workshop, events and much more. The laboratory worked for the future and high skilled competences began to get mixed with modern technologies.
It is between 2014 and 2016 when Agricolus, at that time incubated in TeamDev, is accepted into different acceleration programmes within the FIWARE initiative. This fact is a huge opportunity for the company, as it facilitates the development of different modules to be integrated in the overall Agricolus Suite. 

The most important milestone, however, was probably the realization of the S.I.G. 2015 project.
Thanks to Misura 1.2.4 of PSR Umbria 2007-2013 “Cooperazione per lo sviluppo di nuovi prodotti, processi e tecnologie nei settori agricolo e alimentare e settore forestale”, an innovative workgroup (A.T.I.) was created. It was a cooperation between research and farms able to create a connection between production and research for agriculture. The aim of the project was to collect data in order to create DSS application (Decision support System) to manage crops. These collected data allowed to create specific thematic maps showing homogeneous areas in the crops.
Thanks to the positive feedback of S.I.G. project 2015, it was possible to create the first products for Precision Farming. On October 26th, 2015 Department of Agriculture of Umbria Region announced the program to monitor olive fruit fly with innovative software. The software was produced and developed for precision farming: OLIWES, one of the app of Agricolus suite.
In 2016 Agricolus product achieved the first successes at international level: in February, in fact, it was selected as a testimonial in the Showcase of GSMA at Mobile World Congress 2016 in Barcelona. Agricolus was the only one Italian project selected.
At that time vertical products development started: TobaccoDSS (for tobacco crops) Grape DSS (for Vineyards) and, thanks to AgricolusDSS, the project won the H2020 SME Instrument Phase 1 grant. 
Given the good reception of Agricolus in the market and the interest by a number of investors, a decision of founding a product company only devoted to the Agricolus suite was taken. 2017 is the year Agricolous Srl is legally incorporated and is currently in the process of kicking off their activities and ready to launch a new version of the platform.

entityName: Institute of Landscape Ecology, Slovak Academy of Sciences
entityDescription:
Institute of Landscape Ecology of Slovak Academy of Sciences (ILE SAS) is a public research institution. The scientific research activities of ILE SAS are oriented toward the development of the theory and methods of research of ecological properties and processes on the systems level. These activities develop the theory and methods of landscape ecology, deal with the problems of ecological processes and the dynamics of the landscape, and produce models for optimum ecological use of the landscape. The Insttitute studies the material and spatial differentiation of biotopes in relation to landscape biodiversity and looks at the question of resources at the ecosystem level of local and spatial systems. ILE SAS develops methods of ecologically-sound landscape planning and special methods for the application and interpretation of ecological and environmental knowledge in the field of nature and landscape protection as well as in environmental management.
- ILE SAS provides consultancy and other expert services in line with the main field of activity of the institute.
- ILE SAS provides PhD opportunities according to national legislation.
- ILE SAS publishes the results of scientific research activity in both the periodical and non-periodical press. Publishing follows the relevant resolutions of the Presidium of the SAS.

entityName: International Commission for the Hydrology of the Rhine Basin
entityDescription:
The International Commission for the Hydrology of the Rhine basin (CHR) is an organization in which the scientific institutes of the Rhine riparian states formulate joint hydrological measures for sustainable development of the Rhine basin.
Agreed working and funding structures are available within the Rhine-bordering countries. These allow the CHR to continually generate adequate and future-oriented scientific knowledge pertaining to the hydrology of the Rhine, for the targeted use of policy-makers and stakeholders. The CHR is a leading worldwide example of successful and peaceful international collaboration when it comes to transboundary river basins.
The CHR provides a scientific knowledge base for the hydrology of the Rhine catchment area, conducting both solicited and unsolicited research. The CHR makes these results available to scientists, decision-makers and stakeholders in the region. Consequently, we are focussing on advising politically-active and technically-oriented organizations, such as the International Commission for the Protection of the Rhine (ICPR) and the Central Commission for Navigation of the Rhine (CCNR), to support them with reliable science-based information for the implementation of guidelines, policy, management and decision-making.

entityDescription:
The Crick’s mission is discovery without boundaries. We don’t limit the direction our research takes. We want to understand more about how living things work to help improve treatment, diagnosis and prevention of human disease, and generate economic opportunities for the UK.
In our institute more than 2,000 staff and students use their wide-ranging knowledge and expertise to work across disciplines and explore biology at all levels, from molecules through cells to entire organisms.
The Crick is the outcome of a merger between the MRC's National Institute for Medical Research (NIMR) and CRUK's London Research Institute (LRI).The new institute was named after the UK scientist Francis Crick in recognition of his contributions to understanding the genetic code, the key to understanding how living things work.
We were established by our six founding partner organisations: the Medical Research Council (MRC), Cancer Research UK (CRUK), Wellcome, UCL (University College London), Imperial College London and King’s College London.
We began operating in our new, purpose-built institute in early 2017 and now have more than 100 research groups. Research groups from NIMR and LRI have been joined by groups seconded from each of our three partner universities, and we have recruited a significant number of newly recruited group leaders.
The institute is governed by a Board of Trustees, comprised of independent members and representatives from each of our founding partners. We are funded through core funding from the MRC, CRUK and Wellcome, as well as external research grants.

entityName: MIICT-Mediterranean Institute of Innovation , Communication and Technology
entityDescription:
The MIICT's Historic Milestones
The MIICT’s commitment to technological research has been unwavering throughout its short but prolific history since its establishment in 2004 and its legal constitution in 2013. As a non-profit organisation, we have always prioritised innovation and advancing the state of technology, even in the face of limited funding.
Over the years, our pioneering work in research and innovation has helped to push the boundaries of what is possible in some of the fields in which we took an active research interest. From developing proofs of concept for cutting-edge technologies for healthcare, education, public procurement, agriculture and the environment, to creating novel solutions for societal challenges, the MIICT has always been at the forefront of technological innovation.
Despite the challenges that we have faced, we have remained steadfast in our mission to make a positive impact on society through technology. We have collaborated with numerous partners from academia, industry, government agencies and supranational government bodies to bring our ideas to life and to make them accessible to those who need them most on a free, open-source basis.
Looking to the future, the MIICT remains committed to pushing the boundaries of what is possible through research and innovation. We will continue to invest in the development of groundbreaking technologies and collaborate with partners around the world to create a brighter and more innovative future for all. We are very proud of our achievements and all the people who led us here. 

Our Approach
At the MIICT, our approach is grounded in our unwavering commitment to innovation, communications, and technology. We believe these are the essential levers of societal progress, and we are dedicated to utilising them to foster change, bridge divides, and empower individuals and communities. This focus drives our efforts to develop innovative solutions, explore new frontiers in communications, and leverage advanced technology to address pressing societal issues. Our aim is not just to contribute to immediate change but to make a lasting impact that will continue to benefit future generations. Through our multifaceted approach, we strive to spark transformation that reverberates beyond the immediate context, shaping a brighter, more inclusive future for all.

entityName: TECHNOLOGY FOR PROPULSION AND INNOVATION SPA
entityDescription: T4i was founded in 2014 as a Spin Off of the University of Padua. Thanks to the technical competences from the Space Propulsion Group of the Aerospace Department, today T4i offers specific solutions in the aerospace sector and develops new technologies. T4i develops electric thrusters for satellite applications based on helicon technology. Due to their simplicity they are versatile, scalable and economically competitive in the nano-micro-mini-satellite market. Moreover T4i develops small hybrid rocket engines in the class of 100-1000 N of thrust, medium ones up to 30 kN and monopropellant engines of 10-200 N of thrust. The chemical engines find application in satellites and launcher small upper stages, launcher ring adapters, capsules, landers and sounding rockets’ applications (sub-orbital flights). T4i also understands and helps the customers on the selection and characterization of the proper propulsive system for their mission and identifies the interactions between the propulsion system and the other satellite subsystems or the external environment. T4i is involved in technology transfer projects towards the manufacturing industry, developing plasma sources and plasma antennas, advanced diagnostic systems and sensors. The company also supports industries in new technology development projects thanks to the multidisciplinary competences gained on the space activities.

entityDescription:
Ingeniarius, Lda., (ING) is a private SME that aims for R&D&I in the many fields of engineering, with emphasis in field robotics. The company’s philosophy is to create disruptive robotic solutions, either through the refitting of existing machines, or the full in-house development. The company tackles challenging field applications, namely within the domains of agriculture, forestry, construction, and others. ING’ team is experienced in the full chain of mechatronics development and robotic software design.
Since 2016, ING led four national consortia, STOP, CORE, SEMFIRE and SAFEFOREST, being currently engaged as participant in other EU projects (H2020), such as 5GSMARTFACT (956670), FEROX (101070440) and OPENSWARM (101093046). Beyond intercommunity projects covered by European programmes, ING has also been developing user-centric robotic solutions for private clients worldwide, as is the case of Viking (Germany), FallProtec (Luxembourg) and Corbar (Spain). These solutions have been tailored for specific needs, with the SolarCleano F1A and B1A robots being the most successful example of real-world field applications developed by ING[1],[2] and currently available in the market.
The experience with mobile robotic technologies endows ING with the necessary expertise to demonstrate the use of robotics in challenging domains, especially around heavy-duty tasks.

entityName: Hochschule Darmstadt - University of Applied Sciences
entityDescription:
Darmstadt University of Applied Sciences (Hochschule Darmstadt, h_da) puts science into action. With a student body of about 17,000, it is one of the largest and most distinguished universities of applied sciences in Germany. Its excellent reputation is the result of a scientifically grounded, real-world approach to higher education and the professional success of its graduates.
Graduates of Darmstadt University of Applied Sciences are particularly popular with HR managers in German companies. This is confirmed by the annual "Wirtschaftswoche" rankings. For the University Ranking 2019, the personnel service provider Universum Global surveyed 650 small, medium-sized and large companies nationwide. From a total of 216 universities of applied sciences in Germany, they were able to select those whose graduates met their expectations particularly well. Accordingly, h_da ranks among the top 10 in Germany in the fields of mechanical engineering (rank 3), computer science (rank 8), electrical engineering (rank 7) and industrial engineering (rank 4).
In the university ranking of the Centre for Higher Education Development (CHE) 2019, the h_da scores particularly well in terms of practical relevance and preparation for the profession. Accordingly, students of the study courses Civil Engineering, Electrical Engineering and Information Technology, Mechanical Engineering and Environmental Engineering praise the very good equipment of the practice laboratories. The h_da is here in the national top group. The same applies to the quality of excursions, which students of architecture and environmental engineering rate as very good. The h_da is also top nationwide when it comes to contacts to professional practice. The CHE Ranking lists the University of Applied Sciences Darmstadt in the study courses electrical engineering and information technology, mechanical engineering and mechatronics in the national top group.
The high reputation of the h_da study courses is based on a good supervision ratio with manageable groups and a clear practical orientation. Here, science and practice intermesh in a targeted manner. This is because the professors of h_da know what they are doing: They all come from professional practice and know the future professional demands on their students. In the practical professional phases of the study programmes, students can also test and expand what they have learned with employers in business and society.

entityDescription:
FlowCore AI with FCAI as abbreviation is a limited liability company founded in 2023. The company’s headquarters is in Sofia, Bulgaria. FCAI is building on the AI-based IP that was generated from ThePoWow.Me Ltd., whose initial goal was to design, develop and deliver to the market a new generation of healthcare experiences and solutions for people with diabetes by leveraging AI and ML to analyze and model diabetics’ lifestyle data and build a lifestyle recommendation system based on an individualized model of each diabetic. The COVID-19 crisis significantly impacted the company’s product operations. The video part of the product has been acquired byVideoEngager Inc., based in San Francisco, the US, whereas the AI has been retained and is currently in the core of the FlowCore AI. FCAI currently operates on the professional services side, initially focusing on software-as-a-service (SaaS) solutions and gradually shifting towards cyber-physical systems (CPS). Currently, the FCAI’s prime focus is on the intersection of AI/ML, safety- and mission-critical systems, incl. a range of automation services.
1) Infrastructure Automation
- Infrastructure as Code,
- Audibility, traceability, scanning for compliance before release,
- Disaster recovery with RTO in a range of minutes to a few hours and RPO in a range of a few hours,
- Migration to new regions or providers,
- Different release strategies,
- Implementation of a complete cyber-resilience strategy
- Security Automation
- Security by design,
- Architectural considerations to address OWASP’s top 10 security threats,
- Deployment considerations,
- Threat detection, investigation, mitigation, and response.
2) Lifecycle Automation
- Dependable, efficient, and cost-optimized SaaS product/service architectures,
- Delivery of predictable CX and services,
- Avoid/minimize SLA breaches for SaaS solutions,
- Release strategies for SaaS solutions, incl. green/blue deployments, A/B testing, and canary releases.
3) Intelligent Automation
- Integrating AI in existing processes to drive better decision processes,
- A data-driven approach, incl. unstructured data from heterogeneous sources to drive actionable insights,
- Leverage historical data to make processes predictive.
4) Process Automation
- Creation of digital twins,
- Edge/cloud compute continuum,
- What-if scenarios,
- Optimize processes on a system level, e.g., on a farm level for the agricultural market.
For a short period, the company signed contracts to support international ends-users from North America and EMEA regions.

entityDescription:
Sensoworks is an innovative startup born in January 2020 that offers the market an "as a service" solution for monitoring critical infrastructures. Sensoworks acquires, monitors and analyzes data from sensors connected to infrastructures such as bridges, viaducts, tunnels, buildings, water and sewage networks. It connects to all the sensors to allow the configuration of the infrastructure and all its customizations. Once configured, all sensors are monitored in real time, data is collected, logged and securely structured to be analyzed by machine learning algorithms. The data is analyzed by AI algorithms for the identification of structural anomalies or predictive maintenance activities.Sensoworks can be easily configured to set up automatic actions based on collected data, events and performed analyses. It allows for the generation of highly configurable reports that can be stored in the blockchain. Sensoworks presents itself as a software product vendor in the critical infrastructure monitoring market. The results obtained to date show how a technologically advanced platform has become a fundamental element of the monitoring processes. Road, motorway, sewage and water network operators are able to easily insert the Sensoworks platform within their monitoring and intervention processes, improving them, thanks to the introduction of a system capable of monitoring in real time, acting in autonomy when certain conditions occur, to the creation of advanced reports that can be certified in blockchain.Sensoworks therefore allows you to monitor complex infrastructures making data analysis very simple and allowing you to prevent the onset of certain phenomena by reducing risks and optimizing investment costs for maintenance activities.
The competitive context
The IoT (Internet of Things) is revolutionizing the way critical infrastructure, such as bridges, viaducts, tunnels, water and sewage networks, are monitored and managed. The goal is to improve the efficiency, safety and resilience of these infrastructures through the use of sensors, monitoring devices and advanced algorithms to analyze the data collected. The competitive environment of IoT in critical infrastructure monitoring is characterized by intense competition between IoT solution providers and infrastructure management service providers. Companies offering IoT solutions compete to provide the best sensor technology, monitoring devices and data analysis software, while infrastructure management companies seek to adopt more efficient and secure solutions at reasonable costs. IoT technologies can provide a number of competitive advantages over traditional monitoring solutions, such as the ability to collect data in real time, which allows for rapid response in case of problems, and real-time data analysis to identify potential problems before they occur.
Sensoworks positions itself in this context as a software product vendor, a complete, end-to-end IIoT (Intelligent Internet of Things) solution, which includes:
- Sensoworks IIoT Edge Gateway: an edge/fog computing software for real-time acquisition and analysis of static and dynamic parameters acquired by sensors connected to the infrastructure and a native cloud platform
- Sensoworks IIoT Platform: a native cloud platform for Big Data & Analytics management, Predictions, Alarm Management, Document Management, BIM Integration to support Digital Twin of Monitored Infrastructures, GIS Integration to support spatial analysis;
Compared to competitors on the market who typically offer custom IoT solutions with high implementation costs or with different application modules that require integration activities, Sensoworks offers a ready-to-use end-to-end solution that supports customers for monitoring activities, predictive maintenance and simulation of the behavior of the infrastructurs as the modal parameters vary.

Spatineo Oy is the top expert in quality of service and interoperability of spatial web services in Europe. Spat¬in-eo actively participates and innovates in the context of OGC and INSPIRE to further develop the standards and engage with the parties leveraging them. Spatineo helps organizations to optimize their investments in the Spatial Data Infrastructure and prove the value of their spatial information and web services. Spatineo was founded in 2011 and it has headquarters in Helsinki, Finland. The mission is to help customers to improve the use and usability of spatial web service technologies for both public and commercial uses.
Spatineo has developed easy-to-use cloud-based applications for usage analytics, service level monitoring and performance testing of spatial web services. The applications provide important metrics for service development and reporting and can also be used as data for impact analysis. Customers that use Spatineo’s pro-ducts represent a range of different industries from numerous countries, industries such as cadastral and land registry authorities, mapping, environmental and natural resources organisations, transportation agencies, IT service providers, cities, regions and municipalities.
Spatineo is a member of OGC (Open Geospatial Consortium), an active contributor and strongly committed to the technical development of the INSPIRE Directive, with in-depth involvement in the standardization work support to make sure standards and technical guidances are practical and helpful.

entityDescription:
Knight Optical is a leading global provider of scientific optical components, with a successful track record spanning over 30 years. Under the leadership of our managing director, Colin Overton, we have established ourselves as a trusted name in the industry, committed to delivering superior quality products and services.
Despite our modest beginnings, Knight Optical has achieved remarkable growth, expanding our operations in the UK and establishing a presence in the United States in 2015. Our ongoing objective is to continue expanding and serving the global market. Located in Kent, South East England, we benefit from convenient distribution to Europe, being only 20 minutes away from the Channel Tunnel rail link.
Our Services
We cater to a diverse range of industries, including scientific research, defense, medical, pharmaceutical, optoelectronics, entertainment, education, laser technology, engineering, manufacturing, and oil and gas. Our highly qualified and skilled workforce enables us to offer custom-made optical solutions in virtually any shape or size, economically. By combining traditional techniques with state-of-the-art systems and metrology equipment, we guarantee superior quality, competitive pricing, and prompt delivery within 2-3 weeks from the receipt of an order.
At Knight Optical, we handle projects of all scales, from one-off research orders to large-scale production runs with call-off delivery schedules. Our dedicated staff members are always ready to assist you with any inquiries, as we prioritize providing excellent customer service. Through collaborative partnerships with our customers, we can determine specific requirements, recommend suitable materials and tolerances, ensuring optimal outcomes.
In addition to our custom optics, we maintain an inventory of over 3,000 stock items readily available for prompt dispatch. These items can be conveniently purchased from our website. Rest assured, all optical components dispatched from Knight Optical undergo rigorous testing in our state-of-the-art metrology laboratory, ensuring their readiness for immediate use.
Bringing Quality Into Focus
Quality is the cornerstone of our operations at Knight Optical. We have implemented stringent quality management systems and have received ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 14001:2015 accreditations. Our workforce is well-versed in these quality management systems and adheres to established quality standards, including ISO 10110, BS4301, and MIL-SPEC, through comprehensive training programs.

To expand and strengthen its objective, in 2020 it acquired the Innovilab Laboratory in Rende, located in Contrada Mazzarella, operational since 2016 with expertise in Research and Innovation Projects in the healthcare sector, using CLOUD solutions operating in clinical centers, nursing homes, and patient homes in the field of telemedicine and remote real-time monitoring. Réaltra is a company dedicated to the design, development and manufacture of cost-effective space electronic systems using cutting-edge technologies. entityDescription:
Réaltra Space Systems Engineering is a Division
of Real Time Technologies Ltd (IE).

Réaltra provides dedicated design & development engineering expertise for space electronics systems combined with Realtime’s proven manufacturing capability for space applications. 

Réaltra is the Irish word for Galaxy, and at the core of our company is an exceptional team of people who consistently deliver excellence through a commitment to innovation, attention to detail, passion and flexibility to adapt and respond to our customers’ evolving needs and a dedication to quality.

The enhanced combination of engineering design and production of spacecraft electronics equipment available in Réaltra enables our customers to meet the challenging technical and cost constraints across a wide range of commercial and non-commercial space missions.

Réaltra has built its reputation in the space sector based on the core principles of;

- Innovative Design
- Technical Excellence
- Quality Processes
- Exceptional Support

The Réaltra Space Systems Engineering Division of Realtime Technologies provides engineering design, development and integration solutions for spacecraft and launcher electronics systems;

- Utilizing Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) electronics to design & deliver launch vehicle telemetry products and systems to the Global space launcher market.

- Adaptation and ruggedization of COTS electronics to create radiation tolerant high-performance payload & platform avionics products and systems for spacecraft used in LEO missions.

- Design, build & qualify custom rad-hard, high reliability payload & platform avionics products and systems for spacecraft used in Deep Space missions.

- Develop real time anomaly detection solutions based on Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence led approaches using high performance AI acceleration platforms and deploying AI/ML algorithms to existing spacecraft & launcher avionics system.

- Perform state-of-the-art cross cutting research to develop technologies that support the core strategies to lower cost, lower risk, and increase performance.

Company description: Establishment of the Foundation for the Support of Education at the “Aviation Valley Association” took place as a result of long-term cooperation and initiatives jointly undertaken by universities and enterprises associated in the Aviation Valley. The main reason for the establishment of the Foundation was the unflagging interest of children and young people from the entire Podkarpackie province in educational programs such as “Super Cool Physics”, “Suggestion” or “Children’s Technical University”. Thanks to the involvement of representatives of various backgrounds - business people, teachers, researchers, students and pupils, it was possible to broaden and expand the offer of these programs in such a way that it would meet the expectations of their recipients and at the same time make the best use of the growing opportunities of industry and science. 
The founder of the Foundation for the Support of Education at the “Aviation Valley Association” is the Association of the Group of Aviation Industry Entrepreneurs “Aviation Valley”. Since its establishment, it has been pursuing the objectives set out in the statutes, conducting educational and scientific activities in the field of: 
− popularizing science and education. Developing interest in science as an area of attractive exploration and experience; 
− raising the level of education of children and young people, especially from rural areas, urban and rural areas and small towns. Creating and equalizing educational opportunities, development opportunities and self-fulfillment; 
− increasing the importance of the role of science and education in the consciousness of inhabitants of rural areas, urban and rural areas and small towns as a factor of the development of society and the growth of the quality of life, and showing and promoting the benefits of knowledge and education; 
− promoting the idea of lifelong learning. 
The Mayor of the City of Rzeszów and the Marshal of the Podkarpackie province took the honorary patronage of the Foundation’s activities. The Foundation also cooperates with the Board of Education in Rzeszów, which ensures that the offer addressed to students is adapted to the curriculum and that it reaches the places where there is a special need for such activities. 
The Foundation implements activities at all levels of education, from primary school to secondary school, as well as for adults, such as postgraduate studies for teachers of vocational subjects implemented jointly with the Rzeszów University of Technology.
