entityDescription: Istognosis is a software house based in Nicosia, Cyprus established in 2011 with well-established expertise in cloud-oriented and big data technologies with emphasis on Internet of Things (IoT) systems while at the same time excels in designing and developing web-based applications and services across a diverse spectrum of industries such as transportation, healthcare, energy and agriculture. Istognosis invests in R&D activities involving machine learning, image analysis, computer vision, robotics, intelligent systems and networks. Currently, Istognosis provides solutions mainly in three overlapping directions: (a) in the design and development of highly available cloud based applications and solutions, (b) in providing IoT hardware/software solutions mainly for vehicle fleets using state-of-the-art algorithms and tools, as well as (c) in designing and developing energy-efficient and cost-effective renewable energy solutions for private and commercial buildings under the brand name Save Electricity. Businesswise, Istognosis developed and owns (a) the NAVARCHOS fleet management platform which currently serves more than 30 small-scale fleets of a total of 200 commercial vehicles and (b) the ARCHIMIDES framework for cost/energy-efficient PV system analysis and design. Furthermore, Istognosis develops, maintains and supports numerous web applications and solutions for a wide range of customers from both the public and the private sector such as Bank of Cyprus, University of Cyprus, Open University of Cyprus, Costas Papaellinas Organization and others. Moreover, Istognosis has been involved in several EU-funded and RPF-funded projects such as REDUCTION project (7th Framework Programme Call 7), AgriRobot project (RPF, 2010-13), SAVSAR project(Bilateral Greece - Israel 2014-15), BaSE project (EU funded project under the Erasmus+ 2015-16), and NAVARCHOS 2 project (RPF 2018-20), for the innovative enhancement of the existing NAVARCHOS platform.

entityDescription: Metasat UK Ltd is a Glasgow-based 'Clean Space' start-up founded in December 2020 in response to the growing interest in space sustainability. The company provides SMEs with consultancy-based services on space sustainability, develops space technologies and creates new software/tools all with the concept of sustainable development at their core for the benefit of the orbital and Earth environment. Our goal is to help the space sector innovate for a more sustainable future. To do this, Metasat UK aims to lessen the environmental footprint of their customer's products, processes and services through life cycle assessment (LCA) / ecodesign and develops a variety of space technologies for (and in collaboration with) its clients, designed to aid in boosting sustainable development. Such technologies include (but are not limited to) space debris detection technologies and solar power satellites. The company also creates numerical models, methods, simulations, tools and software using a combination of in-house and external data products which cover both space situational awareness and the Earth system. The company's innovation and customer-focussed approach has already allowed it to gain considerable interest from a variety of international clients.

entityDescription:
A story almost 40 years in the making
At ZyLAB we believe that technology can be leveraged to perform legal discovery with more speed, defensibility and depth. It's been almost 40 years since we began our journey to realizing that vision, and it continues to this day. KeysightTechnologies Austria GmbH has one of the leading industrial research labs on microwave GHz measurement including high-frequency PNA technology, GHz calibration algorithms, and tomographic imaging reconstruction. entityDescription: Eurospace - a non-profit organisation founded in 1961 - fosters the development of space activities in Europe and promotes a better understanding of space industry related issues and problems. Its members are the main space industry manufacturers and launcher service providers. Eurospace members cover the whole span of the space industrial chain, are present in 13 European countries and represent more than 90% of the European space industry activity from both a turnover and employment point of view. Eurospace plays a key role in the European Space Technology Strategy process, officially presenting the whole European space manufacturing industry views on technology evolution and harmonisation. With 50 years of presence in the space policy arena, Eurospace has established and maintains a comprehensive network of contacts with the main national space agencies in Europe (ASI, UKSA, CNES, DLR,...) and with the relevant national ministries. As policy evolution required, Eurospace extended its reach to new institutions, such as the WEU, EDA or the French DGA for defence matters. Eurospace mandate covers the relevant EU bodies, including Commission Directorate Generals, the Council, the Parliament etc. and eventually Eurospace established a dedicated office in Brussels in 2001. Eurospace is a recognised interlocutor to the European Union, and an active participant to EU led industry consultations on space, providing data, analysis and assessments on space industry related issues to relevant DGs as required.

Salutes Space offers Space Infrastructure Services to promote Life 3.0, Web 3.0 and Decentralization in the form of A.I./IoSTs/Drones, 6G/SBSP/Satellites and EdTech services.
Slogan:
Your company needs a space strategy, your company needs salutes.
Mission Statement:
Salutes Space aims to revolutionize the Space Industry by promoting Life 3.0 through the provision of decentralized, blockchain-based advanced Space Infrastructure as a Service, utilizing cutting-edge technology in Satellites, Artificial Intelligence, IT, Cloud services, Drones, and EdTech for research, development, and services such as earth observation, telecommunications, and remote sensing
Business objectives:
The planning and execution of space missions using artificial intelligence, IT and EdTech, the development and production of space-related technologies and systems, the provision of satellite operations services, space technology consulting, and the provision of space infrastructure services (SIS) with a focus on the use of neuromorphic and quantum computing and space-based solar power, IoT, drones, and, as well as the use of space-based technologies and distributed systems to provide valuable data and infrastructure to support the development of smart cities through the deployment of next-generation satellite communications technologies to ensure quality of service distribution and cybersecurity. The company may enter into any transaction that serves the aforementioned object. The company is, furthermore, entitled to establish branches and/or subsidiaries in Germany and abroad.

Vision:
Decentralization in space technology means distributing decision-making power and resources away from a centralized authority. This is achieved through the use of autonomous and semi-autonomous systems, such as swarm robotics and blockchain technology, to reduce reliance on centralized control and increase distributed coordination and collaboration. The overall goal of decentralization in space technology is to create more resilient and efficient systems that can adapt to changing circumstances and operate independently, increasing the sustainability of space technology. The concept of decentralization in space technology provides high value to smart cities, which rely on technology to create efficient and sustainable urban systems.

entityDescription:
Crowdpolicy is an SME founded in 2012, active in the field of IT and specialized in crowdsourcing methods and techniques within the fields of fintech, civictech and open innovation. Our company’s aim is to develop methodologies and technologies for crowd participation in organisations, a mentality that is reflected in the company's mission statement: Bridge the gap between organisations and the crowd.
During its 10 years of operation, Crowdpolicy has implemented numerous projects developing complex information systems for the private and public sector, companies, financial institutions and local governments such as municipalities, regions and ministries. It has also implemented numerous events, workshops and competitions related to the promotion of innovation in various thematic areas.
Crowdpolicy has built on open technologies and data, as well as open innovation processes, developing applications and platforms in the fintech, govtech and open innovation sectors (hackathons, accelerators, etc.). This mentality still permeates the operation of the business, with the result that many parts of the technology produced are openly disseminated in order to generate wider added value.
Today Crowdpolicy is active in developing applications and platforms in the key areas of Fintech, Govtech/Civictech, Open Innovation and AI Chatbot development building on open technologies and data, as well as open innovation processes.
The founders of the company have actively participated on c-level positions in more than 30 flagship digital transformation projects in Greece, such as Opengov (consultations, recruitment), Clarity - diavgeia (post decisions of public sector), Open Innovation for Public Administration, Open Data – Geodata and more. Building on that background, the company has worked on open data and collaborative principles, turning them into applications and platforms within the fields of govtech/civictech, fintech and open innovation (hackathons and accelerators for the later). CrowdPolicy is also a member of the Eurocrowd- European Crowdfunding Network. On most of these project the main role of Crowdpolicy is the development of digital tools and existing know-how for their implementation as well as the dissemination of innovative productive and pilot applications through numerous channels, being in a privileged position to upgrade the know-how acquired by the execution of this project.

CNIM Systèmes Industriels (CSI) has an expertise in the engineering and manufacturing of high added-value and large components for space applications. Its expertise and competencies lies in large dimensions end-to-end projects: turning, milling, drilling, electron beam welding, large scale of high-precision controls, heat treatment. 
Backed up by a long partnership with ArianeGroup, CSI now manufactures nozzle casings for the Ariane 6 and Vega C launcher and cryogenic tanks components.
Main activities:
Design, industrialization and production of systems and equipments meeting the highest standards in harsh environment.
Expertise in elaboration and production of composite & polyurethane products meeting the highest level of quality & performance requirements.
Large-size 3D controls and thermal treatment.
CSI manufactured all three-elements of Ariane 5’s nozzles thanks to its expertise in precision machining and welding.
CSI has a state-of-the-art industrial equipment: large scale electron beam welding and now offers a new process to manufacture quicker and to reduce costs: the flow-forming technology.
CSI has both static and mobile control means, suitable for large-size and high-precision metrology (including MMT-ZEISS).
CSI has a strong expertise in Composite & Polyurethane used in space industry.

entityDescription:

Laboratory Brochure: please copy and paste this link: 27108_Laborbroschu_re_DLR_051021.pdf
The Institute of Space Systems in Bremen designs and analyses future spacecraft and space missions (launchers, orbital and exploration systems, and satellites), and assesses them with regard to their technical performance and cost. It applies state-of-the-art methods of multi-disciplinary engineering in system design and analysis – for example, a computerised system for concurrent design.
In addition, the Institute of Space Systems cooperates with other DLR institutes and research institutions to develop, build and operate its own spacecraft and missions. These are used to conduct scientific investigations and technology demonstrations involving, for example, small satellites and planetary landers. The Institute is a centre of excellence for systems engineering with capabilities in system design, system integration and systems testing, for which it plays a coordination and integration role.
At the Institute of Space Systems, research is also conducted into important systems technologies, such as the behaviour and handling of cryogenic fuels in tanks, landing technologies, attitude and orbit control systems, avionics systems and high-precision optical measurement systems, to enable future space missions or improve existing technologies.

entityDescription: The Senckenberg – Leibniz Institution for Biodiversity and Earth System Research (SGN) was founded in 1817 by local citizens in Frankfurt with the name Senckenbergische Naturforschende Gesellschaft, which translates to the Senckenberg Natural Science Society. In regard to biology, the museum is one of the most important natural history museums in all of Europe, as well as one of the biggest. The SGN sponsors seven research institutes and three natural history museums. The museums are located in Frankfurt, Goerlitz, and Dresden. According to its tradition, the societies’ primary purpose is to conduct biological and natural research, and to make this accessible to everyone through publication, education, and its museums. Today, its purpose is more important than ever, due to a global increase in both interest and curiosity which leaves many biological questions to be answered, such as those regarding climate change and the conservation of our planet

entityDescription:
Soitec plays a key role in the microelectronics industry. It designs and manufactures innovative semiconductor materials. These substrates are then patterned and cut into chips to make circuits for electronic components. Soitec offers unique and competitive solutions for miniaturizing chips, improving their performance and reducing their energy usage.
In meeting the technical and economic challenges of mainstream electronics, Soitec is helping to speed up the mobile and digital revolutions. Its products are used to manufacture chips that go into smart phones, tablets, computers, IT servers and data centers as well as electronic components in cars, connected devices, and industrial and medical equipment.
Soitec's technologies, projects and industrial capacity make it one of the crown jewels of France's industrial sector. The company was founded 25 years ago in Grenoble's high-tech ecosystem and now has a presence throughout the world.

Soitec has been a listed company (Euronext, Paris) since 1999. Its management team is headed by Pierre Barnabé. Its board of directors is supported by four committees (strategic, audit and risks, compensation, nomination and governance) and an internal control system managed by the finance division.

Creative Industry Košice is a non-profit organization founded in 2008 by the city of Košice which deals with the support and development of culture and creative industry (CCI).
We closely collaborate with the city of Košice on strategic documents such as master plans, cultural strategy plans, and economical and social document development plans.
In 2020 CIKE, a project partner of Košice 2.0, established Citizen Experience and Well-being Institute (CXI) as one of its departments. The institute collects, analyzes, and processes data on the quality of life of city residents and their experience with public spaces and services. Based on research, it prepares recommendations for solving urban problems, creating new policies, and further developing the city. It is interested in current research and good practice of cities worldwide and investigates new methods and ways of processing information about the urban environment. Our team consists of data analysts, architects, service designers, and graphics.
CIKE's mission is to increase the quality of life in the city by developing its creative potential. We search for and support talents and provide educational, networking, and employment opportunities, thus contributing to sustainable urban development. Collaboration and data-driven decision-making based on a creative approach bring the best solutions.

Decent Cybersecurity s.r.o. is specialised in designing, implementing, securing and testing the highest security standard blockchain infrastructure. Applying basic types of attacks to real world cases our solution can help our customers secure: supply chain attacks, physical attacks - infrastructure tampering, computer network exploitation, cloud infrastructure multi tenancy and operation, data corruption or modification and also  software and hardware vulnerabilities.

Services offered:
Private Blockchain
- Customised Integration: Private blockchains running on DCore protocol can be flexibly customiszed for individual use cases to meet highest security and performance standards.
- Cloud Hosting or Dedicated Servers: With automated implementation, it’s possible to efficiently deploy infrastructure on AWS/Azure or dedicated infrastructure.

Blockchain & Log Security
- Proving the Integrity and Authenticity of Log Files: Log files are a means to precisely govern all activities in an IT-heavy business. Logs can, however, be manipulated with, if not protected appropriately. Blockchain makes sure your infrastructure logs are free from manipulation and exploits.
-Proving the Integrity of Configuration Files: Using a decentralised system is a guarantee for your configuration files to stay exploit-free inside your infrastructure

Blockchain& IoT
-Top-Notch Security for IoT Devices: Considering the interrelated manner of IoT devices, employing superior security standards is not only essential but critical. By integrating blockchain technology, the number of attacks on IoT devices can be reduced to negligible amounts
-Protecting Smart Homes: In today’s world of what seems to be an uprising of “smart” systems, building a smart home has become easier than ever before—there is a catch, however: privacy compromises. Blockchain & SCADA

- An Extra Layer of Security: With its intrinsic security-focused nature, blockchain can be implemented to existing infrastructures as an additional security layer.
- Hardware & Software Fusion: Our solutions easily combine software and hardware integrations toward absolute efficiency and security.

entityDescription: The start-up will develop and engineer the innovative liquid-propellant atmospheric and orbital propulsion systems for subsequent commercial exploitation in the customized and market-driven space transportation services.Therocket engine on non-toxic " green" fuel components(H2O2 and ethanol)is intended to be flight-tested in 2024-25, enabling the launch of its serial production in 2025. The engine is developed as an essential element of space transportation systems, enabling spacecrafts' orbital delivery and orbital maneuvers. Our propulsion system would solve at least several challenges in the access to the Low Earth Orbit for microsatellite-type payloads and the provision of in-orbit services: (1) expensive launches with light launch vehicles, and (2) lack of efficient and reliable propulsion systems for on-orbit maneuvers.The universal propulsion system is designed for multiple use as a main engine in newly developed launch vehicles, and/or as a steering engine of orbiters. Theengine’s thrust will meet the demand of the (ultra)light rocket launcher developers and LEO transportation services providers, while designed with a view to the global trends of abandoning hydrocarbons and shifting to hydrogen fuel.

MISSION:I-ENERGYLINK’s is accelerating clean energy by supporting innovative solutions that most effectively increase energy efficiency, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, consolidate the regulatory framework and improve overall power systems reliability. EXPERIENCE: I-ENERGYLINK is built on the experience of over 30 years in the electricity industry in electricity T&D&G Projects and Studies, as well as Regulation, Policy and Innovation Solutions. Cybersecurity solutions and Digitalisation of the power sector are part of our experience and priorities. We deliver high-quality research and innovation solutions, as well as original analysis to energy stakeholders and policymakers to help them make informed choices on energy related projects, solutions, and policy. Electricity Transmission: Professional working experience with European Network of Transmission System Operators-ENTSO-E and Mediterranean TSOs –Med-TSO, on System Operations, Project’s implementation in Electricity Transmission Grid, SCADA systems, Protections and Automations. Working close to the Agency for the Cooperation of Energy Regulators (ACER) and the National Regulatory Authorities, in the field of the Internal Electricity Market. Managing several Network and System Development Projects for the preparation of the Ten-Year Networks Development Plan – TYNDP, HV electricity infrastructure, Smart Grids, Network Codes, Electricity Highways. Strong impact on Electricity Interconnections and on harmonisation the regulatory framework in the Mediterranean Region. Experience with DSOs on leading strategic, financial and technical analysis, defining and implementing DSO strategy. Working with major European DSOs. Focusing on investments & Smart Grids, RES & DG integration to the Electricity Distribution Grid.

All project cycle management: studies, design, tenders, defining and supervision of the execution of the Work Plan for Project investments. Implementing Wind and PV Plant generation and operation with innovative cyber-security solutions.

CLOUDWATER Ltd is a Research & Development startup SME company focusing on low-cost GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) receiver development established in 2021 at Nicosia, the capital city of Cyprus. CLOUDWATER also conducts high-level research on GNSS receiver’s software and hardware development, as well as on GNSS Meteorology, Geodesy and Positioning, Atmospheric Remote Sensing and Weather Prediction. The company designs and develops an innovative, customized low-cost GNSS receiver unit, particularly for the estimation of Precipitable Water Vapour (PWV) in Earth’s atmosphere. Our PREcipitable WAter vapour Monitor, PREWAM, is a unique product based on the novel concept of low-cost near-real time monitoring of PWV over an area, by exploiting all available GNSS systems (GPS, GALILEO, GLONASS and BeiDou). 
Website: https://cloudwater.com.cy

description:
DYCSYT (DYnamics and Control of SYstems – Tools) is a spin-off of ISAE-Supaero, which develops and distributes the SDTlib (Satellite Dynamics Toolbox – Library), a software dedicated to the modeling of flexible space systems and aimed at improving their GNC/AOCS design, with a unique expertise in:
* flexible dynamics,
* parametric uncertainties,
* mechanisms and vibrations.
 The SDTlib was initially developed in an academic context through published studies, in partnership with ESA, CNES, ONERA, and industrial partners, for applications such as vibrations isolation, control/structure co-design, in-orbit servicing, high-accuracy pointing missions, characterization of vibration anomaly observed in flight…
 Through a subscription service, our objective is to maintain a state-of-the-art, fully documented modeling tool in line with the industrial needs, along with services based on our expertise in this field.
entityDescription:
DyCSyT (DYnamics and Control of SYstems - Tools) conducts research and development in the modeling and control of microvibrations in space systems. It aims to provide numerical tools to satellite constructors to improve their GNC design, particularly for missions with stringent performance requirements, by bridging the gap between mature academic research and industrial applications.

The main activity of DyCSyT is the development of the SDTlib (Satellite Dynamics Toolbox - Library), the result of 15 years of academic research at ISAE-Supaero. The SDTlib allows the control engineer to easily assemble the model of complex space systems in a multi-body framework ; it has the unique advantage of providing a fully parameterized model, based on the LFT (Linear Fractional Transformation) formalism, to take into account uncertain or time-varying parameters and enable advanced tools to perform robust analysis and control.

The SDTlib, along with these advanced model- and optimization-based tools:
- reduces the tedious iterations in the design process - by providing a precise performance prediction early in the design process, taking into account the robustness as well as all performance constraints as of the controller synthesis, or again optimizing the structure simultaneously with the controller ;
- improves the performance - e.g. in terms of pointing precision, actuator's solicitation, or minimization of the satellite's mass.

Company description: DyCSyT (DYnamics and Control of SYstems - Tools) conducts research and development in the modeling and control of microvibrations in space systems. It aims to provide numerical tools to satellite constructors to improve their GNC design, particularly for missions with stringent performance requirements, by bridging the gap between mature academic research and industrial applications.

The main activity of DyCSyT is the development of the SDTlib (Satellite Dynamics Toolbox - Library), the result of 15 years of academic research at ISAE-Supaero. The SDTlib allows the control engineer to easily assemble the model of complex space systems in a multi-body framework ; it has the unique advantage of providing a fully parameterized model, based on the LFT (Linear Fractional Transformation) formalism, to take into account uncertain or time-varying parameters and enable advanced tools to perform robust analysis and control.

The SDTlib, along with these advanced model- and optimization-based tools:
- reduces the tedious iterations in the design process - by providing a precise performance prediction early in the design process, taking into account the robustness as well as all performance constraints as of the controller synthesis, or again optimizing the structure simultaneously with the controller ;
- improves the performance - e.g. in terms of pointing precision, actuator's solicitation, or minimization of the satellite's mass.

In an academic context, the SDTlib has allowed to tackle various problematics such as: disturbance rejection for fine line-of-sight pointing control, modeling of harmonic microvibrations caused by reaction wheels or solar array driving mechanism, control/structure co-design of large flexible structures, or on-orbit servicing. DyCSyT is committed to making this technology available for practical engineering applications and to continuing its development to meet the industry's needs.

entityName: IRCCS - Fondazione del Piemonte per l'Oncologia
entityDescription:
The Istituto di Candiolo IRCCS is a specialist centre for the treatment of oncological conditions, for a number of which, indeed, it figures as an international benchmark, and is part of theOncological Network of Piedmont-Aosta Valley.
It is the first Research Institute of Admission and Care in Piedmont to be recognized by the Ministry of Health.
For the number of cases treated and the quality of its clinical profiles, the Institute is recognized for its excellent standards in the following areas:
- diagnosis and therapy of cancers of the breast and of the ovaries;
- ​diagnosis and therapy of gastrointestinal and hepatobiliary tumours;
- diagnosis and therapy of onco-haematological diseases;
- diagnosis and therapy of sarcomas and rare tumours;
- diagnosis and therapy of skin cancers;
- diagnosis and therapy of cervicocephalic (ORL) tumours.
The Institute's specialists have at their disposal new Operating Theatres, isolation rooms with controlled microclimate for immuno-suppressed patients, innovative pharmocological protocols (also in the area of innovative “targeted therapy”), of sophisticated apparatus in the field of medical imaging (Computerized Axial Tomography, Positron Emission Tomography, Nuclear Magnetic Resonance, Scintigraphy) and of radiotherapy (the Institute is one of the few European facilities which can boast two Tomotherapy systems).
At the Istituto di Candiolo it is possible to benefit from out-patient care (specialist consultations, diagnostic tests, instrumental surgery):

Multidisciplinary Programmes
At the Candiolo Institute there are a number of specialized multidisciplinary programmes for the diagnosis and treatment of oncological diseases.
The multidisciplinary teams of the Institute make use of specialists with consolidated experience and expertise in: pathological anatomy, pancreatic and colo-rectal hepatobiliary surgery, maxillofacial surgery, oncological surgery, plastic-reconstructive surgery, dermatosurgery, endocrinology, oncological gynecology, nuclear medicine, nutrition , odontostomatology, medical oncology, orthopedics, otolaryngology, psychology, radiodiagnostics, surgical radiology, radiation therapy
Integration of the various competencies makes it possible to tackle the complex problems of oncological diseases, from diagnosis to the planning of therapies to follow-up strategies, to achieving the best clinical results combined with the safeguard of quality of life standards.
It is possible to access the following diagnosis and treatment programmes:
- Pancreatic and Colorectal Hepatobiliary Surgery Programme
- Diagnostic and Surgical Digestive Endoscopy Programme
- Ovarian Carcinoma Programme
- Sarcomas and Rare Tumours Programme
- Stem Cell Transplantation Programme

entityDescription:
Newton Launch Systems was established in 2011 to investigate the feasibility of the UK developing its own small satellite launcher in response to the growth in the small satellite market. In March 2012 it organised and chaired a workshop hosted by the UK Space Agency to bring together key industry players and address the UK's strategic priorities in line with the recommendations from the Space Innovation and Growth Strategy report and access to space roadmaps. This led to the Space-CITI 'Small launcher' study in which Newton partnered with SSTL, Reaction Engines and London Economics to address the technical and commercial feasibility for a UK-based launcher in greater detail. This study concluded that there was indeed a market for a UK small satellite launcher, but the trading conditions were likely to be difficult with fewer than half a dozen launches per annum forecast. Furthermore, since costs do not scale linearly with vehicle size, significant innovation would be needed to reduce development, production and operations costs to a point where private investment could be sought.

Over the past 5 years Newton has focused on its technology development programme in parallel with its on-going market study activity. Current technical activity is centred on the propulsion system, including the development of an innovative hybrid-electric turbopump and a low-cost bi-propellant engine. To support the technology programme, Newton is developing a test and evaluation facility at Spaceport Snowdonia in Llanbedr, Gwynedd, including a test stand for static firing of rocket motors, a thermal vacuum chamber and a launch rail for flying small scale boost glider vehicles. In addition to undertaking its own test programme, Newton intends to offer testing services to other SMEs and universities on a commercial basis. 

Over the next 5 years, Newton will continue to follow an incremental development programme, whereby steady progress can be made towards the ultimate goal on a component and sub-system level, while seeking to exploit this technology as a short-term revenue stream. In the immediate future, the focus will be on testing and consultancy, including advice on R&D tax credits and software services to other SMEs, in addition to testing services at Spaceport Snowdonia. In the medium term, Newton will seek to earn revenue directly from the sale or licensing of its technology, such as the upper stage bi-propellant rocket engine currently under development.

Newton believes that it is in the national interest for the UK to develop its own launcher technology rather than relying on imported vehicles, systems and components. Not only does this approach provide security of supply but it also encourages the development of key engineering skills. In this respect, Newton is proud to support Aspirespace in its quest to develop a new generation of aerospace engineers and looks forward to working with its partners at Spaceport Snowdonia in order to ensure that the regional and national economic benefits from the venture are maximised.

In March 2012 it organised and chaired a workshop hosted by the UK Space Agency to bring together key industry players and address the UK's strategic priorities in line with the recommendations from the Space Innovation and Growth Strategy report and access to space roadmaps. This led to the Space-CITI 'Small launcher' study in which Newton partnered with SSTL, Reaction Engines and London Economics to address the technical and commercial feasibility for a UK-based launcher in greater detail. This study concluded that there was indeed a market for a UK small satellite launcher, but the trading conditions were likely to be difficult with fewer than half a dozen launches per annum forecast. Furthermore, since costs do not scale linearly with vehicle size, significant innovation would be needed to reduce development, production and operations costs to a point where private investment could be sought.

Over the past 5 years Newton has focused on its technology development programme in parallel with its on-going market study activity. Current technical activity is centred on the propulsion system, including the development of an innovative hybrid-electric turbopump and a low-cost bi-propellant engine. To support the technology programme, Newton is developing a test and evaluation facility at Spaceport Snowdonia in Llanbedr, Gwynedd, including a test stand for static firing of rocket motors, a thermal vacuum chamber and a launch rail for flying small scale boost glider vehicles. In addition to undertaking its own test programme, Newton intends to offer testing services to other SMEs and universities on a commercial basis. 

Over the next 5 years, Newton will continue to follow an incremental development programme, whereby steady progress can be made towards the ultimate goal on a component and sub-system level, while seeking to exploit this technology as a short-term revenue stream. In the immediate future, the focus will be on testing and consultancy, including advice on R&D tax credits and software services to other SMEs, in addition to testing services at Spaceport Snowdonia. In the medium term, Newton will seek to earn revenue directly from the sale or licensing of its technology, such as the upper stage bi-propellant rocket engine currently under development.

Newton believes that it is in the national interest for the UK to develop its own launcher technology rather than relying on imported vehicles, systems and components. Not only does this approach provide security of supply but it also encourages the development of key engineering skills. In this respect, Newton is proud to support Aspirespace in its quest to develop a new generation of aerospace engineers and looks forward to working with its partners at Spaceport Snowdonia in order to ensure that the regional and national economic benefits from the venture are maximised.

entityName: DLR - INSTITUTE FOR THE PROTECTION OF TERRESTRIAL INFRASTRUCTES (DLR PI AN)
entityDescription:
The Institute for the Protection of Terrestrial Infrastructures (PI) has been dedicated since its foundation in 2019 to theprotection and security of critical infrastructures on earth. We develop concepts, processes and technologies that strengthen and improve the resilience of organisations and systems. In this, we focus on people, technology and the system as a whole.
Modern societies depend on the unrestricted availability of their critical infrastructures. Protecting them from dangers is essential for prosperity and social stability.Critical infrastructuresare, for example, water and energy supply, rail and air transport, hospitals, public authorities, fire brigade and disaster control facilities or hazardous materials storage facilities. In that sense, infrastructures are systems, processes and resources that in their entirety provide for the supply of society.
Crime, terrorist attacks and the effects of natural disasters and pandemics as well as cybercrime arereal dangersthat threaten the security of societies. The more complex and interconnected societies and their infrastructures are, the more vulnerable they are to threats. As a key tool for responding to threats and improving the resilience of infrastructures, we apply theconcept of the Digital Twin.
Digital twins represent the closest possiblereplication of a real system. The virtual image is continuously updated by comparing it with real-time data. Based on this time-accurate virtual image, a variety ofanalyses and forecastson the behaviour of the real system can be carried out and visualised. In this way, all parties involved can gain a deeper understanding of the respective infrastructure and initiate the influencing of the real system with the help of suitableactuators or decisions.
In order to detect imminent dangers at an early stage,intelligent sensors are far superior to human senses in certain situations. We develop sensor technologies for different purposes and create methods for evaluating sensor observations.
Using methods of prediction, simulation of scenarios, operational resilience management and decision support, operators and emergency forces are supported in the best possible way to get ahead of the situation, i.e. to anticipate the negative development of the situation.
In our view, the concept of the Digital Twin is the key to realising a resilience cycle. This enables us to assess and continuously improve the resilience of the infrastructure under consideration in almost any situation:
- By continuously monitoring the infrastructures, disruptions and triggers of cascading effects can already be detected as soon as a crisis situation occurs and operational measures to protect the infrastructurecan be initiated.
- During a crisis, the concept of the Digital Twin of the real infrastructure allows us to understand the situation and adapt to the dangers and threats.
- After a crisis, we can use the data and models to simulate threats and impacts on the threatened systems.
- Based on these findings, we analyse the trajectories and can derive the necessary optimisation of the infrastructure.

The Mediterranean Aerospace Company S.c.r.l. (www.samaerospazio.it), which represents the first Italian reality of aggregation of SMEs in the aerospace sector, was established in 1998 in order to respond to the need to adapt to market needs and for greater development opportunities both at a regional and national and international. entityDescription: PASI is a startup company whose main objective is the democratization of expertise and education in the field of human spaceflight. PASI provides human spaceflight consulting services to public, private, and defense organizations through specialized consultants. Personnel involved in the proposed study: Laura André-Boyet has 16 years of experience in the Human Spaceflight industry. She worked for Medes as a Space Physiology Experiment Manager at the Centre National d'Etudes Spatiales (National Center for Space Studies, CNES) in Toulouse, France. She works in the training division of the European Astronaut Center (EAC) in Cologne, Germany, as an Astronaut Instructor and Simulations Director at the service of the European Space Agency (ESA). In 2018, she founded the Professional Association of Space Instructors® (PASI), where she works as a parabolic flight instructor and as a human spaceflight expert consultant for public, private, and defense organizations. She regularly participates in many collaborative research projects, mainly focused on physiology in extreme environments and space analogues.Finally, within the framework of national defence, she graduated in 2022 from the Cycle d'Etudes Stratégiques de la Marine and joined the operational reserve of the French Air Force the same year as a Lieutenant-Colonel expert in space operations.

entityDescription: HyImpulse is a New-Space start-up based in Hardthausen, Germany. We are developing a mini launcher using disruptive technologies to provide low-cost small-sat launch opportunities for Europe and the whole world. HyImpulse was founded by 5 DLR employees with excellent experience in chemical and hybrid rocket propulsion as well as a good network in the international space industry. We are sure that disruptive technologies and ways of thinking can lower the cost of orbital launches and at the same time increase flexibility for our customers. These disruptions include in the first place inherently safe hybrid rocket propulsion systems with advanced paraffin-based fuels. Our launcher therefore will use "green propulsion"​ without toxicity and environmental harms. Other important disruptive technologies include COTS components for avionics, state of the art production technology for light weight composite structures, 3D printing of various parts, and decreasing cost by serial production. For example, our main engine will be used several times on the launcher. Our first product in development is a single stage sounding rocket using a hybrid rocket engine to deliver institutional and commercial experiments into a micro gravity environment during a suborbital flight. Based on that technology demonstrator, a mini launcher with a target payload of 400 kg into a Low Earth Orbit will be developed.

entityDescription:
Ikkaido is an NGO with Special Consultative Status to the United Nations, working in the field of diversity and inclusion for youth, women and girls and all persons with fewer opportunities, especially persons with a disability in sport, education, empowerment, employment and entrepreneurship.
 
A Registered Charity, Ikkaido is a signature to the Marseilles Declaration on Inclusion and the Geneva Convention 190 for the elimination of violence and harassment in the world of work, with an additional focus on domestic violence and gender-based violence against women.
 
Based in the multi-cultural City of Oxford, Ikkaido works with disadvantaged communities; NEETs, and young people with fewer opportunities, especially those with a disability and mental health issues, to help them tackle their issues and motivate them towards taking steps towards better health, recovery and engagement in the community. Ikkaido has grown participation in sport and physical activity for over 7500 disabled and disadvantaged young people. Most of the participants are NEET receiving some form of benefit support. The main centre of operation is in Stoke Mandeville Stadium; the birthplace of the Paralympics with resultant connections and working relationships with Paralympic, Olympic and Special Olympic federations all around the world.
 
Ikkaido is a Recognised VET Centre of Education and is regulated by OFQUAL. They are experts in inclusion and the development, writing and delivery of accredited inclusive qualifications.Ikkaido builds qualifications with inclusion theory at the core, allowing any participant to achieve. Ikkaido has established inclusive qualifications at levels 1 through 6 in the field of coaching and education for youth with fewer opportunities, youth workers, coaches, teaching assistants and teachers nationally, in Europe and internationally. Elearning and blended learning are used and reinforced by non-formal learning.
 
Ikkaido has MoUs with many martial arts federations and associations around the world to create Ikkaido Inclusive Festivals of Martial Arts providing participation for persons with a disability.
 
Ikkaido has provided keynote addresses on inclusion including in both Japan and Korea at the World Congress of The Association For International Sport for All (TAFISA), the World Festival of Martial Arts in Russia, the World Martial Arts Games in London, the World Kickboxing Championship in Germany, the Fudokan World Championships and the International Conference of Inclusive Sport in Portugal.
 
The Ikkaido board is inclusive and contains 80% disabled and 20% non-disabled people and maintains gender balance. All Ikkaido staff are persons with disabilities and fewer opportunities.
 
Learning from over 25 Erasmus+ projects as Coordinator and several as a partner organisation, Ikkaido has enhanced their knowledge in sport, tutoring, assessing, mentoring and coaching and improved their competences in the fields of empowering youth through physical activity, non-formal education, entrepreneurship, employment, intercultural learning, communication, information technology and social media. Additionally, Ikkaido has grown its structure and improved project and financial management skills.
 
Ikkaido has a core team of seven full-time employees, and part-time, ten coaches, five tutors, two assessors, four IQAs and four teachers delivering coaching, education and creating inclusive tools to integrate and empower people with fewer opportunities.

entityName: Technische Hochschule Nürnberg Georg Simon Ohm
entityDescription:
Nuremberg Institute of Technology, or Nuremberg Tech for short, is one of Germany’s largest universities,with over 13,000 students.
The university is a corporation under public law with the right to self-govern within the framework of legislation, while also being a State institution. In accordance with Article 2 of the Bavarian State Universities Act, the universities for applied sciences provide application-based teaching in order to deliver education that enables students to apply scientific methods and use creative activities independently in professional practice. Within the scope of the existing infrastructure, universities of applied sciences are able to undertakeapplication-oriented research and development projects, if predominantly third-party funding is available.

The university’s roots (history) can be traced back to the year 1823 and the founding of the Städtische Polytechnikum (Municipal Polytechnic) – the oldest of our forerunners. The university is named after the world-renowned physicist, Georg Simon Ohm (biography), who was a physics and mathematics professor in Nuremberg between 1833 and 1849, and also fulfilled the role of rector. 
Innovative technological developments shape our living environment today and will do so tomorrow. A systematic transfer of research outcomes strengthens the innovative ability of small and medium-sized enterprises. As one of Germany’s universities with the largest amount of third-party funding, Nuremberg Tech exerts an important influence on structural policy within the Nuremberg Metropolitan Region. 
The aim is to continue developing this collaboration with regional, national, and international partners. Together, the engineering Faculties at Nuremberg Tech operate over 150 laboratories, which represent a high degree of innovative potential to find solutions to the key issues facing our society and our business sector.

entityDescription:
Switzerland Innovation Park Biel/Bienne (SIPBB) is a private Swiss non-profit organization that performs and supports industry-focused applied research and development. As part of the national and international network of the Switzerland Innovation Foundation, SIPBB want to generate research investments from abroad, promote Swiss innovation and startups and implement research results quickly into marketable products.
SIPBB is active in 4 R&D field:
1- The Swiss Advanced Manufacturing Center (SAMC) operates several labs for research in optics, lasers and processes for additive manufacturing (AM) processes. Because not only process but also research chain of AM cover a broad range of competences, the SAMC focuses on its core competences like optics, process and integration. Along the AM process chain the SAMC maintains a strong network of interaction with research facilities complementing its own activities, resulting in a strong and leading competence network.
2- The Swiss Smart Factory (SSF) internationally recognized center of competence in application-oriented research and transfer of Industry 4.0. Swiss Smart Factory has established itself as the first test and demonstration platform for Industry 4.0 in Switzerland.
3- The Swiss Medtech Center (SMTC) is a meeting place for research, medicine and industry to work on interdisciplinary innovative projects in the fields of medtech and health-tech. 
4- The Swiss Battery Technology Center (SBTC) collaborates with well-known Swiss research partners, such as ETH, EMPA, PSI, CSEM, the Bern University of Applied Sciences (BFH), and more, in order to translate the latest technologies into market-ready batteries

As a national geological, geophysical and meteorological service, GeoSphere Austria makes an important contribution to increasing the overall national resilience and crisis resistance and contributes to the precautionary approach to climate change, its consequences and the sustainable development of Austria. 
GeoSphere Austria employs around 500 people. Locations are in Vienna at Hohe Warte and Neulinggasse as well as in Linz, Salzburg, Innsbruck, Graz and Klagenfurt. GeoSphere Austria also operates the Sonnblick Observatory in Salzburg and the Conrad Observatory near Pernitz and a geophysical test site near Melk in Lower Austria.

entityDescription:
Arsakeio(Αρσάκειο) is the general name of theArsakeia – Tositseia Schools, a group of co-ed private schools in Greece, administered by the Philekpedeftiki Etería (Φιλεκπαιδευτική Εταιρεία,Society for Promoting Education and Learning[SPEL]), which is a non-profit educational organization. The Arsakeio comprises six schools, with campuses in Psychiko [Attica], Ekali (Tosítseio campus) [Attica], Thessaloniki, Patras, Ioannina, and also Tirana, Albania. The school has more than 6.500 students and 700 educators.

Arsakeio has several Departments and Services. The pedagogical system and the curricula are supervised by the Supervisor (Επόπτης) aided by a board of Coordinators. Each Coordinator overviews and guides the educators of a set of subjects (i.e. languages, physics, maths, informatics, etc.). There are three FL departments (English, French, German). The Counseling Services (psychologists and career counselors) have offices on all campuses and run relevant programs. The Cultural Programs Service organizes various cultural events, educational programs and guided tours to museums and archaeological sites for the students. In Arsakeio there are a Junior Achievement - Young Enterprise Europe Group, and active groups of robotics, STEM, and F1 in Schools. The Arsakeio digital Program Department runs and supports the digital school e-arsakeioTM. Arsakeia schools at Patra organize yearly a MUN conference (ATS MUN). The Supervisor and her assisting board organize every year a two-day student conference, Arts and Letters Contests, day-conferences and competitions on Mathematics and Physics, meanwhile the Arsakeio's students participate in various European programs (Erasmus+, Forensics, European Youth Parliament, etc.) and in national and international competitions (F1 in Schools, MUNs, Olympiads of Physics and Mathematics).

Arsakeio is the biggest educational organization in Greece. The administrative board consists of 11 eminent persons of the Greek society. Since 1988, president of the board is Georgios Babiniotis, emeritus Professor of linguistics, ex dean of the University of Athens, and ex-Minister of Education. Under his administration two new schools in Ioannina and Tirana (Albania) were founded, as well as a new modern campus in Patra, and the “The Book's Archway” (Στοά του Βιβλίου) in the premises of the original Arsakeio building downtown Athens, where many bookstores are hosted in the area of the old arcade. The Book’s Archway has become a very active institution which hosts cultural events and facilitates the “Free University”, a lifelong learning institution. In 2013 G. Babiniotis and Professor Gregory Nagy, Francis Jones Professor of Classical Greek Literature and Professor of Comparative Literature, Harvard University and director of Center for Hellenic Studies-Harvard University, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for close collaboration of Philekpaideftiki Etaireia and CHS-Harvard (joint conferences, educational exchanges, etc.).

description:
Instituto Pedro Nunes (IPN) is a non-profit private organization which promotes innovation and the transfer of technology, establishing the interface between business and academia. Created in 1991 through an initiative of the University of Coimbra, IPN has currently a team of almost 100 permanent staff to support start-ups and researchers in these activities. IPN operates in three complementary areas: 
1. Incubation and acceleration of technology-based enterprises activities. IPN help start-ups with technical guidance in the establishment and early stages of business development, tutorial follow-up for developing business plans, support for attracting investment and securing funding, intellectual property and legal assistance (e.g. technology transfer contracts and the registration of patents or trademarks), access to and contact with various national and international research centres, knowledge institutions and sources of funding. 
2. Research and technological development. IPN’s technological infrastructure includes a set of six laboratories in diversified technological areas which, along with its established connections with higher education institutions, R&TD organisations and both national and international companies, place IPN in a privileged position for jointly conducting R&TD activities with enterprises. IPN is thus able to provide multidisciplinary support for product creation and innovative processes within an entrepreneurial environment. This includes technological development, access to sources of funding and assistance with intellectual property queries and entry to international markets.
 3. Highly specialized training.

Since 2014, Instituto Pedro Nunes leads the first European Space Solutions Centre, among the other 21 ESA centers across Europe, hosting within the same entity the three areas promoting downstream businesses: ESA Business Incubation Centre, ESA Technology Brokers and ESA Business Applications Ambassadors Platform (AP). ESA Space Solutions Portugal has the support of ESA - European Space Agency, Portugal Space - Portuguese Space Agency and ANACOM, along with a wide range of stakeholders such as incubators, universities and regional authorities, amongst others.
entityDescription:
Instituto Pedro Nunes - Association for Innovation and R&D in Science and Technology is a non-profit private organization founded in 1991. IPN promotes innovation and technology transfer, being the main link between the University of Coimbra and the business sector. IPN work is made trough RTD in partnership with enterprises; specialized training; dissemination of scientific and technological knowledge and support to start-up tech companies. 
IPN has its own technological infrastructures of seven laboratories, besides accessing a network of researchers in the scientific and technological system, particularly from the University of Coimbra, mainly through the Faculty of Sciences and Technology. IPN Laboratories are: LAS - Laboratory of Automation and Systems; LEC - Laboratory of Electroanalysis and Corrosion; LED&MAT - Laboratory of Wear, Testing and Materials; LIS - Laboratory of Informatics and Systems; LABGEO; POLYMERS and FITOLAB. IPN promotes the creation of spin-off companies by giving support to innovative and technology-based ideas generated by its own laboratories, the private sector and other scientific institutions, particularly the University of Coimbra. Beside these infrastructures, also IPN possesses an Industrial Property Promotion Unit, and belongs to several national and international networks, including EBN, TII, EARTO and Proton.

entityName: FiberSight - Smart Sensing Solutions, Unipessoal Lda
entityDescription:
FiberSight is a CERN spin-off that was created with the hope of being the main vehicle for the transfer of distributed fibre optic sensors know-how from CERN’s infrastructure division to the market at large scale.
FiberSight was founded in August of 2021 and our core business is the development of intelligent solutions for monitoring environmental parameters of temperature and humidity, using state-of-the-art technology based on standard telecommunication lasers, optical amplifiers, and optical fibres. FiberLoop is our first project and is the first highly sensitive distributed thermo-hygrometer sensor with kilometres of sensing length. FiberLoop technology relies on a photonic device that launches several light pulses into the optical fibre and measures the Rayleigh backscattering signal that is generated during the pulse propagation. The fast analysis of the pulses received makes it possible to distinguish all positions along the optical fibre with an accuracy of less than 1 metre. The software analyses the changes in all fibre positions and converts the backscattering signal into two measurands at the same time: temperature and humidity/moisture. The optical fibre cable withstands harsh environments and can be buried in the soil, embedded in concrete, or installed in high radiation environments.

entityDescription:
Advanced Drivetrain Technologies GmbH is a service provider for drivetrain R&D in the mobility sector focused on new zero- or low-emission drivetrains. We are working together with our customers to develop high quality drivetrains with lowest possible environmental impact and maximum end user satisfaction. 
Our detailed knowledge in gear design and development enables us to find the best suitable solution in terms of gear quality, tolerances and modifications considering the characteristics of shafts, bearings, housing and application. 

Innovation: Leading or being partner in European or international projects gives us the chance to improve our knowledge and to go beyond the state of the art. New ideas can be elaborated and validated and then transferred to development projects with our customer.

Collaboration: We have a partnership with one of the world’s leading gear calculation software developers. Testing pre-launch software development as well as performing trainings for the users of the software is our daily business. Furthermore, we have a good network in the aviation and drivetrain R&D society. 

Protection: We consider impacts of new technologies on society and environment already in the design process. For us, a successful solution means to satisfy the customers‘ needs and to contribute to the protection of the environment.

High efficiency, low noise and less mass are key enablers for new and powerful technologies in drivetrains and transmission systems. We offer our engineering in the mobility sector - beginning in drivetrains for e-bikes via transmissions for cars and trucks up to new propulsion solutions for planes and helicopters. The focus is on R&D up to TRL 6.

Aarhus is the second largest city of Denmark, with a population of more than 336,000 inhabitants. It is the centre of "Greater Aarhus", which has a population of approx. 1.2 million people. Aarhus Municipality has approx. 30,000 employees.

Being a part of the 100 cn&sc-mission and the European Digital Innovation Hub, the municipality is committed to ensuring safety, sustainability and support for good living conditions for each individual citizen while at the same time focusing on cost-effective, innovative and ‘smart’ ways of delivering its services to citizens, e.g. urban development and maintenance. Furthermore, Aarhus is very active in relation to smart city initiatives and sees technologies such as IoT, robotics, AI, lidar and digital twins as enablers for creating a good and living city in the future with quality but cost-effective public services. Specifically, Aarhus sees potential in exploiting experiences and results from the project in relation to creating a more “smart”, digitalized and automatized handling of the urban maintenance within the city. Aarhus has already digitalized a large number of citizen services and therefore, already has over 200 digital citizen services in operation. Therefore, Aarhus is already the most “digital” city in Scandinavia.

In the recent decade, Aarhus has achieved several milestones as an international knowledge Centre: A great number of international businesses have decided to establish themselves or expand their activities in Aarhus; Aarhus University ranks among the top 100 of the world’s 17,000 universities, and more and more international employees, researchers and students are coming to Aarhus.

entityName: Technical University of Košice - Faculty of mining, ecology, proces control and geotechnologies
entityDescription: The Faculty of Mining, Ecology, Process Control and Geotechnologies historically refers to the Mining Academy in Banská Štiavnica, promoted to the academic level by Maria Theresa, queen of Hungary and Bohemia, in 1762. This institution, probably the first university of its kind in the world, is the basis to which our faculty and university proudly avows. In this context, it is necessary to perceive our faculty as an institution which proudly holds a significant position within mining academies in Europe. As one of the three founding faculties, the Faculty of Mining, Ecology, Process Control and Geotechnologies (Mining Faculty in that time), was involved in the establishment and formation of the Technical University of Košice. The university has adopted part of rich and estimable mining and academic traditions that are internationally accepted via “Declaration of Spiritual Heritage Successors of the Mining Academy in Banská Štiavnica”. On this deep and strong basis, our faculty provides education in traditional mining disciplines, including geology; mining; mineralurgy and environmental technologies; technologies in fuel and gas industry; mining mechanization, transport and deep drilling. Attending to growing society needs for the knowledge economy development, the faculty also provides education in attractive and requested study programmes covering economy of Earth resources; geodesy and geographical information systems; geotourism and mining tourism, informatization and process control; industrial logistics; and rescue, fire and safety techniques. The faculty has balanced team composed of pedagogical, science & research and administrative staff, ensuring that students acquire all the necessary knowledge integrating them into the technical intelligence society. I believe that, besides obligations that university study requires, students of our faculty will spend here one of the most beautiful phases of their lives and reach one of their lifetime goals and successes.

entityDescription: Today, NaviBlind ApS sells a navigational aid for blind and visually impaired people. The aid is called NaviBlind and comprises an app and a wearable GNSS accessory which connects to the app. NaviBlind enables blind and visually impaired people to walk to new destinations on their own, without prior training. Using the product, a blind person can, e.g., independently walk to a store, a job interview, or an event. Our customers are public entities, such as The City of Aarhus, and blind and visually impaired citizens. To guide blind people, extreme positional accuracy is required. Maps and GPSs on smartphones cannot provide this extreme accuracy, and NaviBlind therefore includes precise mapping of routes and an external GNSS device that delivers better than 0.5 meters accuracy. The routes that users follow are mapped using our own software applications. There are no similar services on the market, and we have experienced great interest in our technology. We believe that the precise mapping and positioning technology that we have developed for NaviBlind has the potential to be used in other industries, e.g. rental of electric scooters.

Helix Space provides three services to companies using SpaceTech: 
1. Soft Funding: Helix Space helps Luxembourgish start-ups and SMEs, or foreign ones that wish to set-up offices in Luxembourg, obtain Soft Funding through national (e.g., Luxembourg Space Agency, Belgian Space Office), or intergovernmental (e.g., European Space Agency, European Union Space Agency) grants to develop their product or service. The tasks that Helix Space provides to its Soft Funding customers are: 
• Analyse and identify public grants or tenders that fit the customer’s requirements. 
• Create or guide the customer in the preparation of the Business Plan, Cost Sheets and Financial Model material required by the public procurement agency. 
• Review and determine if there are any gaps in the technical, legal and management material prepared by the customer’s team. 
• Assist the customer during the negotiation phase with the public procurement agency. 
2. Product/Market Fit: Helix Space works with you to make sure your product or service is Feasible, Desirable and Viable. We help and/or guide you through the following tasks: 
• Value proposition design 
• Market analysis and assessment 
• Competitive analysis 
• Business model 
• Go to market strategy 
• Product development roadmap 
• Implementation roadmap 
• Financial model, sensitivity analysis and scenarios. 
• Commercial risk analysis

• Structural calculations
• Energy calculations
• Design of technical installations
• Etc.
 
ICT, BIM and VDC
ICT stands for Information and Communication Technology. Within construction, ICT is the common denominator for all the digital tools and methods that are used to systemize and control the design and construction processes throughout all phases of a construction project.BIM stands for Building Information Modeling.BIM is the concept of modelling buildings in 3D and adding information to the individualbuilding parts which can be used throughout the entire lifecycle of the building.VDC stands for Virtual Design and Construction.
 
Digitalization consultancy in the construction industry
Digital tools and methods keep gaining greater ground in the construction industry. Every part of the industry can benefit from exploiting the digital opportunities to a greater extent. However, the possibilities are endless, and it can be very difficult to gain the complete overview.For many, it is a complex process to implement new digital tools and work methods while concurrently running a business.Therefore, it may be worthwhile to collaborate with a digitalization consultant who specializes in construction.Bygkontrol can help you map your specific needs and possibilities within digitalization and guide you through the implementation and use of the tools and methods that will make a difference to your construction company. 
 
VDC is a way of analyzing and simulating a construction workflow before the construction phase. It helps optimize the construction process and minimize mistakes.Bygkontrol can handle or assist all your ICT, BIM and VDC work including 3D laserscanning and softwaredevelopment.

description: DemandSide Instruments (DSI) is developing a unique end-to-end solution for farmers to better manage resource usage in agricultural fields. The solution is comprised of connected sensors deployed in plots, allowing farmers to procure a detailed and accurate analysis of the crops at any given moment. The farmer can track the sensors performance and manage them remotely through DSI’s mobile app- AliaTerra. The solution is currently deployed in an operational environment, and has over 100 active clients in Reunion Island and Normandie. The company offers an array of connected sensors, measuring various soil, air, and water parameters in cultivated plots. The data collected indicates the parcel’s irrigation, pesticides and fertilization needs, thus helping farmers manage their resources better. To connect the data from different sensors and process it, we utilize Edge computing technology- Each sensor functions as a node in the network, and information is transferred securely from the sensors in the field to a gateway bridge using LoRaWAN technology. The solar-powered bridge performs independent data analysis, and interacts with DSI’s cloud service (Dandelion) for further data processing. Analysis is done by Decision Support Tools (DSTs) integrating related data from different sensors to present a comprehensive analysis of the field. The DSTs are Machine Learning algorithms developed by DSI, learning data on different irrigation needs (depending on climate, type of crop, field size, etc.) and generate recommendations for the farmers on preferred irrigation schedules. The farmer (i.e., the end-user) interacts with the data, the sensors and the recommendations made by the DSTs via the company’s management application (AliaTerra). The app allows farmers to remote control irrigation, thus simplifying the work flow in the field. Moreover, the system reports any anomaly concerning the crops, which enables the farmer to get ahead of losses linked to frost, drought, leaks, etc. By utilizing DSI’s solution, water consumption and pesticide application can be significantly reduced while yield increases.

The medicalvalues GmbH is an innovative company based out of Karlsruhe, Germany. A team of IT-Engineers and medical experts is developing an AI-first software platform as a medical product.
With the medicalvalues platform we support the medical diagnosis process for diseases like anemia, diabetes and fat metabolic illnesses through a combination of research knowledge, clinical guidelines and machine learning based on historical doctor’s decisions. Our knowledge graph is being combined with multiple data sources from space e.g. location, weather conditions or regional nutrition etc.
The key differentiators of our platform are a combination of a decentral and central architecture allowing strict data protection and anonymization as well as cross-institutional knowledge sharing. In addition, we combine a validated knowledge graph with our machine learning technology to make our decision support system more accurate and explainable to the medical doctor.

The University of Basel has an international reputation of outstanding achievements in research and teaching. Founded in 1460, the University of Basel is the oldest university in Switzerland and has a history of success going back over 550 years.
As a comprehensive university offering a wide range of high-quality educational opportunities, the University of Basel attracts students from Switzerland and the entire world, offering them outstanding studying conditions as they work towards their bachelor’s, master’s or PhD degrees. Today, the University of Basel has around 13,000 students from over a hundred nations, including 2,900 PhD students.
The University of Basel has seven faculties covering a wide spectrum of academic disciplines. At the same time, the university has positioned itself amidst the international competition in the form of five strategic focal areas: Life Sciences, Visual Studies, Nanosciences, Sustainability and Energy Research and European and Global Studies. In international rankings, the University of Basel is regularly placed among the 100 top universities in the world thanks to its research achievements.
The University of Basel has deep roots in the economically powerful and culturally rich Basel region. The university also works closely with domestic and international partners to make relevant contributions to the advancement of the sciences and society. This also means that the University of Basel pays particular attention to aspects of sustainability, equal opportunity and knowledge transfer.

entityDescription:
DamoTech Srl is an innovative startup focalized on the development of innovative products and services with high technological value in the field of cyber security and ICT sectors. 

In particular, DamoTech innovative feature is represented by the methodology applied at development and management approach: DevSecOps for products, and Agile for management.
DamoTech seeks also to develop a variety of services, including an analysis on cyber risks deriving from the human factor, and the assessment of a company’s cyber maturity level, with regards to new technologies, and internal and external processes.
Since its birth, DamoTech has been deep inside the cyber security field, possessing a high-level of multidisciplinary skills. In this context, a specific R&D project emerges: our Cyber Threat Intelligence platform, aims to collect, handle and process unclassified information, through the emission of high quality, semiautomatic reports guarantees by analysts and AI/ML components. The platform is entirely dedicated to the Space environment and Space's assets (OT and IoT).
DamoTech’s scientific methodology comes from its team based on a group of managers and experts which is combines University background as ethical landscape (PhD is the target), that incorporates a multidisciplinary approach in developing technologies and products perfectly aligned with the customers' needs.

Furthermore, the company has as its object the training in the cyber security field, both technical and non-technical, with the aim of spreading the culture of information security and the acquisition of digital skills both in the public and private sectors, at a professional and non-professional level.

Indeed, within DamoTech we have established two Laboratory:
1) The Center for Cyber Security and International Relations Studies (CCSIRS) established in 2015, aims at promoting and deepening the knowledge on cyberspace's dynamics through a policy and technology oriented approach. More specifically, activities are focused on analyzing the influence that cyberspace exercises over both national security and the international system's stability, peace and security.
2) The X-Lab, established on April 2021 combines tests and effective simulations and emulations on Space assets. At the same time, the Lab seeks to investigate, study and test disruptive technologies at the edge of innovation landscape. The aim of the X-Lab is to analyze impacts and opportunities with an empirical approach.

entityName: Ústav makromolekulární chemie AV ČR, v. v. i. The Institute of Macromolecular Chemistry, Czech Academy of Sciences (IMC)
entityDescription:
The Institute of Macromolecular Chemistry, Czech Academy of Sciences (IMC), is an internationally recognised research and educational organisation in the field of synthetic polymers. Its mission is advancing the area of macromolecular chemistry, organic chemistry, macromolecular physical chemistry and macromolecular physics including their related interdisciplinary fields with the purpose of acquiring knowledge about relations between structure, properties and function of macromolecular systems and about controlled creation of supramolecular structures.
Our research is oriented on the development of new synthetic and technological processes, on new polymer materials and their applications as well as on design of polymers for electronics, for medicinal chemistry and for tissue engineering including investigation of interactions of biological systems with polymeric materials. The combination of interdisciplinary teams of knowledgeable experts with up-to-date experimental facilities is the main asset of the Institute. Although the Institute is primarily focused on fundamental research, it also closely cooperates with the application sphere. This is particularly true for application of polymers in medicine, but also for material research and for assessment of the ecological impact of plastic waste. The Institute provides training in polymer science for postgraduate, graduate as well as undergraduate students enrolled at Czech universities. It also traditionally runs internationalpostgraduate courses in polymer scienceunder the auspices of UNESCO and IUPAC.

entityDescription:
Hans-Christoph Steiner been working with Guardian Project https://guardianproject.info/ for over a decade, on privacy in the mobile context and has been involved in the ideas, development, and UX design of Tor embedded in Android, private messaging with ChatSecure, untrackable software distribution with F-Droid, and more. He is also part of the core team of the F-Droid decentralized app distribution ecosystem; and a Tor Core Contributor, focusing on Tor on Android, and Tor integrations. He has been a Debian Developer since 2012, where he founded and still leads the Android Tools Team for including the Android SDK and related auditing and inspection tools.
ProofMode (https://proofmode.org) is a system that enables authentication and verification of multimedia content, particularly captured on a smartphone, from point of capture at the source to viewing by a recipient. It utilizes enhanced sensor-driven metadata, hardware fingerprinting, cryptographic signing, and third-party notaries to enable a pseudonymous, decentralized approach to the need for chain-of-custody and “proof” by both activists, journalists, documentarians, and everyday people alike. ProofMode is an open-source project developed by Guardian Project for over 10 years.
Rivka Karasik, a passionate privacy enthusiast with a background in art and education, has been working with Hans-Christoph Steiner on projects related to free software and tracking detection and awareness. They recently completed work on two European based projects together: "Tracking the Trackers" funded by NLnet PETO and "The Search for Ethical Apps" funded by NLnet NG10Discovery. Rivka Karasik has also been working together with the F-Droid community on the creation of a board and statutes. She also works with Guardian Project on various F-Droid and related projects.
atorat KG, established in September of 2022, and based in Vienna, Austria represents the working partnership of Hans-Christoph Steiner and Rivka Karasik. It also represents Guardian Project on projects in Europe.
The funding we are pursuing with the ESA is focused on engaging citizen science, gamification, and open standards and services for geolocation and mapping. These are all highly relevant to our work on ProofMode, and activities that we already have underway. atorat KG is the EU representative of Guardian Project's work on ProofMode that will be the managing entity for this application.
