entityDescription:
Villinger GmbH is an Austrian SME founded in 1989, specialized in the following fields:
- Beyond state-of-the-art air disinfection systems based on our unique LEA™ technology
- Highly energy efficient thermal control systems to keep equipment above temperature limits
 
Air Disinfection Systems
Together with an international consortium of medical engineers and doctors, our patented LEA™ (Laminar Electrode Array) technology features beyond state-of-the-art air disinfecting capabilities, without producing ozone or nitrogen oxide as byproducts. LEA™ is capable of removal but also immediate inactivation of airborne particles including viruses, bacteria, mold, fungi, pollen, VOCs and dust. During laboratory tests, using aerosolized MS2 bacteriophage with particle sizes ranging from 0.1µm – 0.5µm, LEA™ yielded an average 6.09 +/- 0.03 net LOG reduction, which corresponds to an average 99.99992% reduction rate of airborne MS2 virus particles. LEA™ may be installed as a stand-alone technology or to support HEPA/ULPA filters within the ECLS unit.
 
Thermal Control Systems
Utilizing our unique heating technology based on electrically conductive coatings, we offer highly energy efficient surface heating systems in order to keep various spacecraft and space station components, i.e. battery packs, above temperature limits.

entityDescription: A.S. Prote Maritime Ltd is an innovative technology SME founded in Cyprus in 2013 and subsequently expanded through theestablishment of an official branch in Greece. The company operates in the fields of security, maritime surveillance, criticalinfrastructure protection, environmental monitoring and advanced unmanned systems. Our primary focus is the development anduse of autonomous vehicles in the maritime environment.The company currently employs six highly qualified professionals and complements its capabilities through project-basedcollaborations and external experts according to project requirements. Our personnel's experience is demonstrating 30+ years inthe Hellenic War Navy, 12+ years in the Merchant Navy and 15+ years in Higher Education (Virtual Reality).Since its creation, the company has invested continuously in proprietary UAV technologies. We are holding a patent granted by theHellenic Industrial Property Organization entitled “Marine Area Surveillance System Using Unmanned Aircraft Systems to Avoidand Prevent Merchant Ships from Piracy” (International Classification: B64C 39/02, B64D 47/00, G06Q 50/10, G06V 10/10). Thisinnovation demonstrates the company’s capability to develop UAV-based solutions addressing maritime security challenges.Building on this foundation, we developed the PHORCYS UAV platform for maritime surveillance, inspection and securityapplications. Through theseactivities, our company has accumulated significant expertise in UAV systems engineering, autonomous operations,communications, sensor integration, simulation and maritime-domain applications.The knowledge, technological assets and intellectual property generated through these activities support the commercialexploitation of ΛIMHN, our next-generation UAV platform for surveillance, inspection, environmental monitoring, criticalinfrastructure protection and port and anchorage operations.

Radtest Ltd provides a comprehensive portfolio of radiation testing services across a wide range of sectors where exposure to ionising radiation may be encountered. For space customers, we offer TID, TNID and SEE testing, combined with thermal and vacuum environments. Our own walk-in cobalt-60 irradiation facility routinely accommodates multiple samples at various dose rates. Regular slots for heavy ion beam time ensure that projects do not need to wait long for testing. All aspects of the test process (sample procurement, package preparation, test plans, test hardware and software, data acquisition, hands-on testing, data analysis and reporting) can be included.

We are proud to be the only test house outside the USA to be awarded DLA laboratory suitability for total dose testing under all test conditions defined in MIL-STD-750 and MIL-STD-883 test method 1019 including test condition A.

Our SEREEL2 is now an established product for pulsed laser SEE testing. This provides an alternative to heavy ion testing, affording rapid access to data for screening, fault injection studies and comparative testing. SEREEL2 uses only the most reliable, stable and industrially proven components (lasers, movement stages and optics) to deliver a high quality experience for users.

entityDescription:
The Institute of Agriculture and Tourism, with its 145 years of continuous organised work, is one of the oldest-running scientific research institutions in the Republic of Croatia. From its foundation until today, the Institute has become a scientific research institution that has significantly contributed to the development of agriculture and tourism, at the regional as well as national level. Acting regionally, but with national and international recognition, through a number of realised domestic and international projects, the Institute nurtures the fundamental role and goals for which it was founded: rural development with emphasis on agriculture and tourism, acquisition and transfer of knowledge, affirmation of scientific research and professional activities in agriculture and tourism, and preservation of biodiversity, as well as natural and traditional values. Nowadays, in the time of indispensable interdisciplinary, necessary competitiveness and the need to create lasting cooperation and international relations, the Institute of Agriculture and Tourism can rightly be considered one of the leading scientific research institutions in the field of agriculture and tourism in Croatia, as well as one of the few institutions in the world with such research symbiosis. We firmly believe that the Institute will remain a strong and respectable scientific research organisation, primarily in the environment in which it operates, but at the same time will still be recognised and respected nationally and internationally, as a centre of knowledge for rural development, agriculture and sustainable tourism. We also believe that the aspirations of the Institute's employees go further, constantly surpassing the current scientific and research achievements.

DEPARTMENT OF TOURISM

University North is a public institution of higher education registered in the court register of the Commercial Court in Bjelovar under the number MBS 060260692, and in the Register of Higher Education Institutions under the registry number 336 kept with the Ministry of Science and Education. It is organized as an integrated structure based on two equal university centres: University Centre Varaždin and University Centre Koprivnica. It was established for the purpose of educating competent staff in the field of technical, biomedical, biotechnical, social and humanistic, and interdisciplinary sciences and arts, while its activities and scientific accomplishments seek to contribute to the advancement of the economy of the north-western region.
The University operates in the region of north-western Croatia and is complementary in its mission to the development needs of the region; it possesses highly educated, scientific, artistic and professional staff and a quality structure of various study programmes in the fields of technical sciences, biomedicine and health, biotechnical and social sciences. There are constant investments into the academic advancement of teachers, the number of publications and employees’ teaching materials are continuously increasing, and significant financial resources are provided for the further development of practicum and the equipping of new laboratories.
University North is one of the youngest public university in Croatia and an integrated, regional university of the macro-region of North-western Croatia. It is attended by over 5,000 students from all over Croatia and the surrounding countries, with more than 400 employees and external associates working in all scientific-teaching, artistic-teaching, teaching and associate titles.
University North educates personnel primarily in the technical and biomedical fields and provides teaching in 28 study programs with more than 80% of students in the so-called STEM areas. University North educates people in scarce occupations not only in Croatia but also at the European level, which is supported by the fact that the stock exchanges have a percentage of students who have completed some of the mentioned programs below the Croatian average, often around 5 percent or below. University graduates are very successful, largely due to the fact that students in theory acquire a good deal of knowledge through practice, learning from leading experts in the real sector and science. Also, as part of various international cooperation programs, part of the teaching or student internship can be done in one of the European countries, which is of great importance to students.

entityDescription:
GeoX Ltd. is a private company founded in 1998, Hungary, primarily focused on spatial information (e.g. digital maps, navigation and POI databases) The global players; Google, HERE, TomTom use GeoX’s base data in their spatial products.
GeoX has also broadened its business with customized spatial databases and map application development in different environments. These new fields of activities involved micro-segmentation/profiling, spatial resource-optimization, road navigation and route-optimization, data-mining, management of large and heterogeneous datasets. By the changing demands and circumstances, we have kept our focus on the spatial aspects of the tasks, their solution and spatial modeling.
At the beginning of 2010, GeoX has entered the field of mobile application development, resulting in two main products: “SurveyCloud”, which is a complex data survey and data-collection management platform and application (www.surveycloud.eu), and “Egérút”, a free navigation application that is available for all major mobile platforms (www.egerut.com). Within the framework of the Hungarian Unified Emergency Call (112) the Egérút’s routing and navigation engine is used by the mobile units of police and emergency rescue departments (www.antaresnav.hu).
Based on our experiences in data collection, analysis and application development, and seeing the amount of data accessible, discovering its immanent potential makes us to focus on linking, joining and analysing sensor- and spatiotemporal data.
Based on these wide range of expertises, GeoX has been involved in several local and international R&D projects in various fields: EURADIN (2008-2010; GA: 317002) - European Address Infrastructure; FusePool (2012-2014; GA: 296192) - Fusing and pooling information for product/service development and research; FusePool P3 (2014-2016; GA: 609696) - Fusepool Publish-Process-Perform Platform for Linked Data; SOPCAWIND (2012-2014; GA: 296164) - Software for the Optimal Place CAlculation for WIND-farms; TIMON (2015- GA: 636220) - Enhanced real-time services for an optimised multimodal mobility relying on cooperative networks and open data.
GeoX has been working together with Nokia in a group communication solution for public safety since 2017.

The Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias (IAC) is a Spanish public research organization that manages two of the best international observatories of the world: the Observatorio del Teide (Tenerife), and the Observatorio del Roque de los Muchachos (La Palma). Administratively, it is a public consortium, made up of the General Administration of the Spanish State, the Public Administration of the Autonomous Comunity of the Canary Islands, the University of La Laguna (ULL) and the Consejo Superior de Investigaciones Científicas (CSIC). The IAC is recognized by the Spanish Government as a "Severo Ochoa Centre of Excellence".

The IAC also manages the IACTEC institute, a technological and business collaboration space whose mission is to develop an innovative ecosystem for the transfer of high technology between the public sector and the companies. The lines of action of IACTEC include a Space Programme, Medical Technology Programme, Large Telescopes Programme, Free Space Optical Communications and the Incubator of High Technology in Astrophysics and Space (IATAE).

entityDescription:
The Hellenic Naval Academy is committed on serving its objectives which are the continuous improvement and modernization of education processes along with advanced research in Naval Sciences and Technology. Modern higher educational processes require the international cooperation between the Hellenic Naval Academy (HNA) with other Military and Civil Educational institutions in European countries and the rest of the world, in order to promote scientific research and expertise, enhance military training, improve the educational operations at all levels - undergraduate, postgraduate - and to disseminate the cultural heritage between the countries. HNA adopted a strategy for the development of the cooperation which will be determined by high quality standards of partner institutions, involving students, staff --both Academic and Military-- as well as educational and research infrastructures. The HNA’s continuous intention and will is to play a leading role at the development of inter-university cooperation at all areas of naval science, technical engineering science, environmental science, basic sciences, law science, as well as economics and humanities. Particularly in the educational objective, HNA will continue to endorse the cooperation in the Military Erasmus Initiative and expanded this with cooperation with other European Institutions (civil and military). Additionally, in the research field, HNA will be seeking the cooperation possibilities with recognized international institutions and industrial of all sizes, Large as well as Small & Medium-sized Enterprises (SME’s). The aim focuses in the establishment of research infrastructures, which could improve the basic research capabilities of HNA and incorporate innovative applications for life improvement. The utilization of HNA’s high level human resources and the exceptional level of infrastructure are the key elements for the achievement of the objective of inter-university cooperation. The role of HNA is well established through history. It is one of the oldest institutions in Greece established in 1845. The important role of the HNA not only in European, Balkan, Mediterranean and Middle East countries but also in those of Asia, Africa, Pacific and American continents, should emerge through rational planning and targeted strategic steps.
More Information visit the history of HNA: https://www.hna.gr/en/the-academy-en/history

entityDescription:
DON’T BE SCARED, BE PREPARED 
Have you ever felt limited in your adventures by fear of safety? Wanted to go on solo outings but feared it’s too risky? 
As from now, the days of limiting yourself are gone. 
The O-BOY Watch, the first multiple use wearable rescue device using satellite (not LTE/GSM), will get you help, ANYTIME, ANYWHERE!
NO SIGNAL? NO PROBLEM! 
While many smartwatches double down as rescue devices, they lack one major thing: connection that is independent from a phone, and connection BEYOND a phone’s reach. Instead of using the cellular network, O-BOY’s technology relies on a private SATELLITE network to transmit your signal. What does that mean? You can explore the most remote areas without worrying that you’ll be out of reach in case of emergency. 
1 DEVICE. 1 BUTTON. 3 SERVICES
O-BOY offers the flexibility to mix-and-match 3 different services on a pay-per-play basis.
1. GETME: Send a custom message with your gps coordinates to your favourite contacts. 
2. RESCUEME: Send an SOS signal to the Emergency Operation Coordination Center who will then dispatch a rescue team. The RescueMe service also includes an insurance covering up to $100k of the cost of the search & rescue operation. 
3. TRACKME: Use this to send automatic location updates and record your progress live. 
 
INITIAL TARGETS 
Extreme adventurers whose activities: 
i. Take them to areas without network coverage
ii. Make carrying a cellphone impractical
iii. Can put their physical integrity at risk (lost, carried away by the current, injured, etc.)

entityDescription:
Wetsus, the European centre of excellence for sustainable water technology is a facilitating intermediary for trendsetting know-how development. Wetsus creates a unique environment and strategic cooperation for developing profitable and sustainable state-of-the-art water treatment technology.
The inspiring and multidisciplinary collaboration between companies and research institutes from all over Europe in Wetsus results in innovations that contribute significantly to solving the global water problems. Wetsus’scientific research program is defined by the private and public water sectors and conducted by leading universities.
Wetsus is part ofWaterCampus Leeuwarden.
WaterCampus Leeuwarden is the physical core of the Dutch water technology sector and has the ambition to play a sector-uniting role for the rest of Europe as well.
WaterCampus stimulates cooperation between (inter)national businesses, knowledge institutes, and governments within the water technology sector, to create synergy for world-class innovation, education, and entrepreneurship.
This strengthens the global position of the European water technology sector. Additionally, WaterCampus offers a unique research infrastructure and is a meeting point for scientists and companies from all over Europe.
The international cooperation organized and stimulated by WaterCampus Leeuwarden leads to knowledge, talent, and entrepreneurship that contribute to solutions for global water problems.

entityDescription: EduFIT is an online health education and functional fitness company. We specialise in designing, implementing and evaluating evidence-based exercise and lifestyle interventions for the treatment and management of chronic disease, healthy ageing, and the menopause. Our team consists of clinical exercise physiologist, exercise physiologist and sports scientist, nutritionist, health researchers and a number of fitness instructors. Dr Diane Cooper (CEO, Founder, Clinical Exercise Physiologist, Health Researcher) and Dr Kiera Ward (Exercise and Space Physiologist, Sport Scientist, Health Researcher) are metabolic researchers who worked on the last 60-day head down tilt bed rest study in the DLR, Cologne. Our specialist area of expertise is exercise physiology, metabolic health and novel biomarkers of insulin resistance. We published our first paper "Frontiers | Fetuin-A as a Potential Biomarker of Metabolic Variability Following 60 Days of Bed Rest (frontiersin.org)" in October 2020. We currently have more papers in review. We specialise in translating our learnings and findings from the bed rest studies to healthy ageing here on earth.

entityDescription:
Dental and Medical Excellence
The DPU department of Medicine/Dentistry stands for excellence in teaching, science and research. It offers its students undergraduate courses, postgraduate courses in a Master of Science in Specialisation (MSc) and a scientific doctoral programme in Dentistry (PhD). "State-of-the-art" knowledge is imparted by renowned professors, with an excellent supervisory relationship between the teams of academics and students. In addition, practical training is implemented on the basis of the latest methods and state-of-the-art equipment, starting from the first semester.
Studying successfully as a community

Despite stringent academic demands, studies at DPU take place in a positive, familiar atmosphere. Mutual consideration and learning as a community take the place of selfish competition. Internationality

Based on these core technologies Spin Digital has developed solutions that include HEVC and VVC live encoders, transcoders, and media players, as well as an SDK ready to be integrated into custom applications.

Spin Digital is based in Berlin, and operates in an international B2B environment, working with customers and partners in several countries and market areas.

entityDescription:
Living in an Interconnected WorldIn today’s interconnected world, data in public safety becomes a valuable asset to improve situational awareness and is key to fast and efficient emergency services. Next Generation standards, such as NG-911 and NG112 provide blueprints for modern, interconnected and IP-based architectures.
GridGears was founded in 2017 with the goal to contribute to those standards and enable better, more integrated and more efficient emergency services. We truly believe in standards and are deeply convinced that the aggregation of multiple services, provides much greater value than the sum of it’s parts. This core value is even reflected in the company’s name, where we see that theGrid-the aggregation- of multipleGears-the services- drives the motor of innovation.
Digitalization of Emergency ServicesFuture emergency services need to keep up with and take advantage of the ever-growing digitalization. They must utilize this trend and its new possibilities to provide more accurate and efficient help to those in need. To achieve the best possible solution, these state of tomorrow systems need to interconnect with multiple components within and outside of the emergency network. Efficient and cost-effective exchangeability and interconnectivity between those components can only be gained by moving from proprietary interfaces to well defined and recognized standards.
Our ProductsGridGears provides multiple Next Generation Core Components, includingEmergency Call Routing Function(ECRF),Policy Routing Function(PRF),Forest GuideandLocation Information Service(LIS) withAdvanced Mobile Locationintegration. Our products support on-premise, cloud-based or even hybrid deployment options to allow easy and cost-efficient integration into existing systems. The interfaces and protocols adhere to the standard and were evaluated during multiple ETSI Plugtests from GridGears' earliest beginnings. GridGears' products were also an essential part of theCross-border ESInet and LoST Hierarchy Emergency Services Testing(CELESTE) consortium in EENA’sNext Generation 112 Project.
Future Emergency ServicesTechnology and their level of integration and acceptance is moving at an enormous speed. Nobody can predicate how we will communicate and interact with technology in the future. Therefore, it is even more important to establish a stable foundation for future innovations in public safety. At GridGears we believe that NG112 and NG9-1-1 are the foundation for integrated, multi-vendor and cross-border solutions and we are strongly committed provide standard conform solutions, which enable the best possible emergency services, whenever and wherever you are.

Alma Technologies S.A. designs, markets, sells and supports its high-quality, innovative and feature-rich FPGA and ASIC semiconductor IP products since 2001. The company is a pure IP provider that plans and develops IP as a product, without marketing any custom design services or internal design reuses as IP cores. Alma Technologies is a self-funded, privately owned, company that has been profitable since 2003. 
Alma Technologies applies a certified Quality Management System in line with the EN ISO 9001:2008 standard for the Scope of "Production, sales and technical support of semiconductor intellectual property cores". We focus on high product quality, innovation and complete customer satisfaction as key advantages over competition. Our products stand out for their engineering, being complete, easy-to-use and reliable solutions. World-class technical support and a long track record of proven designs by more than 250 licensees in over 20 countries provide our customers with excellent service and great value. 
Alma Technologies IP is successfully used in a very broad range of applications which includes aerospace, automotive, consumer electronics, defense, industrial, medical, pro-imaging and surveillance products. The users of our IP range from small startups to long established market leaders and Tier-1 semiconductor manufacturers.

entityDescription:
Our Chair at a glance:

We focuson cutting-edge research in satellite autonomy under constrained resources and advancing space sustainability by enabling more efficient use of in-space resources through federated satellite system approaches.
We contribute to the advancement of research in satellite engineering, systems engineering (including applications outside of the space industry), and technology management.
We are also interested in researching the New Space sector from technology, process, and business perspectives.
Our teaching offer at TUM is primarily focused on project-based experiential courses, with an emphasis on cutting-edge research projects, peer instruction, and active student participation in addressing open questions in space systems engineering and technology management.
We strongly support the nucleation of entrepreneurial ideas in space technology to be developed by PNS alumni and affiliates via startup companies within the TUM ecosystem and integrated within the activities of the European New Space Sector.

entityName: University of Ljubljana, Faculty of sport
entityDescription:
EDUCATION
Faculty of Sport is the leading educational, professional and scientific-research institution in the field of kinesiology and sport in Slovenia. It implements three bachelor’s degree programmes and three master’s degree programmes (one in cooperation with the Faculty of Economics) as well as one doctoral programme. At the bachelor’s level, it educates professionals for work in outside school sports activities and in sports programmes in private sector. It also educates for sports coaches and other professionals for physical preparation in sports organisations as well as in tourism and preventive health programs. Graduates of master’s study programmes can become physical education teachers in schools or sports professionals who carry out sports activities with the elderly or with people with chronic diseases or injuries or they can work in the field of sports management. The doctoral programme is aimed at scientific research and development work in the field of kinesiology.
RESEARCH
The basic scientific research activities take place within two research programmes. The research programme “Bio-psycho-social context of Kinesiology” examines on the one hand the effects of sports training in hypoxic conditions and on the other hand physical activity and health, including motor development in children and youth. In the research programme “Kinesiology in mono-structured,poly-structural and conventional sports” researchers study human movement in space and time in terms of modelling competition and success as well as the issue of preparation processes of athletes in accordance with appropriate measurement procedures and technologies. Applied research activity takes place within the framework of various international projects in cooperation with industry and other societal stakeholders.
DEVELOPMENT – COOPERATION WITH THE PRIVATE AND PUBLIC SECTOR
The main target of the implementation of multidisciplinary research, measurement and consultancy projects is to support the development of athletes aiming at quality and high-level competitive sports. The Faculty’s participation in designing and testing of sports equipment is conducted for the needs of the fields of elite sports and sport for all. A highlight comes in dealing with optimizing the movement of high-level athletes and their sports equipment, as well as the protection of health and the positive effects of exercise (research work in the field of biomechanics). The Institute of Kinesiology targets the market of high-level Slovenian athletes and carries out tests and projects for many athletes from abroad. Of special interests are the preparations for the World Championships and Olympic Games.

Solving world problems using the power of the crowd, satellites and a bit of gaming

Our tailor-made maps or data labels generated as a service typically cover a large area thoroughly, yet they are very affordable and can be created in a matter of just a few days. This is achieved through a mapping concept unique in the market: 
We use game-based crowdsourcing to create our maps through our crowdsourcing platform Cerberus having over 100 000 minds at the ready!
entityDescription:
BlackShore — mapping what matters:
BlackShore delivers accurate, up-to-date and low-cost map products based on the crowd-sourced interpretation of satellite data and aerial imagery. We map what matters most in the world. Topics range from forest monitoring to disaster relief and food security. Our tailor-made maps typically cover a large area thoroughly, yet they are very affordable and can be created in a matter of just a few days. This is achieved through a mapping concept unique in the market: we use game-based crowdsourcing to create our maps.

The concept of game-based crowdsourcing:
Even with today’s advanced artificial intelligence, the best interpretation of visual imagery is still being performed by humans. Putting a team of specialists on an interpretation quest for thousands of square kilometres is a very expensive and time-consuming task, though. This is where crowdsourcing comes in.

With our award-winning Cerberus(tm) gaming platform, we utilise the eyes of hundreds to thousands of people throughout the world as sensors. Game players are briefed through e-learning first, which not only improves quality, but also raises awareness and builds knowledge for the topic at hand. After the training our crowd starts playing and gathering information. The more people mark the same object or visual change in an image, the more likely it is that this object or change is true. With so many people visually interpreting our imagery, we can use statistical methods to extract the right information with large confidence. This ensures our maps are thorough and accurate, though still very affordable.

Through Cerberus people are encouraged to actively participate in solving the world’s pressing problems. This is why so many players return to our crowdsourcing projects time after time. Through their eyes we can create information products that map what really matters.

Key advantages of BlackShore’s map products:
• Our mapping method is specifically designed for large and remote areas
• Low-cost information products compared to traditional techniques
• Thorough, accurate and reliable results
• Almost real-time information through fast and easy delivery of maps
• Customisable: get exactly the information you want

entityName: GISIG - Geographical Information Systems International Group
entityDescription:
GISIG is a European Association founded in 1992, as a University Enterprise Training Partnership, supporting innovation and technology transfer for Geographical Information. GISIG has a long record of experiences and multidisciplinary skills on geoinformatics and related application domains (coastal area, land planning, water resources, nature conservation, utility networks management). 
Since almost three decades, GISIG has been promoting and coordinating several projects, particularly in the Education and Training and Research and Innovation EU Programmes, by involving multidisciplinary networks of partners and gaining well-recognised experience in managing large scale cooperation projects. 
GISIG is the coordinator of EO4GEO, the ERASMUS+ Sector Skills Alliance on Copernicus (www.eo4geo.eu). EO4GEO supports the Copernicus user uptake through an innovative strategy for skills development and capacity building in the space geo-information sector. EO4GEO is promoted by GISIG in connection to the Copernicus Building Skills Action and the Copernicus Academy Network, where GISIG is member. GISIG is also Communication, Dissemination and Training leader of the H2020 RECONECT Project (www.reconect.eu), dealing with spatial planning and ecosystems regeneration for mitigating hydro-meteorological risks, grouping 36 partners and more than 20 pilot sites worldwide.
Expertise that GISIG can share in the specific call are:
· Capacity building and training on geoinformatics and Copernicus
· Technical and financial management
· Communication, Dissemination and Networking
· GIS applications and spatial data services

description: OHB Hellas single member L.L.C, which is a subsidiary company of the German multinational technology group OHB SE based in Germany, started its operation in Greece in 2018. OHB Hellas is owned 100% by OHB SE. The creation of this company follows the signed MoU in December 2017 with the Greek State. The establishment of a subsidiary in Greece marked the first step of the OHB Group's vision to support the development of the space industry in Greece. OHB Hellas is the first dedicated Space Systems company in Greece with the ambition to develop space business with the collaboration of the already established local space companies, to expand the OHB SE supply chain to Greece as well as to support bilateral collaborations between Greece and Germany in the space domain. The core technologies on which OHB-Hellas is building strong competencies are in the domain of high-performance data processing including artificial intelligence (AI) on-board the satellite and modular, flexible and reusable architectures as well as in the domain of Smart Manufacturing - polymer-based Additive Manufacturing (AM) for aerospace applications.
entityDescription:
OHB Hellas mon. E.P.E. (single member L.L.C), which is a subsidiary company of the German multinational technology group OHB SE based in Germany, was established in Greece in 2018 following the MoU signature in 2017 between the Greek State and OHB SE. OHB Hellas is owned 100% by OHB SE. The MoU had foreseen the establishment of a daughter company of OHB in Greece and highlights the intention of OHB and the Greek state to join the effort for building space systems in Greece under a common entity. 
OHB Hellas is the first dedicated Space Systems company in Greece with the ambition to develop space business with the collaboration of the already established local space companies, institutions and universities, as well as European partners. Further, OHB Hellas’ objectives include expanding the OHB SE supply chain to Greece, to cooperate with the other OHB subsidiaries, to support bilateral collaborations between Greece and Germany in the space domain, as well as to design and integrate space hardware (satellite parts, microsatellites) in Greece. 

The core technologies on which OHB Hellas is building strong competencies are in the domain of high-performance data processing including artificial intelligence (AI) on-board the satellite and in modular, flexible and reusable architectures. Technologies like High Performance Payload Computers (HPPC) coupled with a hypervisor open up new possibilities for reconfiguring satellite hardware in flight in a safe and controlled manner. This is one of the next big areas of opportunity for innovation in spacecraft operations and is introducing new business models like satellite as a service. Furthermore, as presented and agreed in the frame of the overall OHB Strategy 2025, OHB Hellas is aiming to become the center of excellence on High Performance Payload Computing (HPPC) activities, in perfect complementarity to the Group’s needs and Greece’s strengths in the domain.
Moreover, OHB Hellas is involved in systems-level studies for space missions, as well as in the domain of Smart Manufacturing – polymer-based Additive Manufacturing (AM) for aerospace applications.    
OHB Hellas, bringing extensive know-how and experience directly from the OHB Group to Greece, is providing services on space architectures, Systems Engineering as well as space studies and digital transformation and innovation. Finally, the core technologies developed in Greece have a clear vision for OHB, Greece and Europe, targeting missions that benefit everyone. The identified strategic mission scenarios that OHB Hellas is working on include satellite as a service (SaaS), space defence through situational awareness, optical ground stations and Industry 4.0 (smart manufacturing). 

OHB Hellas generates an opportunity for young motivated Greek engineers to work in the space industry in Greece. It intends to contribute to the return of highly educated Greek scientists, engineers and professionals in general, who are working abroad, back to Greece. The strength of OHB Hellas lies on its personnel, who bring along expertise from multiple engineering disciplines including space systems engineering, RF, mechanical, electrical engineering, AIT, machine learning and AI, EO, software engineering, FPGA development and more.

entityName: Mednarodna podiplomska šola Jožefa Stefana - MPŠ
entityDescription:
The Jožef Stefan International Postgraduate School (IPS) was established in 2004 as an independent higher education institution. Its study programmes were approved by the Slovenian National Council for Higher Education. The initiative for the establishment of IPS came from the Jožef Stefan Institute(JSI). It was strongly supported by industry (Gorenje, Kolektor, Salonit) and an international network of cooperating universities and research institutes from the European Union, USA, Japan, and many other countries. The Jožef Stefan Institute provides the central research and educational basis, whereas other partners, such as invited research institutes, industrial and other enterprises also contribute their knowledge and innovation capacities for solving developmental problems.

Mission
"Direct integration of research and postgraduate studies to create knowledge and promote innovativeness"
Vision
IPS aims to achieve worldwide recognition among leading institutions providing postgraduate education in the fields of nanosciences and nanotechnologies, ecotechnologies, information and communication technologies, and sensor technologies. Its goal is to provide the highest quality postgraduate studies at the master and doctoral level through a joint research and educational process in an intensive research and development and innovative environment and to contribute to the strengthening of the role of science and high technologies in the developmental potential of society. This can essentially contribute to the economic strength and harmonic social development. IPS acts as a centre of excellence which closely integrates basic research with postgraduate education and development of innovations.
Quality
IPS strives for constant quality improvement of its services and to meet the demands and expectations of all participants involved in its educational and research processes.
This is achieved by:
- planning educational, research, managerial and support processes,
- implementing the processes,
- monitoring the efficiency of these processes and
- taking actions in order to ensure constant improvement of the processes.
Our Research-Educational Strategy
Postgraduate studies for Master and Doctorate degrees are oriented towards solving research and development problems that require a multidisciplinary synthesis. The main research-educational strategy of IPS is, therefore:
- widening and deepening knowledge, and mastering and development of research methods and techniques, in natural sciences and high technologies, information and communication sciences and technologies, environmental sciences and ecotechnologies, and in management of technologies and innovations – with the aim of supporting excellence in basic research, strategic choice of priority developmental areas, systematic control and permanent innovation of processes and products, increasing economic efficiency and environmental acceptability;
- development of an integral process of thinking which will support multidisciplinary communication, comprehensive definition of problems and their solving in group work, decision making in uncertain conditions, and long-term oriented strategic planning with emphasis on sustainable development.
Realisation of this strategy is presented more in detail in IPS study programmes:
- Nanosciences and Nanotechnologies,
- Information and Communication Technologies,
- Ecotechnologies,
- Sensor Technologies.

entityDescription:
In 2019, Frederik Keysers and Roy Jeunen started working on the idea of simplifying identity and access flows. Whenever they visited an industrial site (background in aviation, logistics and port facilities) they encountered the same problem. They had to arrive 15 to 45 minutes in advance to have their IDs checked/scanned, go through safety briefings and attend safety trainings. In addition, they were given insecure RFID badges as an access control method.

In August 2020, they founded Nine Engineering with the mission to simplify identity and access flows, improving site security, and increasing facility safety. To further develop their solution, Nine Engineering received initial funding from the European Space Agency (ESA) through the ESA BIC programme and VLAIO. Based on research and an iterative process with customers, the company launched NineID� in 2021. The solution consists of a SaaS platform where user data (ID documents, training, certificates) can be collected in a privacy-compliant way, even before the individual is on the site.Upon arrival, the NineID� XS1 hardware can grant access to doors, barriers and gates based on facial authentication, QR code or smartphone scanning (all in one device). This combination provides an end-to-end digital access flow with high levels of security. 

In May 2022, Nine Engineering raised �1.1 million to continue their commercial growth. 

In September 2022 the company received the Outstanding Security Performance (OSPA) Award for Outstanding New Security Product. The company is in a final stage to become ISO27001 and ISO27701 certified by December 2022. At the moment the company has 7 employees and an annual turnover of �217.000.

entityName: SIX - Secure Communication and Information System
entityDescription:
Secure Communications & Information (SIX)
The Program Center SIX, with its headquarters in Ditzingen, Germany, comprises the Business Units "Radio Communication Products" (RCP), "Protection Systems" (PRS), "Network & Infrastructure Systems" (NIS) and "Crypto Defense Solutions" (CDS). Product and system solutions are offered in the defence and security sector. The portfolio for the defence sector includes combined tap-proof multi-band troop radio systems, complex command and control information and reconnaissance systems, tactical radio and command and control systems for mobile operations, software defined radios (SDR), systems for tactical reconnaissance and data evaluation, communication and navigation systems for surface ships, training systems and systems for field camp protection.
Another core area of activity is the development of new dish management systems for use in national and international system solutions for the civil and military market.
The portfolio is rounded off by activities in the field of after-sales. Since, on the one hand, the equipment in use by the German Armed Forces must remain operational for years to come and, on the other hand, equipment in the civilian sector must be sustainably maintained, this results in orders for the elimination of obsolescence, which require a highly specialised development effort.

Since, on the one hand, the equipment in use by the German Armed Forces must remain operational for years to come and, on the other hand, equipment in the civilian sector must be sustainably maintained, this results in orders for the elimination of obsolescence, which require a highly specialised development effort.

entityDescription: C-Astral is an aerospace solutions provider based in Ajdovscina, Slovenia, the “hub” of advanced aerospace development and integration in this part of Central Europe. C-Astral unmanned systems are much smaller than manned aircraft, easier to maintain and transport and therefore much more cost-effective, providing excellent productivity and fast return on investment. The industry leading BRAMOR UAS family is electrically powered and is able to achieve superior stability and endurance through its unique advanced Blended Wing Body airframe aerodynamics. It is capable of achieving the most precise surveying results in the small UAS category down to 0,6 cm, with a Ground Sampling Distance that starts at 0,7 cm. The company is a global market leader with established reputation in the specialized, fixed wing small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) manufacturing and services field, with a specific focus on high productivity, endurance, surveying and remote sensing. C-Astral’s customer base is diversified between the commercial UAS operators, larger institutional networks, scientific users as well as government entities. Currently, C-Astral systems are flying with six sovereign entities on force protection, border protection, fire control and surveillance operations on four continents and more than 100 commercial and scientific operators globally. C-Astral established a multidisciplinary software and hardware laboratory for aerodynamics and systems integration work and a prototyping CAD/CAM workshop facility for composite materials manufacturing and modeling. The founders of C-Astral have been active in aerospace since 1999 and have been pioneering UAS integrated solutions ahead of the market curve. C-Astral systems are now flying over all continents, including extreme environments such as high altitude open-pit mines, deserts, mountains, Antarctica, over the Arctic and global agricultural lands. The company is starting work and development of space based communications hardware related to remote sensing, communications systems as well as contributed to the development of the first Slovenian remote sensing satellite NEMO-HD.

entityDescription:
APO-GEE ENGINEERING specializes in ball bearing engineering in aerospace industry (www.apo-gee.tech).

because success of space missions can no longer be dependent on ball bearing failure.

Ball bearing is without doubt one of the most widespread mechanical components. But when a ball bearing is subjected to high speeds, heavy loads or a harsh external environment, its behavior remains misunderstood.

Under these extreme conditions, bearings may become unstable or deteriorate. Many space missions have been disrupted or even aborted, precisely because of bearing performance problems, with very serious consequences in scientific, technical, political and, above all, financial terms.

The common feature of most bearing damage is the kinematics of the balls. However, this kinematics is difficult to understand and to model accurately. In fact, it had never been properly described to date. We did.
In particular, we have solved the CAGE INSTABILITY PROBLEM, to which no fully satisfactory response has been possible for more than 50 years (patent pending EP22191261).

WE WORK WITH:
- SPACE AGENCIES

- SATELLITE LAUNCH COMPANIES

- AIRCRAFT MANUFACTURERS

- EQUIPMENT MANUFACTURERS (REACTION WHEELs RWA, TURBO PUMPS...)

Based on an original kinematic and power based analysis, APO-GEE is able to accurately and completely characterize the movement of the balls within a bearing, and model the complete equilibrium of the bearing.

We can therefore analyze the phenomena specific to your applications in depth, provide tailor-made solutions for your applications, and thus ensure the success of your aerospace projects and missions.

entityName: Univ Portsmouth - Centre for Applied Geosciences (CAG)
entityDescription:
The UNiversity of Portsmoth's Centre for Applied Geoscience (CAG) brings together applied geoscience research and consultancy activities across four departments. We specialise in the investigation and management of natural and manmade hazards and the conservation of our geo-heritage.We study our planet – from its oceans and rivers, to its complex geology. We investigate the atmosphere above us, and delve into the depths of our planet's metallic core. We observe how animals and living things — including humans — impact Earth, and measure the past, present, and future behaviour of our planet.
There's never been more of a global focus on improving sustainability, tackling climate change and managing the changes to our planet caused by human activity. Our research has a direct impact on communities, helping them adapt to environmental change and improve the resilience and sustainability of homes, jobs and cultures.
Members of the team are internationally recognised experts in the fields of Engineering Geology & Geomorphology, Geotechnical Engineering, Remote Sensing, Disaster Management and Geographical Analyses.

entityDescription:
PERIGEE enables humanitarian and development aid organizations, fundraisers and disaster risk financing providers to harness the power of data 

PERIGEE uses the power of machine learning to provide a solution for the vast, yet untapped market of humanitarian fundraisers, international aid organizations and governmental bodies. Our highly innovative Software-as-a-Service identifies potential donors based on their online behavior and makes them directly addressable through social media channels.This allows to reduce donor acquisition costs, to improve the return on advertising spend and to connect with people based on their interest towards a cause. Furthermore, our predictive analytics functionalities allow to estimate how interest towards an emergency is expected to develop.This removes the guesswork from campaigning – and allows to reduce campaign spends significantly.

We help to improve preparedness and response, to find new donors and above all to connect with people in ways that move them to action.

entityDescription:
Geodetski zavod Celje d.o.o. (GZC) is a Slovenian private company founded in 1955. With more than 65 years of experiences we are successfully providing consultations and technical assistance services to public sector financed programs and private sector. GZC is specialist in land management, cadastral, topographic, photogrammetric and GIS services, spatial and rural development programming, implementation, monitoring and evaluation and in the provision of technical assistance for capacity building of national and local institutions promoting spatial, agricultural and rural development. The company is one of the leading providers of technical assistance to many Ministries in Slovenia and within potential candidates and candidate countries in the Western Balkans. Company has experience in world Bank Loan funded projects and EU founded projects (Phare, IPA).
The Company has more than 70 employees and has managed numerous projects and programs in Slovenia and abroad. GZC is the only contractor for all on the spot controls and Controls with Remote Sensing in Slovenia since 2006, sharing its experiences also in Balkan and other countries. GZC also has direct experience in management and execution of similar EU IPA funded LPIS and IACS projects in the EU member states and Candidate Countries including Turkey, where we have successfully implemented two EU funded projects related with the LPIS/IACS and SW implementation.
 
The most important and relevant projects in the region are (but not limited to): 
· Slovenia; LUCAS field survey 2009, 2021, 2015, 2018.
· Croatia; LUCAS field survey 2018.
· Slovenia; National Orthophoto 2016 - 2022.
· Turkey; Technical Assistance for Training Staff on the Spot Controls (OTSC), Risk Evaluation and IACS Software 2017 – 2019.
· Turkey; Technical Assistance for Training Staff on IACS Procedures 2016 – 2017.
· Montenegro; Production of oblique and orthophoto images for the territory of Montenegro, 2017 -2018.
· Slovenia; 3D photointerpretation of hydrography data and water surfaces land use 2015 - 2016.
· Macedonia; Further upgrade of the Land parcel identification system 2013 - 2014.
· Macedonia; Design of a functional integrated administration and control system (IACS) and associated capacity 2010-2011.
· Slovenia; Implementation of the complete IACS controls in the Republic of Slovenia since 2006.
· Croatia, Macedonia; Controls with remote sensing in agriculture in Macedonia 2013, 2014 and Croatia 2012, 2013.
· Scotland; LPIS update Scotland 2017, 2018.
· France; LPIS update France 2014.
· Slovenia; Census of agricultural holdings 2010

entityDescription:
VIGO Photonics SA is a world leader in the production of uncooled, infrared photon detectors. In the 80s, at the Military Technical Academy, a team led by prof. dr. hab. Joseph Piotrowski developed a unique technology for the production of detectors working without cryogenic cooling and then implemented it into a newly created company.
Detectors produced in VIGO are used in various areas such as:
-railways (detection of faults of high speed trains while in motion)
-Energy (verification of the status of the transmission infrastructure of electricity)
-Military technology (observation and targeting systems for unmanned flying objects, smart and homing munitions)
-Medical (detection of early stage cancer markers, cancer changes in soft tissue or disorders of the blood circulation system).
-Industry (energy optimization).
The status of the official supplier of components for the US space agency NASA is the confirmation of unique market position of VIGO. In cooperation with NASA VIGO developed and produced detectors working on the rover Curiosity exploring the surface of Mars.
The special asset of the company is the ability to combine research and development in the field of infrared technology with the production, in close cooperation with the user.
VIGO Photonics SA does not forget about its roots – for many years in the joint laboratory, VIGO has conducted advanced research works on new types of infrared detectorsin cooperation with scientists from the Military University of Technology and other domestic and foreign research institutions.

entityName: UNIV STRATHCLYDE - National Manufacturing Institute Scotland
entityDescription:
The National Manufacturing Institute Scotland is the future of manufacturing at the heart of the Advanced Manufacturing Innovation District Scotland.
It is where industry, academia, and the public sector work together on ground-breaking manufacturing research to transform productivity levels, make companies more competitive and boost the skills of our current and future workforce.
The National Manufacturing Institute Scotland (NMIS) is a group of industry-led manufacturing research and development facilities with a network of Partners across Scotland brought together to boost the manufacturing community.
Together we are focused on revolutionising skills, productivity, and innovation to help attract investment and make Scotland and the wider UK a global leader in advanced manufacturing.
Growing out of the Scottish Government’s manufacturing action plan published in February 2016, NMIS is an integral part of the Making Scotland’s Future programme.
Our ambitions are to:
- Increase productivity by reducing barriers to innovation
- Grow the economy by galvanising investment and increasing manufacturing competitiveness within Scotland and internationally
- Catalyse job creation and strengthen supply chain links across the country
- Provide leadership, build collaborations and enhance capability to influence adaptation and exploit manufacturing opportunities to boost Scotland’s transition to a net-zero emissions economy by 2045
- Inspire and attract talent and equip current and future workforces with the skills they and the manufacturing and engineering community need
We do this by working with manufacturing businesses of all sizes from across Scotland, the wider UK, and beyond making it easier for them to access innovative technologies and connecting them with our widespread national and international network of world-leading industry and academic experts and collaborators.

entityDescription:
School of International Futures (SOIF) is a global non-profit collective of practitioners in strategy and policy for current and future generations.
Our vision is a better, fairer and more sustainable world for current and future generations. We achieve this by empowering people to use participatory futures and foresight to drive societal transformation through their organisations, communities and countries.
We bring together three disciplines in the service of societal transformation
Foresight and futures: We advise decision-makers about how to use foresight approaches

Participation and governance: We put people at the heart of the future.

Network weaving: We weave, incubate and scale networks of social change agents.

We are a values-led organisation. We have always worked with people who are using foresight to create positive change and hope. And our approach ensures that the end of any foresight journey is rooted in impact. We improve outcomes at three different levels:
Citizens are involved in shaping their desired futures: citizens — especially next generation voices — have the power to make and shape their desired futures by participating in decision-making.

Organisations and sectors are prepared for the future: Organisations, social movements and sectors are able to engage with upcoming signals of change and navigate an uncertain future

Leaders make intergenerationally fair decisions: Leaders are supported and enabled to take the interests of future generations into account in their decisions.

SOIF was founded in 2012. It is headquartered in London and operates globally, using diverse teams to work with organisations and communities to make change for the better.

entityDescription: The National Institute of Telecommunications (NIT) is a modern research & development institution operating in the area of telecommunications and information technology. It conducts works in the scope of development of the state telecommunications network, normalization and standardization of telecommunication systems and devices. The National Institute of Telecommunications operates pursuant to the Act on Research & Development Units of July 25th 1985 (with later amendments) and the Statutes of the National Institute of Telecommunications acknowledged by Ordinance No. 25 of the Minister of Infrastructure dated August 20th, 2005. National Institute of Telecommunications has the status of State Research Institute since May 31st, 2005. The National Institute of Telecommunications is authorized to grant a scientific degree of the Doctor of Technical Sciences. The National Institute of Telecommunications now employs about 250 persons among them the team of scientists and experts with high competences in the field of telecommunications and information technology, in its three centers: in Warsaw, Wroclaw and Gdansk. It has a stable economic position and manages to operate effectively in new market conditions and in a quickly changing environment. An extremely quick pace of changes in those areas and a related emergence of the information civilization understood as a combination of the information society and the knowledge-based economy, constitute challenges the Institute is able to meet. Undoubtedly it is possible due to a long-term tradition of the NIT and resulting experiences, highly qualified scientific and engineering staff and tangible resources. General mission of the National Institute of Telecommunications is: to serve purposes of the development of information society and knowledge-based economy, to provide a scientific, research and technical support to any institutions of the state, to perform works used in practice by entities operating in the market.

entityDescription:
Deep Space Energy (DSE) is developing a new European radioisotope power system (RPS) built around its proprietary Radioisotope Dynamic Generator (RDG). The RDG achieves up to 5× higher fuel-to-power efficiency (per Watt-electric) compared to legacy RTGs, while also offering enhanced reliability.
While the RDG is designed to be compatible with multiple radioisotope heat sources (RHS) and fuel forms, DSE is also advancing its own composite Sr-90 fuel and heat source, enabling delivery of the full power subsystem as an integrated solution.
Target applications include:
Sub-kilowatt lunar surface power for surviving the lunar night and operating in permanently shadowed regions.

Auxiliary power for strategic space assets, providing resilience against non-kinetic threats.

entityDescription:
Precise environment data is essential for protecting the Earth's climate. Without such data, there would be no climate models. And without for example comprehensive measurement data for greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4) and nitrous oxide (N2O), the calculations of greenhouse gas emissions of individual countries and regions cannot be validated.

The network of measuring stations and available data is patchy, not only in Germany, especially when it comes to climate-relevant data, for example on greenhouse gases. This is a task for politics, business and science. To this end, we offer serious information, advice and reliable products to close the gaps in the data network.

McKinsey is the leading management consulting firm in the world. We have served as a trusted advisor and counsellor to the world’s foremost public, social and private-sector organizations for more than 90 years and have helped them to tackle their most difficult challenges. While helping our clients solve the most pressing economic and social challenges to improve the lives of citizens worldwide, we tailor every team to client needs, drawing on our global pool of cross-sector expertise, resources and talent, while incorporating a highly collaborative, client-focused working model that aligns stakeholders to ensure delivery.

• Serving clients directly on social and public sector issues
• Investing in research on critical social, economic, and government issues

ISP Optics Corporation is a vertically integrated manufacturer offering a full range of the infrared products from high-performance MWIR and LWIR Lens Assemblies to catalog and custom infrared optical elements.
Our infrared IR Lens Assembly product line includes dual FOV and fixed focal length lenses for cooled and uncooled cameras including designs targeted for lightweight and compact models.
ISP Optics manufactures in-house precision optical components including spherical, aspherical and diffractive coated IR lenses. In addition to our built-to-print optical elements product line, we also offer custom optomechanical assemblies, coatings and diamond turning services along with IR catalog optics. We manufacture optics from various infrared crystals such as Amtir and others.
FTIR materials are grown in-house including NaCl and KBr to manufacture build-to-print optical elements for the FTIR market and KBr lenses for wideband imaging applications.
Our manufacturing processes utilize CNC grinding, diamond turning, continuous and conventional polishing, optical contacting, advanced coating and design technologies to deliver consistent top quality solutions that serve the growing industry demands with an unwavering commitment to our worldwide customers.

entityDescription:
Using satellite data and artificial intelligence to monitor and manage offsetting projects, Tracks CO2 drives positive environmental impact and market transparency.

Tracks CO2 is formed by a group of a multidisciplinary team whose members have extensive experience in business, digital transformation, innovation, and specifically in telecommunications engineering. Currently, the main project manager is Teresa Domenech (CEO), who is 100% dedicated to this project. She graduated in Telecommunications Engineering and has a Master Degree in Telecommunications with specialization in machine learning and deep learning, which is the technology on which the development of the AI ​​model for carbon sequestration is based.
The tech team consists of Isabel Manresa and Sara Martínez, both telecommunication engineers specialized in remote sensing and AI.
The company also has the support of Saul Garcia, Tomas Terradas and Rafael Terradas who have a partial dedication to the project, more focused on the commercial field and on raising financing that can help accelerate the development of the product and technology. 
Their profiles and professional contacts are vitally important for the company to generate new commercial leads, but also to seek new sources of private financing to materialize our vision. 
As the company obtains new sources of financing and/or clients, it intends to grow the team in a sustained manner and make them part of the project through the transfer of phantom shares.The company also has an expert advisory team that help the company grow and expand; it includes the collaboration of Carlos Lopez, Ph.D. from the Universidad Politecnica de Catalunya, specialized in remote sensing and Earth observation, who is part of the research centers RSLAB - Grupo de Investigacion en Teledeteccion and the CommSensLab-UPC - Center UPC Communication and Detection Research Specific.Therefore, we have the perfect mix between relevant academic background and great motivation to lead a project that aims to contribute to the fight against climate change.With this team, Tracks CO2 intends to position itself as the most accurate tool for emissions offsetting investments, using Satellite Technology and Artificial Intelligence.

entityDescription:
CMP Composites is a new and innovative company operating in the field of composite materials. Since its creation in 2016, it has been offering its customers the development of solutions to achieve different objectives for their structures or components ; the manufacturing of prototype parts (from a few grams to a couple of metric tonnes), the optimisation of mass, of their thermomechanical resistance, of their cost or finally their environmental footprint. On the scale of technological maturity, CMP Composites is able to lead projects from very low levels of maturity (TRL1) to technological demonstrator (TRL6).
Depending on their customer needs and the type of application, CMP can also offer serial manufacture (TRL9) or perform technology transfer.
The company relies on its design office made up of doctors and engineers specialized in the design and simulation of composite structures. Its close link with the workshop enables the manufacture prototypes using processes such as infusion, RTM, prepreg molding and filament winding.

Since 2017, CMP Composites has been supporting CNES in the development of cryogenic fluid storage tanks made of composite materials. These developments have been the subject of two patents and CMP Composites continues to develop its linerless technology. On the basis of this work, new research activities have been initiated with various actors in the "new space" sector, in particular to provide innovative solutions for the fairing or inter-stage skirt.

The Institute of Environmental Protection – National Research Institute (IEP-NRI) is a departmental institute supervised by the Ministry of Climate and Environment. The primary goal of the Institute is to create the scientific basis for environmental protection, to provide knowledge to the governmental and self-governmental administration and economic entities, as well as to raise the level of ecological awareness and shape the ecological attitudes of society.
In its activities the IEP-NRI deals with the following issues:
- Air quality
- Waste management
- Climate change
- Protection of the Earth’s surface
- Protection against noise
- Management of emissions
- Sustainable development
- Eco-toxicology
- Environmental analyses
- Research
- Ecological education
IEP-NRI is the country’s leading scientific and research unit in the field of environmental protection. The Institute’s rank is confirmed by the comprehensive assessment of its scientific and research and development activities for the years 2013-2016, conducted in 2017, in which IEP-NRI was once again awarded scientific category A.
High qualifications, significant activity and commitment of the Institute’s staff, as well as the level of research and development work corresponding to European standards have contributed to the position of a significant research centre both in the domestic scientific community and abroad, as well as a reliable and fully professional partner for the economic environment. The Institute’s laboratory base is equipped with modern research apparatus and the technical infrastructure meets the high requirements necessary to conduct scientific research and development work at the highest world level.

entityDescription:
The company aim is to provide dedicated, fast and flexible MOCVD wafer growth services to worldwide customers in R&D and small scale production of compound semiconductor devices (InP / GaAs/ GaSb/ InAs ).

As "Pure Play" MOCVD fab we offer customers affordable development of epitaxial layer stacks on 2" substrates of choice (working on 3" capabilities) and full information on technology of growth processes and related data characterization.

The information shared include:
- full data logs of Aixtron reactors (process temperatures, pressures, flows etc.)
- full logs of MO lines equipped with ultrasonic in-situ gas delivery sensors (exact info on reagent flow to reactor)
- full in situ monitoring data from LayTec EpiRAS or EpiCurve (true wafer temperature, RAS, reflectance or curvature), which provide unique fingerprint of process grown,
- standard characterization data: HR XRD, 300K PL, Hall, ECV,
- other relevant characterization data, are additionally offered as on request and are additionally charged (SIMS, XPS, SEM, TEM, AFM).

We do support our customers in technology transfer of developed process or device structure to large foundries or companies, that could offer benefits of large scale manufacturing and cost reduction out of reach for SME.

If needed we are happy to support customers also in area of device simulation and epitaxial design of lasers, LEDs, detectors, and solar cells (in house or via large network of specialists we have cooperate with).

Over the years, we have been working with/for AMS Sensors, AMS-OSRAM, Modulight, DenseLight, POET Technologies, VIGO System/Photonics, Brolis, Ensemble3, Bright Photonics, Huawei, Lancaster University, Institute of Microelectronics and Photonics (Poland), Military University of Technology (Poland).

entityDescription:
David Nixon is an independent consultant in the space field. He began his career as an architect in the UK and was among the first handful of architects to work on the US space programmefrom the mid-1980s onwards. His fifty-year career has covered a range of experience in the US and Europe in fields of architecture, industrial design and space design. In the 1970s he worked at several leading London architecture practices, including the office of Sir Hugh Casson and the early offices of Lord Norman Foster, Lord Richard Rogers and Sir Nicholas Grimshaw. In 1978 he founded the avant-garde studio of Future Systems in London with architect Jan Kaplicky with whom he collaborated for a decade on many exploratory and competition projects.

In 1980 he moved to California and taught architecture at Southern California Institute of Architecture (SCI-Arc), University of California, Los Angeles and California State Polytechnic, Pomona. At SCI-Arc in 1985 he directed graduate research funded by NASA on full-scale prototype design of crew quarters for the recently-announced Space Station. This led to his growing involvement in the space field through his own office that he established in Los Angeles in 1992. He has worked on space projects for organizations ranging from government agencies to private companies and start-up ventures in the US and Europe. They include NASA, the European Space Agency, the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, British Aerospace, Alenia Spazio, McDonnell Douglas, Spacehab, Kistler Aerospace Corporation and Rotary Rocket Company. In 2000 he formed a start-up venture to develop miniature spaceflight products to support STEM education. The first prototype–a portable phone-sized experiment to boost student interest in maths and physics–was tested on the European/Russian Foton-3 space mission and the Airbus A310 Zero-G research aircraft in 2007.

David Nixon holds a Doctor of Philosophy from the university of Liverpool and a Diploma inArchitecture from the Central London Polytechnic. He has received awards and commendations for work in architecture, industrial design and space technology and his projects have appeared in publications worldwide. He has authored thirty technical papers and reports and the book 'International Space Station–Architecture Beyond Earth' published by Circa Press in 2016. The first retrospective exhibition of his work 'Thresholds of Space' took place at the National Technical Library in Prague in 2014. He is a Fellow of the Royal Astronomical Society, a Fellow of the Royal Aeronautical Society, a Senior Member of the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics and a Chartered Member of the Royal Institute of British Architects.

entityDescription:
The University of Zielona Góra is a dynamically developing university. It is the largest state university in the Lubuskie Province. In 2021, UZ celebrated its 20th anniversary. It is worth mentioning that the academic traditions in Winny Gród date back to 1965, when the Higher School of Engineering started its activity, later transformed into the Zielona Góra University of Technology. In 1971, the Higher Teachers School was established, which in 1973 became the Higher Pedagogical School and took the name of prof. Tadeusz Kotarbiński. The University of Zielona Góra was established on September 1, 2001 as a result of the merger of PZ and WSP. On September 1, 2017, the State Higher Vocational School in Sulechów was incorporated into the university. In the academic year 2021/2022, 9.1 thousand students are educated there. students at the 1st and 2nd degree of studies and in doctoral schools. Studies are conducted in full-time and part-time systems. The rich didactic offer of the University also includes postgraduate studies. Currently, our university consists of 12 faculties: -Artistic -Construction, Architecture and Environmental Engineering -Economics and Management -Computer Science, Electrical Engineering and Automation -Physics and Astronomy -Humanistic -Medical and Health Sciences -Mathematics, Informatics and Econometrics -Mechanical -Biological Sciences -Social Sciences -Law and Administration
At individual Faculties, students have the opportunity to study over 60 fields of study, in many specialties, in the fields of: humanities, social, economic, natural, medical and health sciences, exact and technical, and even artistic. The University of Zielona Góra is included in the elite group of classical universities, the so-called adjectivalless ones. The university has the right to award the academic degree of habilitated doctor in 7 disciplines and to award the academic degree of doctor in 17 disciplines. In two doctoral schools (Humanities and Social Sciences of the University of Zielona Góra and of Exact and Technical Sciences of the University of Zielona Góra), in 16 disciplines, full-time doctoral studies are conducted. The structures of the University of Zielona Góra include: -Park of Science and Technology sp.z o.o., whose main goal is to create conditions for the use of the scientific and industrial potential in the region and to stimulate the development of industry; -Lubuski Ośrodek Innowacji i Wdrożeń Agrotechnicznych sp.z o.o., whose mission is research, development and implementation (R&D and implementation) for the agri-food sector; -Centrum Energetyki Odnawialnej sp.z o.o., whose main areas of operation are focused on research and development in the field of renewable energy.
Thanks to the funds from the European Union, the University of Zielona Góra has acquired, among others, a modern University Library, the largest scientific library in the voivodeship, serving not only employees and students of universities, but also residents of the city and the region. The Lubuskie Center for Social Research was established at the Institute of Sociology. The Botanical Garden functions within the structure of the Faculty of Biological Sciences. Since the beginning of the existence of the University, the Publishing House has been operating within its walls, which publishes an average of about 130 publications per year, of which 40-50 are fully edited and edited.

0Optech is a College Centre for Technology Transfer (CCTT) incorporated as a non-profit organization. We specialize in applied research in optics and photonics and help businesses and organisations such as universities carry out their research and development activities for products and processes. We innovate through in-house R&D and we support our clients in their innovation efforts using optics and photonics technologies at every development stage – from feasibility studies to the design, prototyping, testing and operational validation phases – as well as for small-scale production.
We have structured our technological know-how around five main components: fibre optics, illumination & imaging, metrology, microsystems and physics-driven Artificial Intelligence. Our cross-disciplinary structure helps us to reach different types of organizations operating in a variety of innovative fields including medical technologies, multimedia, industrial production and the environment.
We are happy to report that, since 2002, we have helped to develop over 1,000 innovative projects and assisted over 400 organizations. These projects have actively contributed to the development of wealth and knowledge for SMEs, the college community and our society.

entityName: LUKASIEWICZ Research Network - INSTITUTE OF AVIATION
entityDescription:
Łukasiewicz – Institute of Aviation (formerly Institute of Aviation, established in 1926) is one of Poland’s leading research and development centers in aerospace technologies. As part of the Łukasiewicz Research Network, the institute focuses on international cooperation, including participation in ESA projects and EU Framework Programmes (FP5, FP6, FP7, Horizon 2020). Its expertise covers a wide range of areas such as aircraft, helicopter and rocket aerodynamics and structures, propulsion systems including turbojet and piston engines, composite materials and advanced manufacturing, wind tunnel testing, avionics and system integration, environmental testing and biofuels, as well as landing gear design and testing. Human factors and simulation systems, such as the High-G Human Centrifuge, are also part of its portfolio.
Research and development activities are primarily conducted within the Center of New Technologies and the Center of Space Technologies.
