entityName: Oficina Técnica de Estudios y Control de Obras, S.A.
entityDescription:
OFICINA TÉCNICA DE ESTUDIOS Y CONTROL DE OBRAS, S.A. (OFITECO) is a Spanish engineering company founded in 1971. With the always growing concerns about dam and reservoir safety, combined with the fundamental role played by transportation in the field of environmental engineering, OFITECO has highly developed in two main fields of activities: hydraulic and transport infrastructures.
The first sector includes dams and reservoirs, flood management, hydropower, water supply, wastewater treatment plants, irrigation, or river restoration. On the other hand, among the topic treated within the second sector, there are roads, highways, railways, and high-speed and underground lines. Tunnels, viaducts, and hillsides are also widely treated by the company.
OFITECO oversees all the services related to the life phases of both hydraulic and transportation infrastructures, from the design and the construction to the entire operational functioning.‎ 
During the construction phase, OFITECO manages the monitoring and quality control activities throughout the entire duration of the works. Besides, a particular focus is given to the monitoring, surveillance, and automation of dams, tunnels, and bridges.
Similarly, during the operation phase, flood risk management techniques are applied to dams, hydrometeorological networks, and canals. Detailed inspections and corrective actions are carried out for dams, tunnels, and viaducts.
OFITECO has constantly focused on R&D. The contribution of the company to the research and development fields is based on the applications of DamData, TunnelData, and BridgeData, which have been proven to be excellent real-time web services for remote data management in dam monitoring.
OFITECO is a fully established company in the SPANISH MARKET, holding offices in numerous Spanish cities such as Madrid, Valencia, Zaragoza, Granada, and Valladolid. Moreover, it is also consolidated on a more international perspective, conducting projects in Canada, Peru, Colombia, Guatemala, Algeria, Iraq, Qatar, Panama, Costa Rica, Uruguay, Georgia, ‎ Poland, and Saudi Arabia. OFITECO holds a branch office in Peru.

entityName: AECSIC - CENTRO NACIONAL INSTITUTO ESPAÑOL DE OCEANOGRAFÍA
entityDescription:
The Spanish Institute of Oceanography was created by Royal Decree of April 17, 1914, is a public research organization (OPI) dedicated to research in marine science, especially in relation to scientific knowledge of the oceans, sustainability of fishing resources and the marine environment. The IEO depends on the Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities.The IEO is not limited to carrying out basic and applied research, it also provides scientific and technological advice to administrations in matters related to oceanography and marine sciences. In fact, according to the Marine Fisheries Act of 2001, the IEO is the investigative and advisory body for the fisheries sector policy of the Government. In addition, it is the scientific and technological representative of Spain in most of the forums and international organizations related to the sea and its resources.
The IEO is an autonomous body, with its own legal personality and assets, with an approximate workforce of 700 people -of which 80% is research staff and research support-.
The budget of the IEO exceeds 65 million euros and has a wide geographical coverage and important facilities. It has a central office in Madrid and nine coastal oceanographic centers: A Coruña, Baleares (Palma de Mallorca), Cádiz, Canary Islands (Santa Cruz de Tenerife), Gijón, Málaga (Fuengirola), Murcia (San Pedro del Pinatar), Santander and Vigo five plants of experimentation of marine cultures; twelve gauge stations and one satellite image receiving station. Its oceanographic fleet, with more than twenty vessels, has five important oceanographic vessels, among which the 46 m twin vessels stand out. Ramón Margalef and Ángeles Alvariño.
The Spanish Institute of Oceanography performs basic and applied research in oceanography and marine sciences, as well as other services for scientific-technological development and maintenance of industrial, social and business activities, with the aim of increasing scientific knowledge of the oceans and that they make a sustainable use of them.
Its basic functions are:
- Scientific research in oceanography and marine sciences and multidisciplinary study of the sea.
- Advice to the General State Administration on its fishing and marine policy in general.
- Representation of Spain in international fisheries and marine science organizations.
- Promotion of cooperation in marine research at the regional, national and international levels.
- Train marine researchers and disseminate oceanographic knowledge.
A brief summary of the activities of the IEO includes: conducting quality research in oceanography and marine science; represent Spain in international forums related to oceanography and fisheries; study vulnerable marine ecosystems; develop, coordinate, carry out and manage research programs on fisheries resources as well as on marine crops; report on scientific and technological projects that are submitted for consultation and that are related to the marine sciences; study the seas and continental margins with a multidisciplinary approach; establish and participate in agreements with public and private organizations, both national and international, to carry out research projects and other scientific and technological activities; participate in international scientific research programs.

entityDescription:
Asociacija DRONEA (www.dronea.lt), a non-profit organization, is a partnership of the leading stakeholders interested in innovative drone solutions, research and development, and performance and political processes to advance a drone ecosystem. 
Together with its partners and affiliates, DRONEA represents experts from across the aviation community, from civil air navigation service providers to civil airspace users, academia, and municipalities. The members of the Association at all levels demonstrate the corresponding qualities of commitment, flexibility, innovation, and team-working. 
It is worth mentioning that DRONEA's key members were actively involved in the successful implementation of the Baltic Functional Airspace Block, and the development of the interoperable iTEC, a next-generation air traffic management system concept as well as in SESAR activities. 
As an Association we provide the framework for academia and industry, thought leaders and technology experts, regulatory and advisory bodies to connect, collaborate and promote the development of a drone ecosystem that is simple to use, affordable, commercially and operationally friendly, yet capable of addressing all societal concerns such as safety, security, privacy, and environmental protection.
DRONEA is an “outward-facing” organisation, effectively interacting with a wide range of stakeholders, formal and informal, working in an integrated way within the Association, and has close links to their expert counterparts in other EU or multinational structures.
European Commission appointed Asociacija DRONEA as a member of the Informal Drone Experts Group (E03533) to assist the Commission in the preparation of its “Drone Strategy 2.0 for a smart and sustainable unmanned aircraft eco-system in Europe. Moreover, Asociacija DRONEA is a founding member of the Joint European Drone Associations (JEDA) and its Chairman Vidmantas Kairys has been elected as a vicepresident of JEDA . JEDA aims to develop and maintain a common understanding of the seamless integration of UAS/RPAS into aviation and the European airspace system. Asociacija DRONEA is a member of Alliance for New Mobility in Europe (AME). AME seeking to create a real European Market for the New Mobility industry

entityName: Consorzio MedITech - Mediterranean Competence Centre 4 Innovation
entityDescription:
MedITech (legal name Consorzio MedITech - Mediterranean Competence Centre 4 Innovation) is one of the eight Industry 4.0 Competence Centres established by the Italian Government. It was founded in 2020 by 8 universities and 22 industrial partners, and it is supported by an ecosystem of about 100 SMEs associated with the Competence Centre.
MedITech acts as a research and technology organisation (RTO) with the aim to foster the digitalization of the economy through technology transfer activities benefitting SMEs and public administrations. If focusses on key digital enabling technologies, notably 5G, IoT, cloud computing, machine learning, AR/VR/MR, and cyber-physical systems. It works in close collaboration with the other seven Competence Centres and the network of Digital Innovation Hubs to achieve national objectives while having a clear regional focus (with specific KPIs) on Southern Italy. This area is listed among the less economically developed in the EU, and MedITech acts as an enabler along with regional and national stakeholders to support convergence policies. MedITech is partner in three out of the 13 Italian EDIHs contributing skills and facilities through a targeted productised offer of digital solutions and “Test before Invest” services, with the aim to support the development of pre-commercial digital solutions.
MedItech has developed its test before invest strategy adopting digital assets as one of the main approaches to leverage the digitisation of SMEs. To this purpose it has set up a FIWARE Lab and a Big Data laboratory (adopting GAIA-X framework). The aim is to bring SMEs in its target geographical area closer to the adoption of open-source platforms for the development of smart solutions and to support them in the creation of business cases. At the same time, it is developing a rich training programme, leveraging resources from its founding members, to ensure the upskilling/reskilling of SMEs staff on the adoption and use of digital enabling technologies. 
MedITech is FIWARE Gold Partner. It is acting within its wider enterprise ecosystem as FIWARE evangelist through dedicated workshops and the promotion of business cases. In its network of associates, MedITech has identified several SMEs that already develop solutions using FIWARE and that are working collaboratively to create an enlarged community that will use FIWARE platform in their businesses.
In addition to a mandate to enable the growth of SMEs through the adoption of Industry 4.0 technologies, MedITech has a duty to support the digitisation of public administration services. In this sense, it is already working closely with a few Municipalities in the framework of EU funded projects, facilitating their efforts in the adoption of big data-based solutions for smart city and mobility applications.

entityDescription:
Executive agency “Exploration and maintenance of the Danube river”, in accordance with Art 54 of the Administrative Law, is an administration to the Minister of Transport and Communications for providing administrative assistance to natural and legal persons, as well as carrying out activities and services related to ensuring safe navigation.
As an executive authority body the EAEMDR acts in the interest of society and in accordance with international commitments (obligations) entered into by the Bulgarian state, in compliance with the Belgrade Convention on navigation on the Danube, the Agreement between the governments of the Republic of Bulgaria and Romania regarding fairway maintenance and improvement in the Bulgarian-Romanian section of the Danube dated 13 February 1956, the Memorandum of Understanding on the development of common European transport corridor VII (Danube river).
EAEMDR operates under the Maritime Areas, Inland Waterway and Ports in the Republic of Bulgaria act, Administrative Law, Water Law, Rules of Procedure of EAEMDR and other legal acts.

entityDescription:
About DLR - Cutting-edge research from fundamental principles through to applications. DLR is the Federal Republic of Germany's research centre for aeronautics and space. It combines its scientific work and technological developments in these areas with its expertise in energy, transport, security and digitalisation. The German Space Agency at DLR plans and implements the national space programme on behalf of the federal government. Two DLR project management agencies oversee funding programmes and support knowledge transfer.
Climate, mobility and technology are changing globally. DLR uses the expertise of its 55 research institutes and facilities to develop solutions to these challenges. Our 10,000 employees share a mission – to explore Earth and space We conduct research and development activities in the fields of aeronautics, space, energy, transport, security and digitalisation. The German Space Agency at DLR plans and implements the national space programme on behalf of the federal government. Two DLR project management agencies oversee funding programmes and support knowledge transfer. and develop technologies for a sustainable future. In doing so, DLR contributes to strengthening Germany's position as a prime location for research and industry.

Locations
In total, DLR has 34 locations: Cologne (headquarters), Aachen, Aachen-Merzbrück, Augsburg, Berlin, Bonn, Braunschweig, Bremen, Bremerhaven, Cochstedt, Cottbus, Dresden, Geesthacht, Göttingen, Hamburg, Hanover, Jena, Jülich, Kiel, Lampoldshausen, Neustrelitz, Oberpfaffenhofen, Oldenburg, Rheinbach, Stade, St. Augustin, Stuttgart, Trauen, Ulm, Weilheim and Zittau. 
DLR also has offices in Brussels, Paris, Tokyo and Washington D.C.
Locations and offices in Germany and abroad: https://www.dlr.de/en/dlr/locations-and-offices 

DLR Executive Board
DLR is managed by its Executive Board. Since October 2020, Prof. Dr.-Ing. Anke Kaysser-Pyzalla has been Chair of the Executive Board, while Klaus Hamacher is Vice Chairman. The Executive Board also includes Prof. Dr. Karsten Lemmer, responsible for the Executive Board department "Innovation, Transfer and Research Infrastructure", and Dr. Walther Pelzer, responsible for the "German Space Agency at DLR" based in Bonn.

The ICMS is structured into five Research Units located in the Isla de la Cartuja building and an External Unit on the Reina Mercedes campus, Faculty of Physics.

entityDescription: GeSiM was founded 1995 as a spin-off from the Rossendorf Research Center. The company is a non-public and privately held entity. Building upon a broad expertise in micromachining technologies, GeSiM has evolved into a bioinstrumentation company focusing on submicroliter liquid handling instruments and microfluidics. GeSiM is specialized in liquid handling automation, microfluidics and micro contact printing. As a leading supplier of submicroliter dispensers GeSiM developed a unique design for piezoelectric pipetting tips, based on silicon-glass chips. The benchtop pipetting system Nano-Plotter runs up to 16 of these accurate dispensers and is mainly used as non-contact arrayer for microarrays, biochips and biosensors. Liquid handling by contact printing is available with the GeSiM micro-contact printers. These instruments transfer sample into tiny 2-dimensional patterns or generate 3-dimensional structures by Nano-Imprint-Lithography (NIL). Recent developments are focused on instrumentation for 3D printing of biocompatible materials, e.g bioscaffolds. Common 3D printers are usually not capable of processing biocompatible materials. The latest development is a compact synthesis station for radiochemistry, which combines liquid handling, solids handling, reaction engineering. These systems perform autonomously radio synthesis in commercial available hotcells on the basis of the GMP standards. Micro structuring methods are used to manufacture miniaturized fluidic components from silicon, glass, ceramics and PDMS to create products which cannot be made by conventional methods. GeSiM's specialty is the ability to offer complete tailor-made solutions to customers, including not only microfluidics, but also packaging, mechanics, macrofluidic engineering, and specialized control software (World-Chip Interface.

GeSiM is specialized in liquid handling automation, microfluidics and micro contact printing. As a leading supplier of submicroliter dispensers GeSiM developed a unique design for piezoelectric pipetting tips, based on silicon-glass chips. The benchtop pipetting system Nano-Plotter runs up to 16 of these accurate dispensers and is mainly used as non-contact arrayer for microarrays, biochips and biosensors. Liquid handling by contact printing is available with the GeSiM micro-contact printers. These instruments transfer sample into tiny 2-dimensional patterns or generate 3-dimensional structures by Nano-Imprint-Lithography (NIL). Recent developments are focused on instrumentation for 3D printing of biocompatible materials, e.g bioscaffolds. Common 3D printers are usually not capable of processing biocompatible materials. The latest development is a compact synthesis station for radiochemistry, which combines liquid handling, solids handling, reaction engineering. These systems perform autonomously radio synthesis in commercial available hotcells on the basis of the GMP standards. Micro structuring methods are used to manufacture miniaturized fluidic components from silicon, glass, ceramics and PDMS to create products which cannot be made by conventional methods. GeSiM's specialty is the ability to offer complete tailor-made solutions to customers, including not only microfluidics, but also packaging, mechanics, macrofluidic engineering, and specialized control software (World-Chip Interface.

CIL4Sys Engineering has developed Sim4Sys, a process and tooling that accelerate agile model based systems engineering. CIL4Sys applies this process to deliver efficient systems design services and proposes to supply the tooling, train the teams and support them as they apply the agile Sim4Sys process.
With Sim4Sys the engineers model the behaviors with UML, generate code with their models, control objects in a virtual world to verify the behavior described in their models and automatically generate the specifications of the behavior, consistent with their model descriptions.

At the heart of the toolchain is the tool used for UML design.To make it simple for engineers to built a UML model, existing tools have been customized. Only the useful menus are shown and some popup windows request information when needed, such that engineers are guided all along the design process.
Besides the design tool, Sim4Sys Virtual Bench offers a virtual environment in which the user can continuously "visualize" the resulting behavior of the logical design, thus allowing testing and validation. entityDescription:
Com&Sens bvba (Composites and Sensing) is a Spin-off company of the University of Ghent, Department of Material Science and Engineering. It is specialized in embedding fibre optic sensors in composite laminates and structures to monitor the development of (residual) strains inside the material. Monitoring in this, means using the response of the (embedded) sensors to judge on the quality of the component during processing of the material or the structure¿s integrity during its operation.
 The core asset of Com&Sens is its team of experts which can provide support across the complete process from composite fabrication up to the real use of the FRP components. 
 Com&Sens can act on different levels: research and experimental mechanics (material science), prototyping, development-trigger to take it to the next (industrial) level, technology partnership and/or link between academic research and applied composite industry.
 The company pursues to cooperate in close collaboration with the customer to develop the best-performing and most cost-effective solution.

entityDescription:
Norbite upcycles plastic waste into sustainable goods.

Norbite has developed a disruptive approach towards end-of-life polymeric materials for which there is no viable re-use or recycling solutions. Based on one specific insect,Galleria mellonella, the developed scalable process enables the insects to digest and transform plastics into proteins, lipids and biofertilizers.
Instead of disposal or incineration, the conventional end-of-life scenario in a linear plastic value chain, Norbite develops the technological and commercial foundations to allow residual polymeric materials e,g, packaging, textile, furniture, to be utilised as a food source for G. mellonella. As the larvae of the insect are refined for multiple high-value products, aimed to food & feed, and organic farming applications; the utilisation of plastic waste in this way gives it the opportunity to re-enter the economy.
The insect’s transformation capabilities mean the elimination of residual products in the plastic industry through their conversion into input material for another value-creating one i.e. industry symbiosis.

description: In INSIGHIO we accelerate IoT adoption, from conception to final product. We have developed a unique application-agnostic technology stack, supporting terrestrial - and soon - satellite IoT connectivity. We offer the necessary hardware, firmware and software to quickly build, test, deploy and scale new end-to-end IoT services in the field.
entityDescription:
At INSIGHIO we accelerate IoT adoption, from conception to final product, with a unique application-agnostic hardware and software technology stack. We help third parties to overcome the technological entry barriers which prevail today and are slowing down the IoT uptake. Relying on an in-house developed technology integrating terrestrial and satellite connectivity and a fast-track IoT applications design and implementation service, we solve one of biggest challenges in today’s new IoT projects, that is, the inadequate Proof-of-Concept during early stages. Thanks to a flexible and modular hardware, which is backed by a fully customizable firmware and Cloud software, INSIGHIO bridges the gap between prototyping and production, scaling an IoT deployment from a few nodes to hundreds of nodes, in a very short time frame. We foresee countless domains for our offering, e.g. precision agriculture, environmental monitoring, asset tracking, and alerting in remote oil, gas and construction industries.

We offer the following products & services:

- insigh.io Node: A generic IoT hardware device embedding multiple technologies used as a development board or in end applications
- insigh.io Platform: An end-to-end IoT software suite with many integrations taking care of all end-point and cloud functionalities
- insigh.io Service: A bundle of rapid IoT application design, prototyping and deployment, built on-top of the insigh.io stack

Our main customers are:

- Integrators & Solution providers who look for the core IoT building blocks
- Businesses in the need of IoT hardware/software to automate processes
- R&D groups requiring the proper IoT enablers to back their research work
- Any company/organization wanting to test a new IoT idea

A representative set of completed/ongoing projects are:
- Soil and environmental monitoring in remote farms for precision agriculture
- Beekeeping management optimization through beehives weight monitoring
- 24-h indoor air-quality assessment for smart post-COVID workspace control
- Connected weigh-scales to incentivize recycling and promote cyclic economy

entityName: DLR - EARTH OBSERVATION CENTER - GERMAN REMOTE SENSING DATA CENTER - NATIONAL GROUND SEGMENT (DLR DFD-NBS)
entityDescription:
German Remote Sensing Data Center, Neustrelitz, Department: National Ground Segment

The acquisition, processing and archiving of payload data from remote sensing and small-satellite science missions is handled by DFD’s National Ground Segment department in Neustrelitz. This work is undertaken as part of the German space program, commissioned by ESA or industry, or carried out in cooperation with international space agencies. In addition, the ground segment supports the German Space Operations Center by providing satellite command services, and it functions as a backup station for selected missions. Other responsibilities include the near-real-time processing of acquired data, which includes generating and distributing thematic information products, and operating the Calibration and Validation Test Site DEMMIN.
The Neustrelitz ground segment department employs engineers, physicists, mathematicians and technicians, most of whom are engaged in research and development. During more than 45 years of ground station operations the range of activity could be continuously expanded and further developed. Work focuses on the following areas:
- A permanent acquisition station for small earth observation and science satellites
- Automated round-the-clock operation of mission processing and archiving centres, (PAC), including near-real-time processing and data distribution
- Development of hardware components and software tools for acquiring, processing and archiving satellite data
Mastery of the entire chain from data acquisition to processing and final distribution makes high quality, homogenised data sets, free of systems artefacts and with high information content, quickly available to users through streamlined access procedures. User consultations and training play a large role. The National Ground Segment Department currently participates in over 10 national and international missions, including functioning as an ESA Earthnet receiving station for European earth observations missions, and it cooperates closely with a multitude of science and commercial partners and public authorities. Close cooperation among various DLR institutes and locations is also cultivated. For example, together with the Institute of Communication and Navigation in Neustrelitz the National Ground Segment operates the space weather service SWACI and works with the Neustrelitz Maritime Safety and Security Lab to facilitate safe maritime traffic and to protect the oceans. Also in the area of maritime safety there is close cooperation with the Remote Sensing Technology Institute team at the Bremen Maritime Safety and Security Lab.
Core expertise
- Designing and configuring components and processing chains for data reception
- Developing station software for monitoring and controlling tasks
- Designing and implementing test and simulation systems
- Planning and assembling real-time processing systems
- Constant operation of a real-time data centre in a multi-mission scenario 365 days/year, 24 hours/day
- Validation campaigns for terrestrial and maritime applications
- Management of earth observation data and long-term data archiving in the German Satellite Data Archive, a distributed system located at DFD in Oberpfaffenhofen and Neustrelitz
- DEMMIN Calibration and Validation Facility

Beetle ForTech (BFT) is a young R&D company in the timber tracing and forest data sector. The interdisciplinary start-up is characterized by specializations in the areas of timber-related technologies, data science, software development, UI/X and international timber markets.
Having roots in hardware and software development, BFT is developing an end-to-end machine-based timber tracing and certification system, making each harvested log automatically traceable the exact origin of growth, ultimately enabling regenerative forest management on a global scale – an innovative approach for which BFT was awarded 1st place for Galileo Masters AUT 2021 and 1st place for Copernicus Masters AUT 2021. The company is entering business incubation by ESA BIC Austria in August 2022.

entityDescription:
The company ROEZ R&D is technology company, which was established alongside ROEZ, s.r.o. for the tasks of industrial development.
The ROEZ R&D company participates in tasks and projects increasing energy efficiency, saving resources and finances, as well as in industrial development with the ambition of regional leadership with the possibility of added value and competition with its own technologies in the world.
The focus of the company's research and development activities is primarily oriented on the area of energy, petrochemical, and mechanical industries, with each project being based on three main pillars:
1) Environmental balance
2) Industry for the 21st century
3) Minimization

All three pillars have the same weight in our values and are our main benchmark in the development of new products. In our opinion, the combination of these three pillars is key to the correct direction of development in industrial production. Minimization of products thanks to modern technologies, simulations and analyzes brings a lower price, faster production, but also savings of the necessary material and thus a reduction of the environmental burden.

We are technology company with own technologies for ammonia manufacturing from green hydrogen, low potential heat utilization to electric energy and special hard-faced welding for nuclear power plant valves.
In additional to the technologies themselves we are ready to offer our expertise and experience in area of analyses and testing (computational fluid dynamics and strength analyses via finite element method in combination with experimental results). We are indirect partner for hydrogen storage for aerospace and IPCEI project. Besides we are designers and manufacturers of pressure equipment (reactors) for nuclear, oil and gas industry. High demands on expertise and quality of work in nuclear fields (we are certified in this area) simplifies transfer to other industrial fields, for example for space.

entityDescription:
MedSoftOrg Ltd. is a research and development team, found in 2001. 
Have been acting to integrate remote sensing technology into different public administration systems dealing with innovative development projects over the last 20 years. Deep experience of understanding the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP), the challenges of rural development and higher-level integration of new technological solutions linked to Earth Observation. 

Over 20 years of practical experience in development of: 
- remote sensing applications, 

- geographical information systems for direct payment control and management, 

- spatial databases for managing area based direct payments under the supervision of the EC, 

- Development, management and quality assurance of physical block-based Land Parcel Identification System (LPIS), control with remote sensing (CwRS) of area based direct payments of the EC.

- Quality Assurance System following ISO and EC-Joint Research Center definitions, to verify how member states are complying with the EU requirements, 

- GIS modules for the Integrated Administration and Control System (IACS-GIS) for paying agencies. 

Experience and motivation in Earth observation, especially analyzing by remote sensing land cover and land use changes in relation to agri-environmental systems in their temporal aspects. Integrating agricultural land use and social-economical models targeting integrated planning to support strategic decisions in our ever-changing environment.
Designing rural development and greening-linked strategies, based on land use aspects, integrating new technologies, enforcing data sharing and data use concepts in Public Administration. 
Enforcing remote sensing image processing techniques to introduce the monitoring approach in relation to Checks by Monitoring and Area Monitoring System of the new performance-based CAP, which brings a fundamental paradigm shift both into planning the agri-environmental policy and into the direct payment management system.

entityName: IMEDEA - Instituto Mediterráneo de Estudios Avanzados (CSIC-UIB)
entityDescription: The Mediterranean Institute for Advanced Studies (IMEDEA) was established in 1986 in Mallorca as a partnership between the Spanish National Research Council (CSIC) and the University of the Balearic Islands (UIB). IMEDEA is a public research centre dedicated to advance and share key scientific understanding of the global processes of planet earth and the beings that inhabit it, with particular focus on marine, coastal and insular systems. Its activities hinge on a sustained commitment to excellence, interdisciplinary science, and education for the benefit of society and the environment. The unique geographic placement provides superb opportunities for integrative studies of Mediterranean ecosystems and the research portfolio of IMEDEA bridges the gap that generally compartmentalizes marine and terrestrial institutes, or different disciplines, and spans the continuous spectrum of Mediterranean ecosystems emphasizing interdisciplinary research approaches to ecology, biodiversity, natural history, oceanography, and global change. Today IMEDEA is a reference centre for the national and international scientific community as well as for the environmental agencies of the Balearic Islands. Attracting talent and contributing to the training of the new generations of scientists, IMEDEA is on a successful path to lead in the study of Mediterranean ecosystems and their response to natural and human-induced variability.

EOX is a geospatial engineering and service company based in Austria, a non-startup, founder-managed business.
EOX creates Open Source software and tools to allow people to consume geospatial data in the cloud and on the Web.
EOX focuses on getting the most value out of the vast amount of the data acquired by Earth observation satellites.
EOX furnishes software and cloud infrastructure services to selected customers in geoscience and European government organizations.
Feel free to contact us anytime, we’re looking forward to hearing from you.
entityDescription: EOX IT Services GmbH is a young, innovative company, combining interdisciplinary skills with specialized know-how for providing spatial observation information technology solutions. The main area of EOX activities concerns the development and advancement of e-Environment and geo-spatial information infrastructures with special emphasis placed on satellite Earth Observation systems and next generation applications. EOX is strongly aligned and committed towards utilizing Open Standards, open software systems, and Web services (in EOX's main field these are those in accordance with OGC, W3C, ISO, CEOS und ESA). EOX has been founded in the year 2008 as a Management Buyout/Spin-Off of then ten year long operating "Intelligent Infrastructures and Space Applications" department belonging to the Austrian Research Centers GmbH (ARC), Austria's largest Contract Research Organization. The EOX shareholders and co-founders in person are also the key staff members operating the company in full independence. EOX is a partner of choice in major European environment monitoring and space programs for research and development among which the European GMES and SEIS initiatives are the most important ones. EOX has also a consumer mass market orientation by offering development services for integrated applications of remote sensing, satellite positioning and mobile communication. The EOX Team has proven records related to its capability to manage IT projects, its practice in quality assurance and its experience with a wide range of tools in the information technology and communication domain. EOX gathers internationally well known experts in the fields of Geospatial Data Infrastructures, online Earth-observation and GIS services, Web-based information and factual data user services, as well as standards for international interoperability. Strong personal affiliations exist with related system developments in international organizations (CEOS, OGC, ISO, ESA, EEA, EC JRC, IAEA, etc.) and with numerous projects implementing decision support services in geospatial and regional planning domains.

Main activities:
Development of advanced innovative products characterizing Earth atmosphere and surface
Hardware development: ground-based instruments and satellite payloads for remote sensing applications
Consulting on diverse topics of the remote sensing.
The company collaborates with public and private environmental organizations worldwide, universities and space agencies (ESA, EUMETSAT, NASA, JAXA). entityDescription:
Fundação Gaspar Frutuoso, FP (FGF) is a non-for-profit public Foundation of private law, which is governed by its statutes and, in the omissive cases, by specific legal provisions in Portuguese law. FGF was created in 1999 as an initiative of a single organ settlor, the University of the Azores (UAc), with the purpose, in close collaboration with the UAc, to take over as core competencies the promotion, support and execution of scientific research activities, technological, cultural and economic development, training, consultancy and dissemination, promotion initiatives that enhance cooperation between the UAc and other national or foreign entities, especially those that contribute to the strengthening of its involvement in the community and, in general, support and develop any initiative which falls within the aims and activities of the University. Later on, in 2004, was recognized and granted public utility status under dispatch by the President of the Azores Regional Government and renewing it in 2013. FGF acts as the front institution for scientific collaboration of multiple research groups. Many of R&D activities are developed with international teams and with both national and international funding.
FGF is also the management structure responsible for financial and formal project management tasks (including contractual documents, organization of report distribution and archiving, financial records, cost claims, service acquisitions and scholarships, among other aspects). All the research and services are carried out by University researcher’s staff or human resources contracted by FGF strictly on their behalf.

Founded in 2006, CVIS International is an established HPC partner in R+D, providing HPC architecture design, hardware delivery, implementation services, managed services and support for new and existing HPC clusters – including onsite HPC clusters, cloud-based clusters and hybrid forms. With a strong network of technology partners including Microsoft and Bright Computing, CVIS has successfully implemented dozens of HPC clusters, many of which it still manages today. At CVIS, our main aim is to help R+D organizations shorten their ‘Time to Insight’, so they can accelerate scientific discoveries. CVIS acts as a single point of contact for R+D organizations in terms of the management of their HPC resources. This gives R+D professionals more time to focus on their core business and become more adept at using their HPC cluster, as opposed to spending time performing tasks that are not directly related to their profession, such as keeping the HPC infrastructure operational.

The Fraunhofer Institute for Systems and Innovation Research ISI conducts applied research in seven Competence Centers with a total of 28 Business Units and sees itself as an independent institute for society, politics and industry. Our expertise in the area of innovation research is based on the synergy of the technical, economic and social science knowledge of our staff members. In our work we apply not only a broad spectrum of advanced scientific theories, models, methods and social-science measurement instruments, but continually develop them further, utilizing the empirical findings from the research projects conducted.
On behalf of our customers we investigate the scientific, economic, ecological, social, organizational, legal and political framework conditions for generating innovations and their implications. We use scientifically based analysis, evaluation and forecasting methods. Our assessments of the potentials and limitations of technical, organizational or institutional innovations help decision-makers from industry, academia and politics in making strategic decisions and thus assist them in creating a favorable environment for innovations. Thus Fraunhofer ISI one of the leading innovation research institutes in Europe.

entityDescription:
UNIWA was founded in March 2018 by the National Law 4521. The foundation of the newly established University came from the merging process of the former Technological Educational Institute of Athens and Piraeus University of Applied Sciences. In 2019, the National School of Public Health joined the newly established university.
UNIWA operates with high educational and research standards and strives to respond to the ever-increasing demands of a modern society for the creation of executives that have attained a solid scientific and technological background.

Today, UNIWA includes twenty-seven departments, organized into six Schools, covering a wide range of disciplines. The School of Public Health, the School of Management, Economics and Social Sciences, the School of Food Sciences, the School of Health and Welfare Sciences, the School of Applied Arts and Culture and the School of Engineering. The Schools’ fields of study cover a wide range of modern science, including social, administrative and economic sciences, engineering sciences, health and welfare sciences, food sciences and art studies.

The newly established university is the third largest in the country in terms of student numbers. It has approximately 52,000 undergraduate, 1,150 postgraduate and 210 doctoral students. UNIWA has expanded to three Campuses within the metropolitan region of ​​Athens. The Egaleo Park Campus lays in the administrative boundaries of the Municipality of Egaleo, surrounded by the streets Milou, Agiou Spyridonos, Dimitsanis, and Edessis. The Ancient Olive Grove Campus is also located in the Municipality of Egaleo, on Petrou Ralli and Thivon Streets, on the border of the historic Athens Olive Grove, where Ancient Athenian Philosophers gave academic lectures. Finally, the Athens Campus is located in the Municipality of Athens on Alexandras Avenue and is housed in the premises of the former National School of Public Health in a building of particular historical value that underwent restoration works a few years ago. The operation of the institution is supported by its highly-qualified and experienced administrative staff.

description:
Kinéis operates a satellite constellation providing global coverage connectivity services (data transmission capacities, bidirectional) optimized to the internet of the things: small and cheap devices that can be easily deployed in wide geographic areas. 
Our advantages: 
-Global coverage with no white spots
-Small data packets (typically 24 bytes, to optimize on low energy consumption, but bigger packages are also possible)
-Low energy consumption: 100-250 mW for data transmission = long autonomy on small battery
-Ease of integration into any IoT device: small form factor modems (2cm x 3cm x 2 mm), UART interface and AT commands
-Ease to hybridize with terrestrial networks (LPWAN, 3GPP, etc)
-Low cost: modems about 15-30 euros, airtime about 1 to 5 euros per month and device
-Bidirectionality, a downlink is available to remotely configure the devices 
Kineis sells modules (modems, the electronic components that are the heart of all devices that use the Kineis network); and provides and operates IoT connectivity by satellite. Integrators (VAMs, Value Added Manufacturers) can easily embed Kinéis modems in any device; this is used to transmit small amounts of data (typically 24 bytes) to the satellite and then back to the ground and the end-user (server, user platform, etc.). A downlink can be used to send commands remotely to the devices. Uplink messages typically include position information as well as other sensors such as, temperature, engine status, etc... The use of the Kineis network will incur a charge, typically 2-3 dollars a month for a few messages a day. 
Kinéis also provides doppler geolocation directly calculated by our satellites, without the need for any GNSS chipsets. Precision is lower than GNSS (several hundreds of meters), but for many applications this precision is good enough and saves a GNSS chipset in the device and the high energy cost of GNSS usage. 
The following markets are just some examples of those that can be addressed by the Kineis VAMs/VARs: 
-Transport and logistics
-Maritime (small fishing boats, etc)
-Smart agriculture: soil conditions monitoring, irrigation infrastructures, forestry conditions and grow monitoring, pest control… 
-Personal safety
-Smart farming (cattle monitoring, extensive farming)
-Infrastructure applications
-Energy management and Smart metering
-Environmental monitoring and science, oceanography, meteorology
-Military applications
-Fishing industry 
These vertical markets are addressed by specialized VARs/VAMs and all require some form of global connectivity provided by Kineis. 
With respect to our competitors on the IoT satellite market (Hiber, Myriota, Astrocast, Swarm, etc), we have the advantage of our long experience: the current Argos (Kinéis) constellation has been operated for 40 years; the technology is mature, and all initials problems at the beginning of the learning curve have been solved decades ago. We guarantee a high quality service and client support. 
Kinéis is currently working in the preparation of the launch of our next 25 nanosatellites in the 1st semester 2023; this will strongly improve performances, introduce new low-energy consumption modulations, etc.

entityDescription: Delivering high-standard MSc courses in a wide context of mechanical engineering related different majors and specializations is considered a primary task of this Faculty. Therefore, BSc training was primarily tailored – in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Energy Engineering and Industrial and Product Design branches – to properly prepare students for further education in MSc, then, in certain cases even further, to PhD training, generally speaking, for life-long learning and continuous renewal of their knowledge. BSc courses of the Mechanical Engineering Faculty transfer knowledge and competences certified by a diploma, issued by the Faculty at the end of the first cycle of education that enables students to enter any MSc training in mechanical engineering offered in Europe or in any well-developed industrial regions of the world. Taken all round, by all representatives of the industry, it is qualified the most prestigious Hungarian diploma in engineering. Accordingly, the Faculty invites the most talented students attracted by this profession to its courses directly connected to mechanical engineering and integrating diverse engineering fields. The goals specified in our mission are attained in cooperation with the students in an environment that preserves the traditional values of our University education, and sensitively follow the rapid changes in science and technology. Active relationships in training and research with dominant higher educational institutions of mechanical engineering in Europe are of top priority for the Faculty. This helps MSc students and enables PhD students to start building a network of international relations as early as in their university years. Determining elements of the above are our international relations that comprise reception of foreign students, our MSc training, in particular majors, open to the world, BSc and MSc courses conducted in English and international students exchange agreements. A traditionally strong element of training at all levels is the solid background in mathematics and interdisciplinary natural sciences necessary for mechanical engineering tasks. Similarly, laboratory work offering practical insight into major fields of mechanical engineering jobs is also essential. The Faculty maintains fruitful contacts to other engineering faculties of BME that historically outgrew of mechanical engineering foundations. The Faculty intends to be a driving force and initiator of interdisciplinary training programmes in a steadily changing industrial and economic environment. BSc and MSc courses in Energy Engineering, Mechatronics, Industrial and Product Design are demonstrative examples of this approach. Research at this Faculty is strongly related to the current needs of the local and global economy. As part of its mission, the Faculty works on basic research fields where new perspectives can be opened up for industry via participating in Hungarian and international projects, respectively. Mid-term research cooperation with companies directly interested in research, development and innovation, the involvement of these companies in our long-term basic research projects with their directions jointly set, as well as the transfer of the latest internationally competitive scientific knowledge and technological development trends are of similarly outstanding significance for our Faculty. Finally, as a national centre of mechanical engineering, the Faculty is permanently available for the industry with its professional know-how and competence to support quick and effective solutions of practical engineering problems requiring non-standard approach or deeper expertise than usual.

description:
In Anzen Engineering we provide RAMS analysis for our customers. 
We are highly specialized in reliability and safety analysis, counting with highly qualified professionals with several years of working experience in the aerospace and defence sectors. 
Our activities span from support to systems engineering tasks, mainly with the application of model based systems engineering (MBSE) methodology and tools; to detailed system safety assessment. 
Anzen is also developing a Model Based Safety Analysis framework to improve quality and reduce human effort in safety and reliability analysis. This framework connects the disciplines of system engineering and RAMS and allows to perform automated safety and reliability analysis directly from the model based representation of the system.

description: ENBIO specialises in the application of thermal control coatings for space satellites and REACH compliant primers for space and aerospace application. ENBIO also provides testing and analytical laboratory services for the space sector, including thermal vacuum testing services, thermo-optical characterisation, chemical and mechanical test services and environmental ageing services. ENBIO’s proprietary CoBlast coating technology provides innovative permanent metal surface transformations. ENBIO’s first thermal control coating, SolarBlack, was the fastest adopted technology in ESA history and became mission critical for a large number of parts on the Solar Orbiter spacecraft, including the primary heat-shield. ENBIO’s second thermal control coating, SolarWhite, was developed in collaboration with University College Dublin in 2011 and is also used on the Solar Orbiter radiator assembly panels. ENBIO’s technical team includes a core of dedicated research and production engineers supported by contracted advisors. The team has the skills and experience to develop technologies from basic research stages right through to final TRL level and production. ENBIO has two locations—the head office with R&D labs are in Dublin, Ireland and the dedicated Space Technologies Centre is in Clonmel, Ireland. The ENBIO Space Technologies Centre in Clonmel, Tipperary was funded by ESA and is ENBIO’s centre of excellence for the production of thermal management treatments for satellites, spacecraft, and space related hardware. The R&D labs house a number of coating enclosures for treatment of simple and complex geometries. To support the R&D work, ENBIO have developed extensive in-house material characterisation facilities.
entityDescription: ENBIO offers the space and aerospace sector a range of proprietary next-generation thermo-optical-mechanical surfaces and coatings. ENBIO's surfaces and coatings are applicable to a wide range of typically metal substrates, including titanium, aluminium, Inconel, stainless steel and precious metal alloys. Its base technical process platform is chemical-free, dry and operates at both ambient pressure and temperature, with no thermal input required into either substrate or dopant material. Uniquely, a robust and highly durable chemical bond is achieved between substrate and induced surface/coating. Examples of our extremely stable thermo-optical offerings include SolarBlack (a high alpha and high epsilon surface) and SolarWhite (a low alpha and high epsilon coating). ENBIO are also developing a REACH compliant adhesive primer for Space and Aerospace alloys through H2020 (OSMOSIS; ref 757088) and achieved equivalent or better performance than commercial conversion and anodise treatments. ENBIO also provide thermal design and thermal vacuum testing services to the space sector. For more details, visit our website.

ATLANT 3D Nanosystems is a Danish deep tech company founded in 2018 and a global pioneer
combining unique advanced technologies to enable first-ever atomic
layer 3D printing. 
The company was founded by Dr. Maksym Plakhotnyuk, Ivan Kundrata, and Prof. Dr. Julien Bachmann
with a vision to enable on-demand micro and nanoelectronics manufacturing atom by atom on Earth and beyond. 

ATLANT 3D™ state-of-the-art technology is based on a unique microfluidics chemical reactor, 
named micronozzle,
mounted on a dynamic platform that allows selective area direct atomic layer processing
with more than potential 450 different
materials (for terrestrial applications) with atomic resolution. 
ATLANT 3D™ platform technology is applicable across various industries and domains, such as advanced materials,
sensing and actuating,
printed electronics and RF devices, neuromorphic and quantum devices, etc.
The company received significant government support and recognition on a global level.

entityName: CSEM SA. Centre Suisse dElectronique et de Microtechnique SA
entityDescription: CSEM is a private, non-profit research and technology organization and a Swiss innovation accelerator—a catalyst for the transfer of technologies and know-how from fundamental research to industry. It delivers unique advanced technologies to the industrial sector, thereby reinforcing the sector’s competitive advantage. Supported by federal and cantonal authorities CSEM bridges the gap between academic findings and industrial requirements. CSEM’s research strategy is built around five strategic programs: 1. Microsystems technology—Design, integration, and packaging of devices that sense and monitor our environment and aspects of our daily lives, exploring new frontiers at the interface of nanotechnologies, materials science, and biotechnologies and delivering enhanced performance, miniaturization, and new properties. 2. Systems engineering—An application-oriented interdisciplinary program with a special emphasis on system integration, systems engineering aggregates different components and subsystems designed to collaborate and deliver targeted functionality, taking into consideration resource limitations (in terms of processing and power consumption), reliability, production cost, maintenance, and environmental conditions. 3. Ultra-low-power integrated systems—A strong focus on analogue and mixed IC design as well as wireless communication and vision technologies, the key technologies required to build very-low-power, wirelessly interconnected, embedded smart systems or remote sensing nodes. Surface engineering—Focuses both on the novel properties of engineered surfaces and interfaces, to deliver breakthrough surface effects, and on their “up compatible” manufacturing processes, to bridge the gap to industrial applications. 4. Photovoltaics & energy management—Development, covering the full chain from prospective PV cell and module technologies through fully integrated energy systems, where energy efficiency and management is delivered by intelligent hardware and algorithms. CSEM has been involved in space business for ESA for more than 30 years. It provides a broad range of high-tech systems and sub-systems for the design, manufacturing, assembly, integration and testing of spaceborne and ground-segment equipment and components. Traditionally CSEM is well known by the space community for its developments of precise mechanisms and scientific instrumentation for space. However, it is also providing outstanding systems in other fields, enumerated below: • Atomic clocks • Flash imaging LiDAR • Robotics, control engineering, firmware • Micro-sensors, MEMS and MOEMS (from design to small volume production and reliability) • Biomedical engineering (integrated sensors, telemedicine) • Life support and habitation systems at the ISS • Telecommunication (intra-satellite wireless communication, antenna miniaturisation, etc ) A comprehensive multi-disciplinary space programme is performed in cooperation with a network of European companies, universities and research centres. In order to best serve the space sector, close relationships are maintained with ESA, the Swiss Space Office and the European Commission.

entityDescription:
ANAXAM is a technology transfer center and enables industry to benefit from state-of-the-art analytical methods using neutron and synchrotron radiation (X-rays). This means analytics of materials far beyond the laboratory scale. 

ANAXAM offers the flowing analytical technologies: Imaging, Diffraction, Scattering and Spectroscopy. 

At the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI) in particular, the center enables the use of these technologies, which were originally developed for basic research, but are now also available for industrial challenges. Our synchrotron analytics provide new insights, since the flux of photons delivered by the synchrotron source is higher by a huge factor of 10 billion (10 000 000 000) than that delivered by laboratory-scale X-ray sources. Our neutron analysis is only possible at large research facilities in the first place and is not available in any form on a laboratory scale. Due to the dimension of these facilities, which we use for our analytical methods, it is understandable that our services go far beyond the laboratory scale and the associated possibilities. Moreover, they are unique in Switzerland. This is what material analytics far beyond the laboratory scale means to us: We break through the boundaries of materials analytics with the help of neutron and synchrotron radiation!

ANAXAM has set itself the goal of supporting industrial customers throughout the life cycle of their products and processes with its analytical competencies such that they can offer innovative and high-quality products on the market. For this purpose, ANAXAM offers material analytics far beyond the laboratory scale. The analytics offer the focus on product and process optimization, quality control, quality assurance and downstream tests in the advanced manufacturing process of these products.

Basically, ANAXAM pursue two different models of cooperation: On the one hand, service projects, in which we work with industrial or academic customers on a purely service basis. This means that we offer our customers from consulting and measurements to the analysis and interpretation of the results from a single source. In this way, our customers benefit from the most modern analytical methods in the fields of imaging, diffraction and spectroscopy to solve the challenges they face. On the other hand, development projects, in which we are working together with our partners within the framework of a project on the development of new tailor-made infrastructures. These enable realistic experimental conditions for the execution of experiments. A tailor-made infrastructure could either an apparatus that allows the investigation of samples in real time under different environmental conditions such as temperature or pressure. Or they are, for example, automated sample manipulators, which allow a higher sample throughput possible. This then leads to more efficient use of the available beam time and the standardization of results. Such developments are co-funded by ANAXAM and industrial or academic partners contribute to the project costs either in the form of a monetary or an in-kind contribution. The developed infrastructures are then also available for use in other/later service projects for other customers. Examples of successful projects one can find online on the ANAXAM webpage https://www.anaxam.ch/en/customer-projects

entityDescription:
MARKOPOULOS ENERGY&MECHATRONIC SYSTEMS LTD is active in two main business. In the Renewables (PV Solar Tracking) Sector under the brandname "DegerHellas" our company has installed allover Greece and Cyprus 5000 Solar Tracking Systems for PV installations using active sun following sensors. DegerHellas site iswww.degerhellas.gr. In the electronics and motioncontrol/sensors industry our company is active under the brandname "ZEROONE" (www.01mechatronics.com),
ZEROONE LTD: “Driven by your requirements”. This section of our company is involved in Space Related Projects.
ZEROONE seeks to design and develop products and services using embedded and robotic technology. To deliver more for less by incorporating cutting edge technologies into complicated, customer specific “turn key” solutions. Professionalism, innovation, agility, fidelity, and accountability define ZEROONE. These capabilities enable us to offer unique solutions to meet specific customer requirements.

In July 2014 we were finalists in the Enterpreneurship Workshop organized by the European Union - Robotics, Innovalia, and Robolution Capital in Rovereto, Italy, in March 2014, for a product proposal developed by our company. Then ZEROONE introduced a new generation of miniature digital motor controllers, as well as the accompanying microprocessor development boards 01TM Supermodified for servos and motors up to 5Amp @ 24V, to the global market. Supermodified introduces a new step in RCservo technology, providing accurate and low-cost motion control, communication, and programmable facilities that were previously only available in expensive motor drivers and controllers, as well as in other expensive components. Development boards for a variety of architectures, as well as a variety of data collecting modules, are also available. Furthermore, our product MagEnc LowRev is a magnetic absolute encoder with a resolution of 32768 ticks per revolution, which is a significant improvement over the industry standard.

As a result of this evolution and numerous customer requests, we came up with the idea of providing to our customers and the global electronics and prototyping community a ZEROONE's technology is a new philosophy on how to build FAST and FLEXIBLE controllers that are EASY to integrate into robotics projects, which we named "Driven by your requirements." The PID velocity/position control system with a 15-bit absolute magnetic encoder operates over an infinite 360° range for DC brushed motors up to 24V @ 5Amps in a tiny form factor, but is extremely powerful and can revolutionize robotics prototype and IoTproduct development.

Since then we have marketed and distributed our products succesfully together with our innovative knowledge in automation and have more than 500 customers worldwide. Among others:
DLR German Aerospace Center, Aerosimulators BV (R&D Department),Sailrocket LTD, Goalcam LLC, Magnetdrives AG, Uni. Heidelberg (Ziti Automation),National Technical University of Athens, Probotics BV. ,Eccomotion BV, BMW, ROBOTEQ Inc, FIBERQA LLC, Salvagione Design, Energid Technologies

The Faculty of Maritime Studies in Split was founded in 1959. Originally, it began its activities as Maritime College, while since 2004 it has been functioning as the Faculty of Maritime Studies of the University of Split.
In the course of its development, the path was not always smooth. Several studies have been developed which have been recognised on the labour market both in Croatia and worldwide. The students of the Nautical department, Marine engineering, and Marine electrical engineering and information technologies have been recognised as professionals easily finding work opportunities on shore and on board vessels. In this undertaking we are helped by our students cherishing their love of the sea, teachers with the appropriate scientific-teaching titles, but also our partners from Croatia and abroad recruiting our students.
The students of Marine yacht and marina technologies as well as those of Maritime management are oriented towards maritime industry, i.e. maritime market and nautical tourism. Through EU projects, we have recognised their qualifications for the Croatian and EU labour market.
Education at the Faculty is carried out at undergraduate and graduate levels. Since 2019 we have also begun to deliver postgraduate study. In the process of education teachers in the scientific-teaching and vocational titles (officer ranks), lecturers from economy, profession, as well as colleagues from abroad take part.
Included into the education process are our students, ex-students (Alumni) and clients (teaching bases) who help us update our programmes in accordance with the latest trends in maritime affairs. Teaching is carried out using modern equipment consisting of simulators, didactic equipment, well-equipped library, computers for CBT, and video material and e-learning facilities. Teaching also takes place on board school ships, sailboats, Faculty laboratories, workshops exterior to the Faculty, etc.
Due to successful education of maritime personnel, we have been recognised by the Japanese system of education and training in maritime affairs (Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Traffic of Japan and Japanese Shipowner Association).
Our education process has been recognised by the international Accreditation Committee of the Agency for Science and Higher Education –AZVO.
Our training and education of seafarers is aligned with the requirements of the Ministry of the Sea, Traffic and Infrastructure, and in compliance with the requirement we have developed the quality management system ISO 9001.
We are members of IAMU (International Association of Maritime Universities) with whom we have aligned our curricula.
Due to our experience in the education of high-quality maritime personnel, the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia has entrusted us with initiation in 2018 of the education of cadets for the Croatian Army, Coastguard of the Republic of Croatia, Ministry of the Interior, and NATO partners of the Republic of Croatia. The cadets are educated at the integrated studies of naval nautical studies and naval marine engineering.
Our scientific research work is disseminated through our international scientific conference IMSC - International Maritime Science Conference, and international scientific journal ToMS - Transactions on Maritime Science. The scientific research work is carried out within projects tendered by the European Union, projects by the Republic of Croatia, and internal projects.
Teaching at the Faculty is delivered in Croatian and responding to the needs of the Erasmus students in the English language. Starting with 2020, we are planning to initiate teaching in English.

entityDescription:
With almost 30 years of know-how in the energy industry, over 100 customers in 15 countries and 150+ successful projects, HAKOM has positioned itself as a strong and sought-after partner of the energy industry. Since 1991 HAKOM has been following its successful path steadily and successfully and is a reliable and innovative partner for its customers.

The smallest components of matter are elementary particles, the smallest elements of the energy industry are data with time stamps, collected in time series. The further we look into the future, the more important time series become for the energy industry and those who depend on it –Smart City, Industry 4.0, Agriculture 4.0, Smart Metering, IoT, autonomous driving or 5G mobile networks are just some of the buzzwords that will change our world forever. Tomorrow. There, time-stamped data will be the lowest common denominator, the elementary particles of the energy industry collected in time series to control and link complex systems. Without the management of time series at all levels, our modern world will no longer function technically.

This current and booming market of the future is HAKOM's core business, making the elementary particles of the energy industry controllable and creating added value. Enrich data with time stamps so that numbers become values. This is HAKOM's sought-after competence.

The challenges in the area of time series management, in a disruptive market environment such as the energy industry, are enormous. In order to master them, it takes decades of expertise and a commitment to dedicate oneself exclusively to this highly complex subject with passion. The ability to validate and monitor Big Data, to analyze Big Data, no matter from which local source, system environment, formatting or screening the data material may originate and to always deliver useful results in a short time in this process, requires an innovative basic technology like HAKOM:
Ingestion of Big Data at unbeatable processing speed,
full database independence,
proven energy logic,
perfect API for easy integration into 3rd party systems,

are some core premises. HAKOM has developed its proprietary FeasyUse® technology to ensure that the whole thing remains suitable for everyday use, intuitive and easy to use without having to compromise on quality or performance. Because ingenious is simple and not complex.

description: GeoCodis Information Systems is a private company specialising in software development in the field of remote sensing, water management, GIS and mobile network industry solutions. It provides cost-efficient SW applications to all kinds of businesses (www.geocodis.com). In the space sector, GeoCodis Ltd. developed a visualisation and analysis portal focused on surface water and flood areas utilising data gathered from Sentinel-1. Results of the radar satellite image analyses are integrated into the final portal www.vodakje.si which is regularly used by Slovenian Environmental Agency. This solution has Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA), developed REST API and WMS services that enable integration of data into other systems. GeoCodis was involved in the ESA-founded project Customised Earth Observation Services (using SOA). Several EO services for the detection of build-up areas and water bodies were developed for serving Word Bank needs in Sub Saharan Africa countries. GeoCodis developed a prototype system MLEO to use Sentinel-2 and other EO data for the creation of machine learning data samples and analysing satellite images using the U-Net model. Automatically generated products were already integrated into the water management project UPMIS in Uganda. GeoCodis is developing a web-based Utility Performance Monitoring and Information System (UPMIS) which uses internet-connected technologies like smartphones and network computers (using SOA). GeoCodis has several years of experience with the collection of GPS and utility data in the field. GeoCodis has an extensive library of its own programmed code snippets from other projects using Sentinel data (based on Sentinel HUB, ONDA or CREODIAS platform) that will be reused also in this project. Programming code is based on PHP, .NET C# and Python. The company employs experts in all mentioned programming languages. Their last achievement is machine learning U-Net based algorithm and other related operations for online detection of built-up areas in Sub Saharan Africa. This system is exploring Sentinel Hub services and API’s.

entityDescription: Micrima Limited is a company that originated out of Bristol University in 2007.It has developed a Radio-wave based technology for breast cancer detection.We expect to commercialise MARIA®in late 2022/early 2023.The tool will initially be deployed as a diagnostic adjunct to Mammography but ultimately, we are looking to deploy the technology for use as a automated breast cancer screening tool in remote and community settings.The use of radio waves overcomes the two main issues of the current predominant screening modality (Mammography) that has issues in denser breast tissue (which significantly impacts the sensitivity and specificity of the device in 40%-50% of the existing screening population and prevents the additional screening of younger women).In addition, Mammography uses ionising radiation which limits the frequency of use of the device, which can allow cancers to develop and spread outside the breast, which significantly reduces the chances of survival.

entityName: UNIVERSITEIT ANTWERPEN - LEIA-Lab for Equilibrium Investigations and Aerospace
entityDescription:
LEIA aims to perform pioneering research in the domains of the vestibular system and of spaceflight.
LEIA began with performing research on the use of various tests to evaluate the function of the vestibular organ for the purpose of routine clinical testing. As a logical next step, different research projects were initiated to increase our understanding of certain vestibular-related diseases and conditions. Currently, LEIA’s research focus entails (i) developinga treatment option for Mal de Débarquement Syndrome (MdDS) as one of the few centres in the world, (ii) investigating the effect of a otolith-vestibular implant to treat patients with severe bilateral vestibular function loss, (iii) using state-of-the-art magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)techniques to diagnose Ménière’s Disease, (iv) to test the outcome of the Balance Belt in chronic dizzy patients, and more.
The second domain of research entails the investigation of the effects of spaceflight on the vestibular system and on the brain. Because the vestibular organ fails to detect gravity-dependent head movements in a weightless environment, downstream functions of the vestibular system, such as gaze stabilisation, balance, orientation and navigation, are affected in this condition. LEIA’s research activities in the field of spaceflight include (i) the investigation of the effects of pharmaceutical treatments for (space) motion sickness on the vestibular organ, (ii) testing the vestibular organ function before and after long-duration spaceflight by means of centrifugation, currently in already 71% of the cosmonauts who have flown to the ISS, and (iii) running the first prospective MRI study in cosmonauts and astronauts to uncover various structural and functional changes to the brain in response to space missions.
With these research endeavours, LEIA aims to resolve various forms of dizziness and imbalance in patients and to address biomedical challenges for astronauts engaging in human space exploration missions.

entityDescription: SATIM is an industry leader in the automatic, Al-based detection and classification of objects on Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellite imagery, being recognized among the main players on the market. Since 2012, SATIM has been creating innovative and high-quality products and services, among others, in collaboration with the European Space Agency. ESA has funded 9 research and development projects with some of them primarily focused on SAR signatures simulation and Al-based object detection and classification. Within two projects with ESA (SATREC 1.0 and SATREC 2.0), SATIM has developed two innovative software packages for highly-accurate SAR signature simulation (SSIG software), and for automatic Al-based object detection and classification on SAR (OREC software). In OREC software, simulated SAR signatures are used to train Al models. This synthetic data is generated in SATIM's SAR simulator (SSIG). SSIG allows generating simulated SAR signatures of any 3D object and any SAR system. Using synthetic SAR signatures to train Al models, SATIM has the capabilities to provide near real time, highly accurate detection and classification of different objects on SAR data acquired from different SAR sensors. Moreover, SATIM’s AI models are specifically optimized for detecting and classifying a various of objects across multiple domains. The company has developed specialized AI models that can automatically detect and classify vessels with 110 different classes, aircraft with 18 classes, and vehicles with 8 classes. These models enable SATIM to provide detailed and precise object recognition, making it an invaluable partner for industries such as maritime surveillance, aviation monitoring, and ground vehicle tracking, where rapid and reliable data interpretation is crucial.

entityDescription:
Rheinmetall Norway AS has been an established player in the Nordic region for over half a century, located in Tønsberg, south of Oslo. The company cooperates closely with Norwegian and Swedish Armed Forces, developing capabilities for existing and future needs.
Rheinmetall Norway specializes in high-tech products for dismounted soldiers as well as sensor and observation systems, reconnaissance and fire control systems. These range from target acquisition systems, cameras, 40mm fire control system, weapon improvement and weapons mount products to advanced mortar systems. Mortar weapon system 81 mm has successfully been implemented with the Norwegian Armed Forces. A 120mm mortar system is developed and tested.
The company exports to more than twenty countries around the world. Furthermore, Rheinmetall Norway has a number of licensee’s around the world, most notably American Rheinmetall Systems which is a major sub-supplier of Rheinmetall Norway products for the US Common Remotely Operated Weapon Station (CROWS).
A first-rate engineering department keeps Rheinmetall Norway on the global cutting edge of defence-technology making it the ideal strategic partner for both, military users and defence industry, when it comes to developing new capabilities for the world’s armed forces.

entityDescription:
Quantum Blockchains Inc. is a startup aiming to create functioning Blockchain technology capable of resisting the currently emerging threats from Quantum Computers. The company is planning a radical step, and instead of post-quantum algorithms, it will use the latest achievements of quantum cryptography to create provably secure solutions, which enhance data protection, integrity and processing speed.
The startup is registered as a private limited company in the city of Lublin in Poland in the European Union. It’s headquarters are in Lublin and its secondary office is in the city of Lodz, Poland.
It currently employees five specialists: quantum information scientists and developers. Five company shareholders’ are also active in its development.
As for the mid of 2022 the company works on the core development of its quantum blockchain concept and implementation, on the software for hardware QRNG, quantum cryptography Knowledge Graph and on scientific foundations for the future quantum blockchains where quantum processes can redefine both security properties and consensus algorithms to elevate blockchains to the new dimensions of quantum processing.
