description:
WASDI is a cloud platform for Earth Observation (EO).
We help EO developers turn their algorithm into an operative service in the cloud, with just a drag & drop of their code. We call this Develop at Home, Deploy to the Cloud. Once their application is deployed, it can be executed from the web and, if the owners wish to, they can publish it in a marketplace, where end users can run them to solve their business needs. 
We currently support ENVI IDL, Python (both ananconda and pip), C#, JavaScript, Java and Octave. Moreover, WASDI also allows the execution of SNAP workflows (also known as SNAP graphs).
WASDI runs federated instances across multiple clouds and DIASes. For the user, this means exploiting data and services from different providers is very easy, without the burden of managing cloud technologies and protocols.
entityDescription:
WASDI SARL is a Luxembourgish startup aiming at democratising Earth Observation (EO). The company is a joint venture between Fadeout Software in Italy and the Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST).
The company runs the WASDI cloud platform that helps EO experts develop algorithms and turn them into applications in the cloud. Additionally, the platform allows them to publish their applications in a marketplace to reach end users. With a unified interface, seamless access to data, and online tools, WASDI allows professionals to concentrate on work that matters rather than grappling with IT-related difficulties.
On top of this enabling horizontal technology, the WASDI team develops vertical applications. In collaboration with world-class partners, the team developed several applications used in international initiatives in different areas (e.g. natural hazards, environmental monitoring, and urban areas). Vertical applications built with WASDI include the monitoring and mapping of floods, water bodies, drought risk, urban areas, fires & burned areas, impact assessment, oil spills, and air quality. These applications enabled innovative services such as parametric insurance.
Recently, WASDI launched its latest product, RISE - Remote Imaging Support for Emergencies, developed as part of the WFP’s Humanitarian Innovation Accelerator. RISE is a fully automated EO web platform designed to monitor areas vulnerable to natural hazards by leveraging remote sensing technology to provide historical data and near real-time monitoring of floods, drought risk, human settlements, and their impacts. The system is also built for future expansion to support the monitoring of additional hazards and models, such as forest fires, air quality, landslides, and deforestation.

entityName: DLR - RESPONSIVE SPACE CLUSTER COMPETENCE CENTER RSC³ (DLR RS)
entityDescription:
The use of navigation systems, bookings in stock trading to the split second, the almost centimeter-accurate control of huge container ships - all this would be inconceivable without space-based services.
This is all the more true for the military sector and applications in the field of security: Space-based systems are essential for the capabilities of the German Armed Forces, the “Bundeswehr”, and are generally essential in the security sector. The Bundeswehr's concept for the space domain states:
The security and functionality of a modern information society depend on unhindered access to space-based information and communication channels. The same applies to the operational capability and readiness of the Bundeswehr, which depends on space-based applications and satellite systems to fulfill its missions. Space is to be regarded as an operational domain.
To protect, repair, augment or further expand the critical infrastructure Space, the technical capability is required to launch new satellites with a wide variety of payloads into orbit and bring them into service within a few days or even hours. In the international military context, this is referred to as "Responsive Space Capability".
The Responsive Space Cluster Competence Center RSC³ at the DLR site in Trauen was established with the overall objective to setup the required technology base for a Responsive Space Capability and conducting technology demonstrations in a timely manner. For this purpose, technologies in the entire architecture, consisting of space, ground, launch and mission segments, are investigated and further developed. In line with the cluster concept, the competence center works in close cooperation with existing DLR institutes and facilities as well as with end users and industry.

Company description: The use of navigation systems, bookings in stock trading to the split second, the almost centimeter-accurate control of huge container ships - all this would be inconceivable without space-based services.
This is all the more true for the military sector and applications in the field of security: Space-based systems are essential for the capabilities of the German Armed Forces, the “Bundeswehr”, and are generally essential in the security sector. The Bundeswehr's concept for the space domain states:
The security and functionality of a modern information society depend on unhindered access to space-based information and communication channels. The same applies to the operational capability and readiness of the Bundeswehr, which depends on space-based applications and satellite systems to fulfill its missions. Space is to be regarded as an operational domain.
To protect, repair, augment or further expand the critical infrastructure Space, the technical capability is required to launch new satellites with a wide variety of payloads into orbit and bring them into service within a few days or even hours. In the international military context, this is referred to as "Responsive Space Capability".
The Responsive Space Cluster Competence Center RSC³ at the DLR site in Trauen was established with the overall objective to setup the required technology base for a Responsive Space Capability and conducting technology demonstrations in a timely manner. For this purpose, technologies in the entire architecture, consisting of space, ground, launch and mission segments, are investigated and further developed. In line with the cluster concept, the competence center works in close cooperation with existing DLR institutes and facilities as well as with end users and industry.

Located in Hamburg, the private and independent Hamburg Ship Model Basin - HSVA - is a service and consulting company for clients in the maritime industry worldwide.
Our products contribute to a greener, more sustainable usage of marine environments. We help reducing emissions from shipping and we increase safety in marine transportation.
We are partners to our clients for the development of innovative, tailor-made solutions in shipping and offshore operations. For experimental investigations we are offering world class testing facilities.
Its leading role in national and international research programs makes HSVA a most competent partner in science and services in the field of maritime hydrodynamics, maritime aerodynamics and arctic technology as well as associated disciplines.

description: Solar Foods produces protein using air and electricity. Solar Foods revolutionises food production with a method that is not dependent on agriculture, the weather, or the climate. Solar Foods stands as the first company to produce food by using air-captured CO2 in a continuous mode, including the preparation of the actual final food products. Solar Foods produces an entirely new kind of nutrient-rich protein, Solein®, by using air and electricity as its primary raw materials. Based on natural fermentation, this process revolutionises food production, as the production of Solein is non-dependent on the weather, climate, or agriculture. It is also a promising candidate for closed-cycle food production for long-duration human exploration missions.

Together with our clients and our extensive network of partners, we unlock the potential of our societies’ green transition.

entityName: Scuola Sant'Anna - Istituto di Intelligenza Meccanica (IIM)
entityDescription:
The Institute of Mechanical Intelligence (IIM) was established in May 2021 bringing together the two research groups of Scuola Superiore Sant’Anna working on Perceptual Robotics (PERCRO) and Advanced Optical Sensors, with the aim of developing hardware and software components of artificial systems and for studying their interactions with humans. 
IIM research stems from the vision that the emerging pervasiveness of the integration between physical and digital systems will soon call upon humans to share in their everyday life complex digital and physical environments with artificial entities, like robots, androids and virtual humans. The need to interact with these entities requires that research into their design and development be accompanied by a multidisciplinary study of their interaction with human beings. 
In this framework, the Institute of Mechanical Intelligence, based on the notion that the intelligence of an artificial system derives from the integration of hardware and software aspects, carries out interdisciplinary research, innovation activities and technology transfer into five areas: Human Robot Interaction, Intelligent Autonomous Systems, Extended Reality, Robotic Mechanisms and Materials, Optical Fiber Sensors and Integrated Photonic Subsystems.

DVOKUT-ECRO is a renowned company with extensive experience in Croatia and the wider region: Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Montenegro, Hungary, North Macedonia, Slovenia, Serbia, Kosovo, Turkey, and Ukraine.

The expertise of our employees and our references have enabled us to obtain the licence to preform professional tasks related to the preparation of expert input documents, EIA Screening reports and EIA studies in 1997 by the competent authority at the time, the National Directorate for Environmental Protection. That same year, our modern air quality monitoring equipment, the Mobile Ecologic Laboratory, qualified us for a licence to perform professional tasks in monitoring air quality and emissions into the air, and other expert tasks related to monitoring. 
In the meantime, as the regulations changed, we have responded to the opportunity to expand our range of services and consequently obtained licences to perform other professional activities. Today, DVOKUT-ECRO holds 25 licences for providing services in environmental and nature protection. Additionally, we offer to our clients the preparation of feasibility studies, design documentation, due diligence audits and reports.
We have been continuously investing in our team of thirty experts, and in most advanced equipment. This allows us to consistently expand our areas of activity, develop and offer new services for our clients in both private and public sectors.

entityDescription:
Lympik products are developed for the ski sport, in order to offer competitive athletes in this area the possibility to measure and analyze all their trainings. This gives them the opportunity to increase their performance. In the field of timekeeping for sports, the obsolete, extensive and complicated radio technology is currently mainly used. Therefore, these products are hardly used for training, but almost only for competitions.
What makes our system so unique is the use of satellite technology for accurate determination of time and location and the IoT technology for the sensors. That's why our solution is simpler, more accurate, more flexible and less error-prone. In addition, our devices are much smaller and lightweight through the use of these technologies.
Furthermore, we offer operators of ski resorts fixed, digitized tracks that can be used by the masses. A solution for ski schools complete the offer.
We provide our customers live results and what´s more a direct connection to social media. Thus, we connect the digital world with the physical.

entityDescription:
The Bavarian Red Cross (BRK) is a regional branch of the German Red Cross (GRC) and part of a worldwide movement assisting victims of conflict and disaster and people affected by social or health related crisis. The fundamental principles of the Red Cross Movement are Humanity, Impartiality, Neutrality, Independence, Voluntary Service, Unity and Universality. The Bavarian Red Cross is integrated into the German Civil Protection System and partner within different national and international research projects. 
The Bavarian Red Cross (DE-BRK) is the largest charity and disaster relief organisation in Bavaria. In the field of ambulance services the (DE-BRK) provides about 80% of the services with more than 4.300 professional paramedics, 8 integrated command centres (emergency call number 112), 2 rescue helicopters and 320 Rescue Station. Furthermore, the BRC is active in several areas of essential welfare services. About 120.000 volunteers from all sectors of services, such as the Mountain Rescue, Water Rescue and the Youth Red Cross provide about 4 million hours of service a year. In addition, the Bavarian Red Cross is involved in the crisis management in the COVID-19 situation. The Bavarian Red Cross Headquarters in Munich coordinates the requests and shares the relevant Information between all NGO and GO`s.

For this reason, the HCU offers the entire range of disciplines required for understanding and designing the urban environment: - Architecture, Civil Engineering, Geomatics, Urban Planning – in each case as a Bachelor’s degree with the option to continue studying to obtain a Master’s degree;
- Metropolitan Culture – as a Bachelor programme;
- Urban Design and Ressource Efficiency in Architecture and Planning (REAP) – as interdisciplinary Master’s degrees;
- A cross-curricular programme, inter- and transdisciplinary, complements the curriculum of the individual study programms at HCU.

entityDescription: Munich-based automation specialist Cevotec offers one of the world’s most advanced production systems for complex fiber composites. description: Pan Galactic Developments Ltd is a registered Limited company developing applications and blockchain for Space. Pan Galactic are specifically working in R&D to create a carbon negative blockchain using new consensus methods and their own pro-active environmental work. In addition to the network technology, Pan Galactic are also developing a suite of logistics and verification applications using blockchain and NFTs. Pan Galactic also provide a series of B2C applications to engage the imagination of everyday people to look to Space as a future destination to work, live, visit through DeFi applications and tokens, creating a viable and democratic Space currency system and decentralised exchange. Further work also includes working with a series of senior academics within the universities sector and leaders within the blockchain sector to develop useful solutions to a series of problems. Pan Galactic is already working with a number of Space colleagues on outreach on STEM education and Space with groups around the world.
entityDescription:
Pan Galactic Developments Ltd is a diverse UK Tech Start-up tasking itself with the development of future communicative Blockchain technologies for the Space industry which can also be applied on Earth.
Specifically Pan Galactic Developments is working to create a Blockchain network on which to host a series of our own native applications whilst providing our platform for others to use to contribute to solving commercial and logistical problems in Space. The Pan Galactic Blockchain being our biggest project to develop we also seek to create the first Space based blockchain which is Carbon Negative without sacrificing high performance speed and capacity.
In regards to our own native Space applications we are creating a series of logistics solutions to help Space Agencies and businesses to securely manage the full logistics journey, certification of provenance and tracking for items moving through the wider Space supply chain. We will also offer decentralised finance applications for use of Space Tourists and Residents to transact and make purchases within Space and the emerging space economy this will include non-custodial wallets applications and an optional digital currency system enabling users to make use of our native coin or other digital assets such as Central Bank issued Digital Currencies, Government Issued Digital Currencies and other Space related digital currencies giving the user the option of how to transact.
During the building phase of our Pan Galactic Blockchain technology we are working with Space partners on outreach and educational projects to inspire people to think about Space exploration and the future. entityDescription:
The Leibniz-Institut für Verbundwerkstoffe GmbH (IVW) is a nonprofit research institution of the state of Rhineland-Palatinate and the Technische Universität Kaiserslautern (TUK). It researches fundamentals for future applications of composite materials, which are of great importance for the mobility of the future, the fields of energy, climate and environment, production technology as well as for health care. New materials, construction methods and manufacturing processes are investigated and - after the basic understanding has been developed - tailor-made for the respective requirements.
The focus is on the entire process chain, from basic materials to characterization and simulation, from construction methods and production technology to component testing and recycling. New ideas and innovative concepts are not only an essential part of the research and further development of the institute, but also lead to spin-offs. Newly acquired knowledge is transferred, above all into science, but also into teaching, the interested public and industrial applications.
As a member of theLeibniz Association, the institute receives institutional grants in accordance with the AV-WGL for the joint financial support of institutions by the federal and state governments (federal share 50%, share of the state of Rhineland-Palatinate and the entirety of the states 50%).

entityDescription:
Greenwishes offers off-site waste management in our connected warehouse and a local 100% French recycling circuit. 
We begin by an implementation of selective sorting in your premises: papers, drinks, and other waste.
After, recyclable waste is collected in rolls according to a schedule that meets your needs. A roll is provided for each customer, each site and each collection. During the collection on site, the waste is identified thanks to a bar code.
Then, the waste is oversorted and gathered by homogeneous recyclable materials. Once processed by our sorting agents, the waste is compacted into bales (a format that is more suitable for transport and handling). 
We are able to weigh the waste to the nearest 200 grams per customer per day, by the agents after over-sorting, and to enter the data into the reporting system for each site.
Finally, the recycling and recovery of all waste is done France. We offer more than 30 French recycling partners for the treatment of your waste. The group has its own garbage truck to collect residual waste in case of collection incident.

The Ministry participates in the development of programmes and projects, and the implementation of the EU-funded projects as well as projects funded from other international sources.

The Ministry cooperates with the ministry competent for management of state property in all affairs regarding management and disposal of shares and interests in state-owned companies, as well as companies which are primarily engaged in activities within the jurisdiction of this Ministry.

The Ministry performs tasks related to the participation of the Republic of Croatia in the activities of European Union bodies and other international bodies pertaining to its competence.

entityDescription:
AmbieSense is a research-oriented business with specialities in applications of AI, machine learning, data science, information fusion, embedded hardware, and software. AmbieSense performs research and innovation projects with particular focus on enhancing situational-awareness for humans and robots through combination of new sensors, mobile apps, with intelligent edge, and cloud. We help transform new research into products and services, are experienced in EU projects, and active in publishing research results in scientific journals and conferences. AmbieSense is a pioneer in bringing state-of-the-art research-based technology into innovative and intelligent information solutions for complex physical environments. AmbieSense’s mission is to create technology that gives customers the information they need, when they need it — whatever the challenges of the environment.
The offering of science-driven expertise and consultancy is a key feature of the AmbieSense value proposition. Our team perform industrial research and innovation projects, as well as development of new products such as intelligent cameras for local and remote sensing, smart objects, artificial intelligence, multimedia search, and wireless devices that incorporate aspects of our research outputs. As three recent examples: we offer intelligent robot cameras for autonomous detection and tracking of airplanes, vehicles, ships, and small vessels for autonomous navigation and safety. We also offer intelligent ocean vision for subsea operations, maintenance, and oceanology purposes. And, we offer intelligent, solar-driven trackers and sensors as eco-friendly solution for autonomous monitoring of international shipping cargo and mobile assets.
We work closely with partners and customers to bring people the right information, as and when they need it. Thus, we help bring relevant information to the right situation and user - based on new and emerging technologies.

entityDescription:
The basic mission of Center Noordung is to research, collect and communicate the knowledge of space and space technologies to the public in a way that sensibly connects and intertwines the science, economy, tourism and art.
The basic activity of the public institute Center of Space Technologies Herman Potocnik Noordung is the promotion of space technologies and the manifestation of human achievements in space with the interweaving of art and high technologies. The offer includes the development, installation and marketing of space content in the form of art exhibitions, exhibitions of items and multimedia interactive applications that we offer to the general public.
Also, by connecting with and integrating into international connections, we ensure greater recognizability of Slovenian and international institutions in the field of space activities in all areas. Through the implementation of dedicated symposiums, we present and expand the significance of space exploration to the general public.
Since 2018 we have been active in the field of social innovation. More in the research field and as supporting institution. With the help of EU funding we have organized networking events, awareness campaigns and an online training session for public administration. As the final output of the project, consortium partners prepared a white book and policy recommendations on how to better support and develop social innovation initiatives and practices in each country (Austria, Germany, France, Italy and Slovenia).
In 2021 the Ministry of Economic Development and Technology included Center Noordung in another SI project where the aim is to build an SI ecosystem and to start creating a competence center that would be supporting further development of SI in Slovenia.
We are continuing to collaborate with partners in Slovenia and abroad to serve as a support institution and as a HUB where people can connect, find inspiration, get basic training and network with local, regional and national partners as well as institutions from abroad.

entityDescription:
SDTools is an independent and privately owned software development company that provides off the shelf scientific libraries called from the MATLAB environment and consulting services to implement custom applications using these libraries.

SDTools was formed in 2001 by Etienne Balmes to transform the original academic Structural Dynamics Toolbox, sold by Scientific Software Group (now The MathWorks, France) since 1995, to a fully professional product. From 2001 to 2008 SDTools collaborated with the MSSMat Laboratory of Ecole Centrale Paris, where Etienne Balmes headed the Vibration research group. Starting september 2008, SDTools is now hosted by the PIMM laboratory at ENSAM Paris. Current PhD theses are funded by PSA, SAFRAN and SNCF.

In 2002 SDTools partnered with INRIA to combine efforts in the development of a general purpose multi-physics finite element library OpenFEM. This joint effort greatly augments the number of people involved in developing FEM capabilities distributed with SDTools products.

Today Kaunas STP is the largest partner of science, public and business cooperation in Lithuania. It is the only STP in the country with business incubation facilities, Technology Demonstration Centre and R&D laboratories on site.
Kaunas STP aims to increase the competitiveness of tech businesses globally by providing the highest-level innovation support services, making efficient use of the resources of innovation ecosystem, developing the community of innovative businesses and fostering innovation culture within Kaunas region. Kaunas STP is a component of Lithuanian innovation ecosystem and as an organisation it is putting an effort to meet the present needs of business.
Kaunas STP has performed such roles as Assistant in E-Learning to innovative SMEs, Mediator of 500 Business Partnerships, Author of Regional Innovation Strategy, Facilitator of newly established businesses, Connector of different generation activities in Innovative Space Creation, and National Coordinator for the EU-scale Spatial Data project and many more.

Kaunas STP is an experienced & qualified partner to more than 50 science institutions and business associations from 23 countries. International partnership is realized via participation in European and world-wide networks and associations (more than 2000 companies): International Association of Science parks and Areas of Innovation (IASP), Baltic Association of Science, Technology Parks and Innovation Centres (BASTIC), Science Park and Innovation Centre Experts (SPICE group), World Alliance for Innovation (WAINOVA).
There are three shareholders of Kaunas STP: Ministry of the Economy and Innovation of the Republic of Lithuania, Kaunas University of Technology and Vytautas Magnus University.

It is located in the Asprela Campus, the main university campus in the city of Porto. FEUP is in the heart of Porto Innovation District and is the engine behind the success of The Science and Technology Park of the University of Porto, UPTEC, the winner of the 2013 European Region Stars Award for Smart Growth.
FEUP is also helping to turn the northern region of Portugal into a centre for innovation. Since 2014, FEUP was Co-financed in over 25 million euros by the European Regional Development Fund, spreading modern, structural change across the north of Portugal, FEUP is demonstrating how active universities in previously poorer regions of Europe can lead the move to smart growth.

entityDescription:
Denis Dilhan Consultant Co. offers a 42 years skill in pyrotechnics to any company dealing with these Technics. This experience has been acquired in a first time as a project manager of pyrotechnic devices for Defense at E. Lacroix Company and then at CNES (the French space Agency) as Pyrotechnics and Solid Propulsion engineer and technical manager of the Pyrotechnics Laboratory.
The 24 years of activity at CNES have been recognized by the CNES appointment of Senior Expert in Space Pyrotechnics. This professional period has covered in particular the management of the CNES pyrotechnics R&T and developments, the participation to reviews (PDR - CDR- QR) of pyrotechnic devices for satellites and launchers and also mechanisms and propulsion systems, the involvement in various ECSS WGs as member and as the convenor of ECSS E 33-11C “Explosive devices and systems”.
At the CNES Pyrotechnic Laboratory, I initiated and then operated the technics for the measurement and the duplication of pyrotechnic shocks. Various specific test equipment for pyroshocks generation have been developed and are implemented for the test requirements of CNES, ESA and Industry.
These past experience give Denis Dilhan Consultant Co.a wide knowledge to provide technical support for any development phases and experiments of pyrotechnic device. 
The operational responsibility of the CNES Pyrotechnics Laboratory requires the knowledge and the enforcement of the national safety regulations. I was in charge of the drafting of the pyrotechnic procedures, safety consignees of the laboratory required for the approval the work safety studies by the French authorities. Since 1995, I have been delivering pyrotechnic safety trainings to AIV teams of CNES, ESA, Airbus Defense & Space and Thales Alenia Space France and Italy, etc. Thanks to this experience, Denis Dilhan Consultant Co. propose also assistance in training and courses in pyrotechnics.

entityDescription: IBM Research - Zurich (English) IBM Research – Zurich is one of IBM’s 12 research centers around the globe. This network of some 3000 scientists is one of the largest industrial IT research organizations in the world. The Zurich laboratory was established in 1956 and is home to world-class scientists representing more than 45 nationalities. Cutting-edge research and outstanding scientific achievements—most notably two Nobel Prizes—are associated with this lab. The spectrum of research activities range from exploratory research in nanoscience and –technology and quantum computing for future computing, to cloud and computing infrastructure, security and privacy, computational sciences, Blockchain, data analytics and artificial intelligence (AI). One focus is the application of AI to solve industry-specific innovation challenges. So-called cognitive systems are able to learn at scale, reason with purpose and interact with humans naturally. Rather than being explicitly programmed, they learn and reason from their interactions with us and from their experiences with their environment. Cognitive systems can make sense of huge amounts of data, including the 80 percent of the world’s data that computer scientists call “unstructured”, and help us discover new insights to make better decisions. Also located at the lab is the IBM Research THINK Lab - Zurich. This thinktank and briefing center provides a unique place in Europe to gain insights from IBM researchers, industry and trend experts, in order to tackle today’s and tomorrow’s challenges.

entityDescription:
Avesta Battery & Energy Engineering (ABEE) is a dynamic engineering company specialised in the field of battery processing, manufacturing, battery system design, prototyping, and recycling and in particular for advanced Li-ion and solid state battery technology. ABEE is supporting the industry in development of tailored made solutions from battery materials to recycling for automotive and stationary applications through development of dedicated multiscale simulation tools and functions embedded in different platforms. 
In addition, ABEE is setting up state of the art battery manufacturing infrastructures and battery system design platforms. In this regard, ABEE has state of the art electrode processing pilot line for advanced Li-ion, solid state batteries (oxide and sulfide) and innovative solutions for LiM coating. ABEE pilotline is fully integrated within an unique dry room of 250m2 with dew point of -60°C. 
Further, ABEE has extensive knowledge and expertise in the field of artificial intelligence techniques, state estimations for batteries and process modeling.

3D4MEC Srl , the first Italian company to develop and market specialized 3D printing systems for metals, was founded in 2016 and is part of the group of companies headed by Ivano Corsini, an entrepreneur with more than 35 years ’ experience in the mechatronics and manufacturing sectors. 
The years spent within the metal additive manufacturing sector combined with the years matured in the mechanical sector have empowered Ivano Corsini to develop a productive method , Corsystem , a superfast 3D printer for mechanics.
3D4MEC produces specialized machines for the process of specific alloys , customized for the production needs of each single customer, to optimize performance and make production with additive manufacturing the most efficient and cost effective possible. 
3D4MEC produces , upon order, 2 different specialized systems of 3D printing for metals, customized to the production needs of each customer. 3D4STEEL and 3D4BRASS.

3D4STEEL: First 3D printer specialized in the process of steel
3D4BRASS First 3D printer in the world for production of brass components

3D4STEEL
First 3D printer specialized in the process of steel• Automatic system for recycling unused powder• Specialized system for steel powder distribution• Owner of open software for reduction of costs• Certification for eco sustainable filter disposal• Sole use of self produced nitrogen• Remote control via mobile app and desktopIn Brief: Compared to other metal additive generalist and multi material technologies , 3D4STEEL, thanks to its specialization in processing steel alloys , permits the production of complex pieces at the lowest cost possible with maximum mechanical properties and performance suitable to mechanical applications

entityName: Nederlands Centrum voor Interim-Management B.V. - NCIM
entityDescription:
The core business of NCIM is staff augmentation with IT Specialists for system integration, support and staffing of projects in technological, scientific and military settings, often in highly secured domains The highly-qualified NCIM IT professionals are supporting clients with work on mission-critical programs. All of NCIM’s professional staff hold academic degrees ranging from BSc and MSc to PhD and have excellent IT skills. 
The majority of NCIM employees hold active Security Clearances at NATO/EU Secret or higher levels and work on classified, secure and challenging high technology projects.
Over the past 33 years NCIM has obtained an outstanding reputation in the Dutch Defence, NATO, Europol and Public Security Domain by making customer satisfaction its top priority. NCIM is characterized by entrepreneurship, innovation and agility. 
NCIM is known for its adaptive approach, customer intimacy and personal touch in augmenting client teams. NCIM emphasizes the importance of long-term relationships and invests as much time as necessary to bolster these relationships. The company is known for reliability and a good price to quality ratio. NCIM currently holds a ISO 9001 and 27001 certificates and is currently recertifing its ISO 14001 certificate.
NCIM provides solutions in various Defence and Public Safety areas, ranging from NATO, the Dutch Army, the Dutch Airforce, Europol, the Supreme Court of Justice, the Dutch Parliament, to the Netherlands Forensic Institute and the Dutch security services AIVD and MIVD (the General Intelligence and Security Service and the Military Intelligence and Security Service).
Apart from the Defence and Public Security domain NCIM has built up a strong name and reputation in commercial organizations like the Dutch Chamber of Commerce, ING Bank, ABN Amro and the Dutch Rail Road Organization.
NCIM is a member of AFCEA ( Armed Forces Communications and Electronics Associations), the NAG (Netherlands Aerospace Group) and NIDV (Stichting Nederlandse Industrie voor Defensie en Veligheid), the Dutch Defence and Security-related Industry Association.

entityDescription:
PickWerk was founded in May 2020 by three engineers from the Fraunhofer Institute for Integrated Circuits in Nuremberg, Germany. With an innovative solution for tracking workers' hands, PickWerk helps the producing industry to avoid errors in material distribution and manual assembly processes. At the same time, the efficiency of the processes is increased through an automatic acknowledgement mechanism. The focus is on the psychological and physical relief of the workers.

The technological basis of the business is a tracking technology based on magnetic fields, which has already been used in professional football in the form of a goal detection system. Instead of the football PickWerk tracks wristbands by means of a sensor frame. This way the movement of hands can be tracked and analysed continuously in three dimensions.

entityName: Ústav fyziky materiálů AV ČR, v. v. i. - Institute of Physics of Materials AS CR, v. V. I.  of The Czech Academy of Sciences (IPM)
entityDescription:
The activities of the Institute of Physics of Materials of the Czech Academy of Sciences (IPM) are focused on the investigations of relationships between the behaviour and properties of materials and their structural and microstructural characteristics. The priority is the research of advanced metal-based materials, ceramics and composites in relation to their microstructure and the method of preparation. The aim of research activities is the optimisation of functional properties of materials and reliable prediction of their operational lifetime.
The Institute has a long-term focus on the field of materials research, reaching back to 1955 when it was founded with the aim of studying properties of metallic materials. Through natural development, the research portfolio has extended also to other materials suitable for highly sophisticated engineering applications.
At present, great attention is paid, for example, to materials for safe and environmentally friendly generation of electrical energy, new generation of high-strength steels used in automotive and aviation industries, nano-materials with unique properties, high-temperature superalloys used in turbines, materials for implants, functional materials, ceramic materials and composites. The range of expert activities also responds to current trends in the field of materials engineering. A part of research capacities is devoted to the investigation of properties of metallic materials and components produced by the method of 3D printing.

Artificial intelligence, cognitive systems and intelligent software architectures for autonomous systems. Research for the future is part of our DNA. Helping to ensure people’s safety is our scientific responsibility.
The researchers at the Fraunhofer Institute for Cognitive Systems IKS are always thinking one step ahead when it comes to new software technologies, working to adapt them to the requirements of an increasingly complex world.
Serving as an independent partner of industry, we conduct applied research into dependable software technologies for safety-critical applications in the areas of Industry 4.0 and automotive, as well as mobile machines and commercial vehicles. This allows the enormous potential of intelligent software to open up completely new opportunities.
Our approach is called safe intelligence. We reconcile intelligence and safety in the truest sense. Through safe intelligence we ensure that cognitive systems function and are used with the best interests and well-being of people in mind. Systems that we can place our full trust in. For a world that we can depend on.
In order to drive these issues forward, the former Fraunhofer ESK was used as the foundation for the creation of a new Fraunhofer institute: the Fraunhofer Institute for Cognitive Systems IKS.

VACOM Vakuum Komponenten & Messtechnik GmbH (VACOM) was founded in 1992. The headquarters is in Großlöbichau. Secondary locations are in Jena, Antwerpen (Belgium) and Naples (Florida, USA). Approximately 10% of the employees are apprentices and 10% are assigned to the R&D department consisting of mechanical and electrical engineers as well as physicists, mechanics, project managers, and laboratory technicians.
VACOM is currently one of the largest vacuum suppliers and manufacturers in Europe. The product portfolio includes measurement equipment (e.g. pressure gauges and residual gas spectrometer), different types of interfaces between atmosphere and vacuum (e.g. optical interfaces like optical fiber feedthroughs or viewports as well as mechanical feedthroughs and electrical feedthroughs), ion getter pumps and all kind of standard and customized vacuum components (e.g. vacuum chambers and connector parts). An essential part of the products is self-developed and self-made at the headquarter in Germany. In addition, VACOM is world leader in cleaning service of vacuum components. The service consists of the development of cleaning strategies and processes of own and customer vacuum components as well as the specification and warranty according to the company’s own purity and vacuum classes. The cleaning service also takes place at the headquarter in Germany.

entityDescription: MYWAI S.r.l. is an innovative Italian startup that has developed on proprietary technology (UIB patent nr 102018000005044 granted on 24/08/2020) different solutions that combine Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things and Blockchain on distributed Edge networks and Cloud computing for professional, industrial, biomedical and smart cities customers and markets. At the end of 2021 MYWAI S.r.l. acquired by incorporation Zenatek S.p.A., a historic brand of IoT system integration in the professional field in Italy, inheriting as customers some of the most well-known and innovative Italian industrial and biomedical companies on the market (e.g. Fincantieri, Almaviva, ESAOTE, MITSUBISHI Electric, etc.) as well as acquiring significant funding for important research projects in the context of various EU (e.g. Trinity Robotics, IoT 4 Industry, IntellIIoT, etc.) and National (PromenAIde™ project, for the prognostic maintenance of biomedical machinery using neuromorphic chips and AI algorithms on edge) initiatives developed in the new research center opened by MYWAI S.r.l. in the prestigious context of the Bay of Silence in Sestri Levante, Eastern Riviera Ligure between Portofino and Cinqueterre, where it is catalyzing the skills of numerous national and international researchers.The MYWAI™ Technology, developed based on the previously mentioned patent, contains a method and a solution to integrate artificial intelligence on Edge and Very Edge devices by certifying their data and algorithms with next-generation DLT networks. In particular, MYWAI™ technology supports the evolution of critical infrastructures and equipment in the industrial, biomedical and smart cities sectors towards the Equipment and Infrastructure as a Service (EIaaS) model, thanks to the integration of sensors and boards for neuro-computing on edge to enable innovative services in the field of technical assistance (e.g. preventive/predictive maintenance), Fintech (e.g. Pay-per-Use services, Pay-per-Outcome, NFT payments and Smart Contracts) and/or Insurtech (e.g. warranty extension, parametric insurance).MYWAI™ technology supports the collection of field data (e.g. sensors, storage systems, other IT systems already in the field), visualization on GUI, processing and analysis (labeling, creation of descriptive models) and the execution of AI algorithms - in real-time or on historical data - for the recognition of behavioural patterns, prognostics on devices, the search for malfunctions, etc. Depending on the output of the algorithms, it is possible to activate alarms and/or programmed actions (e.g. alerts, device control, test routines). In addition, the possibility of certifying the validity and immutability of data and processing results by publication on DLT/Blockchain is supported.MYWAI S.r.l. supports national and international market and RD initiatives in identifying areas for the development of innovative products and equipment and then proceed to the complete development of the project up to the executive implementation, through the integration of ICT and OT management consulting skills, integrating Knowledge, Experience and Method in a mix of high professional level. Basing its operational approach on the principles of partnership and collaboration with customers as a distinctive characterization, MYWAI S.r.l. offers ICT and OT services as a complement to and complement its MYWAI™ technology.

entityDescription:
Fraunhofer FHR is one of the leading and largest European research institutes in the area of high frequency and radar techniques. It develops customized electromagnetic sensor concepts, processes, and systems for its partners, from the microwave range through to the lower terahertz range. In 2020 Fraunhofer FHR generated a total income of 38.0 million Euro and had a total headcount of 390.
The core topic of the research at Fraunhofer FHR consists of sensors for high-precision distance and position determination as well as imaging systems with a resolution of up to 3.75 mm. The applications range from systems for reconnaissance, surveillance, and protection to real-time capable sensors for traffic and navigation as well as quality assurance and non-destructive testing. Fraunhofer FHR's systems are characterized by reliability and robustness: Radar and millimeter wave sensors are suitable for demanding tasks, even under rough environmental conditions. They work at high temperatures, with vibrations, or under zero visibility conditions caused by smoke, vapor or fog. Thus, radar and the related high frequency systems, are also key technologies for defense and security. In this area, the Institute has been supporting BMVg (the German Federal Ministry of Defense) since the Institute was founded in 1957.
On one hand, the processes and systems developed at Fraunhofer FHR are used for research of new technology and design. On the other hand, together with companies, authorities, and other public entities, the Institute develops prototypes to unsolved challenges. The special focus here is on the maturity of the systems and their suitability for serial production to ensure a quick transformation into a finished product in cooperation with a partner. Thanks to its interdisciplinary positioning, the Institute possesses the technical know-how to cover the entire value creation chain, from consulting and studies up to the development and production of pilot series. The used technology ranges from the traditional waveguide base to highly integrated silicon-germanium chips with a frequency of up to 300 GHz.
The ability to carry out non-contact measurements and the penetration of materials open up a range of possibilities for the localization of objects and people. Thanks to the advances in miniaturization and digitalization, the high frequency sensors of Fraunhofer FHR with their special capacities are an affordable and attractive option for an increasing number of application areas.

•Defense
•Space

•Traffic
•Production
•Human and Environment

Thanks to its interdisciplinary positioning, the Institute possesses the technical know-how to cover the entire value creation chain, from consulting and studies up to the development and production of pilot series. The used technology ranges from the traditional waveguide base to highly integrated silicon-germanium chips with a frequency of up to 300 GHz.
The ability to carry out non-contact measurements and the penetration of materials open up a range of possibilities for the localization of objects and people. Thanks to the advances in miniaturization and digitalization, the high frequency sensors of Fraunhofer FHR with their special capacities are an affordable and attractive option for an increasing number of application areas.

description:
MIRAD microwave is the trusted supplier of state of the art antenna transmitter, receiver, tracking and filter technology for the satellite communication industry. Our solutions and components are key factors for the success of global communication systems and interplanetary space missions.

For satellite up and downlink signals MIRAD is the trusted provider of passive RF infrastructure hardware and services for ground station antennas of any type and make.

From 1 GHz up to 70 GHz, we deliver a complete range of antenna & waveguide solutions with Swiss precision & quality.
We design and manufacture: 
- Feed systems (single and multi-band)
- Feed networks
- Switching & combining systems
- Standard waveguide component like directional couplers, terminations, filters, diplexers, OMTs, waveguide routing, air inlets and pressure windows

We also provide:
- Antenna geometries for the main- and sub-reflector for new ground stations including reflector deformation analysis
- Antenna performance simulations (antenna efficiency, radiation pattern, G/T calculations)
- Definition of antenna key parameters as a starting point for the feed system design
- Feasibility assessment of antenna upgrades 
- Beam waveguide calculation

In our in-house anechoic chamber (8m x 6m x 6m), MIRAD tests the antenna characteristics of our own systems and prototypes, as well as third party RF products up to 70 GHz. (contact us to check availability and for a quote). Our measurements are three dimensional and in high resolution. The test procedures are software defined for synchronic VNA and hardware-motion controlling.
All our solutions consistently deliver the best possible RF performance, due to our proven RF engineering skills and in-house availability of adequate simulation and testing infrastructure.

entityDescription:
We are the world leader in ultra-black, light absorbing coatings and foils. Our products are qualified for space and in use in numerous satellite-borne instruments. Main application fields are straylight suppression, Laser power absorption and high-emissivity coatings in the wide field of photonics.

Acktars™ inorganic coatings are fabricated using Acktar™ proprietary vacuum deposition technology.A very high specific surface area coating is created with a tightly controlled morphology to produce a very low reflectance level.

The coating thickness is a few microns (typically 3-5 µm) and its density is typically ~1.8 g/cm3. The deposition process is carried out at wide range of temperatures depending on the substrate.By controlling the composition and morphology of the layer microstructure it can be tailored to achieve desired levels of absorption or reflectance over a wide range of wavelengths(EUV-UV, VIS,NIR-FIR). The deep black foils and coatings can be applied to almost any surface (metal, glass, silicon, ceramic, plastic) - for example for stray light optimization, laser absorption, improvement of signal-to-noise Ratio (SNR) and high-emissivity coating in technical optics.

Target industries are:aerospace, laser technology, technical optics, sensor technology,measurement technology, medical technology and diagnostics,biotechnology and industrial image processing.

With multiple partnerships, including the European Space Agency (ESA) Business Incubation Program, winner of the University Challenge with Galileo Masters, and in the register of the European Commission, SEAC Business School has established its presence at worldwide level. Based on a new innovative method, it embraces the modern model of education, which is delivered 100% online and live, enhancing space education accessibility to anyone in the world, with the objective of empowering the Space Leaders of tomorrow. entityDescription:
Founded in August 2020, INERGIO Technologies SA is based in Lausanne, Switzerland. Concerned by Climate Change, we build clean, lightweight and efficient power generators based on Fuel Cell technology.
Vision
Our vision is to accelerate the green energy transition following a systematic and step-by-step approach. Our fuel flexible fuel cell technology generates reliable electricity using any kind of fuel from commercially available natural gas and LPG to Green Hydrogen.
Mission
Our mission is to help our clients to build a better product and provide a better service by securing 24/7 operation at low maintenance cost using green power generator.
History
The technology behind INERGIO is a product of more than 10 years of research at Swiss higher education institutions. Different aspects and technological challenges of micro-SOFCs have been studied and valuable know-how developed through several PhD thesis. INERGIO spun-off from EPFL and HEIG-VD

Product

Miniaturised power generator based on fuel cell technology with a power range between 50W to 2.5kW suitable for mobile, off-grid and space applications. The unit could use Propane (LPG), Methane, Syngas, Biogas, ammonia, etc. as input fuel.

entityDescription:
The Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft, headquartered in Germany, is the world’s leading applied research organization. With its focus on developing key technologies that are vital for the future and enabling the commercial exploitation of this work by business and industry, Fraunhofer plays a central role in the innovation process. As a pioneer and catalyst for groundbreaking developments and scientific excellence, Fraunhofer helps shape society now and in the future. Founded in 1949, the Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft currently operates 75 institutes and research institutions throughout Germany. The majority of the organization’s 29,000 employees are qualified scientists and engineers, who work with an annual research budget of 2.8 billion euros. Of this sum, 2.4 billion euros are generated through contract research.
As Fraunhofer IMM, we work in the fields of chemistry, energy and diagnostics. Our scientists perform the transfer from the scientific idea towards innovation. Thereby, we are able to improve the reliability and efficiency of compact material and energy conversion systems as well as of decentralized, mobile power supply units. We increase process reliability and availability of materials, measurement data and information for product, manufacturing and analytical issues, also in the field of diagnostics. We improve the reliability of process monitoring and increase the robustness of sensors. Our laboratory and pilot scale system solutions can straightly and consistently be transformed into production scale. It is our mission to act in a professional, quality-conscious, economical and sustainable way taking our expertise as a foundation.”

entityDescription:
Small Robot Company is delivering Per Plant Farming to the world's largest food crops.
 
Using a suite of robots (called Tom, Dick and Harry) linked and controlled by an AI driven operating system (called Wilma), weprovide a near-real time view of each crop plant as it grows through the season, and then deliver precise, timely interventions to make that plant reach its full potential.
 
Tom lives on the farm, continuously gathering data on the plants and the environment.Wilma is the brains of the operation, converting Tom’s data into instructions for Dick and Harry.
This is per plant intelligence

Dick nurtures and protects the crop. He only treats the plants that need it.
Harry precisely plants the crop at exactly the right depth and spacing for the conditions, giving it the best chance of the highest yields.
This is per plant action.

Through this system, we aim to reduce inputs by 90%, and convert arable farming from emitting up to 3 tonnes/CO2e/Ha to sequestered up to 2tonnes/CO2e/Ha for the 4bn Ha or arable farmland in the world.

Our system is dependent on the most accurate global positioning capability, combined with layered data, from satellite level down to individual plant level.

entityName: AECSIC - Instituto de Astrofisica de Andalucia
entityDescription:
The IAA occupies a strong and unique position in astrophysics and space research in Spain, being the biggest centre for astrophysical research in the CSIC. Its multidisciplinarity and the experience in multi-range astronomy favour the existence of transversal synergetic projects. It is our declared goal to transform the IAA into one of the leading institutes in astrophysics and space science in Europe and to evolve its research and structure to a level where the IAA is placed at the pole position for the exploitation of the upcoming next generation of advanced, ground-breaking experiments.

IAA researchers are internationally recognized leaders in the remote and in situ studies of the planetary atmospheres and surfaces, as well as of minor bodies. Their expertise embrace laboratory experiments, instruments design, data acquisition, data analysis and theoretical modelling on multi-timescale changes and coupling in the Earth’s middle and upper atmosphere, on the martian atmosphere composition and escape to decipher water history on Mars, on the atmospheric composition of the icy giants, giant planets and of Titan, on the interior structure and rotational state of comet nuclei and asteroids, or the study of physical properties of TNOs using stellar occultations, or the scattering properties of relevant refractory material in planetary systems.This wide expertise has allowed the IAA researchers to be Co-PI or Co-I of the majority of ESA interplanetary missions in the last three decades. The eLightning ERC CONSOLIDATOR GRANT, devoted to decipher the origin and the behaviour of the lightning discharges in the upper atmosphere of the Earth is developed in the planetary atmospheres group. IAA researchers are involved in ground-breaking instrumental on polarimetric observations of the Sun to infer the origin and dynamics of its magnetic field.

IAA plays a leading role in the development of space-borne and ground-based instruments. This is a unique feature and strength of the IAA, unmatched by any Spanish institute, and only by very few international peers. Examples for recent IAA important contributions to instruments onboard successful interplanetary missions are GIADA and OSIRIS (ROSETTA), ImaX/Sunrise, BeLA/Bepi Colombo, NOMAD/Exomars, SO/PHI, JANUS and GaLA/JUICE in the near future, and CoCa, MANIaC, EnVisS and OPIC/Comet Interceptor in the future.

entityDescription:
IObundle, Lda. is a system-level Semiconductor IP (SIP) company, founded in April 2018, and with its main office in Lisbon, Portugal.
 
With the demise of Moore’s law, architecture is becoming more and more critical. The demand for processors, hardware accelerators and specialized designs is increasing.
 
Our goal is to create, distribute and support alternative architectures using RISC-V CPUs, programmable hardware accelerators, and various custom hardware blocks.
 
IObundle promotes IOb-SoC, an open-source and free of charge Verilog/C++ System on Chip template, comprising a size-optimized RISC-V processor, internal RAM system with boot loading support, and a configurable cache system with L1 instruction/data caches plus a shared L2 cache. IObundle also promotes IOb-Versat, another open-source and free of charge Verilog/C++ SIP. IOb-Versat is a Coarse-Grained Reconfigurable Array for accelerating edge computing applications in an energy-efficient way.
 
Our business model provides commercial IP cores and software using the above infrastructure and offers IP rights warranty, technical support, and customization design services to users of our infrastructure.
 
Our IPs are verified using software models, RTL simulation and FPGA testing to provide a quality experience to our customers.

entityName: DLR - INSTITUTE OF MICROWAVES AND RADAR
entityDescription:
With its know-how and expertise in passive and active microwave remote sensing, the Microwaves and Radar Institute contributes to the development and advancement of ground-based, airborne and spaceborne sensors.
The focus of its research work is on the conception and development of new synthetic aperture radar (SAR) techniques and systems, as well as sensor-specific applications. The Institute‘s strength is the execution of long-term research programs with applications in remote sensing, aeronautics and traffic monitoring, as well as reconnais- sance and security. In line with the German space program, the Institute works in close collaboration with other DLR institutes, the German Space Administration, the European Space Agency, German industry and responsible ministries. The education of young scientists in the form of hosting and supervising internships, as well as diploma and doctoral theses is also an important part of the Institute’s mission.

description:
Uptimai is a state-of-the-art company for Uncertainty Quantification (UQ), Statistical Optimization (SO) and Data-Analysis (DA). Our approach combines advances in statistical modelling with elements of AI & Machine Learning and such that provide unique efficiency and accuracy. 
We are a Czech company with offices based in Prague, that was founded in 2018 as a spin-off from space research project solving spacecraft re-entry. Our algorithm (and know-how) was originally developed to estimate the impact area of space debris and estimate uncertainties for hypersonic flows. 
But math is used everywhere, so we extended the algorithm for general use in Computer-Aided Engineering and extended our approach to other potential applications driven by data-analysis and new optimization methods.

entityDescription:
AlgoSource has over 25 years of experience in selection, cultivation, extraction and formulation of functional ingredients from microalgae.
In particular, the company has developed real know-how related to Spirulina and its principle active ingredient, phycocyanin, for which it has patented a cold extraction method that excludes the use of solvents or chemicals, to preserve all of its original bioactive properties. From this expertise came an exceptional and effective product of natural origin: Spirulysat®
In addition to this historic strain, AlgoSource is working on other microalgae to extract the best molecules of interest for the cosmetics and health nutrition sectors. From Chlorella to Scenedesmus, without forgetting Tetraselmis or Isochrisis, AlgoSource conducts research on a dozen strains simultaneously, each offering functional ingredients of very high added value.
Lastly, to best protect these molecules of interest without subjecting them to a thermal change which could damage their bioactive activity, AlgoSource has developed exceptional mastery of a cold sterilization process, including in small volumes.

AlgoSource Technologies is the R&D subsidiary of AlgoSource, which develops high scientific and technologic skills in the field of circular engineering and industrial ecology using microalgae with the aime to recycle and valorize several "wastes" like CO2, water, fatal herat, urine, ...

entityDescription:
Gisat provides a wide range of geoinformation services based on Earth Observation technology. It focuses on operational application of satellite mapping to monitor various aspects of our environment and development of dedicated web based platforms for geoinformation data analytics.
GISAT is a privately owned SME sized company. It is based in Prague, the capital of Czech Republic. Since 2008, the company has been ISO9001 & ISO14001 certified to guarantee the quality of provided services and responsibility in environmental impacts of its activities.
GISAT’s team has proven expertise in automated image analysis, GIS and statistical techniques driven by object-based (OBIA), artificial intelligence (machine & deep learning, neural networks), feature extraction and semi-automated approaches. Specialized operational automated cloud based processing chains for land use & land cover, agriculture crops & practices mapping and monitoring, ground subsidence & infrastructure deformation, flood mapping or vegetation evolution monitoring from various optical and radar sensors have been developed in frame of research or operational projects. Customized open source tools based on geospatial statistics and area frame sampling for land applications have been designed and implemented at the company. The company’s specialists use both COTS and open source tools to facilitate effective geo-spatial intelligence extraction from EO imagery.
GISAT is very successful in delivering interactive data2information web platforms solutions based on open source components. The company develops its own framework for the web analytical platforms aiming at interactive data exploration & analysis and dealing with synchronized interactive maps, charts, and tables. It allows users with no prior GIS experience to access, explore, visualize, analyse and share spatial data from a variety of sources in an interactive and customizable way.

entityName: CMMI Cyprus Marine and Maritime Institute
entityDescription:
The Cyprus Marine and Maritime Institute (CMMI) was established in April 2019 and it is a Centre of Excellence for marine and maritime research, innovation and technology development. It is based in the city of Larnaca in Cyprus, an island located on the crossroads of three continents and major maritime routes with a proud maritime tradition and a commendable maritime industry. CMMI has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 Research and Innovation Programme and matching funding from the Cyprus Government.
CMMI’s vision is to drive sustainable Blue Growth by addressing the needs of industry and society within the spectrum of the marine and maritime sectors. It has ten Research and Innovation Centres that are involved in marine observation, marine robotics, maritime digitalisation, maritime engineering, marine and coastal ecosystems, the maritime human element, marine cultural heritage, marine and maritime policies and regional cooperation and underwater and seabed technologies.
CMMI’s Scientific staff is already involved in significant projects that will create solutions to issues that concern both the industry and society such as protecting marine biodiversity, addressing decarbonization, promoting digitalization and addressing climate change. They have expertise in various areas including among other naval architecture, mechanical and electrical engineering, aquaculture and marine resource management, oceanography, marine sciences, robotics and artificial intelligence. Major industry players, such as large ship management companies on the island, have already shown their support and interest in working with CMMI.
Target Markets
CMMI will pursue opportunities and implement solutions for the below sectors:
- Maritime Transport
- Shipbuilding and Repair
- Marine Renewable Energy (Offshore Wind – Ocean Energy)
- Port Activities
- Coastal Tourism
- Marine Living Resources
- Marine Non-Living Resources
- Blue Biotechnology
- Marine Infrastructure
- Maritime Defence, Security and Surveillance

(*) CMMI was established by the CMMI/MaRITeC-X project as a “Center of Excellence in Marine and Maritime Research, Innovation and Technology Development” and has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation program under grant agreement No. 857586; and matching  funding from the Government of the Republic of Cyprus.FacebookTwitterLinkedInGo to Top

entityName: UNIVERSITAET BREMEN - Laboratory of Applied Space Microbiology
entityDescription:
The Laboratory of Applied Space Microbiology (within the ZARM, at the University of Bremen) was created, primarily, to develop microbe-based technologies in support of future crewed outposts beyond Earth. 
Indeed, sending humans to Mars within a few decades is now a realistic goal of leading entities of the space sector, be they public agencies or private companies. While first missions will likely be short-term, a permanently or semi-permanently inhabited outpost, akin to polar stations, would be desirable to perform extensive research activity on site. But while the vision of long-term human presence on Mars is compelling, providing consumables to sustain crews is a challenge. Recycling is part of the solution, but 100% recycling efficiency cannot be reached since losses are unavoidable. There is, however, a promising alternative: in situ resource utilization, or producing resources from local (Martian) materials. Its implementation could rely on biological systems, as we often do on Earth: microorganisms, for instance, could be used to produce drugs, food, oxygen, biomaterials and various industrially useful chemicals, to mine metals and to process waste. However, if biological systems rely exclusively on materials imported from Earth, their running time without re-supply is limited. To be sustainable, such systems should be fed with resources available on Mars. 
The key could lie in cyanobacteria. Owing to their photosynthetic abilities, nitrogen-fixing activities and lithotrophic features, some species could be fed with materials available on Mars: atmospheric gases, water mined on site from ground ice and atmospheric vapor, and mineral nutrients from the regolith. They could be used directly for various applications, including the production of food, fuel and oxygen, but also indirectly: products from their culture could support the growth of other organisms, opening the way to a wide range of life-support biological processes based on Martian resources. 
The LASM works on gathering the necessary data to provide cost and yield estimates for cyanobacterium-based processes in biological life-support systems. Notably, we aim at determining the optimal atmospheric conditions for cyanobacterium growth: how close can the gas mixture in the culture system be to the Martian atmosphere (to minimize costs and risks) while sustaining productive cultures?
In the middle term, we aim to offer a practical and well-characterized solution to be implemented in future crewed missions away from Earth. While Mars is a primary focus, efforts are being made to make the system adaptable to, for instance, the Moon base foreseen by ESA.

entityDescription:
The Cyprus Geological Survey Department (GSD) was established in 1950 with a mandate to consult the state on geological matters. It is a state-funded public institution under the Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Environment and its mission is to safeguard the public interest through the identification, the exploitation and protection of mineral and groundwater resources, the investigation and assessment of the geological environment and geohazards, the monitoring and assessment of seismicity, the investigation of foundation conditions, the protection and promotion of sites of geological and mining heritage and the production and dissemination of unbiased geological information to society. Today, the survey is staffed by 19 geoscientists and 76 sub-professional and technical personnel supporting the principal sections of the survey, Economic Geology, Hydrogeology, Engineering geology, Geophysics and Seismology, General Geology, GIS and Cartography, Geochemistry and Environmental Geology. The activities of the core sections are supported by a number of auxiliary services including a digital seismological network and centers, the chemical, lapidary and the geotechnical and industrial minerals laboratories, as well as the drilling rigs and pumping test units.
The department archives extensive collections of analogue and digital geological data, like reports, maps, borehole data and bibliography related to the geology of Cyprus. In addition, the department stores extensive collections of rock and mineral collections but most importantly, it stores large collections of thin sections and borehole cores dating to the founding days of the department. This together with the fact that the department is the only organisation dealing with geological matters, constitutes it a leader.

The Law for Geological Surveys (N. 140(I)/2013) regulates licensing for field geological surveying and research and also the use of government boreholes by third parties. The law also establishes the responsibilities of the Geological Survey Department, mainly relating to the survey of mineral and water resources and geohazards, their location, research, monitoring and subsequent policy making through the Minister of Agriculture, Rural Development and Environment. More specifically, the law establishes the Cyprus Geological Survey as the adviser of the Minister of Agriculture on geological matters, the national curator of the seismological stations and network, and the national curator for the protection of geomorphosites, fossil collections and geological data archives. The GSD is also responsible for the implementation of several EU Directives such as the Nitrate Directive (1991/676/EEC), the Groundwater Directive (2006/118/EC) and part of the Water Framework Directive (2000/60/EC).

description: At Skudo (skudo.tech), we realized that for guaranteeing the highest level of security that these fields require, hardware encryption is a must. The core product is a Hardware Security Module developed within a single FPGA chip. On top of this, the company is developing modified versions of space protocol (e.g. CCSDS SDLS) adding asymmetric cryptography and PKI with the use of digital certificates which we implement for space and drone applications. The implemented asymmetric encryption architecture is based on the well-proven TLS 1.3 scheme with the adoption of a PKI, digital certificates, ECDH, and symmetric encryption (AES/GCM). All the encryption primitives and key-related functions are implemented within our HSM/FPGA chip (no use of third-parties IPcore).
entityDescription:
Skudo is a European cybersecurity company based in Estonia, established in 2019. The company develops hardware-based secure communication solutions for space, UAV, and defense applications, focusing on FPGA-based embedded systems and cryptographic IP cores to protect critical data transmission.
Skudo’s main objective is to provide verifiable, backdoor-free European-made security solutions. All designs are fully auditable by independent third parties. The company has developed a Hardware Security Module (HSM) architecture implemented inside a single FPGA, supporting symmetric encryption (AES), Post-Quantum Cryptography (Kyber, Dilithium), and RISC-V processor cores. Skudo’s technology has been space-validated on ESA’s OPS-SAT mission.
Skudo has been awarded two European Defence Fund (EDF) projects:
EDF2023 – HSM4COM: development of hardware encryption and attestation systems for satellites, UAVs, and ground vehicles.

EDF2024 – SIGMA: development of advanced secure communication modules and cryptographic protection systems for space and dual-use defense applications.

The product portfolio includes:
KIRO: an FPGA-based encrypted Iridium SBD satellite modem for telemetry and command uplinks in long-range UAV operations.

Supernova: a secure FPGA-based module providing encrypted telemetry (MAVlink) for UAVs.

SERPE v3.0: an FPGA-based encryption system for real-time analogue FPV video signals, providing low-latency AES-CTR based video scrambling and asymmetric cryptographic pairing.

Encrypted Iridium telemetry and messaging modules: hardware-based fallback secure data links for UAVs and autonomous platforms operating in RF-contested environments.

CyEx is a knowledge-based cyber security service provider offering proactive cyber solutions for both domestic and international markets, primarily for large corporations and governments. CyEx offers end-to-end cyber security consulting, from information risk assessments that help benchmark safety measures and shore up weaknesses, to testing what checks for robust defences. CyEx is also specialised in cybersecurity trainings both for non-cyber IT and security porfessionals and cybersecurity and cyber defence experts in course formats, cyber drills, and cyber exercises.

Città Sotto Scacco Srl (CSS) is an urban mobility planning consultancy firm, for urban accessibility and sustainable mobility; registered in the special section of the Order Planners of the Province of Venice.
The company is present in Venice from 2020 and is active throughout the national territory.
The company's "core business" is the development of services for planning mobility and accessibility with ideas of sustainability in urban or rural areas.
CSS is the Italian partner of the Goudappel Group, a group active throughout Europe in the field of developing strategies for sustainable mobility. A network that sets the standard in mobility planning in different European Countries, in particular The Netherlands since 1963 with over 250 specialists in planning, engineering, design, modelling, GIS and research.
The primary mission of CSS is to develop cities to make them "vibrant, liveable and loveable". The city is a place where there are different kinds of interests, where everyone decides what to do, in a free and regulated way at the same time. Città Sotto Scacco Srl helps all the interests of every single “pawn of the city” for greater coordination in all phases of a planning process to build together a livable city for all.
CSS deals with urban planning tools, territorial analysis and development of scenarios and strategies for the territory, both for the public and private sectors. Furthermore, it deals with territorial information systems and participatory processes.
With regard to accessibility and mobility, he is dedicated to drawing up plans to improve urban and territorial accessibility, including Bikeplan and Plan for removing architectural barriers (Italian acronim: PEBA). In addition, he carries out consultancy for sustainable mobility and corporate and school Mobility Management.
CSS has carried out consultancy activities for the drafting of Toponymy Plans, Communication Plans and the development of territorial information tools. In addition, the company has been involved in carrying out various territorial analyzes and the development of strategies for public bodies and associations.
