entityDescription:
Thin Red Line Aerospace capabilities focus on development of the highest performance flexible-deployable architecture for space exploration, including systems engineering and integration of complex fabric and polymeric film structures. Thin Red Line’s work at the leading edge of fabric and film structure engineering is founded on mastery of both fabrication and of the associated scientific concepts. Current projects pertain to planetary entry systems/EDL; heat shield development; hypersonic inflatable aerodynamic decelerators; planetary aerobats; inflatable airlock and habitat architecture; thermal/MMOD & radiation shielding. 
Thin Red Line’s dedication to development of space exploration technology is led by staff with invaluable insights into space environments and spacecraft systems engineering, with experience spanning the decades following the Apollo program, and having supported NASA programs such as Chandra X-ray, EOS-Terra, Compton Gamma Ray Observatories, as well as the TOMS satellite. While primarily dedicated to space related technologies, Thin Red Line staff also have extensive “terrestrial” experience—in design, testing, and the hands-on field integration of critical application aviation, tactical and ground support soft goods for deployment in inclement environments around the world.
Thin Red Line’s unique fabrication capabilities were developed from the ground up to enable construction of extremely complex, high-mass flexible structures. In our almost 600 square meter (6000 square foot) high-bay facility, precision reproducible work features digitally controlled material feed for the largest fabric and film structures with material handling capability supporting multi-ton systems integration. Thin Red Line’s fully-automated calibration equipment measures fiber component elongation properties to almost thirty meters in length and loads up to 20,000 kilograms, and is capable of applying non-contact calibration marking with 0.01 millimeter resolution. Thin Red Line performs in-house design and analysis of custom fixtures for specialized contextual testing of soft material configurations.

University of Ioannina participates in the development of several research projects in the research areas of science, chemistry, new materials, economic studies, biochemistry, biology, medicine, biomedicine, nursing care, environment, agriculture, education technologies and science, arts, as well as information and communication technologies.

entityDescription:
AIDRO Hydraulics & 3D Printing is an Italian high-tech SME specialized on the design and manufacturing of hydraulic parts and metal devices, both by traditional technologies and by metal Additive Manufacturing (AM).
With 3.8m€ turnover and 15 employees, the company was founded almost 40 years ago as an engineering and manufacturing company for Fluid Power solutions, such as hydraulic valves, hydraulic manifolds, heat exchangers. In search of a market differentiation and pushed by the need to innovate, in 2016 metal AM was introduced as production process on top of existing core activities.AM is used to produce parts of new and existing products, bringing them value in terms of weight saving, customization, fast prototyping, function/component integration and material substitution. In few years, by experimenting and by doing, Aidro has become acknowledged for being a worldwide pioneer in combining Fluid Power, its core competence, to AM know-how. Moreover, AM proved to be an enabling technology for the company, opening new markets, like Oil & Gas and Aerospace. Leveraging its hands-on experience, the company became active member of international working groups focused on the definition of guidelines and standard for AM in Oil & Gas sector (Joint Innovation Program piloted by DNV GL and American Petroleum Institute). In 2018, Aidro obtained the aeronautical certification EN9100 and became member of the Lombardy Aerospace Cluster, a business network including prime and tier companies, which defined specific programs on AM for aerospace. Thanks to the new business relationship established, Aidro is now proving the viability of AM for very regulated industries and in some challenging applications, especially those where fluids under pressure flow in channels, specifically re-designed according to new concepts and free form geometries enabled by AM technology. In 2019, Aidro has been invited by EOS - Electro Optical System, the worldwide technology and market leader in AM, to join as a partner its ecosystem. Currently Aidro owns nr. 2 EOS M290 metal printers (LPBF) and has in-house design, post-finishing capacities and skilled engineers and operators.

entityDescription: At Beamagine we build solid-state imaging lidars for demanding applications, including all types of autonomous vehicles or high-accuracy inspection. The lack of moving elements provides L3CAM with the highest levels of robustness and long term stability in the market. Furthermore, it also provides the best capabilities in terms of balance of image resolution and frame rate on the market. Further, L3CAM may combine passive and active imaging modes in a single unit. The result is fused information without parallax errors, which you may call either an image with depth information, or a point cloud with colour information embedded. RGB, SWIR or polarimetric imaging modes are available and can be selected by the user. Units including IMUs or GPS are also available.

We secure embedded and critical systems, from the design phase right up to the technical evaluation and accreditation phase.
Thanks to our dedicated Space and Defense Skills Center, we work on the ground segments or global system and cloud base architectures security, of main European missions and satellites (ISIS, GALILEO) to assist our manufacturer customers and space data managers in Europe.
We are involved in securing dual systems by deploying our industrialized methodologies of Risk & COTS Assessment, cyber-security management for complex projects, technical evaluation and hacking of embedded components or of business information systems.

- Support for accreditation of ground systems

- Drafting of approval documentation

entityDescription:
Cellnex Telecom is the main infrastructure operator for wireless telecommunication in Europe.
Cellnex has made a firm commitment to developing its network, which currently comprises c.128,000 sites, 71,000 of them already in the portfolio and the rest in the process of closing or planned roll-outs up to 2030 and positions the company to develop new generation networks. It provides services in Spain, Italy, Netherlands, United Kingdom, France, Switzerland, Ireland, Poland, Portugal, Austria, Denmark and Sweden thanks to the investments undertaken to boost its transformation and internationalisation drive.
Offers to its customers a range of services to guarantee the conditions for reliable and high-quality transmission of voice, data and audiovisual contents.
It also develops solutions in the field of “smart city” projects that optimise services to the citizen via networks and services that facilitate municipal management. In this area, Cellnex Telecom is deploying a network of intelligent communications that permits a connection between objects, and therefore the development of a solid ecosystem for the Internet of Things (IoT).
Cellnex Telecom also plays a relevant role in the deployment of safety and emergency networks for the security forces, known as PPDRs (Public Protection And Disaster Relief). This line of activity summarises both the degree of expertise the company’s team of professionals and the ruggedness and reliability of the architecture of its networks and equipment.
The company is listed on the continuous market of the Spanish stock exchange and is part of the selective IBEX 35, EuroStoxx 600 and MSCI Europe indices. It is also part of the FTSE4GOOD, CDP (Carbon Disclosure Project), Sustainalytics and “Standard Ethics” sustainability indexes.

entityDescription:
EUROSENSE is an active player in geo-information services for almost 50 years now. Started as a Belgian company in the 60’s, it has nowadays expanded its working region to mainly Western and Central Europe, but can live on experiences of worldwide projects.
Both public as private customers with highly variable needs are contacting EUROSENSE to work out efficient solutions for their problems. Delivering high quality products in time and according to the specifications of the customer, is therefore the main concern of EUROSENSE
The EUROSENSE-group, existing since 1964, has nowadays wholly owned branches in Belgium (Wemmel (near Brussels), Tielt, Zeebrugge and Antwerp), The Netherlands (Breda), Germany (Rheinbach), France (Lille), Hungary (Budapest), Slovakia (Bratislava), Poland (Nadarzyn, near Warsaw), Bulgaria (Sofia), and Romania (Bucharest). The main office of the EUROSENSE-group is located in Belgium (Wemmel).
The EUROSENSE-group employs a staff of about 200 highly specialized members: engineers, geographers, topographers, hard- and software specialists, etc.
All services offered by the EUROSENSE-group are fully integrated within the group: aerial photography, aerial LIDAR (aerial laser scanning for height measurements), photo interpretation, aerial thermography, processing and interpretation of aerial and satellite images, production of photogrammetric and topographic maps, GIS- consultancy, inventory of forests and natural resources, digital orthophotography, cartography, hydrography, environmental studies, and lots of other activities. EUROSENSE offers highly accurate and technological solutions in all of these disciplines.
All production steps, from the airborne, spaceborne or seaborne data acquisition up to the finalized product, are fully integrated within the company, in order to meet the highest standards for quality, precision and reliability. EUROSENSE feels this as a requirement to guarantee that the projects are executed to the clients' most demanding specifications and desires.
Next to the available expertise within the EUROSENSE-group, EUROSENSE furthermore can appeal to partners such as “esri BeLux NV” and “Walphot”.
EUROSENSE feels very strongly about quality. The entire group works according to ISO 9001:2008 procedures and applies a quality system which is continuously improved and adapted to the latest quality needs.
International (EC, World Bank, FAO, ...) as well as national and regional governments, cities and municipalities, public and private service corporations, consultancy firms and software providers are part of EUROSENSE's clientele.

description:
For many years, fortiss has been conducting first-class research activities, with a highly-recognized level of expertise, into the development of software-intensive systems, an issue that plays a central role for Bavaria’s high-tech industry. These systems are increasingly based on closely-related technologies in the field of artificial intelligence (AI). Several aspects have special significance, including: 
- a pioneering role in the manageable development of reliable and safe software, AI and Internet of Things (IoT) applications.
- a multifaceted, direct correlation to industry partners for the solutions-oriented implementation of the results of the research and development activities.
- an attractive service offering for the transfer of knowledge related to current developments in software, AI and IoT. internal, expertise-oriented structures that offer talented researchers the best development opportunities.
In the Neuromorphic Computing field of competence, we concentrate our activities on research into the third generation of neural networks referred to as spiking neural networks. With this technology, the data between the information processing units is encoded in the form of spikes, similar to the human brain. Spiking artificial neural networks enable the energy- and latency-efficient processing of information, especially when neuromorphic hardware is utilized.

entityName: UNIV OF BERN - Mountain Research Initiative
description: Founded in 2001, the Mountain Research Initiative (MRI) is a global research coordination network that promotes global change research in mountain regions across borders and disciplines through connection and collaboration – with a view to supporting pathways towards sustainable mountain development.
entityDescription:
The Mountain Research Initiative (MRI) envisions a world in which research to identify and understand drivers and processes of global change in mountains is promoted and linked across disciplines and mountain regions worldwide.
The MRI serves as a coordination network for research collaboration, bringing the global mountain research community together. Since its origins in the 1990s, and with the founding of the MRI Coordination Office in 2001, the MRI has striven to promote basic and applied research to understand how drivers and processes of global change present challenges and opportunities in mountain social-ecological systems.
Through the convening role of the MRI Coordination Office, the MRI has initiated numerous collaborations and networks of researchers, implementing actions that enhance the profile and value of global change research in mountains, whilst also integrating and synthesizing the results of this research and thereby informing stakeholders about the implications of these results for policy and practice.

The MRI is hosted by the Centre for Development and Environment (CDE) at theUniversity of Bern, and funded by the swiss Academy of Sciences (SCNAT).

entityName: CENTRUM BADAŃ KOSMICZNYCH PAN - SPACE RESEARCH CENTRE POLISH ACADEMY OF SCIENCES
entityDescription: Centrum Badań Kosmicznych PAN (CBK PAN) (eng. Space Research Centre, Polish Academy of Sciences, SRC PAS) founded in 1977, is the only institution in Poland fully dedicated to the space research (geophysics, astrophysics, Earth sciences) and space engineering. The Centre is located in Warsaw, Bartycka 18A (headquarter), with three divisions in Wrocław (Solar Physics Department), Borówiec close to Poznań (Astrogeodynamic Observatory) and Zielona Góra (Dynamics Laboratory of Satellite Manipulators). CBK PAN has constructed over 70 instruments sent into space on board various satellites and interplanetary probes including Solar Orbiter, Chang'E-4, InSight, Herschel, Koronas-Foton, Rosetta, Mars Express and Cassini-Huygens. The first Polish scientific satellites – ‘Lem’ and ‘Heweliusz’ – were also developed at CBK PAN. Currently, the instruments for the upcoming prestigious space missions such as JUICE, IMAP, ARIEL, Comet Interceptor and ATHENA are being constructed. For many years Centre has been cooperating with the largest space agencies in the world, including the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) and the European Space Agency (ESA). Also, CBK PAN belongs to the most prestigious space research organisations.

a) Research on non-conventional technologies, to remove material by EDM, Water Jet Cutting, etc.; b) Research on Innovative Manufacturing and Rapid Tooling, for small volume production of complex parts (Silicone Rubber Tooling, Vacuum Casting, Metal Spray Tooling, Investment Casting, etc.); c) Research on CNC manufacturing;
d) Research on concurrent engineering for Competitive Manufacturing.
The future strategy of the AMaRaP research centre is to develop the ongoing research and to join integrated projects and European Research Platforms.
Cooperation with industrial partners will be a main feature of AMaRaP research centre for Product Design, Rapid Product Development and Innovative Technologies for Competitive Manufacturing. The AMaRaP research centre contributes to develop the abilities and competences of the PhD Students in TUCN. There will be undertaken both fundamental research (results will be published within ISI and BDI articles) and applied research, which will lead to commercial contracts with industrial partners (significant results will be patented). The results of this research will allow the development of new services in Romania, such as Rapid Manufacturing of Customized Implants made out of biocompatible and bioactive materials.

The University of La Rioja, recognized as a Campus of International Excellence within the Iberus project, was created on May 14, 1992 through the unanimous approval, in the Congress of Deputies, of the Law of Creation of the UR.
Inaugurated in the 1992-1993 academic year, it is currently the only public center for higher education and scientific research in this autonomous community.
In these more than twenty years, the campus has consolidated its work of higher education, research and innovation, dissemination and generation of knowledge. The University of La Rioja has trained some 20,000 thousand professionals in various fields of knowledge, has increased its teaching offer and has multiplied its research activity, closely linked to the needs of the environment, with the Institute of Vine and Wine Sciences and five own research centers.
Structured into four faculties and two university schools, it has 19 degrees adapted to the European Higher Education Area (EHEA) and imparts 19 undergraduate degrees, as well as a complete postgraduate program (master, doctorate and own degrees) and initiatives related to the lifelong training (summer courses and University of Experience).At present, it maintains in force more than 800 agreements with companies and public institutions that allow practically all of its students to carry out professional practices related to degrees; and agreements with a hundred campuses around the world that facilitate international stays for students at the University of La Rioja and give it a markedly cosmopolitan character.

entityName: UNIV FEDERICO II - Dipartimento di Scienze Chimiche
entityDescription: Department of Chemical Sciences is part of University of Napoli Federico II. The main activities are research and higher education, typical of a University Department. The Research activities cover several areas of Chemistry, including the design and synthesis of new molecules and polymers, the purification and the analytic characterization of natural and synthetic molecules, polymers and biopolymers, the structural characterization of new molecules through X-ray diffraction, nuclear magnetic resonance, optical and spin electron spectroscopy techniques, mass spectroscopy. The design, the synthesis and the characterization of new molecules are aimed, for example, to the production of innovative molecules with catalytic properties in important chemical and polymerization processes, or to the production of new functional materials, for several applications in a wide range of fields. Research activities also regard the study of biomolecules and biopolymers for applications in biotechnology, from the development of biosensors to biomedical applications, the study of organic functional molecules and organic polymers for special applications, such as the microelectronics, or the development of new materials with innovative mechanical properties, and the study of nanostructured materials for applications in several fields going from the biology to the medicine, from microelectronics to nanophotonics.

The mission of Test Industry is to become a group leader in the design and production of test stands. Test Industry group was firstly established in 2017, by including Bimal (Perugia) and Leonardo (Brescia), two international players in the field of testing. Since 2020, the two companies has merged into Test Industry S.r.l., with headquarters in Milan.

BIMAL, a brand of Test Industry S.r.l., since its establishment in 1984 has been specialized in the design and manufacture of test stands for fluidic and mechanical components with application in the fields of hydraulics, mechanics, automotive and aerospace.
With over 35 years of experience, BIMAL is today considered leading brand in the testing industry, as well as a technological leader in the field of impulse pressure testing.
The company boasts a complete technical "know-how" of its machines and carries out all the activities related to the product: mechanical and electrical design, software development, machine assembly, training and after-sales service.
BIMAL presents itself as a customer-oriented brand with an international perspective, proven by over 200 customers in over 33 countries. Offering turnkey manufacturing solutions for build to print complex parts and structures in aluminium, titanium, super alloys and composites.

entityDescription:
Founded in 1898, we have become a centre of excellence through our practice-oriented approach, international flair and integrative view of studies. 

Research and Education
The University of St.Gallen (HSG) was founded as a business academy in 1898 – in the heyday of the St.Gallen embroidery industry and is nowadays a School of Management, Economics, Law, Social Sciences, International Affairs and Computer Science. The first lectures were held in 1899. The practice-oriented approach and integrative view have characterised the education we offer since those early days. Today, we are one of Europe’s leading business schools and are EQUIS, AACSB and AMBA accredited.

Professional training and character building
In 2001, we introduced Bachelor’s and Master’s degree courses across the board and fundamentally reformed the education we offer. Since then, we no longer focus just on professional training but also on character building. At our university, you can complete studies at Bachelor’s, Master’s and Ph.D. level. The close integration of studies, further education and research is important to us.

International Collaboration
We have 200 international partner universities. Our students have the option to gain a double degree in cooperation with other universities or to spend an exchange term abroad.

Institutes and research centres
Our 42 institutes, research institutes and centers are our hallmark: the mostly autonomously organised institutes finance themselves to a large degree but are closely linked to the university. The institutes are active in research, consulting and further education.

entityName: INSTITUT CATALÀ DE RECERCA DE L'AIGUA - ICRA
entityDescription:
This research institute was created on 26 October 2006 by the Government of Catalonia within the framework of the Research Centres Programme of Catalonia (CERCA).Research Institute attached to the University of Girona, according to the Decree of the Generalitat de Catalunya of 6 July 2018.Inaugurated on 7 October 2009.The trustees supporting it arethe Catalonia Government’s Department of Businessand Knowledge (DECO), the Catalan Water Agency (ACA) and the University of Girona (UdG).The Catalan Regional Government has pledged its backing to the ICRA as a multidisciplinary water research centre.It is an international reference point that focuses research of the integral water cycle, hydraulic resources, water quality (in the broadest sense of the term: chemical, microbiological, ecological, etc.) and treatment and evaluation technologies and to transfer this knowledge to society and business network. In view of the importance of water as a fundamental commodity for life and the issues that surround it, the ICRA aims to become a pole of knowledge with international prestige in the science and technology of water. The research carried out at the ICRA has to do with all the aspects related with water,particularly those associated with its rational use and the effects of human activity on hydraulic resources. The ICRA is particularly interested in investigating and solving the impacts of drought, along with the aspects of quality in the treatment and reuse of water, dedicating priority attention to the Mediterranean Sea.
In brief,the ICRA has been created to conducttop-quality multidisciplinary research in the world of water.

Mission:
ICRA's mission is achieving scientific excellence at the highest level in the field of integrated water cycle in order to respond globally, efficient and competitive problems and challenges linked to it.The areas of study include the state of ecosystems, water resources, the impact of new products, new technologies for the treatment and use of resources, especially in the Mediterranean.
Vision
The ICRA’s vision is to become a national and international reference point.
Objectives
Foster basic and applied research,and promote knowledge andtechnology transfer, innovationand the provision of scientific andtechnological services to public orprivate institutions and companies. Carry out top-level, worldclassresearch activities, witha coordinated, cooperativeorganization structure,encouraging contacts betweenthe ICRA’s researchers and thosefrom other institutions around theworld, applying an interdisciplinaryapproach in a broad spectrumof water-related sciences andtechnologies.
Facilitate funding of researchthrough self-generated resources,subsidies, scholarships, competitivegrants, donations and implementation of technology transfer projects awarded by bothpublic institutions and privateindividuals or companies.
Organize scientific meetingsboth within Spain and abroadand provide specialist servicesand products to the scientificcommunity.
Foster activitiesthat contributeto promoting research in water relatedsciences and technologiesand achieving the ICRA’s primaryobjectives.

entityDescription:
WROCŁAW UNIVERSITY OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND LIFE SCIENCES (WUELS) is one of the best specialized Universities in the country. It focuses its wide-ranging activities on education and research covering agriculture and related sciences. The profile of the WUELS and its mission are directly involved in transformation programmes dealing with rural development and food quality and management, with full respect paid to social support and interaction. The knowledge acquired and the research projects carried out at the WUELS make provision for future development, regarding all aspects of environmentally sustainable development, which is friendly to human and animal welfare.
At present, Wrocław University of Environmental and Life Sciences, a well-recognised scientific and educational centre, is the only agricultural University in the south-west region of Poland. The WUELS employs about 1,600 people, among them 748 are academic teachers. Young faculty represents more than 200 graduate students and 380 scientists under 35 years. Nearly 10 thousand of students are enrolled on 5 faculties in the WUELS. Two campuses located in the centre of Wroclaw have a modern teaching facilities, well-equipped laboratories, and lecture halls. In 2015, high-tech Centre for Geo-Info-Hydro was opened and scientific equipment with a total value of over PLN 16 million was purchase.

description:
Methods and Tools for the Development of Mission-Critical Software-Intensive Systems
Size and complexity of Software increase dramatically in new systems. Moreover, it plays a more and more critical role in many application areas such as avionics, space, ground transportation, automotive, medical devices or nuclear plants. Like in many other engineering domains, size and complexity can be mastered by putting more effort in the early stages of the software development life-cycle. This is also the way to go to increase at the same time quality and productivity for a software intensive project. 
To achieve these goals, Ellidiss offers products, technologies and services that are focused on: 
- An industry proven software design methodology (HOOD). 
- A rigorous architectural design language for the software within its execution environment (AADL). 
- A powerful model processing technology based on the use of the prolog language (LMP).
entityDescription: Ellidiss Technologies provides technical support on software intensive critical systems modelling and verification technologies, and related development processes. Ellidiss Technologies activities consist in:- Technical support to projects using the HOOD design tools (Stood, CP-Hood). - Development of the AADL Inspector model verification framework.- Training courses for tools users or administrators. - Consulting actions for start-up, review or validation of projects using the HOOD method or the AADL architecture language, and for Ada or C reverse engineering.- Tools customization, and modification or creation of new plugins (code generators, checkers), in order to tailorize the usage of the tool within the software development process.- Providing expertise in software engineering and CASE tool architecture.- Participation to innovative Research & Development projects within which Ellidiss Technologies brings its various skills in software tooling technology (prototyping) and contributes to enforcing the links between research organizations and large industrial firms. - Software development using in-house technologies such as LMP (Logic Model Processing) and GMP (Graphic Model Processing). - Active contribution to standardization committees, like the new SysMLv2 modeling language, the architecture description language AADL (Architecture Analysis and Design Language) and promotion of existing standards like the HOOD method (Hierarchical Object Oriented Design).

entityDescription:
AdditiveLab BVBA specializes in finite-element based simulation solutions for metal Additive Manufacturing. Finite element based AM simulation is currently the only existing tool to predict potential metal powder-bed based manufacturing scenarios prior to the actual manufacturing process. AdditiveLab solves the needs of process engineers, design engineers, researchers and scientists working in AM who strive to efficiently investigate, understand and optimize their manufacturing processes. With this predictive capability researchers and engineers can virtually test and optimize different machine, material or manufacturing configurations, and subsequently reduce process failure risk and increase efficiency of the manufacturing process.

Competitive AM simulation solution providers offer predefined AM physics models with rigid workflows and restricted access to simulation data, limiting the users ability to create customized simulation models and in-depth simulation-based assessment of the process. AdditiveLab addresses these limitations; it is currently the only company offering software tool on the market that provides full and unrestricted access to all simulation functionality and simulation data to allow for extensive simulation customization and in-depth result assessment. This guarantees a more customized, accurate and efficient way to simulate the AM process.

AdditiveLab Company develops and distributes AdditiveLab RESEARCH and AdditiveLab LITE software. The software are sold on an annual basis limited to a specific machine at the customer site. In addition to the software, the AdditiveLab team also provides simulation consultancy services. These services are sold to AdditiveLab software’s existing users or to non-user companies based on customer demand.

entityDescription: Fureho designs, develops and manufactures 3D fabric reinforcements for composite materials. The 3D fabrics are produced using fibres such as carbon, ceramic, aramid etc. Among carbon fibres, Furheo has developed the capability to process both PAN and Pitch types of carbon fibres. The Pitch carbon fibre 3D fabric reinforced composite material enables customised three-directional heat conductance. Such lightweight and strong heat-conducting composite materials offer novel thermal management solutions e.g. for dissipating heat from electronic systems. The values such a solution offers are the ability to customise the desired thermal pathways with reduced weight and thus simplify designs for compact and improved efficiency of the electronic systems.

entityDescription: Andreas Vogler Studio is an architecture and design studio based in Munich and founded by Swiss architect and designer Andreas Vogler. The studio combines the fields of Aerospace, Art and Architecture and is following a pull-technology innovation approach. Trans-disciplinary thinking is an important part of the design process. Design is understood as a process for complex problem solving using scientific methods, technological know-how and artistic intuition. The Studio has experience in space mission planning for orbital, lunar and Mars environments. With this background and approach the studio works easily into new fields of technology and keeps the human being, as society and as individual in focus. The future of design is to help companies to create products and buildings, which are more intelligent and which help to preserve our planet and not to destroy it. The role of the designer will become the role of an integrator of digitalization and sustainability, paired with aesthetic and common sense. Designers help to generate alternative futures, but not alternative facts. The studio’s recent work includes the Swiss General Consulate in Munich, the residence of the General Consul of Switzerland in Munich and a new double deck High Speed Train for the United Kingdom developed with the German Aerospace Center DLR. Clients include the public and private sector. Projects of Andreas Vogler have been exhibited in Centre Pompidou, Paris and are included in the permanent collections of the Museum of Modern Art MoMA, New York and the Museum of Science and Industry, Chicago. He is a member of the Bavarian Chamber of Architects, Deutscher Werkbund, the German Society of Architects BDA and the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics (AIAA). He won the German Design Award, the IF Award and Red Dot Award.

The future of design is to help companies to create products and buildings, which are more intelligent and which help to preserve our planet and not to destroy it. The role of the designer will become the role of an integrator of digitalization and sustainability, paired with aesthetic and common sense. Designers help to generate alternative futures, but not alternative facts. The studio’s recent work includes the Swiss General Consulate in Munich, the residence of the General Consul of Switzerland in Munich and a new double deck High Speed Train for the United Kingdom developed with the German Aerospace Center DLR. Clients include the public and private sector. Projects of Andreas Vogler have been exhibited in Centre Pompidou, Paris and are included in the permanent collections of the Museum of Modern Art MoMA, New York and the Museum of Science and Industry, Chicago. He is a member of the Bavarian Chamber of Architects, Deutscher Werkbund, the German Society of Architects BDA and the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics (AIAA). He won the German Design Award, the IF Award and Red Dot Award.

entityName: DLR - INSTITUTE FOR SOLAR-TERRESTRIAL PHYSICS (DLR SO)
entityDescription:
The Institute for Solar-Terrestrial Physics scientific deals with the state and dynamics of the Ionosphere-Thermosphere-Magnetosphere System (ITM) and it´s driving by the Sun and by the lower and middle atmosphere. Within this research field, the Institute for Solar-Terrestrial Physics will focus on the study of Space Weather. Space Weather refers to conditions on the Sun and in the solar wind, magnetosphere, ionosphere and thermosphere that can influence the performance and reliability of space-borne and ground-based technological systems and endanger human life. Space Weather is known to possibly lead to significant perturbations of modern communication and navigation systems and hence to increased risks on safety, economical loss, and reduced life quality. The Institute for Solar-Terrestrial Physics covers both basic and applied research on space weather. The aim is to protect national infrastructures and support affected industries through timely, accurate and reliable observations and forecasts.
Main research focus areas are:
- Investigation of solar terrestrial processes in near Earth space to deepen the understanding of complex coupling processes primarily in the thermosphere and ionosphere and to derive information about potential space weather hazards and their prevention.
- Data-driven physical modelling of solar-terrestrial coupling processes based on energetic particle streams and radiation effects as well as corresponding propagation effects in near Earth space.
- Development of methods to measure, evaluate and predict physical as well as technical quantities, which describe the effects of space weather on technical systems.

entityDescription:
Metaspectral is an artificial intelligence company developing advanced hyperspectral and multispectral data exploitation technologies for space, defence, environmental, and industrial applications. Its core capability is real-time AI-powered spectral intelligence: transforming high-dimensional satellite and airborne imagery into actionable insights about materials, objects, and environmental conditions. Metaspectral’s Clarity AI platform supports workflows such as material classification, spectral unmixing, target detection, anomaly detection, change detection, and quantitative estimation of physical or chemical properties.
For ESA, Metaspectral’s technology is relevant across next-generation Earth observation, onboard processing, and downstream applications. The company combines advanced hyperspectral compression, scalable AI analytics, agentic AI, and user-facing geospatial software to reduce data bottlenecks and make spectral imagery easier to analyze and operationalize. This can support use cases such as environmental monitoring, climate and greenhouse gas analysis, land restoration, resource mapping, maritime awareness, and security-related applications where material-level intelligence is critical.

Research and development 
A3 fosters research and development of technologies, products and services in the aerospace sector, ensuring economic and scientific benefit. 

Inter-mediation 
A3 is a focal point for the interconnection of economic entities in the domestic and international markets for the industry in the aerospace sector. A3 is a mediator between scientific research institutions and economic entities oriented to develop new technologies for aerospace sector with the aim of raising the profile of the domestic aviation space activities both on the domestic and international level. A3 is a focal point for the international aerospace agencies creating the environment where all stakeholders, i.e. industry, academy and public sector, are involved thus enabling the growth in this rapidly changing sector. 

Education and counselling 
A3 provides business and technology consulting for operators and government bodies, expert body to express their opinion on matters of public interest in the field of space technology and aeronautics and the link with supporting scientific and technical disciplines, education and popularization programs in aerospace sector. A3 inspires and supports education and training of the rising generation of qualified aerospace experts and scientists. 

Regional cooperation 
Cooperation rather than competition is the essence of success. Aerospace sector is especially demanding on wide range of knowledge and skills and without their sharing among the countries of the region, and beyond, individual effort of one country is predestined for failure. This observation is great motivation for A3 to congregate aerospace efforts into the regional cooperation.

entityDescription:
Materials Science and Environmental Engineering support sustainable development, where materials science combines natural sciences and engineering expertise to collaborate with industry, chemistry focuses on new functional materials and technologies based on them, and the core of environmental technology is on bio- and circular economy technologies and processes.​

The research in the Unit of Materials Science and Environmental Engineering is focused on three research fields:
Engineering Materials Science utilizes new breakthrough materials to address future challenges related to the environment, energy and human welfare. We develop solutions for all materials used in industrial applications, such as metals, ceramics, elastomers, composites and paper-based materials, as well as study and develop different engineering coatings and surfaces. We take pride in our excellent quality of education; our teachers, laboratories and research are at the cutting edge of materials science in Finland. 
In Bio and Circular Economy, the research focuses on environmental technology, bioenergy and biorefining, and industrial biotechnology with the ultimate goal to promote a cleaner and safer future for the benefit of people and the environment. The research connects widely with water, waste and energy sectors. 
In Chemistry and Advanced Materials, the goal is to foster interdisciplinary solutions for contemporary problems cemented in chemistry in a vivid and international research environment, through privileged access to state-of-the-art instrumentation. We also offer a broad and high-level chemistry education required for successful career development in modern research and industry.

entityDescription:
We are shifting the research paradigm from inefficient 2D cell culture to more relevant 3D culture.

Research of the past years has shown that cells cultured in vitro in three-dimensional (3D) resemble their physiological aspects in vivo much better than cells cultured traditionally on the flat surfaces of tissue culture plates (2D). It is reflected in differential gene expression level, cell morphology, and biomarker expression level. As a consequence, 3D cell culture is often the better choice for research and development. We had developed a unique hydrogel for 3D cell culture, called LifeGel. LifeGelis protein-based hydrogel, free from any growth factors and highly reproducible.

entityDescription:
E4SMA offers its experience to Companies, Institutions and Government Agencies who are responsible of decision-making activities in the energy and environmental fields.
What we do:
- We develop customized energy system models for informed energy systems planning decisions.
- We deliver quantitative and model-based analyses related to the energy transition, climate policies, technology innovation and systems resiliency.
- We provide technical assistance to entities interested in the strategic analysis of the energy system and the development of policy plans.
- We deliver capacity building and training.
E4SMA can support energy decision makers at various geographic scale (from city-level to global), along the entire problem chain: from the definition and formalisation of the decision problem, the data collection, elaboration and organisation, the model development, the quantitative analysis, and the comparison of implications between alternative energy, emissions, and policy pathways.
 
Our services:
Development of customized energy models
o Veda TIMES energy systems models.
o Multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) tools, e.g. PROMETHEE.
o Electricity focused models, e.g. Balmorel, PLEXOS.
o Open-source models, e.g. OSeMOSYS.
o Other techniques and tools.

Consultancy and technical assistances
o Implementation of energy/environmental strategies and plans.
o Delivery of policy and technology-oriented scenario analysis related to the energy transition, climate policies, technology innovation and systems resiliency.
o Impact assessments of energy and climate policies.
o Development of technology roadmaps.
o Maintenance and enhancement of existing energy systems modelling tools.

Capacity building, training and development of training material and manuals
o Capacity building and training activities on Veda TIMES, OSeMOSYS and other tools.
o Preparation of reports and training manuals for techno-economic models.

entityName: Institute of Metals and Technology - IMT
entityDescription:
TheInstitute of Metals and Technology (IMT) was established in 1948 to provide support for the steel industry and became a public research institute in 1997.Itsmission is to create new knowledge in the fields of metallurgy, metallic materials, nanoscience and nanotechnology, vacuum optoelectronics, metrology, engineering materials, environmental protection; transfer of knowledge to industry and training of young researchers.The generalaim is to improve the quality of life and enable sustainable development.
The Institute primarily works in the field of research of metallic materials with an emphasis on research related to steel and aluminium alloys. The main activity of the institute is conducting high-quality research activities in the fields that are of national importance for Slovenia, have a high impact, are in the public interest and are expected to prosper also in the following decades. The main missions of the institute are basic and applied research, developmental and infrastructural activities according totheResearch and Innovation Strategy of Slovenia.
TheInstitute provides basic scientific research according to threeresearch programmesand theresearch infrastructurefinanced by the Slovenian Research Agency:
- P2-0132 Physics and chemistry of surfaces of metallic materials
- P2-0050 Metallic materials and technology
- P2-0056 Vacuum techniques and materials for electronics
- I0-0006 Research infrastructure activity IMT
Theresearch at IMT is organised within threescientific-research departments: Physics and Chemistry of Materials, Metallic Materials and Technology, and Vacuum Science and Opto- Electronics.
IMT is a publisher ofaperiodic scientific journal Materiali in tehnologije -Metals and Technology (MIT), which publishes original and review scientific papers as well as technical news in theoretical and applied natural sciences and technologies from the fields of metallic and inorganic materials, polymers, vacuum technology and nanomaterials.

Institute of Electronic Communications (Vyskumny ustav spojov,VUS), non-profit organization, is the leading R&D centre for electronic communications and postal services in Slovakia. VUS performs project based activities in selected areas of electronic communications and postal services. Using well-equipped accredited laboratories, VUS provides testing and special measurements for various customers including metrology services. Its wide scope of activities covers also technical standardization and other services focused on frequency planning, statistical surveys, consultancy services and many other issues. 
VUS is a prominent research institution involved in performing key activities for bodies of public administration and regulation in the sector of electronic communications. Results of R&D projects produced by VUS for the Ministry of Transport and Construction of the Slovak Republic make a significant contribution in the preparation of conceptions, strategic and developmental documents, new legislation, shaping and promoting state policy in electronic communications sector in Slovakia. VUS also provides technical assistance for Regulatory Authority for Electronic Communications and Postal Services. In addition, VUS provides technical services for providers of electronic communications networks and services. 
The main objective of VUS is to react promptly to fast technological development and fully satisfy increasing needs of customers both in public and private sphere.

description:
Founded in 2016 and supported by top-tier investors and a management team with global legitimacy and track records, Kayrros is the leading global Asset Observation Platform. The company is currently headquartered in Paris with offices in London, Houston, New York, Bangalore and Singapore. 
Strong of 115 FTEs, of which 60 MSc and 20-plus PhDs, Kayrros’s uses of Asset Observation takes Earth Observation to a new dimension : fusing together all data available on a given industry asset, including satellite imagery, to provide reliable, frequent, accurate, geo-referenced, and time-stamped information on the status of selected physical assets. With its dominance of the largest -non-defense- sectors—Energy, Natural Resources and Environment —Kayrros observes more than 200,000 assets daily, and enables customers to uncover, comprehend, visualize and make actionable use of real-time data in mission-critical environments. 
Since its foundation, Kayrros has partnered with world-class research institutions. Most of Kayrros’ projects rely on research work jointly developed with internal teams. In particular, Kayrros won the Concours Mondial d’Innovation in the Big Data category and was awarded the largest ever research grant from the ESA to a private company. Furthermore, Kayrros was awarded an EASME grant to develop a new predictive analytic tool to monitor the energy sector, and conducted the project with success up to the commercial phase later on. Our recent contributions to the Carbon Monitor and our 5-year long expertise in AI and satellite imagery make Kayrros the leading institution to design AI-based solutions to climate change.

entityDescription: With 17 Faculties members, the university is turning into a central development institution attracting talented students from all over the world and providing a development context where excellence is at home at all levels. The management is aware that close ties between the university as a central educational and research institution and its local environment and the industry are of the utmost importance. For this reason, various activities aimed at integrating knowledge and R&D with the industry are being implemented in order to initiate concrete projects contributing to new jobs and new products with high added value. The University of Maribor is thus bringing together knowledge, research findings and the industry. The central project in this area is called IOT – Innovative Open Technologies. The information portal Vzhodna.si will serve as an entry point also in other development projects. These are only a few examples indicating the direction of future development of the University of Maribor. However, various impressive accomplishments can already be celebrated. The development of the first Slovene nanosatellite going into space, the success of the students participating in the Student Formula project, permanent high scores in the Imagine Cup international student competition for innovativeness, technological solutions and development, the prestigious Reimagine Education award for the Demola project where students work on concrete solutions to problems found in companies – placing the University of Maribor alongside the most prestigious universities – are only a few examples of UM's most notable achievements.The University of Maribor is developing new fields, testing new teaching and learning methods and constantly searching for new methods of cooperation with its environment. entityDescription:
Epsilon Italia srl is an independent SME established in 1996 in Mendicino (IT).
The company provides the end users with innovative and technologically advanced solutions in the geospatial domain (GIS, WEBGIS, SDIs - Spatial Data Infrastructures, Satellite Remote Sensing - marine and terrestrial applications, GI Standards).

Epsilon Italia is actively involved in Copernicus:
· As partner of the project EO4GEO “Towards an innovative strategy for skills development and capacity building in the space geo-information sector supporting Copernicus User Uptake”.
· As partner of the consortium executing the EEA Framework Contract “Services supporting the operation and evolution of the Copernicus Reference Data Access node – CORDA”.
· As leader of the research project “TEMAR – Techniques and tools for the analysis and the assessment of the risk of pollution of the bathing waters”, using Copernicus Sentinel 3 data for local scale applications based on space and in-situ data.
Since the entry into force of the European INSPIRE Directive EC/02/2007 link:http://inspire.ec.europa.eu/), the company has been providing professional technical services related to the implementation of the legally binding requirements of the Directive. Support is given for the overall INSPIRE harmonisation process: from transformation and validation of heterogeneous source data and metadata to the publication of Network Services for INSPIRE datasets.
Since 2016 the company is supporting EEA (Environmental European Agency) in activities related to reuse of INSPIRE (data, metadata and services) in e-reporting (CDDA, EU Registry on industrial sites, Environmental Noise Directive) and for Copernicus in situ (CORDA multi-country datasets).

It is member of the OGC – Open Geospatial Consortium.

entityDescription: LIDARIS is an innovative SME offering Laser-Induced Damage Threshold (LIDT) metrology service for companies involved in laser optics development, application and distribution. Following a recent optimization of laser damage testing process, a LIDARIS performs high throughput testing of optical parts in a wide range of environmental conditions. Multi wavelength testing at high (up to 200 kHz) pulse repetition rates and durations ranging from femto- to nanosecond are available at LIDARIS both in vacuum and air. All the testing is fully compatible with currently existing ISO 21254(-1,2,3) standards. Detailed and comprehensive measurement reports are delivered to LIDARIS customers after testing. The key benefits appreciated by LIDARIS customers include: ¿ Guidance in the optimization of the manufacturing of optical elements (either polishing or coating deposition processes) for high power laser applications; ¿ Evaluation of LIDT in a very broad range of experimental conditions; ¿ Help in the selection of appropriate optics vendors for a laser application; ¿ High throughput FEMTO-second and nano-second laser damage certification (as well as non destructive LIDT testing for high quality optics); ¿ Detailed testing and measurement reports containing easy to understand statistical data; ¿ Speed and efficiency in processing the testing orders; ¿ Consulting and cooperation in scientific Research and Development (R&D) projects;

We have since gained dynamic international support from ESA/InnovateUK, the Stanford Space Rendezvous Lab, investors connected to the telecom industry, and established satellite manufacturers in Europe through infrastructure, technical expertise and funding.
Based in Toulouse (FR), Singapore and the UK, we recruited experienced space talent, and are collaborating with some of the best experts in the industry to enable GEO satellite life extension options for global telecommunications companies, at a fraction of market costs.

History

We have since gained dynamic international support from ESA/InnovateUK, the Stanford Space Rendezvous Lab, investors connected to the telecom industry, and established satellite manufacturers in Europe through infrastructure, technical expertise and funding.
​

Read the article Services & technology
We are building core competency in two areas:
- Autonomous space navigation. A plug and play module which allows satellites to track other satellites using several optical sensors and a computer, and which ultimately will be utilized for situational awareness (SSA), high precision formation flying and rendezvous operations between satellites. 

- Docking. A mechanical docking system which can anchor our satellites to other satellites. This system targets features that are currently common to 90% of satellites.

The combination of these two capabilities is a core competency which will become building blocks of
many crucial future applications in the space industry
in the next 10 - 20 years.

A revolution in spacecraft design will move us towards modular, fractionated and other systems which will allow satellites to be rapidly upgradeable space platforms instead of customized, single mission oriented relics of the past. Core competency in navigation will be crucial for these platforms to thrive

entityDescription:
AMSAT-Deutschland e.V., or AMSAT-DL for short, was founded in April 1973 in Marburg/Lahn and is an association of dedicated engineers, technicians, scientists, students, radio amateurs and space enthusiasts. AMSAT-DL develop, build, operate and use satellites for non-commercial purposes.

AMSAT-DL is one of the few space organizations that carry out satellite projects from planning through development and construction to operations. AMSAT-DL projects strictly follow the "open source" principle. This means that the techniques and procedures developed can be viewed and used by third parties. This also applies to the knowledge and research results gained during operational use.

The purpose of the association is the promotion of science and research.

The purpose of the statutes is realized in particular by the creation and operation of space satellite systems and high-flying communications systems for the performance of communication and space science research.

The association carries out its scientific research with the assistance of the amateur radio services and their associations in order to obtain a large number of observation results. The scientific research results obtained are made generally available through appropriate publications.

EIE GROUP is an engineering company, an excellence in the Italian Industrial panorama. It is a leader in Management & Contracting, Engineering & Design, Production & Services, and it operates in the fields of Astronomy, Astrophysics and the Big Science, besides producing machines, equipment and integrated systems for the industry and the scientific research fields.
It has focused on the development of industrial and civil projects, becoming a leader in the production of Telescopes, Radio-telescopes, Astronomical Observatories and scientific equipment, all through focused engineering assets and solid know-how in fabrication and assembly processes, as well as in mechanisms and plants management.

entityDescription:
Based in Milan and offices in Shanghai and Tirana, Stefano Boeri Architetti (Boeri Studio until 2008) has been dedicated to design and research since 1993, mainly in the architectural and urban planning, but also in the cultural, design and interior design fields. "Multiplicity" is the guideline that has guided a multifaceted activity in over 20 years and spread through design themes and urban and social geographies of the world. 
An approach that has allowed the firm to acquire a strongly defined identity and to establish itself as a point of reference at an Italian and international level in areas such as sustainable biodiversity architecture, social housing, urban development strategies at different scales. Stefano Boeri Architetti has developed architectural and urban regeneration projects in complex places and in multiple continents, supporting and enhancing the synergies between the various development actors, public and private. 
Since 2014 SBA has been active in China with an office in Shanghai headed by Stefano Boeri and Yibo Xu. Among the most recent completed projects, the renovation of the former headquarters of the Shanghai Stock Exchange, transformed in 2015 into a vital center of cultural exchange. In the vast series of works in progress the Vertical Forest of Nanjing, the first Vertical Forest in China: two towers that include in the architecture of the facades 800 trees of 27 native species and over 2,500 shrubs and fall plants, which will reduce CO2 emissions of about 18 tons per year, producing about 16.5 tons of oxygen. Urban, technological and conceptual extension of Bosco Verticale, the Forest City project, presented for the first time at the Paris Climate Conference (COP 21) as a model of a sustainable city, thanks to its ability to consume several tons of CO2 and to produce oxygen in one of the most polluted areas in the world: the region between Bejing, Tianjin and Hebei. Since 2015 Stefano Boeri Architetti has also been operating through an office in Tirana, which is currently developing the new Town Plan and Strategic Vision Project for the city. Baptized "Tirana 2030", the intervention aims at redefining the Albanian capital as a new metropolitan city and is constituted as the largest urban reform in Albania in the last 25 years.
Projects
In addition to the Tirana Master Plan, Stefano Boeri Architetti is developing numerous urban projects, including the one for the new Master Plan for the Republic of San Marino. The assignment for the Doha Qatar New Port Project masterplan and for the development of the "Maspero triangle", a complex of towers and public services along the Nile, in the heart of Cairo, is also recent: an intervention for which he was selected by the Government Egyptian along with three other important international architectural firms. In addition to the famous Bosco Verticale in Milan, the most well-known and relevant built projects include the Villa Méditerranée in Marseille and the Casa del Mare on the island of La Maddalena, in Sardinia. In recent years, only in Italy, SBA has carried out, among others: the Casabosco research for a model of low-cost and sustainable social housing, the interior design for the stations of the new Italian railway company NTV, the RCS headquarters - Corriere della Sera, the restructuring of the Telecom headquarters in Rome. The firm also defined the guidelines and the concept plan for the universal exhibition EXPO Milan 2015, in collaboration with prominent designers such as Richard Burdett, Jacques Herzog and William MacDonough.

Genegoggle is a precision medicine biotech company with the goal of discovering novel therapeutics and intelligent systems to improve human health by leveraging multi-dimensional genomic and epigenetic elements. We apply interdisciplinary expertise and multi-omic strategies to precision medicine and chronic diseases on the Earth and beyond.
We are focused on epigenetic mechanisms of gene expression regulation and the packaging of the DNA chain in the cell nucleus. We identify intracellular processes that can be used for diagnostic and therapeutic purposes. We are particularly interested in the regulatory modes triggered by extracellular factors like medical treatments or modified environments.

At Genegoggle our mission is to enhance the understanding of the human genome and provide tools to support human health. Our personalized approach is powered by artificial intelligence. Our team gathers deep expertise in epigenetics, computational biology, machine learning, and software engineering, and data visualization to mark new directions in medical genomics.

entityDescription:
The Foundation's main purpose is to combat and mitigate human-induced climate change using solutions based on nature and pursue civic, solidarity and social utility purposes. The Foundation's activity is divided into the following activities.
Arboreal Plant Projects
These are projects that create arboreal plants in previously not wooded areas or arboreal plants in areas where the forest has been cleared by natural or anthropogenic disturbances.
Sustainable Forest Management Projects
These are projects aimed at enhancing the storage of carbon in the forest, at mitigating or preventing the effects of natural disturbances and at increasing the resistance and resilience of forest stands to climate change.
Supply Chain Projects
These are projects aimed at enhancing local supply chains and the efficient use of resources from the point of view of the effects on the climate from a bioeconomy and circular economy perspective.
Research and Transfer Projects
These are projects that aim to improve and transfer knowledge on the techniques for designing, planting and maintaining trees in urban and rural environments, on the benefits they generate, on the response of trees and forests to environmental stress factors and the effects of climate crisis. The Foundation develops on a scientific basis tools to support decisions for the implementation of plant, sustainable management and supply chain projects.
Promotion, Training and Communication Projects
Activities aimed at disseminating knowledge based on the best science available to technicians, administrators and citizens regarding the Foundation's objectives and support for governance policies of local territories.

Ovidius” University of Constanta (www.univ-ovidius.ro) is the leading Academic institution from the South-East Region of Romania. The 15.000 students of OUC are registered in 16 faculties, covering a wide range of subjects, from life sciences and humanities to engineering and fundamental sciences. The Institute for Nanotechnologies and Alternative Energy Sources (INAES) is an autonomous research institute established in 2011 by the OUC Senate in order to bridge the gap between scientific research and education activities carried out in the university with the needs for innovation, technology development and smart specializations from the regional economy.

The research projects developed by the INAES cover a wide range of fields, in an interdisciplinary approach, structured on 4 main topics: sustainable energy solutions, materials and nanotechnologies, multiscale modelling, simulation and sustainable transport systems.
The research team involved in the current project covers competencies related to experimental investigations, modelling and simulation, engineering, renewable energy sources, biology-environment, life cycle assessment.
At the same time, the research teams of INAES are developing cooperative activities under the frame of the Black Sea Universities Network (BSUN) - a network of more than 120 universities from the Black Sea Region (www.bsun.org).

entityDescription:
The Ferdinand-Braun-Institut gGmbH, Leibniz-Institut fuer Hoechstfrequenztechnik (FBH) researches electronic and optical components, modules and systems based on compound semiconductors. These devices are key enablers that address the needs of today’s society in fields like communications, energy, health, and mobility. Specifically, FBH develops light sources from the visible to the ultra-violet spectral range: high-power diode lasers with excellent beam quality, UV light sources and hybrid laser modules. Applications range from medical technology, high-precision metrology and sensors to optical communications in space and integrated quantum technology. In the field of microwaves, FBH develops high-efficiency multi-functional power amplifiers and millimeter wave frontends targeting energy-efficient mobile communications, industrial sensing and imaging as well as car safety systems. In addition, high-speed laser drivers are fabricated for use in a variety of applications.
The FBH is a center of competence for III-V compound semiconductors covering the full range of capabilities, from design through fabrication to device characterization. Within Research Fab Microelectronics Germany (Forschungsfabrik Mikroelektronik Deutschland), FBH joins forces with 12 other German research institutes, thus offering the complete micro and nanoelectronics value chain as a one-stop-shop.
In close cooperation and strategic partnerships with industry, FBH's research results lead to cutting-edge products. The institute also successfully turns innovative product ideas into spin-off companies. With its Prototype Engineering Lab, the institute strengthens its cooperation with customers in industry by turning excellent research results into market-oriented products, processes, and services. The institute thereby offers its international customer base complete solutions and know-how as a one-stop agency – from design to ready-to-use modules and prototypes.

entityDescription:
The Consortium of Università e Laboratori Industriali per lo Sviluppo dei Sistemi Elettronici (ULISSE) is composed of: University of Genova, University of Pavia, University of Roma Tor Vergata, Roma TRE University, G&A Engineering s.r.l. and SkyTechnology s.r.l. The Consortium has two sites: in Roma and Genova. The president is Gian Carlo Cardarilli, full professor of Digital Electronics and Electronics for Communication Systems at the University of Rome Tor Vergata. The scope of the Consortium is: 1) Foster the Innovation Technology in the Industry environment by taking advantage as much as possible of the research activities, capabilities and of the internal organisation of the associate partners. 2) Facilitate the Technological Transfer between the research activities carried out by the associate partners and the production line aiming at improving the real application of the research outcomes. Know how points : 1) Advanced CMOS technologies; 2) Non-volatile memories; 3) Custom and semicustom design (based on ASIC and FPGA); 4) Digital, analog and mixed signal design; 5) Antennas 6) High frequency ICs; 7) System architectures and applications; 8) Hardware implementation of DSP algorithms 9) Hardware implementation of Machine Learning algorithms.
Consorzio ULISSE organization chart is the following.
President of the Board of Directors: is the legal representative of Consorrtium 
Director: is responsible of the operative organization of the Consortium
CFO: is responsible of the administrative and financial activities
Program manager: responsible of the administrative management of the projects
The technical development of the projects takes place in collaboration with the associated universities, which provide all the necessary technical support (according to the statute of the consortium). A project manager is identified for each project. He is responsible for the overall control of the technical activities of the project.

Company description: The Consortium of Università e Laboratori Industriali per lo Sviluppo dei Sistemi Elettronici (ULISSE) is composed of: University of Genova, University of Pavia, University of Roma Tor Vergata, Roma TRE University, G&A Engineering s.r.l. and SkyTechnology s.r.l. The Consortium has two sites: in Roma and Genova. The president is Gian Carlo Cardarilli, full professor of Digital Electronics and Electronics for Communication Systems at the University of Rome Tor Vergata. The scope of the Consortium is: 1) Foster the Innovation Technology in the Industry environment by taking advantage as much as possible of the research activities, capabilities and of the internal organisation of the associate partners. 2) Facilitate the Technological Transfer between the research activities carried out by the associate partners and the production line aiming at improving the real application of the research outcomes. Know how points : 1) Advanced CMOS technologies; 2) Non-volatile memories; 3) Custom and semicustom design (based on ASIC and FPGA); 4) Digital, analog and mixed signal design; 5) Antennas 6) High frequency ICs; 7) System architectures and applications; 8) Hardware implementation of DSP algorithms 9) Hardware implementation of Machine Learning algorithms.
Consorzio ULISSE organization chart is the following.
President of the Board of Directors: is the legal representative of Consorrtium 
Director: is responsible of the operative organization of the Consortium
CFO: is responsible of the administrative and financial activities
Program manager: responsible of the administrative management of the projects
The technical development of the projects takes place in collaboration with the associated universities, which provide all the necessary technical support (according to the statute of the consortium). A project manager is identified for each project. He is responsible for the overall control of the technical activities of the project.

entityDescription: Fugro Norway AS (the Company) is ultimately, wholly owned by Fugro NV, a multinational group, headquartered in the Netherlands and listed on the Amsterdam stock exchange. On a worldwide basis, Fugro employs over 10.000 people in more than 50 countries. Fugro’s current activities in Norway fall under the Fugro Marine Division. The Company currently has a total staff of 197, split in the different Service Lines (Satellite Positioning, Positioning Services, Monitoring&Forecasting, Construction Support, Marine Geophysical, Marine Geotechnical and Marine Geoconsulting) and a shared service department that provides administrative functions (IT, HR, QHSSE, legal and finance). The Positioning and Construction Services are placed in Bergen. Monitoring & Forecasting Services in Trondheim whilst Marine Geophysical, Geoconsulting and Marine Geotechnical Services are placed in Oslo. Satellite Positioning has the objective to generate optimal utilization and associated recurring revenue leveraging the Fugro GNSS network infrastructure. The purpose is to serve clients operating vessels in selected market segments with high performance GNSS positioning services. Customers may operate single vessels as well as large fleets of vessels in local, regional or global operations. Fugro is available for support of the services on a 24/7/365 basis. Fugro is also offering installation and maintenance of the related equipment onboard these vessels. Fugro is also operating certain elements of the Fugro GNSS network. Fugro continuously work on further R&D of the GNSS services, with the aim to produce more accurate and reliable services improving customer’s efficiency.

description: Nautilus – Navigation in Space is the business solution built upon decades of experience in the space sector of two world level Italian research groups, the Team of the Radioscience and Planetary Exploration Lab and the Microsatellites and Space Microsystems Lab of the University of Bologna and the DART Team of the Politecnico di Milano. Our experience covers, among others, orbit determination, GNC, mission analysis, GNSS navigation, ADCS, small satellites systems design and development. entityDescription:
Nautilus is the first European private company offering LEO and deep space navigation services. Thanks to decades of experience, the Nautilus team can deliver low-cost mission analysis and flight dynamics services both for scientific and commercial missions.

Our activities:
- Mission analysis and definition: Assess the expected performances of the trajectory reconstruction. Support to link budget definition (SNR affects radiometric noise). Support to CONOPS definition (tracking periods, maneuver execution).
- Operations: Perform Orbit Determination. Propagate the estimated trajectory, along with associated uncertainty. Assess the need for a trajectory correction maneuver. Design and optimize trajectory correction maneuver. Provide support and solutions for GNC algorithms design.
- After end of mission: Perform the a posteriori trajectory reconstruction.

entityDescription:
The company aims at using Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) data for high-precision positioning with mobile devices (smartphones).
The main background of the company lies in satellite geodesy, and its applications. Our Special emphasis is on real-time correction models/methods for satellite data, namely atmospheric corrections.
The company was established as a spin-off entity from German Research Center for Geosciences (GFZ) in Potsdam, therefore the scientific support from GFZ is guaranteed. E.g. the company has access to high accuracy real-time satellite clock and orbit corrections developed at Dept. 1 "Geodesy" of GFZ.
Applying these corrections to smartphone location data, a few meter accuracy for positioning of these devices can be achieved.
By using improved positioning accuracy, numerous applications can be supported, such as augmented reality, location-based services, mobile health applications, monitoring systems, and smart social-distancing, which is a key for avoiding the novel COVID-19 pandemic.

entityName: INSTITUT DE RECHERCHES EN INGENIERI - IREIS
entityDescription:
IREIS is the research and development entity of the HEF group based in France. HEF core activity is the surface engineering of materials including, thin film deposition using plasma vacuum process, varnish, paints, nitriding process in molten salts, electrochemical and electroless deposition, projection using plasma torch and laser patterning. The strength of HEF is based on the numerous processes and their combinations, as well as its presence in more than 21 countries. HEF group employ almost 2000 people. 
IREIS develop thin film deposition process for 30 years. The activity was originaly dedicated to the development of materials to reduce friction like diamond like carbon (DLC). IREIS develop their own plasma sources (magnetron sputtering cathodes, Microwave ECR, cathodic arc,…) and implement them in their equipment dedicated to on demand or mass production. IREIS is then in very good position to develop new processes using its knowledge in plasma reactors.
IREIS is a private laboratory and propose research contract services. To support this activity, a strong characterization platform is dedicated to surface analysis including Secondary Electronic Microscope (SEM) with EDX, Spectro-photometer with integration sphere, AFM (Atomic Force Microscope), profilometer, metallographic analysis, X fluorescence, roughness, hardness, scratch test surface tension,…
IREIS optical coating developments last now for almost 20 years with for examples the protected aluminum coating or 143 mirrors for ESA (ESTEC), the gold coating of sun shield of ISO satellite, the development of flexible electrochromic devices with CEA (SYELSO Project), silver coating for Laser Megajoule. More recently IREIS has developed selective coating for solar thermal applications on tubes 2.6 meter long. In that field, a national project objective is to conjugate thin films and diffraction gratings in order to demonstrate the interest to enhance yield of heat harnessing. Other projects include VO2 development at low temperature, research on photochromic materials using silver nanoparticles imbedded in TiO2 matrix.
All development made at IREIS in the field of thin film deposition are done using industrial size pilot machines, able to demonstrate the large scale feasibility and the production of first production lots.

entityDescription: Climateflux is a company that provides microclimatic modeling support by combining high-resolution simulation tools and monitoring techniques for the physical urban climate and physiological responses of pedestrians. The company has been actively developing software applications capable of assessing the transient behavior of outdoor spaces and microclimatic effects involving building facades, vegetation, and climatic factors. As this approach has been limited by the resolution and quality of available data, Climateflux benefits from its expertise in data-integrated models and combining the simulation approach with environmental sensing techniques to make the connection between the human factor and the built environment.
