entityDescription:
As a leading bio-tech company, we here at Algatek are revolutionising the way in which industries function. Following 7 years of research, we developed and patented a bioreactor known as the Algatek Algae Accelerator (AAA). The purpose is to grow large batches of algae in a swift manner without compromising on quality.

As a company, we are working towards our main goal of creating a future that enhances the health of feed to Humans whilst delivering oxygen, and sequestrating CO2 which protects the environment. There are three main objectives that we want to achieve:

A Better Future
Sustainable Processes
Cleaner Food and Environment
Algae is a ‘super product’ that is renewable and available in abundance. We are already revolutionising the food market, but this substance also has the potential now to support life in severe conditions.
Our method allows us to create a formula that both nourishes the body and keeps the environment protected to sustain Human life.

Our proprietary AAA bioreactor technology enables us to produce large high-quality microalgae. Unlike other methods, our AAA bioreactor technology allows us to cultivate the algae 24/7.

Industrial production of microalgae biomass is even with the latest known production technology suffering from a combination of high production costs, low yields due to reliance on climate and sunshine hours per day and fluctuating qualities. This is caused by lack of control of the critical growth parameters, such as applied levels of carbon dioxide and other nutrients, the water temperature and PH values as well as the correct light spectrums.

Here at Algatek in our "state of the art facility" we believe we can create the dream of sustained Life Support not only for human nutrition, but for the crops also that feed us.

entityDescription:
OKTAL Synthetic Environment (OKTAL-SE) was created in 2001 by its Chief Executive Officer Mr. Jean LATGER as an emanation of the OKTAL company created in 1989. Today, OKTAL-SE is part of the SOGECLAIR Group located in Toulouse-France. Our company is a human-sized structure that ensures a high reactivity and a customer focused attitude.

Our purpose is to provide customers with state of the art multi-sensor simulation software and services. Thanks to the reliability and the performance of our modeling and simulation COTS products, OKTAL-SE has become an international reference in terms of synthetic environment rendering software in both Electro-Optic (Visible, Infrared) and Radio-Frequency (Radar, GNSS) domains.

In more than 15 countries, our customers trust the OKTAL-SE simulation software as the reference and the cost effective solution to design, develop and qualify any embedded sensor system.

Since its creation, OKTAL-SE has built long term relationships with National defense agencies and key players in the aerospace and defense market. In the Electro-Optics and Radio-Frequency domains, the OKTAL-SE engineering tools have proved their validity and their efficiency on major industrial programs (SCALP, AASM…) and we are still supporting our customers all along their projects by providing them with the best of our technology and experience.

Our commitment: getting the most out of sensor simulation for your final application.

entityName: DLR - INSTITUTE OF NETWORKED ENGERY SYSTEMS (DLR VE)
entityDescription:
The Oldenburg DLR Institute of Networked Energy Systems develops technologies and concepts for the future energy supply on the basis of renewable energies. The focus is on the challenge of turning weather-dependent decentralised generation into stable and efficient energy systems. This transformation process is being researched within the framework of a consistent D3 approach (D3 = decarbonisation, decentralisation, digitisation). With its departments of Urban and Building Technologies, Energy System Technology and Energy System Analysis, the Institute is dedicated to system-oriented questions on the intelligent and efficient linking of the electricity, heat and transport sectors. System levels ranging from individual systems to 'smart' buildings to networked residential neighbourhoods and cities are considered. In addition, the Institute evaluates energy systems on a national and international level using its own network structure models and technology assessment methods.

Research Topics:
- Technologies for decentralised power and heat generation
- Technologies for sector integration in buildings, mobility and gas technology
- Power grid technology and management
- Systems integration and energy management in the smart home, smart city and smart grid
- Systems integration of various storage technologies and other flexibility options, future provision of ancillary services
- Modelling of power grids and energy systems
- Technology assessment
- Energy meteorology

NematX Ltd. is a spin-off company from ETH Zurich, incorporated in 2020 and currently supported by the ESA BIC Switzerland program. We develop new materials & manufacturing processes to solve tomorrow's technical & societal challenges - from deep sea to outer space. As the pioneering company to make liquid crystal polymers (LCPs) available for additive manufacturing/3D printing, we can offer materials and a manufacturing platform to produce the highest performing parts from polymer 3D printing. Our parts are 10x stronger than PEEK, they show >250°C heat resistance plus they show superior inertness in chemical & biological environments.

With respect to space compliance testing, ESTEC has recently performed material characterization experiments within the framework of our participation in ESA's Euro Material Ageing and ATOX campaigns. Our 3D printed LCP parts showed minimal outgassing (0.05% total mass loss) and low erosion yields (2.18 E-24 cm3/atom).

entityDescription:
KONGSBERG MARITIME
We are a global marine technology company providing innovative and reliable ‘Full Picture’ technology solutions for all marine industry sectors. Headquartered in Kongsberg, Norway, we have manufacturing, sales and service facilities in 34 countries.
Our solutions cover all aspects of marine automation, safety, maneuvering, navigation, and dynamic positioning as well as energy management, deck handling and propulsion systems, and ship design services.
We boast one of the broadest product ranges in the world, from the engine room to the working deck. This extensive skills and equipment portfolio, combined with our world-class support network of expert staff across 117 global locations, forms our leading solutions: offering expertise and cutting-edge equipment from the drawing board right through a vessel’s operating life.
While we are the largest marine technology specialist organisation in the world, with the most extensive product and knowledge base, our focus continues to be on customers and the environment. Only by listening to our customers and predicting industry needs can we enable the transformation needed to put safety and sustainability first, while continuing to generate value for all stakeholders.
BUSINESS ACTIVITIES
We specialise in the development and delivery of integrated vessel concepts for traditional merchant vessels, ROPAX and fishing vessels, as well as offshore and research vessels and offshore installations. Kongsberg Maritime supplies products and systems for advanced mapping and surveying, sonars, underwater communication, marine robotics (Unmanned Surface Vessels and Autonomous Underwater Vehicles), and deliver deck machinery, propulsion, electrical, automation and control solutions. Our systems enhance efficiency and safety throughout the whole maritime technology spectrum and we offer additional competence in providing turnkey design and engineering services within the shipbuilding sectors.
MARKET SECTORS
Key markets are countries with large fisheries, offshore, shipyard, energy exploration and production industries. In exploration we provide sophisticated underwater and positioning technology and systems for survey vessel operations. In field development, we support construction and offshore vessels with innovative solutions for operation and specialist applications, while in production our hardware and software enhances output and minimises downtime. For maritime transport, fisheries and offshore vessels, we supply The Full Picture, including deck machinery, propulsion, navigation, automation, training, safety and autonomous solutions.

entityDescription:
Jagiellonian University is one of the best and the most prestigious Polish universities. Founded in 1364 it is also the oldest university in Poland, the second university in Central Europe (after university in Prague founded in 1348) and one of the oldest universities in Europe. Initially it consisted of three faculties only, i.e. liberal arts, medicine and law. In 1400 faculty of theology was added, which was regarded at that time in Europe as the highest rank discipline.
University was at the height of its flowering in fifteenth and sixteenth century. In the years 1491-95 Nicolas Copernicus was one of the university students. In the years 1433-1510 the number of foreign students studying in the university reached 44% of all scholars. This fact shows its high international position at that time. 
Nowadays Jagiellonian University educates over 50 000 students on the three levels: bachelor, master and doctoral degree according to Bolonia Process rules. Students can enter 58 different disciplines and 129 specializations with Polish as language of instruction and several specializations lectured in English. About 5% of students are foreigners. Currently, the new campus for physical and natural sciences is under construction. Nearby the Technology Park and the new high-tech (biomedical and informatics) small industry plants are growing. The new facilities are very well equipped with modern advanced scientific instruments. The University is a good European teaching and research institution. It is usually ranked at the first or second place in Poland by the external evaluating agencies, when the quality of education and research are taken into consideration. It was also granted the accreditation from the Department Education of USA for their degree programs for foreign students in English.

entityName: Fundación Centro Tecnológico de Componentes - CTC
entityDescription:
Created in 2000, the “Centro Tecnológico CTC”, is a non-profit private foundation recognised as an Official Technology Centre by Spain’s Competitivity and Economy Ministry. It is the only one in Cantabria’s region with this recognition.
CTC’s objective is to ad value and generate business to its clients through Research, Technological Development and Innovation. CTC is placed at experimental sciences and engineering fields, focused on:
- Navigation and Robotics
- Energy and Industry 
- Nano- and Advanced Materials
CTC leads navigation systems development for robotic applications. Among others, CTC develops advanced algorithms to improve reliability and autonomy of mobile robots and/or process. 
Thanks to its Navigation Laboratory, CTC can develop Navigation Systems, Stabilized Platforms and other “navigation sensor user” applications. The laboratory has relevant and high specialised capabilities in sensor and systems modelling and characterization.
NL has a 2 axis movement simulator ACUTRONIC SIMEX TWO with removable thermal camera, and pay loads up to 45 kg for modelling and calibration of MEMS inertial sensors and for stabilized platforms validation (Hardware-in-the Loop). It has as well experimental devices to develop position calculation GNSS systems and antennas calibration (Phase Centre Variation), including a 2 axis high precision rotation table.
CTC actively participated in several European and Spanish national projects in this field. For example, CTC leaded and coordinated H2020 Project “GREENPATROL”, in which an autonomous robotic solution was developed to detect and control pests inside greenhouses. Now, CTC coordinates another H2020 project, MooringSense. In this project CTC developes an intelligent sensor based on navigation systems.
CTC participate actively in national and international congresses related to mobile robotics and navigation systems and is part of several clusters and associations such as CapTech, Navegación, Guiado y Control de la Agencia Europea de Defensa.

entityDescription:
The Fraunhofer IAPT is one of the leading institutions in the field of Additive Manufacturing (3D Printing). The focus is on the industrialization of additive manufacturing technologies and the associated technology transfer to enable completely new and resource-efficient products. Our additive experts stand for sustainable innovation in the field of additive production. This ranges from developments on the process and material level, the development of novel component designs and system technologies to factory planning and digitization.
The wide-ranging possibilities of additive manufacturing are particularly well suited for the aerospace industry. Weight-optimized parts, for example, have a positive effect on the overall mass of your aircraft. Flow-optimized parts improve the performance of rocket engines. In addition, hydraulic components can be designed to be much more efficient, creating advantages not only within the part itself, but also in conjunction with the overall system. Development times for prototypes can be reduced and downtime minimized by the availability of spare parts. In this way, additive manufacturing can be of great importance to space industry, especially when conventional manufacturing processes reach their limits because of component complexity or when time plays an overriding role due to the associated costs.

entityDescription:
xSpectre AB was founded in August 2020 with the idea to explore developments in miniaturized (mini) spectrometers with the help of an innovative geometric-mathematical model engine. The surge in mini-spectrometers over the past years has led to a multitude of new applications and start-ups, now developing into an ecosystem of businesses and markets. The lions share of all applications rely on back-end (vendor) driven algorithms that translate a spectral signal to concentration or content, either using traditional methods including for instance Beer’s law, or modern Artificial Intelligence (AI). The solution usually entails a physical spectrometer that comes with a preinstalled (or online available) app that is dedicated to a particular application.

The spectrometer development by xSpectre AB is instead a general purpose sensor that comes with:
- exchangeable muzzles for different applications,

- possibilities to analyze solids, liquids and gases,

- abilities to analyze transmittance, absorbance, reflectance, fluorescence and Raman spectra,

- a mobile phone connected app used for control, communication and edge computing,

- an online (backend) cloud service for data management and spectral computing,

- a set of external probes that can be used for directly sensing physical and chemical sample properties together with with spectral sensing,

- a geometric-mathematical model engine that translates spectral signals to abundance,

- possibilities for domain experts to AI assisted development of novel models for translating spectral signals to abundances, and

- preparations for developing a user community.

A patent application has been handed in for the geometric-mathematical model engine to the Swedish Intellectual Property Office (application nr 2150075-6, 25 January 2021).

The first application under development with xSpectre’s handheld spectrometer is for analyzing and predicting soil properties. The Swedish Agency for Innovation Systems, VINNOVA, supported the initial development and we are now (October 2021) ready for tests at Technical Readiness Level (TRL) 7 - system prototype demonstration in operational environment. Company description: xSpectre AB was founded in August 2020 with the idea to explore developments in miniaturized (mini) spectrometers with the help of an innovative geometric-mathematical model engine. The surge in mini-spectrometers over the past years has led to a multitude of new applications and start-ups, now developing into an ecosystem of businesses and markets. The lions share of all applications rely on back-end (vendor) driven algorithms that translate a spectral signal to concentration or content, either using traditional methods including for instance Beer’s law, or modern Artificial Intelligence (AI). The solution usually entails a physical spectrometer that comes with a preinstalled (or online available) app that is dedicated to a particular application.

The spectrometer development by xSpectre AB is instead a general purpose sensor that comes with:
- exchangeable muzzles for different applications,

- possibilities to analyze solids, liquids and gases,

- abilities to analyze transmittance, absorbance, reflectance, fluorescence and Raman spectra,

- a mobile phone connected app used for control, communication and edge computing,

- an online (backend) cloud service for data management and spectral computing,

- a set of external probes that can be used for directly sensing physical and chemical sample properties together with with spectral sensing,

- a geometric-mathematical model engine that translates spectral signals to abundance,

- possibilities for domain experts to AI assisted development of novel models for translating spectral signals to abundances, and

- preparations for developing a user community.

A patent application has been handed in for the geometric-mathematical model engine to the Swedish Intellectual Property Office (application nr 2150075-6, 25 January 2021).

entityDescription:
The Fraunhofer Institute for Silicate Research ISC is one of the leading research and development centers for functional materials in the fields of resource efficiency, energy, environment and health. With around 370 permanent scientists and technicians, the institute works to develop innovative functional materials and technologies for more sustainable products using fewer resources, and to make significant contributions to solving the major global issues and challenges of the future. With the parent institute and its subunits Fraunhofer R&D Center for Electromobility and the Translational Center for Regenerative Therapies in Würzburg, as well as the Fraunhofer Center for High Temperature Materials and Design HTL in Bayreuth with the associated Application Center Textile Fiber Ceramics in Münchberg, Fraunhofer ISC combines profound materials science expertise with many years of experience in materials processing, industrial application, and the upscaling of production and process technologies to pilot scale, as well as in materials analysis and characterization. With a clear focus on sustainability, the institute is a strong partner for industry and supports the reduction of resource consumption and responsible production with its developments.
Keywords include smart materials, high-temperature ceramic materials, specialty glass, inorganic-organic hybrid materials, printed sensing and electro/optical packaging, battery materials and technologies (Li-ion, Li-solid and others), particle technology, biomaterials, biomedicine, 3D tissue engineering, testing and preclinical and clinical studies.

entityDescription:
Università degli Studi “Guglielmo Marconi” (USGM) is the first Athenaeum in Italy following the “Open University” model. USGM was established in 2004 by the Ministry of University and Research (MUR M.D. March 2004) as the first Italian open-university with the aim to spread and produce knowledge, giving everybody access to proper learning tools in Italy as well as worldwide. 
More than 16.000 students are enrolled in our six different Schools (School of Business, School of Law, School of Political Sciences, School of Applied Sciences and Technologies, School of Arts and School of Education Science).
The USGM adopts innovating learning modalities by developing suitable research strategies for most advanced technological solutions and by integrating non residential communication means (e-learning, chat, forum, videoconference, etc.) with seminar activities (workshops, seminars, etc.). The Open University model represents a driving factor within the information society, able to have strategic functions in professional training, knowledge production and spreading of digital culture. 
First of all USGM aims at offering an appropriate array of professional and graduate programs that are accessible and flexible to anyone, anytime, anywhere. USGM is dedicated to the improvement of training through the use of innovative teaching methods as well as technology applied to learning, that require students to become actively involved in the learning process and develop the critical thinking skills necessary for lifelong learning.
USGM has been developing and experimenting an innovative learning methodology merging e-learning, m-learning and t-learning solutions with the aim to meet the different needs and address various learning systems. The main virtual environment for contents delivering is Virtual C@Mpus Platform, an Integrated Multimodal System which integrates the following tools: mobile/mp3 players, personal computer, e-book, television (web TV Marconi Channel). Marconi Studios http://www.marconistudios.it/ includes 2000 square metres, 5 TV studios, audio and post production rooms, voice and recording studios in order to create thousands of different virtual scenarios.

entityDescription:
Since the foundation of Aerosint in 2016, we have worked on an alternative powder re-recoating system that, instead of uniformly spreading just one single powder material, selectively deposits two (or more) powders to form a single layer containing two materials.
We called this technology “Selective Powder Deposition” as it enables full 3-dimensional control over material placement in any powder bed Additive Manufacturing process.
Selective Powder Deposition unlocks a number of very unique use cases in Additive Manufacturing, Powder Metallurgy, and beyond.
Some of our research topics are bi-metallic L-PBF, zero waste SLS or the binder-free printing of ceramics or metals.
Aerosint is part of Desktop Metal (NYSE:DM)since June 2021.

entityDescription: SENER is an engineering, consultancy and systems integration Group whose main objective is to provide its clients with the most efficient technological solutions to their requirements. Innovation, commitment to quality and independence are just three of the key factors which form part of its culture and corporative values. SENER's presence in the market is endorsed by its almost fifty years of experience which has given it a vast technological solvency through its involvement in both national and international projects. Through its dominion of a broad spectrum of technologies and its flexible organization, SENER is now in a position to undertake the most complex multidisciplinary projects. All of the aforementioned, together with its constant involvement in Research & Development (10% of its resources) has allowed its volume of business to exceed 1.800.000 engineering hours per year, with exports accounting for 40% of that figure. SENER Group engineering and consultancy activities embrace the following fields: Aerospace Infrastructurres & Transport Energy Marine All the above activities were traditionally carried out within the SENER Group by the company SENER INGENIERÍA Y SISTEMAS, SAU with VAT number A-48024723 and ESA Codes: EMITS Bidder Code: 18185; ESA-P Bidder Code: 6000006075; ESA-P vendor code: 1000007321. However in order to agglutinate all the Aerospace activities within the group in a single company SENER Group has decided to conduct an internal business reorganization which will involve the transfer within the SENER group of all technical, material, financial and human resources comprising the Aerospace activities being carried out by SENER INGENIERÍA Y SISTEMAS, SAU to SENER AERONÁUTICA, SAU by means of a legal partial division (Spanish “escisión parcial”), expected to be effective as of July 1, 2019. The Aerospace activities comprise the supply of equipment’s, systems integration and engineering services in the fields of space, defence, aeronautics, vehicles and health. SENER AERONÁUTICA, SAU is a sister company fully owned by SENER GRUPO DE INGENIERÍA, SA same shareholder to SENER INGENIERÍA Y SISTEMAS, SAU, incorporated in 2003 under the laws of Spain and domiciled at Avenida de Zugazarte 56, 48930 Las Arenas (Vizcaya) with VAT number A-95291597. SENER AERONÁUTICA, SAU owned a participation stake (51%) in the Spanish aeronautic company named INDUSTRIA DE TURBO PROPULSORES, SA sold in December 2017. In June 2018, SENER AERONÁUTICA, SAU acquired 100% of the Spanish space group named Grupo Tryo comprised by Tryo Aerospace & Electronics, SL (today named Sener TAE, SLU), Tryo Aerospace Flight Segment, SAU (today renamed as Sener TAFS, SAU) and Rymsa RF, SLU. In terms of applicable law, SENER AERONÁUTICA, SAU will be subrogated by universal succession in the legal position of SENER INGENIERÍA Y SISTEMAS, SAU as regards to the Aerospace activities, including, but not limited to, the contracts entered into with the European Space Agency. The subrogation means that SENER AERONÁUTICA, SAU will succeed SENER INGENIERÍA Y SISTEMAS, SAU in the contracts entered into with the European Space Agency and continue the performance of the same since July 1, 2019 as if it had been performing those contracts since the beginning.

entityName: WSL Swiss Federal Institute for Forest, Snow and Landscape Research
entityDescription: The Swiss Federal Institute for Forest, Snow and Landscape Research is concerned with the use, development and protection of natural and urban spaces. The focus of our research is on solving problems to do with the responsible use of landscapes and forests and a prudent approach to natural hazards, especially those common in mountainous countries. WSL occupies a leading position internationally in these research areas. We also provide groundwork for sustainable environmental policies in Switzerland. WSL has, from the start, been active in all regions in Switzerland. In 1888 the first experimental plots were set up across the country to find out more about tree growth and yield. Today WSL maintains more than 6000 experimental and research plots, including large experimental stations for studying rock fall or debris flow, study areas for monitoring the effects of climate change on forests and sites damaged by storms or fires for investigating the impact of these natural hazards. WSL is a research institute of the Swiss Confederation. It is part of the ETH Domain and employs approximately 500 people. In addition to the headquarters in Birmensdorf, near Zurich, and to the WSL Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research SLF in Davos, branch stations in Lausanne and Cadenazzo and Sion generate local synergies and reach out to professionals.

ICD Profile 
The "Informatik Centrum Dortmund e.V." (ICD) was founded in 1989 as a spin-off company of the Computer Science department of the University of Dortmund, Germany. The Informatik Centrum Dortmund GmbH was founded in 2019. Today, ICD is available as a research and development partner for companies coming from different technological areas. ICD strives to improve and accelerate the transfer of current research results in computer science and information technology into industrial products.
The company
The product range of ICD comprises the provision of services related to Internet and Multimedia, the development of specialized software, the application of automatic picture classification, the optimization of complex systems, support for decision-taking using fuzzy logic as well as the development of educational software.
Due to its close contact with the Computer Science and Electrical Engineering Departments of the University of Dortmund, ICD has access to the latest results of current research. The settlement of projects at ICD is done according to industry standards.
ICD makes it easier for companies to take advantage of the broad know-how collected at the University of Dortmund through:
- joint application-centered development projects that are conducted at ICD;
- projects comprising research and development that ICD conducts for its customers;
- courses and tutorials that are being offered by ICD.
ICD considers itself a service provider supporting the realization of latest research results from the area of computer science and from computer applications into industrial products. Its goal is to provide access to the know-how, and also to researchers and graduates of the University of Dortmund, in particular for medium-sized companies in a fast und unbureaucratic way.

entityDescription:
Hasselt University (UHasselt) is a young, independent and innovative university, located in the center of Europe in Belgium. Today, Hasselt University counts seven faculties, four research institutes, three research centres, 6,522 students and 1,540 researchers and staff. 
The university is regionally anchored, has a pronounced regional, national and international orientation and is thus strongly committed to both the region and the world. As a civic university, UHasselt wants to deploy people and knowledge to tackle society’s major challenges, in full collaboration with regional, national and international others. The university is committed to take responsibility and share knowledge in ways that benefit the society. Students, staff, researchers and alumni are both able and willing to make the society smarter, more agile and better. Innovation is a constant in everything the university does. Today’s and tomorrow’s challenges guide teaching, research and social engagement of the university. Therefore, Hasselt University imparts its student knowledge, skills and insights in the world in order to make them critical, engaged global citizens, able to adapt to an ever-changing world. By breaking down the silos between research disciplines in the interdisciplinary research institutes and centers, scientists with a different scientific background can work better together on new answers to complex problems. To enhance knowledge on local, regional and global challenges, Hasselt University collaborates with other universities, research centres, governments, businesses and civil society organisations. The university also employs its networks to send students, staff and academics into the world and attract others to our region. About 17% of all PhDs are joint PhDs, about 42% of the PhD student at Hasselt University are from outside Belgium and 12% of the academic staff is international. This way, Hasselt University becomes a place where the region meets the world and the world meets the region. 
Hasselt University also strives pays a lot of attention to the creation of equal opportunities for women and men in research. A policy plan on gender issues has been developed which describes actions to ameliorate recruitment and promotion of both women and men and to improve the balance between work and family. It is therefore not surprising that Hasselt University was the first Flemish university to obtain the “HR Excellence in Research” label of the European Commission in 2011.
Hasselt University is ranked in the Times Higher Education Ranking in the 2018-2019 edition and is listed in the section 351-400. In the Times Higher Education Ranking of universities less than half a century old, Hasselt University is ranked as number 46.

entityName: Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development
entityDescription:
The Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development determines strategic directions, develops programmes and plans for sustainable development of society on green and cyclic economy policies with the aim of transforming Croatia into a prosperous, resource-efficient and competitive economy, while assuring climate neutrality, conservation and sustainable use of natural resources.
The Ministry's scope encompasses the development and improvement of the Croatian economy, the instruments and measures of economic policy; development of micro-, small- and medium-scale enterprises; industrial policy and the application of innovative and new technologies; management of the guarantee fund for the improvement of industry; jobs related to intellectual and industrial rights usage and the encouragement of innovation in industry and trade, aiming to develop the competitiveness of the Croatian economy; mining; easement and encouragement of subsidising and export.
The Ministry works in accordance with other governmental bodies to coordinate strategic use of state property, including participation in the coordination of restructuring and rehabilitation of legal entities, analysis of restructuring procedures of companies owned by Croatia and management of ownership shares of companies owned by Croatia; trade in the EU single market; supply and pricing; national coordination of activities within the EU single market, including technical legislation and quality infrastructure, coordination and development of national policy for standardisation, accreditation, compliance and measurement assessments; phenomena and the state of the market; protection of consumers; strategic goods stockpiles.
The Ministry conducts administrative and other duties pertaining to the development, improvement and coordination of the public procurement system; development and improvement of the concession system within its jurisdiction and supervision of its implementation and improvement of the public-private partnership system.
The Ministry conducts work pertaining to nature protection and conservation in accordance with the sustainable development policy of Croatia; jobs pertaining to waste management and environmental impact assessments; climate change mitigation and adaptation; water management and other energy-related jobs.
Protection of the environment is one of the most challenging activities that permeates through all aspects of human society. Through proclaiming the National sustainable development strategy, the Ministry became a point of coordination at the national level for subjects pertaining to sustainable development and the coordinating body for multilateral environmental agreements and global questions related to sustainable development on a global scale.
The Ministry conducts work related to Croatia’s participation in EU bodies in areas of its jurisdiction.
The Ministry also conducts other work that falls under its jurisdiction, as defined by law.

entityDescription:
Sorbonne University is a world-class research university, presenting the comprehensive disciplinary range of arts, humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, engineering and medicine. Sorbonne University is at the crossroads of diverse types of knowledge and capable of responding to the intellectual and scientific challenges of the 21st century.
The University offers its 55,600 students the best educational opportunities for the success of each of their personal and professional projects, through monodisciplinary, bi-disciplinary and interdisciplinary programs. Close to 10,200 of its students are international and 4,400 are in doctoral programs. With its three main faculties, it offers varied and original opportunities across disciplines and high quality research and training environment with, for instance, the largest university Library in France. 
Sorbonne University research draws on more than 3,400 professor-researchers and another 3,100 research partners from the major French research organisations, working side by side in more than 130 laboratories. In addition to Nobel Prizes, Fields Medals and other awards, the university has exceptional transdisciplinary institutes and is also theheadquarters for the European Marine Biological Resource Centre. With 8,500 publications per year (approx. 10% of all publications in France), Sorbonne Université is a major player in international knowledge and innovation economy. SU also receives the largest number of EU grants among French universities, with more than 150 awarded H2020 projects, including 40 MSCAs and 27 ERCs. With its research partners, a total of 97 H2020 ERC grantees have been hosted in Sorbonne University’s laboratories. 
Following its tradition in hosting excellent researchers from around the world, the university is engaged into the adoption of the European Charter for Researchers and the Code of Conduct for the Recruitment of Researchers.
Sorbonne University is a member of the European University Association (EUA), the Network of Universities from the Capitals of Europe (UNICA), the International Alliance of Research Universities (IARU) and the League of European Research Universities (LERU).

entityDescription: Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań is the major academic institution in Poznań and one of the top Polish universities. Its reputation is founded on tradition, the outstanding achievements of the faculty and the attractive curriculum offered to students. In addition to its facilities in Poznań, it has campuses in Gniezno, Kalisz, Piła and Słubice/Franfurt-Oder. The University currently employs nearly 3,000 teaching staff, including 371 tenured professors and other professors with title, 1407 assistant professors, 369 senior lecturers and lecturers and over 2200 nonacademic employees. The University was founded in 1919 and currently its student population is nearly 40 000 students (nearly 700 are international students). Students may choose between 180 possible professional specializations. In recent years the educational offer has become increasingly diverse. New educational projects include: integrated studies in humanities, natural sciences, social sciences, and program carried out in cooperation with other institutions both in Poland and abroad. The mission of the University is to advance knowledge through high quality research and teaching in partnership with business, the professions, public services and other research and learning providers. The University is a center of academic excellence, where research and teaching are mutually sustaining, and where the context within which research is conducted and knowledge is sought and applied is international as much as regional and national. The University continuously extends and updates research programs and contents of study curricula, with special emphasis on their interdisciplinary and international nature. The University recognizes its role as a strategic partner in Central Europe, and therefore aspires to contribute to the region’s economic growth social development and environmental sustainability. The University prides itself on its achievements and aligns its principles with those of the Great Charter of European Universities. It promotes pro-European ideas and actively participates in the international academic community, seeks to implement joint research and educational programs. It aims to strengthen ties with the European Union Member States and embarks on new initiatives conducive to cooperation with the countries of Europe. In 2002-2018 our professors coordinated or were partners in more than 130 research projects funded by the European Union Framework Program (FP5, FP6, FP7 and Horizon 2020) and many other international research projects. AMU is a member of: EUA - European University Association, EUCEN - European University Continuing Education Network, The Compostela Group of Universities, The Santander Group - European University Network, European Chemistry Thematic Network and other European Research Networks. During the last 10 years, UAM has participated in 26 Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions projects (within FP7 and Horizon 2020: 8 individual, 4 ITN, 14 other) and 2 ERC projects (1 Consolidator Grant as a leader, 1 Advanced Grant as a member of the research group).

entityDescription:
As part of the Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft, Fraunhofer IZM specializes in applied and industrial contract research. Fraunhofer IZM’s focus is on custom tailored packaging technology solutions and the integration of multifunctional electronics into systems with regard to functionality, costs and reliability.

The institute has a staff of more than 440 and saw a turnover of 37.6 million euros in 2020, of which 76 percent was earned through contract research and benefits from its close cooperation with the Technische Universität Berlin. Fraunhofer IZM assists companies and other institutes with application-oriented pre-competitive research, as well as the development of prototypes and small volume production. Our services include application advice, technology transfer and further qualification of personnel through practical training. In numerous R&D projects, ongoing skills and know-how are continuously being developed which can be passed also to SME-partners on a development stage.

Within Wafer Level System Integration IZM is specialized in developing advanced packaging and system integration technologies on all wafer sizes (100 mm to 300 mm) thus being able to offer customer-specific solutions for microelectronic products in the overall scope of smart system integration. This includes a broad cooperation network with manufacturer and users of microelectronic products as well as with cleanroom equipment producers and material developers from the chemical industry from all over the world. The interconnection technologies are offered on board, module and package levels and the integration of electrical, optical and power-electronic components and systems are at the forefront of the research. By simulating thermal and mechanical coupling and electrical, magnetic, electromagnetic phenomena at stages of the development process, IZM can compare the functionality and capacity of different technologies as early as during the concept design phase. The most important application areas are microelectronics and microsystem technology, RF and high-speed system design, photonic applications including fiber optics and power electronic systems. All technological developments are supported by environmental and reliability analysis reaching from nano-characterisation level to evaluation and optimisation at the system level until they reach market maturity with. Focus is on harsh environment applications like automotive, space and avionics.

entityName: LIP. Laboratório de Instrumentação e Física Experimental de Partículas
description:
LIP is the reference laboratory for research in particle physics and related technologies in Portugal, and the Portuguese reference partner of CERN. The laboratory has nodes in Lisboa, Coimbra and Braga, closely collaborating with local universities. LIP has about 200 international members (100 PhD researchers), is an Associate Laboratory, and was rated as “Excellent” in the 2019 independent evaluation promoted by FCT, the Portuguese Agency for Science and Technology Funding. 
Growing increasingly multidisciplinary, LIP’s research includes a world-class fundamental research programme in particle and astroparticle physics, technological applications to healthcare, space exploration, information technologies and big data analytics. At the centre of LIP’s mission are also advanced scientific and technical training and a strong commitment to engaging society with science and community development. LIP collaborates at CERN, ESA, GSI, SNOLAB, SURF, Fermilab, and the Pierre Auger and SWGO observatories. 
LIP is part of several infrastructures in the FCT roadmap, namely the National Distributed Computing Infrastructure (INCD), ProtoTera, The Portuguese Association for Proton Therapy and Advanced Technologies for the treatment of Cancer, and the Brain Imaging Network. The laboratory offers all conditions and infrastructures for the successful implementation of the work plan: a mechanical workshop, laboratories and competence centers providing support to the research groups and offering high quality services to the community; outstanding computational facilities; administrative support; project management and communication offices; office space.
entityDescription: LIP (Laboratório de Instrumentação e Física Experimental de Partículas) is a technical and scientific nonprofit association created in 1986 by the ex-National Board for Scientific and Technological Research (JNICT) and the ex-Instituto Nacional de Investigação Científica (INIC), lately joined by the Associação Nacional dos Industriais de Material Eléctrico e Electrónico (ANIMEE). Following the reorganisation of the scientific public agencies in Portugal, the present sponsors of LIP are the National Foundation for Science (FCT), the Bureau for International Relations for Science and High Education (GRICES), both under the Ministry of Science and Higher Education, and ANIMEE. LIP was created when Portugal joined CERN as a full member-state and its main objective is the science and technology research in the field of experimental high-energy physics, associated instrumentation and computation. The science and technology activity of LIP takes place in the framework of international collaborations, aiming at the realisation of experiments, mainly in the European laboratory for particle physics, CERN, in Geneva, Switzerland. LIP does part of its job in Portugal (experiment conception, fundamental research on radiation physics and detectors, technology development and data analysis) executing at CERN or elsewhere all that concerns the direct preparation of experiments and data acquisition.

entityDescription:
MiljöMatematik is an idea-driven, non-profit company with a focus on sustainable food systems. We are driven by a will to contribute to knowledge development for thriving companies and society within the planetary boundaries. With an interdisciplinary approach and innovative methods, we carry out assignments and projects in the environment, climate and strategic sustainability work. We are total foodies, food nerds, and we believe that the food system is the perfect place to start if you want to understand and solve all the world's problems, from production systems and the food's climate impact, to social justice and regenerative change. Entrepreneurship, innovation, practical experience from the food industry runs as a green thread throughout the business. 

Our mission is to transform the food system and help make food part of the solution instead of part of the problem. To do this, we work with three areas:
Innovation projects and collaborations
We run our own collaborative projects, where we work with researchers, farmers, organizations and other experts on system innovation based on a societal challenge. An example is the Swedish coal storage project, agriculture as a carbon sink.

Assignments and consulting services
We hold courses and training, we work as consultants for sustainability-driven business development, we develop mathematical models and do climate calculations. Examples of assignments are overall sustainability responsibility for the Hallands Matgille project.

Knowledge and reinvestment
We reinvest all financial surplus in developing both our own business and other ideas that we believe contribute to a better world. It is part of our business concept.

entityDescription:
The Miguel Hernández University of Elche was established by the Generalitat Valenciana in 1996, and teaching activities began in the fall of 1997. The UMH, whose main campus is located in the city of Elche, operates 4 campuses in all: Altea, Elche, Orihuela, and Sant Joan d'Alacant. Its campuses extend over almost 95 hectares, there are 75 university buildings, and constructed areas cover about 210,000 m2. Currently, the UMH is home to 25,000 students, of which 13,000 are enrolled in official degree programs (bachelor, master, PhD), with the remaining 12,000 learning in continuing education programs. 
The Miguel Hernández University has 7 faculties (Faculty of Experimental Sciences, Faculty of Fine Arts, Faculty of Health and Social Sciences, Faculty of Medicine, Faculty of Pharmacy, Faculty of Social and Legal Sciences of Elche, and Faculty of Social and Legal Sciences of Orihuela) and 2 schools (School of Engineering of Elche and School of Engineering of Orihuela).
Regarding academics, the Miguel Hernández University of Elche offers 25 bachelor's, 53 master's, and 13 doctoral programs. In addition to these official programs, the UMH also offers hundreds of its own Continuing Education courses and programs, including University Expert, unique UMH Master's, Advanced University Diploma, University Specialist, Summer, Winter, Refinement, Bridging, university access, and language instruction, among others.

entityDescription:
Fraunhofer IKTS develops in eight market-oriented business divisions solutions by the inclusion of ceramic based technologies and components as well as non-destructive test methods for industries, product concepts and markets beyond the conventional areas of application. These disciplines include ceramic materials and processes, mechanical and automotive engineering, electronics and microsystems, energy, environmental and process engineering, bio- and medical engineering, optics as well as materials and process analysis.
Development of non-destructive testing equipment and physical methodology is offered along the value chain starting at conceptual work, simulation, system development up to prototyping and higher technical readiness level. Ultrasonic, eddy current, x-ray, optical and thermal methods are permanently improved and adapted to measurement, monitoring and process control purposes in mobile or stationary industrial machines. System integrated and structural integrated monitoring systems based on guided elastic waves are transferred into industrial applications. The required electronic components and micro systems are developed for usage in harsh environments. High-grade electronic with demands on long lasting reliability efforts strong support by thermal-mechanical reliability simulations, by materials characterization for selection and by physical failure inspection to avoid failures in field service. The IKTS offers the complete value chain for electronic and sensor system prototyping, starting from the material development (mostly ceramic based), component forming, processing and assembly, testing, quality inspection and customer shipment.

Logic-X as a company started in 2018 and its team is highly passionate about adaptable compute acceleration platforms and sensor interface products. As a team we have been involved in FPGA and sensor product design for almost 20 years. The emergence of new artificial intelligence applications on the edge is seen by Logic-X as an opportunity to design Commercial off-the-shelf products, incorporating the often complex FPGA, MPSOC, ACAP and sensor interface elements.
The products that we offer are designed to provide easy insertion of modern FPGA, MPSOC, ACAP and sensor technology into our customer systems. This allows our customers to focus on their end application and the customer does not have to spend time to develop custom processing platforms. As a result, Logic-X products will improve time to market and reduce overal risk.

Logic-X has a mission to be a provider of high-quality sensor processing products that solve our customers embedded and edge processing challenges.

Agriculture, Food & Nutrition

Management and Economics (Business Administration, Accounting & Finance)
The HMU is highly research-oriented in every scientific field covered by its departments and its research laboratories; therefore, it is an Institute that holds a top position in university research rankings and it is recognized for its contribution in the development of the island of Crete and the country in general. The academic and research staff of the HMU is involved in many scientific activities in collaboration with national and international research groups and teams which have led, on the one hand, to important research results and, on the other hand, to the development of technological innovations in a wide range of research areas and innovative products with international recognition.

entityDescription:
The Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft, headquartered in Germany, is the world’s leading applied research organization. Its research activities are conducted by 75 institutes and research units at locations throughout Germany. The Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft employs a staff of 29,000, who work with an annual research budget totaling more than 2.8 billion euros.
The Fraunhofer Institute for Integrated Circuits IIS, headquartered in Erlangen, Germany, conducts world-class research on microelectronic and IT system solutions and services. Today, it is the largest institute of the Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft.
 
Research at Fraunhofer IIS revolves around two guiding topics:
In the area of “Audio and Media Technologies”, the institute has been shaping the digitalization of media for more than 30 years now. Fraunhofer IIS was instrumental in the development of mp3 and AAC and played a significant role in the digitalization of the cinema. Current developments are opening up whole new sound worlds and are being used in virtual reality, automotive sound systems, mobile telephony, streaming and broadcasting. Any mobile phone you buy today, for instance, uses audio technology developed by the institute, while Fraunhofer codecs provide the basis for sound of more than half of all TV broadcasts worldwide and almost all radio and streaming services. The institute’s professional tools for digital film and media production are also being used globally.
In the context of “cognitive sensor technologies”, the institute researches technologies for sensor technology, data transmission technology, data analysis methods and the exploitation of data as part of data-driven services and their accompanying business models. This adds a cognitive component to the function of the conventional “smart” sensor. The results of this research have been applied in the areas of connected mobility, communication and application solutions for the Internet of Things, digitalization of human sensing, product and material monitoring, and business analytics in supply chains.
Besides other positioning technologies like 5G, WiFi, Beacon systems, one focus is developing GNSS-receivers and antennas, particularly for Galileo OS- and PRS signals.
More than 1100 employees conduct contract research for industry, the service sector and public authorities. Founded in 1985 in Erlangen, Fraunhofer IIS now has 16 locations in 12 cities: Erlangen (headquarters), Nürnberg, Fürth and Dresden, as well as Ilmenau, München, Bamberg, Waischenfeld, Coburg, Würzburg, Deggendorf and Passau. The budget of 167.9 million euros a year is mainly financed by contract research projects. 29 percent of the budget is subsidized by federal and state funds.

entityDescription:
The Fraunhofer Institute for Integrated Systems and Device Technology IISB conducts applied research and development in the field of electronic systems for application in, e.g., electric mobility, aerospace, Industry 4.0, power grids or energy technology. In this connection, the institute uniquely covers the entire value chain - from basic materials to whole power electronic systems.
As part of the Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft, the IISB does contract research for industry as well as public authorities. On that note it is the institute’s main objective to provide excellent research for its industrial partners and to set technological benchmarks as one of the leading research institutions in electronic systems. A tightly woven network build out of local and international partnerships and cooperations helps to carry these aims into effect.
With its two business areas, semiconductors and power electronics, the IISB provides innovation and solutions in various specialized fields:
• materials development
• semiconductor technology and manufacturing
• electron devices
• packaging and modules
• vehicle power electronics
• energy electronics and energy supply systems
These services are supplemented by broad activities in test and reliability, simulation, characterization, and metrology.
In addition to silicon technology, the IISB has a strong focus on wide-bandgap semiconductors, especially silicon carbide (SiC). For SiC, the institute offers a complete technology backbone, including materials science, devices, modules, and their integration in highly efficient power electronic systems.

entityDescription: The Fraunhofer Wilhelm-Klauditz-Institut WKI is an institute of the Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft zur Förderung der angewandten Forschung e.V. (FhG). The department ”Material Analysis and Indoor Chemistry” focusses on the comprehensive measurement and assessment of indoor air pollution as well as on emissions from consumer-oriented and building products. The spectrum of examined materials ranges from classic wood-based materials through plastics and building products to products from the automotive, electronics, aviation and food industries including space related applications. The development of new analysis and sampling techniques as well as the construction of emission test chambers and cells are further important fields of our activity. We investigate questions concerning indoor air hygiene and room climate with regard to the environment, health and consumer protection. In cooperation with other Fraunhofer institutes we work on solutions for the improvement of air quality through the use of filtration devices, such as materials equipped with (photo) catalysis. On our information platform “IAQIP” (Indoor Air Quality Information Platform), a joint project with the Queensland University of Technology (QUT) and funded by the German Federal Ministry for the Environment, Nature Conservation, Building and Nuclear Safety (BMUB), we provide substantiated information on the subject of “indoor air quality” in a compact, comprehensible form for planners and operators of buildings, for decision-makers and for consumers. Besides these activities the WKI specializes in process technology, natural-fiber composites, surface technology, wood protection and emission control, quality assurance of wood products, recycling procedures and the use of organic building materials and wood in construction. Almost all the procedures and materials which result from the research activities at the Institute are used industrially. We operate worldwide and work project-related with research institutions and industrial partners.

Bourban Sébastien Etienne provides scientific expertise in applied mathematics and computational modelling for free surface flow applications.

Passionate, driven and committed to managing and delivering environmental hydraulics consultancy and research projects with large numerical modelling components, Sébastien has over 20 year experience in the UK (with HR Wallingford) and in North America (with the Canadian Hydraulics Centre). He has started his own company in 2020, in parallel to joining the LNHE department at EDF R&D near Paris.

Sébastien is a proven team leader valuing most efficient use of the personnel he relies upon. He formulated and followed through delivery of business plans, research strategies, as well as wrote company-wide mentoring guidance.

Sébastien is a keen business developer valuing face-to-face contacts. He is experienced in authoring and negotiating licensing terms, high-level memorandum of understanding and joint commercial agreements both in French and English. He has organised international workshops and held booths at national and international conferences. He fosters strong relationships with clients, partners and peer organisations.

Sébastien has a strong track record of managing and working on challenging projects, for which numerical modelling is critical and outside the norm, yet valuing delivery to a high quality standard, on time and within budget.

Sébastien has a precise knowledge of the capabilities and restrictions of the numerical modelling tools at use, and consequently of the risks of project specific developments and modelling challenges, valuing a no-surprise relationship with clients. He has been and remains a lead developer of the numerical solvers he uses and of their applications to environmental hydraulics studies.

Finally, Sébastien has strong organisational skills valuing self-motivated discipline. For over 7 years in his career, he has balanced personal time as PhD student against his full time employment.

entityName: Dipartimento di Scienze e Ingegneria della Materia, dell'Ambiente ed Urbanistica - SIMAU
entityDescription: The Department of SIMAU, Università Politecnica delle Marche (UnivPM) has been established in 2011 with the aim of creating a structure in which different skills contribute to high-level teaching and high-profile research in the field of Experimental Physics, Material Science, Applied Geology and Hydrogeology, Geotechnical and Environmental Engineering. The Department is currently composed by 39 full-time professors/researchers, 10 technicians and administrative employees. The Geotechnical Group is producing its research work in the classical fields of “Soil Mechanics and Geotechnical Engineering” as well in the more recent field of “Environmental Geotechnics”, addressing subjects such as new geomaterials and the safety of contaminated lands. In particular, the research work on Soil Mechanics includes studies on the behaviour of geologically complex soils, often involved in large instability phenomena of both natural and man-made slopes. Most relevant subjects of Environmental Geotechnics are those of investigating contaminated lands, site-specific risk analyses, design of clean-up procedures and remedial measures, geotechnical stabilization and re-use of dredged materials. The Geotechnical engineering research work is on topics of particular interest in Mediterranean Area such as soil-structure interaction problems, numerical modelling of soils containing discontinuities, lime or cement soil stabilization and hydraulic barriers, static and seismic analysis of earth retaining structures and foundations. When needed, experimental activities rely upon two departmental geotechnical laboratories, the soil mechanics laboratory and the environmental geotechnics laboratory. The numerical work is carried out through up to date software codes, namely Plaxis 2D and 3D and other codes for soil structure and foundation analyses.

entityName: Project Laboratory for Numerical Modelling of Impact Damage in Aeronautical Structures
entityDescription:
The Laboratory, AeroDamageLab, was established in the 2009 at Faculty of Mechanical Engineering and Naval Architecture (FMENA), University of Zagreb, within the framework of the Technology Project TP-07/0120-30 “Numerical Modelling of Damage in Aeronautical Structures”. One of the objectives is to continue cooperation with flag carrier airline „Croatia Airlines“ in the development of technology aimed at determining foreign object damage (e.g. due to bird impact) in the composite, sandwich as well as metallic aeronautical structures.
The methodology is based on explicit integration methods used within finite element program Abaqus/Explicit, along with the corresponding failure criteria at impact on aluminium, sandwich or composite structures. Special attention was given to the modelling of impactor/bird (using EOS, ALE) in order to be able to compare numerical results with the available references.
The focus of current research activities is application of multiscale methodlogy in the damage modelling of fibre reinforced composite materials. The High Fidelity Generalized Method of Cells (HFGMC) has been used as a micromechanical model to model damage processes at the constituent level. Coupling between the micromechanical model and the finite element analysis has been achieved via Abaqus/Explicit user material subroutine VUMAT. 
Furthermore, the Laboratory is the focal point for development of numerical methods in the mechanics of composites engineering.

entityName: NI Hungary Software és Hardware Gyártó Kft.
entityDescription:
For more thanfour decades, NI has partnered with the talented engineersand enterprises using its test and measurement technologies to solve the world’s most pressing challenges. From data and automation to research and validation, NI’s software-connected approach is helping its customers test new innovations quicker, more reliably and more safely. NI is modernizing the test and measurement industry by coupling its rich software heritage with new cloud and machine learning capabilities to help customers rapidly create what’s next. 

We are proud to work with talented engineers and enterprises who use our systems to find solutions to the world’s most pressing technological challenges, and to grow their businesses together. We will further strengthen our commitment to connecting the bold and creative people, ideas and technologies that move our world forward. All of this means bringing the right people together to create solutions that bring about real change. It also means combining fresh perspectives with new technologies to make even the boldest ideas come true. We are constantly working to build these relationships because that is where we have the opportunity to accomplish extraordinary things today, tomorrow, and over the next 100 years. We are always striving for the better because we know that everything, we learn today will help us on the path to the future. 
About NI's Debrecen-based subsidiary:
In Debrecen, we have been working in the spirit of the above for two decades now, and we are proud that NI has become one of the key players in the city's high-tech industry during its existence in Hungary. 
Far beyond the original plans, in addition to the significant expansion and development of the first overseas production facility established here in 2001, there are also global and regional service centers, such as the IT development department, legal and financial groups, and customer order processing unit. Production is supported by qualified engineers, and through the activities of the Research and Development engineering group, the Debrecen subsidiary has grown into a real knowledge center in the region.
The company in Debrecen now employs more than 1,400 people compared to its existing staff of less than 100 when starting its operation, making it the third largest employer in Hajdú-Bihar County. Thanks to the developments of the last nearly two decades, a significant part of the company's hardware production takes place in Debrecen, and the vast majority of high value-added products are exported.
NI and its employees are dedicated to serving the communities where they live and work. They do all this with their expertise, NI tools and services. The company sees it as a cornerstone of its social commitment, both globally and locally, to improve engineering and science education by making technology enjoyable, inspiring and easily accessible to young people. As a result of the work of the American company so far, it has achieved profound changes not only in the economic but also in the educational life of the city.

entityDescription:
The Floow is a world leader in telematics data management. 

We support the motor insurance and automotive industries in the Americas, Europe and Asia with predictive analytics and digital end-user services that increase customer engagement and safety. 

The Floow has radically transformed conventional telematics by spearheading the use of smartphones as sensors and harnessing contextual analysis for enhanced prediction of claim propensity.

entityName: ATOS IT Solutions and Services d.o.o.
entityDescription:
Atos is a global leader in digital transformation with 105,000 employees and annual revenue of over € 11 billion. European number one in cybersecurity, cloud and high performance computing, the Group provides tailored end-to-end solutions for all industries in 71 countries. A pioneer in decarbonization services and products, Atos is committed to a secure and decarbonized digital for its clients. Atos operates under the brands Atos and Atos|Syntel. Atos is a SE (Societas Europaea), listed on the CAC40 Paris stock index.

Our expertise and services support the development of knowledge, education and research in a multicultural approach and contribute to the development of scientific and technological excellence. Across the world, we enable our customers and employees, and members of societies at large to live, work and develop sustainably, in a safe and secure information space.
 
A global leader in cloud, digital workplace and private cloud, Atos is also #1 in managed security services in Europe and #3 worldwide. Atos strives to help design the future of the information space with the best in class computing power and pioneering quantum technology with the Atos Quantum Learning Machine. The Group believes that digitalization has delivered only a fraction of its potential. While the data deluge of the last decade will accelerate, it will now be topped by a profusion of data-driven services with focus on value, experience and safety. 
 
Atos commis to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2028,a date which is 22 years ahead of the ambitious aim of the UN Paris Agreement on Climate Change to limit the global warming of the planet to 2°C compared to pre-industrial levels(net-zero by 2050).This decision expands Atos’ ambitions on decarbonization even further, positioning decarbonization as a core element of its growth strategy and the company as the decarbonization leader in its industry.
 
Our 105,000 colleagues across the globe during the Covid-19 crisis have provided outstanding reaction to our clients’ challenges offering solutions specifically geared to the current situation. As international leader in digital transformation, we have also mobilized our technological leadership, our skills and our innovation resources to participate to the global effort against Covid-19.
 
Atos has contributed to the Olympic movement for around 30 years, providing digital transformation and IT solutions to the Olympic Games since 1992. As lead technology integrator web bring our long-term experience and trusted expertise to ensure the Olympic and Paralympic Games run smoothly and are secure and digitally enabled. Atos has been the Worldwide IT Partner of the International Olympic Committee (IOC) since 2001, as well as of the International Paralympic Committee (IPC) since 2008.

entityDescription: The Centro de Supercomputación de Galicia (CESGA) was founded in 1993 to promote and provide supercomputing facilities to regional and national researchers. CESGA legal entity is a no non-profit public foundation, whose shareholders are the Galician regional government and the spanish national research council (CSIC). CESGA’s mission is “Contribute to the advancement of Science and Technical Knowledge, by means of research and application of high performance computing andtechnologies resources, in collaboration with other institutions, for the profit of society”. Currently, it provides services and does research and innovation in areas such as High Performance Computing, Cloud Computing, Big Data, Artificial Intelligence for Manufacturing, Communications, Geographical Information Systems and Information Technologies for Education, especially young students. CESGA is certified by ISO 9001 for the provision of services related to computing and communications. In the research and innovation area, CESGA has participated in more than 200 research projects in its 28 years, many of them in European Research Programs, mainly in technological development, ICT for education, and infrastructure. Since 2008, CESGA is recognised as a scientific and technical research infrastructure in Spain (ICTS, Infraestructura Científico-Tecnológica Singular). Since 2015, CESGA is integrated in the Red Española de Supercomputación y datos (RES).

entityName: PARCO SCIENTIFICO E TECNOLOGICO GALILEO SCpA
entityDescription:
PARCO SCIENTIFICO E TECNOLOGICO GALILEO (Galileo Visionary District) is the Science and Technology Park of Padua. Born in 1997, it is a consortium Company whose shareholders are the Padua Chamber of Commerce, the Cassa di Risparmio di Padova and Rovigo Foundation, the Municipality of Padua, the University of Padua. Galileo's mission is to support the local competitiveness through services for developing of innovative processes.
Galileo's competences refer to design (industrial, digital, graphic and brand design), innovative materials and related technologies (technological scouting and technology transfer), support for business development and the birth of new innovative companies, marketing and communication.
Galileo operates in the new-business/startups' area through “Start Cube”, the Incubator of the University of Padua, supporting the birth and the development of new high-tech and innovative enterprises, providing them with rooms, equipment, tools, and dedicated services. 
With over 1400 business ideas assessed, and more than 300 teams supported, Start Cube team has years of experience assisting start-ups in the drafting of business plans aimed at enhancing internal and external communication. Through meetings, organization, strategy, and vision, the staff pushes the business project further than before, posing the right questions to critically analyse the crucial sticking points of the business —from market analysis to the marketing plan and financials. 
This side-by-side collaboration helps start-ups in drafting a business plan suited to improving internal communication in order to lay out guidelines for an effective business strategy. Furthermore, it works to improve external communication with the aim of creating an analytical document for the presentation of the business project that can be used effectively in public competitions, business plan competitions, and presentations to investors. 
Start-ups are assisted step-by-step, from the definition of the business idea, to making an entrance into the market, to the exploration of new targets. Start-ups are supported by Start Cube’s staff who guide them in taking advantage of the best market opportunities— in business organization, and in the subdivision of roles and tasks within the team as well as in the creation of a coherent and sustainable business model. 
Established in 2004, Start Cube has hosted more than 64 companies from university spin-offs and innovative start-ups. Start Cube offers spaces, consultation in business development, mentoring and tutoring to start-ups in order to assist them in their growth. 
Start Cube is intended for whoever has an innovative project and wants to turn it into a company, but also for university spin-offs and previously established companies who need space, acceleration and mentoring. 
At the headquarters of Start Cube, there is the IoT Cube, which represent an instrument of indoctrination, evangelization and conversion to digital technologies, for all interested companies and start-ups to know tools for a possible introduction in their specific activities and for the modernization of processes. The localization within a startup incubator, which hosts around 25 startups, is also the opportunity to put these startups, who offer digital skills and experiences, in touch with local companies.

entityName: DLR - SPACE OPERATIONS AND ASTRONAUT TRAINING (DLR RB) Cologne
entityDescription:
DLR Space Operations and Astronaut Training is the central institution for spaceflight operations in Germany with locations in Cologne, Oberpfaffenhofen and Weilheim. This responsibility includes satellite missions for Earth observation, science and communication missions as well as for the exploration of the solar system and human spaceflight missions. Furthermore, astronauts are trained, space experiments are prepared and sounding rockets are developed and launched from sites around the world. Eventually, DLR works on new technologies, such as on-orbit-servicing in order to master even the most difficult space projects of the future.
In close cooperation with other DLR institutions and together with public and industrial partners, DLR Space Operations and Astronaut Training plays a major role for spaceflight in Europe. Here, groundbreaking space projects are realized and new ideas for spaceflight of tomorrow are developed. As a versatile interface between technology development, operations and utilization, DLR Space Operations serves as an important venue for everyone involved in spaceflight and the general public. This is where groundbreaking projects are realized and new ideas for shaping the future of space flight are developed.

Our History
- Founded in 1887 in Toronto through a bequest from the estate of Senator William McMaster, a member of the first senate after Confederation and founding president of the Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce.
- Maroon and grey were adopted as the official colours in 1912.
- Relocated from Toronto to Hamilton in 1930.

entityDescription:
ECOBUBBLE is an innovative start-up (set up on 28/01/2019) that operates in the Green Tech area, i.e. technology applied to the design and management of green areas. The company aims to spread a new culture of green design in the national and international territory, projected to protect the environment and promote technological progress, particularly in the sector of urban parks and green roofing.
 
The team designs and develops public and private green spaces, even small ones, with high environmental performance, mitigation of noise and low water consumption, through the introduction of innovative, high-tech products and services. The group also provides consultancy services for the quantification and compensation of pollutant and greenhouse gas emissions absorbed by plants.
 
SERVICES 
 
Ecobubble provides "Science based" green design services through Green Easy which is the first web platform to support the design and development of green areas optimized for the mitigation of pollutants ever created in the world.
 
PRODUCTS
 
ECOBUBBLE PARK is an urban park aimed at the containment of external noise, the mitigation of local pollutants and greenhouse gases through NBS (Nature-Based Solution). Green areas include environmental monitoring sensors, report with CO2 and other emissions sequestered and sustainable furnishing accessories.
 
GREEN-BLUE 1 (GB1) is a new type of technological green roof with water reserve that manages the advantages of green roofs with those of blue roofs (roofs with special water tanks) through the integration of different technologies (Multispectral Analysis, Phytoremediation, IoT, Cloud Computing).
 
GREEN-BLUE 2 (GB2) is an architectural equipment developed to improve the food quality, environmental performance and water saving of urban roof gardens.
 
GREEN-BLUE 3 (GB3) is a collection of architectural modules suitably designed to integrate nature and technology within the Stores. GB3 consists of a green roof, a lighting system, a water collection tank, a specific home automation system for Green-Blue Roof and a virtual server that processes the system forecasts.
