entityName: University of Zagreb - Faculty of Geotechnical Engineering
entityDescription:
The mission of the Faculty of Geotechnical Engineering is to conduct scientific research and provide higher education in an interdisciplinary area of environmental engineering as well as to apply and transfer knowledge to a business sector.
The mission of the Faculty is to deliver good-quality teaching for the purpose of increasing the number of experts who are qualified to solve engineering problems regarding environmental protection according to professional rules with the respect for ethical principles and environmental protection legislation.
Scientific-research work
Scientific work enables not only the mobility of professors/scientists and students but also a continual increase in quality with the rational use of human and material resources. The Faculty contributes to the economic prosperity of the society by transferring knowledge and technologies gained through scientific-research work into a business sector.
Through professional work (such as drawing up feasibility studies and projects) the Faculty closely connects theory with practice, which results in engineering solutions which are directed towards increasing the quality of individual environmental components and which contribute to green economy. In that way the Faculty establishes stronger connections with the region and it is actively involved in solving the problems of the local community.

On a national level, the aim of the Faculty of Geotechnical Engineering is to be recognized as a leading institution which specializes in higher education, scientific and professional work in an area of environmental engineering, especially those segments which focus on the identification, design, construction and management of systems for solving the problems of environmental protection.
These problems concern soil, water and air pollution, waste management as well as defining the mechanisms for environmental protection. The aim of the Faculty is to become an internationally recognized institution which is involved in the European research space and mobility programmes for students and scientists.

Synthetica is a Data Science company focused on the broader Industrial Infrastructure Space.
It creates software solutions that analyze billions of data points and extract information otherwise invisible to human eye. It can solve complex organisational challenges and provide insights crucial for decision making, offering cost and productivity improvements.

Synthetica solves the problem of low productivity and inefficiencies in legacy asset infrastructure installed bases due to:

1) Largely non-digitalized processes, resulting in much heavier than required human involvement.
2) Limited reactivity and adaptability due to non realtime (online) connectivity.
3) Significant loss of opportunity due to non efficient data / information mining. It addresses competitive disadvantages of legacy assets, by upgrading existing workflows and processes for the A.I / M.L and IoT (Internet of Things) era.

entityName: Ferrocarrils de la Generalitat de Catalunya
entityDescription:
Ferrocarrils de la Generalitat de Catalunya, public company, was founded in 1979 to operate two historical lines with their origins in 1863 in the introduction of the Barcelona – Sarrià suburban train service. Over the years, new lines have been added to FGC and these historical lines have been improved and have grown with new passenger and freight services in Barcelona and the surrounding areas. This continuous growth, together with the diversification of the business into other sectors such as leisure and tourism, has made us an efficient public company distinguished by its high quality of service and efficiency in infrastructure management and transport operation.
Main figures:
- 90 million passengers/year and freight transport.
- Workforce over 1600.
- 1301 circulations per day with minimum frequency of 112” in Barcelona-Vallès line.
- Rail network stretching over 290 km of track with international, narrow and Iberian gauges.
- 107 stations.
- The only 2 rack railways existing of Spain.
- 4 funicular cable cars.
- Tourist activities: 47 ski lifts and 146 km of ski runs.
 
The two main railway lines, Barcelona – Vallès (BV) and Llobregat – Anoia (LLA), have metro services inside Barcelona city and commuter services with Barcelona surrounding areas. B-V has 53 km of double track with international gauge, 61 passenger trains, 70 million passengers per year and 32 trains at peak hour with a frequency of 112”. LLA has 140 km of double and single track in some sections with metric gauge, 42 passenger trains, 22 million passengers per year and freight transport. FGC has 100% of their installations adapted to people with reduced mobility.
Regarding freight transport FGC is an important local operator which manages transport of mining products from Suria mine to Bacelona Port, new vehicles from SEAT factory and Bacerlona Port, and car pieces between Barcelona Port and SEAT factory.
FGC does and manages infrastructure and rolling stock maintenance. There are two workshops with one of them approved for interoperable equipment maintenance. 
FGC is member of the International Suburban Rail Benchmarking Group (ISBeRG http://www.isberg-web.org/), a prestigious program led by Imperial College of London. This program monitors and evaluates the efficiency of 16 worldwide operators using 27 Key Performance Indicators. During the 4 years of study FGC appears first, second or third in the 10 main indicators:
- FGC is first in: revenue train hours per driver hour, peak fleet availability and total injures per pax journey.
- FGC is second in: train delay per operated train, trains operated on time per trains operated, overall reliability, pax journeys on time per pax journeys. 
- FGC is third in: trains actually operated per trains scheduled, rolling stock reliability, trains service operation cost per train hour.

entityDescription:
CamGraPhIC Srl is an innovative startup established in Italy in 2019.
The Company exclusively manages the Inphotec facility, a high-tech photonic R&D and prototyping center located in Pisa – Italy. The infrastructure includes a 550sqm clean-room and makes available several technology platforms such as Silicon Photonics, Graphene Photonics, Glass and SiN Photonics, LNOI, Hybrid Integration, and Advanced Packaging. CamGraPhIC provides high-end fabrication and prototyping services to the industry and R&D centers. Application fields are: optical telecommunications, space communications, quantum communications, and advanced sensors.
In addition to the R&D services, CamGraPhIC's mission is to improve optical communications in data-center and 5G environments. The company develops the "Graphene Integrated Photonics" (GIP), a technology platform that will enable next generation optoelectronic devices to support the exponential growth in global data traffic.
CamGraPhIC operates in the development, industrialization, and commercialization of optoelectronic components based on its innovative graphene technology. In particular, CamGraPhIC is active on the integration of high-performance, low-cost, and low-power consumption modulators and photodetectors to enable next-generation optical transceivers for the datacom and 5G industries.
CamGraPhIC’s team includes
15 high-skilled people with a robust track-record in the optoelectronic industry, and a solid background in Photonic Integrated Circuits (PIC) fabrication, Advanced Packaging, devices prototyping, product development, and commercialization.

The Fraunhofer Institute for Building Physics IBP was founded in 1929 and is among the most experienced and established institutes of the Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft. A total of 264 employees work at the three branches in Stuttgart, and Holzkirchen. It has an annual budget of over 27,8 million euros, with approximately one third coming from industrial projects.
The primary focus of Fraunhofer IBP’s work is on research & development, testing, demonstration and consulting in the various specialist areas of building physics.

Applying the principles of building physics forms the foundation of the research and development work conducted by the Fraunhofer Institute for Building Physics IBP. In addition to conventional building physics topics such as acoustics, energy efficiency, indoor climate, hygiene & sensor technology, hygrothermics and recycling building materials, the institute also carries out research on a wide range of projects with a high social relevance. Examples include the integrated design of schools and workspaces, improving the environmental friendliness of flying, or exploring ways and means to harness the energy potential of entire cities. Further focal points are the analysis of products, processes and services from an ecological, economic, social and technical point of view and assessing them from a holistic perspective.
Efficient laboratories and testing facilities, as well as the largest known open-air test site at our branch in Holzkirchen, allow us to conduct complex building physics tests. Modern laboratory measurement equipment and calculation methods optimize building products for practical use. We perform analyses in model rooms, on the test field and on the finished object in order to assess the properties of components and complete systems with regard to building physics, both for new buildings and for renovation projects.
Building physics findings are not only used to optimize buildings and structural components; they also inspire developments in plant engineering and extend the application of building physics knowledge to neighboring areas in the automotive and aviation industries. At the same time, close ties to regional industry ensure a strong and steady influx of professional expertise in all the institute’s fields of research.
Fraunhofer IBP runs centers that have been approved by the German building inspection authorities for testing, monitoring and certifying building products and construction types in Germany and Europe. Four of the institute’s test laboratories have been granted flexible accreditation by the German accreditation body Deutsche Akkreditierungsstelle GmbH (DAkkS) according to DIN EN ISO/IEC 17025. This entitles them to develop new test methods or modify existing ones. The accredited certification center is an independent unit within Fraunhofer IBP and carries out monitoring and certification tasks on various construction products within the scope of German state building regulations and the Building Products Act or Building Products Directive. Company description: The Fraunhofer Institute for Building Physics IBP was founded in 1929 and is among the most experienced and established institutes of the Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft. A total of 264 employees work at the three branches in Stuttgart, and Holzkirchen. It has an annual budget of over 27,8 million euros, with approximately one third coming from industrial projects.
The primary focus of Fraunhofer IBP’s work is on research & development, testing, demonstration and consulting in the various specialist areas of building physics.

Applying the principles of building physics forms the foundation of the research and development work conducted by the Fraunhofer Institute for Building Physics IBP. In addition to conventional building physics topics such as acoustics, energy efficiency, indoor climate, hygiene & sensor technology, hygrothermics and recycling building materials, the institute also carries out research on a wide range of projects with a high social relevance. Examples include the integrated design of schools and workspaces, improving the environmental friendliness of flying, or exploring ways and means to harness the energy potential of entire cities. Further focal points are the analysis of products, processes and services from an ecological, economic, social and technical point of view and assessing them from a holistic perspective.
Efficient laboratories and testing facilities, as well as the largest known open-air test site at our branch in Holzkirchen, allow us to conduct complex building physics tests. Modern laboratory measurement equipment and calculation methods optimize building products for practical use. We perform analyses in model rooms, on the test field and on the finished object in order to assess the properties of components and complete systems with regard to building physics, both for new buildings and for renovation projects.
Building physics findings are not only used to optimize buildings and structural components; they also inspire developments in plant engineering and extend the application of building physics knowledge to neighboring areas in the automotive and aviation industries. At the same time, close ties to regional industry ensure a strong and steady influx of professional expertise in all the institute’s fields of research.
Fraunhofer IBP runs centers that have been approved by the German building inspection authorities for testing, monitoring and certifying building products and construction types in Germany and Europe. Four of the institute’s test laboratories have been granted flexible accreditation by the German accreditation body Deutsche Akkreditierungsstelle GmbH (DAkkS) according to DIN EN ISO/IEC 17025. This entitles them to develop new test methods or modify existing ones. The accredited certification center is an independent unit within Fraunhofer IBP and carries out monitoring and certification tasks on various construction products within the scope of German state building regulations and the Building Products Act or Building Products Directive. This applies to products used for windows, thermal insulation, fireplaces and exhaust systems.

entityDescription:
Lo.La Peak Solutions GmbH (Lo.La) is a well-established SME dedicated to the topics of natural-hazard and risk management. The phrase Lo.La is German and stands for LOkale LAge, which can be translated as “Local Situation” and perfectly describes the methodical focus of the company: LOLA aims to develop and implement risk management solutions that perfectly fit the needs of local level actors.
The current product- and service portfolio of Lo.La contains early warning and monitoring systems for the prevention of disasters, tools for modern risk management, educational services, tailor-made trainings and exercises as well as concepts for the optimized integration of local players into disaster management strategies for privately held companies, public authorities and scientific institutions. All products and services are grounded on the long-term practical and academic experience of the team members and respect the latest scientific findings in the fields of risk management, disaster risk reduction, natural hazard management, and resilience and usability studies.
Since 2014, Lo.La has proactively marketed and sold its products and services to a wide range of clients: Many of them are operators of alpine infrastructure (ski-resorts, railway-operators, street operators, operators of critical infrastructures, etc.) that is endangered by natural hazard events of different types. For these clients, hands-on strategies and tools have been developed to withstand natural disasters by reducing their probability, decreasing their impact and increasing the resilience of the organization to better deal with the risk and to develop the corresponding and target-group specific measures.

entityDescription:
TSS company operate in thermal spray coatings field, in Italy since 2011.
TSS capability is related to all technologies of thermal spray and more underlined, concerns Metallization, Plasma and HVOF (high velocity oxy fuel) coatings. The three technologies can perform coatings of all kind of powders on the market, such as WC (tungsten carbide); CrC (chromium carbide); Ni (nikel) base metallic; Co (cobalt) base metallic; all grades of stellites; Cr2O3 (chromium oxide); ZrO (zirconia); Al2O3 (alumina); TiO2 (Titanium oxide); Cu (copper) etc.
Thermal spray coatings have a wide range of applications from aeronautical field to oil & gas, as well as glass and paper production, or aluminum lamination. Furthermore to standard applications, thermal spray coatings are used for many other purposes such as dimensional restore of worn parts, thermal insulations, electrical insulations, anti wearing of rotating parts.
TSS is involved in all the above fields and mainly is specialist of manufacturing of plungers of alternative pumps and mechanical seals of centrifugal pumps, being the principal producer of such items in Italy, for the most important pump manufacturers such as Peroni Pompe SpA and Floserve – Wortinghton Italy.
A deep experience has been developed in the coating of turbine parts (blades and vanes) as well as for aeronautical section as for oil & gas field. Important customers such as Alitalia, Fincantieri, Nuovo Pignone-GE, Ansaldo and CIRA (Centro Italiano Ricerche Aerospaziali) have used and/or use services of the Group.
TSS has also a special skill to develop new application or new solution for any kind of industrial problems solvable with thermal spray coatings. To support these activities, the Group has one of the most complete laboratory to perform all kind of tests needed to set and check performance of coatings.
TSS is located in Cassino I.Z. Italy, at 300 mt from the exit of Cassino on the main Italian high way A1, that connect Milan to Naples, and just in the middle between Rome and Naples.
The production is performed in an industrial building of 1000 sqm with the support of 600 smq of technical and administrative offices.
The industrial capability is supported by:- Metallization, Plasma and HVOF full automatic equipments of last generations, operating in cabins capable of parts till 5000 kg of weight and 2000x2000x1000 mm of dimension.
- A complete mechanical department with lathes and grinding machines for the manufacturing of plungers and rotating mechanical seals.
- A laboratory that can perform test also for aeronautical field.
TSS has many certifications and qualification of the major companies operating in all the above fields mentioned.
TSS is also partner of the University of Naples for research and development of new coatings and new application.

entityDescription: Destinus is developing high-speed aircraft and infrastructure to power the world’s fastest and cleanest transportation system. These vehicles will be a hybrid between airplanes and rockets, we call them Hyperplanes, capable of moving cargo between continents within 2 hours. It will take off and land horizontally at airports using air-jet engines. Once at a certain altitude and speed, the hyperplane will switch to a set of rocket engines that will accelerate the vehicle to hypersonic velocity. The engines will be powered by hydrogen, produced from renewable energy sources for zero-carbon transportation. The hyperplane will complete its entire flight autonomously, from take-off to landing, and transmit telemetry data via ground and satellite communication systems during flight.

description:
TEMIS was founded in 2006 as an engineering company to study and develop electronic systems and products for the F1 & Motorsport sector.

We are specialized in electronics, computing, monitoring and automation, simulation, navigation, structural mechanics and thermal energy.

In 2008 Temis starts to transfer its know-how to the space sector and it realized a telemetry system to be integrated in the Vega launcher for the acquisition of data and video acquired during the entire duration of the flight. (LARES A&H Sub system)

Since 2009 Temis has increased its expertise in the space field thanks to participation both to Institutional and Industrial Program and working together with leading space companies and European and Italian Space Agencies.

TEMIS has its headquarter located in Corbetta (close to Milan), distributed in 400 m2 of offices and about 200 m2 of laboratory for integration and test.

It counts about 20 resources, mostly highly graduated engineers deeply experienced in:

 Project Management Office (including System Engineering and Product Assurance)
 Design & Manufacturing of Test Equipment & Simulators
 Design & Manufacturing of custom Embedded Systems
 Thermo-Mechanical Analysis and Design
 Control Systems Development and Simulation (including satellite AOCS)

TEMIS is part of ART SpA, located in Passignano sul Trasimeno (PG) , a medium sized company (120 resources) particularly proficient in advanced technological solutions mostly in the automotive and defense fields. It also cooperates with a sister company, MATE srl, the Group's testing and certification unit

entityDescription:
CARTIF is a horizontal, private and non-profit technology center. Its mission is to offer innovative solutions to companies to improve their processes, systems and products, improving their competitiveness and creating new business opportunities. CARTIF develops R&D projects, directly funded by companies or public funds raised through competitive calls for national and international level. CARTIF also advises public authorities (municipalities and regional governments) in the planning and development of innovative projects with high economic returns. The Center maintains the same values and objectives since its foundation in 1994, priority is placed on contributing to the development of its social and economic environment through the use and encouragement of technological innovation via the development and diffusion of research. Its disciplinary teams work in five areas of knowledge that correspond to different economic and technological sectors: industry, energy and environment, construction and infrastructures, agrofood and health and quality of life. Supporting this structure, there are laboratories that have emerged from several lines of research: Analysis and Tests, 3D Scanning, Characterization of biomass, Biotechnology and Materials. Complementing these, other technological services such as management of innovation and technology transfer intended to increase the level of business innovation, better organize their R&D and reap greater benefits from the ideas generated.

The Management Struture of Cartif is divided as follows:
The Board is constituted by 19 companies and institutions. There is a permanent Executive Committee composed by the University of Valladolid, ten associated companies that alternate periodically, and two science and technology research advisors appointed by the General Assembly. Dr. Jose R. Peran Gonzalez has been CARTIF CEO since its foundation. He is emeritus professor at Valladolid University, where he managed the Department of Systems Engineering and Automatics.
Dr. Peran's education (he has a PhD in Industrial Engineering and in Physical Science, and is an Economics graduate) has allowed him to work for thirty years in the private sector -he was head of the bodyworks and mechanics factory and Industrial Director of Renault- and to hold outstanding academic positions. Throughout his vast career, he has developed and coordinated more than 100 R&D projects in Spain and abroad, and has published more than 100 articles, books and book chapters. He is a member of the IEEE, in which he belongs to 14 societies of the Automatics Spanish Committee CEA-IFAC and the Royal Spanish Society of Physics.
The institution itself count with several horizontal Departments which are the following: Management, Business Development, Project Management and R&D Programmes. 
Finally, Cartif is divided into 3 Divisions which covers the different fields od specialization of the Center. They are the following: Energy, Food and Processes and Industrial and Digital Systems. Each of this Divions are divided at the same time on different departments covering diferent fileds of each topic.

The National Institute of Aerospace Technology (INTA) is the Public Research Organization attached to the Ministry of Defense. Its functions are the provision of technological services, certification and research, development and innovation (R&D&I) within the fields of defense and security.
INTA has test facilities throughout the Spanish geography, being located its Headquarters in Torrejón de Ardoz (Madrid). Due to its specialization, INTA works on very diverse projects framed within its strategic lines and objectives, developing its own prototypes (full TRL range). In addition, INTA collaborates in programs, projects and actions with companies, organizations, universities and technology centers, both in Spain and outside its borders.
Apart from the technological support to its customers or partners, INTA has a long tradition in R&D&I in space projects and scientific developments. INTA manages its own budget for space projects and the main action lines in this domain are related to design, development, integration, verification and testing of small and medium-sized platforms and payloads (mainly composed of technologies developed in-house or in cooperation with the space industry and academia), ground segment and satellite tracking and operations.

entityDescription: The Fraunhofer Institute for Solar Energy Systems ISE creates the technological foundations for supplying energy efficiently and on an environmentally sound basis in industrialized, threshold and developing countries. With its research focusing on energy conversion, energy efficiency, energy distribution and energy storage, it contributes to the broad application of new technology. Fraunhofer ISE develops materials, components, systems and processes in five business areas: Photovoltaics, Energy Efficient Buildings, Hydrogen Technologies and Electrical Energy Storage, Solar Thermal Power Plants and Power Electronics. Besides the development of terrestrial renewable energy systems, we have been active in R&D to develop next generation space solar cells with highest efficiency and reliability. We have a wide variety of laboratories to support the development of customer specific solutions including solar cell manufacturing, modelling and characterization under various space conditions. We enable specific missions e.g. by our ultra-lightweight devices with record power/weight ratio or our solar cells which are optimized for highest end-of-life performance. Further areas of expertise include batteries, fuel cells, laser power beaming and power electronics.

entityDescription:
Terranea is a German SME specialised in the development of location-based services and spatial innovation. Based on a wide scientific expertise, the company offers creative solutions fusing data from complementing spatial and non-spatial sources. Open government data, social media, new low-cost sensors and satellites offer a variety and large amounts of data. To determine meaningful information from this data jungle, Terranea applies traditional mapping and geospatial analysis techniques as well as advanced big data analytics and artificial intelligence algorithms. The team is also experienced in developing state-of-the-art geo-ICT tools and apps for solving day to day challenges of individuals but also sophisticated decision support systems for large organizations. 
Besides technical developments the team is consulting clients in the fields of Earth observation and especially Copernicus.
Since its establishment in 2012, Terranea successfully implemented projects for the EC, ESA, EEA, ECMWF, the German Environment Ministry and Environment Agency and the private industry.

entityDescription:
High Altitude Pseudo-Satellites (HAPS) are unmanned aerial vehicles deployed at an altitude around 20 Km with the objective of keeping a fixed position to provide communications or remote sensing services to a specific area of interest. These platforms can provide real time services, very high persistence (during weeks or months) and very low latency to an area of interest. In addition, they can be periodically recovered on ground for maintenance, repair and updating activities.

smartHAPS provides environmental monitoring and other remote sensing services of regions, urban and coastal areas during weeks or months. The identification and location of pollution sources and waste dumping, the characterization and monitoring of large agrarian production areas, or maritime areas are current challenges for institutional and commercial customers. SmartHAPS systems deliver a continuous operation over an area of interest with very high spatial, and spectral resolutions and very low information latencies. In addition, they can be recovered on ground and re-launched to the same or alternative locations.
The company is developing its own stratospheric platform, a compact solar powered lighter-than-air-system, based on its team's 15-year experience in the small satellites, and Unmanned Aerial and Surface Vehicles. The use of space proven components and subsystems is enabling an accelerated development of the smartHAPS platform at a lower cost.

- around 18,000 students
- 85 Bachelor's and Master’s degree programmes 
- 500 professors

- 750 part-time lecturers
- 14 departments 
HM Hochschule München University of Applied Sciences is the second largest university of applied sciences in Germany. Our 18,000 students and our location in a leading European business centre afford fantastic opportunities, but also mean we have a responsibility in industrial, economic and social contexts. 
Multidisciplinary variety
We offer degree courses and active academic collaboration in the MINT subjects (mathematics, computer science, natural sciences and engineering), business, the social sciences and public health as well as in architecture and design. Our Department of General and Interdisciplinary Studies is unique in providing every student with a cross-disciplinary education and in developing their personal skills. 
Studying with a profile
It is especially important for us to nurture our graduates' characters: besides their well-founded professional skills, our students should stand out by thinking and acting in a sustainable, entrepreneurial and intercultural way. With these additional qualifications which reach beyond the students' specialist fields, we prepare them to contribute to society and to approach their careers with foresight, creativity and a sense of responsibility. 
From Bachelor's degree to doctoral qualification
We offer and develop individualised study approaches and options for applicants with varied educational backgrounds, thus opening our university and offering a range of paths for lifelong learning and studying. 
Hochschule München ensures excellent applied and research-based teaching in four areas: 
 
- Bachelor's degrees for school leavers and the professionally qualified
- Master's degrees and doctoral qualifications
- Continuing education and life-long learning in all fields
- Applied research 
Growth with a view to the future
Hochschule München actively engages with its educational mandate and aims to secure an outstanding position as a university of applied sciences. It recognises the future demands of society and industry and is changing, with a critical yet open vision for current issues, such as the current digitalisation of all areas of life. It focuses on continually improving quality and on constant development in research, teaching and continuing education.

entityDescription:
TAS-L leverages big data, artificial intelligence and cybersecurity to address complex end-to-end challenges, while fostering excellence in user experience. Its expertise covers innovative design and implementation approaches with customers, minimum viable products development, design and development of key digital building blocks of space systems, rollout and operations of solutions, experimentation of new technologies and concepts, digital business models, and international project management.
The company has currently 28 employees (21 FTE, 7 consultants), growing, and its operational site is located at the Technoport, a start-up incubator in Belval, Luxembourg. TAS-L will move to its permanent office in the third quarter of 2024. Its development environment is cloud native and based on the Thales Digital Platform, a state of the art digital environment operated by Thales and supporting a set of security levels. 
TAS-L’s current portfolio of products and projects encompasses:
· a Secured Digital Platform supporting TAS Earth Observation applications
· Key Digital Components of Space Inspire Ground Segment
· a 3-Dimension visualizer “Orthoglobe” for professionals of the space industry 
· A Proof-of- Concept Digital Twin system. TAS-L acting as Prime Contractor 
· An Artificial Intelligence Data Processing Platform hosting 2 MVPs targeted respectively at Land-Use and Biodiversity impact assessment, and, Greenhouse Gas and Air Quality impact assessment.
These projects and products are developed for either external customers (institutional, private, defence), or TAS Business Lines (Telecom and Earth-Observation).

entityDescription:
Fraunhofer IZFP is an internationally networked research and development institute in the field of applied research. Its activities are focused on the development of "cognitive sensor systems" for the nondestructive monitoring of industrial processes and value chains. The Institute's technical understanding of inspection and sensor physics is supplemented by technologies and concepts from AI research, which are used to develop sensor systems for the NDT of tomorrow. In addition to pure production processes, the activities cover equally processes from materials and product development, maintenance, repair, and recycling of materials.
With better security, reliability and lower costs in mind, the focus of the institute‘s application-oriented, industrial-purpose innovations is improving the quality of the customer‘s products.
Fraunhofer IZFP offers its customers and research partners the entire range of nondestructive testing technologies. The institute‘s researchers, engineers and technicians develop solutions to address modern testing applications including feasibility studies, consulting, training and inspection services and creating prototype systems.
The development results of the institute are systematically interlinked with modern information and communication technologies. Machine learning concepts are used for intelligent signal and image processing or for the automated interpretation and assessment of test and measurement data.

entityDescription:
Livelink Aerospace has been working in passive detection for several years, developing sensors and systems that offer high resilience and excellent cost/ benefit compared to traditional sensor types.Recently winning a tender put forth by DASA (Defence and Security Accelerator), on behalf of the DSTL (Defence Science and Technology Laboratory), we are rapidly prototyping and developing novel technologies that increase detection at low altitude of non-cooperative aircraft (manned and unmanned), whilst driving the cost far below that of conventional methods such as radar.Part of our remit is also to be (where possible), passive in our approach to detection; this gives us great advantages such as zero licensing issues and non-interference with infrastructure near our sensor nodes.

As an SME we have developed passive electronics to accurately locate sources of RF since 2016. The foundational technology has successfully achieved several km of real-world detection from low power sources (which were transmitting at sub one Watt of power in the 2.4GHz and 5.8GHz ranges).

The trajectory of our core technology has been significantly helped by the Defence and Security Accelerator (DASA) which funded an application in 2020 to develop our core technology with the addition of an advanced sensor fusion layer added to it. This has allowed us to significantly increase the number, and complexity of sensors feeding into the LiveLink system. It also allows us to successfully fuse data from a wide range of other sensors such as acoustic, optical, RF and Radar. This ability to receive and accurately process data from a large, low cost mesh of fused sensors whilst handling redundancy, ambiguity and contradiction is significant in a complex environment such as offshore air defence.
This technology enables protection of Critical National Infrastructure against air threats and provide data assurance. LLA has expertise from commercial aviation, sensor fusion, academic R&D and consultants previously involved with military and civilian defence projects.

entityDescription:
Incremental is an award-winning software engineering consultancy based in York. Our dynamic and trustworthy team develops and delivers innovative data-driven software solutions and location tracking systems to the rail industry. 
 
Our range of products helps reduce disruption and delays on the rail network through an efficient and accurate flow of information. Our pioneering GPS data provides unique insights and comprehensive reporting functions that enable train operators and infrastructure providers to manage, monitor and continuously improve their performance.
 
Our ground-breaking technology provides large scale monitoring of train movements, and our aggregation, storage and processing of billions of data points, makes sense of ‘Big Data’ problems. 
 
Fully measurable maps visualise stations, junctions, passing points and signals to unlock and expose a range of performance issues faced on the railway. The rapid analysis capability our software solutions offer allows for immediate awareness of speed restrictions, delay location identification and planning and timetable verification – key information to improve performance across the rail network.
 
Our products give our clients greater control of situations as they happen with easily accessible, accurate and credible data to improve communication between all parties involved, helping UK rail passengers enjoy a more reliable, safe and comfortable journey experience. Using advanced machine learning, remote condition monitoring, data aggregation and trending techniques, we provide insights into vehicle performance that have historically been unachievable.
 
Our range of solutions provide information across mobile, web and desktop enterprise applications and are designed to offer straight-forward, accessible information to our customers.
 
Through our collaborative approach with our clients, such as Network Rail, Northern and Great Western Railway, we jointly identify problems and deliver technology driven applications to alleviate those problems. Our incredibly experienced team delivers solutions that make the railway, greener, safer and more reliable for everyone.
 
We’ve won several awards in recognition of our innovative, industry changing products. We genuinely believe the railway can perform better and we’re passionate about developing the technology that drives that positive change.

description:
Nablawave is an advanced engineering company providing R&D services in the Aerospace, Energy and Turbomachinery sectors. We follow new projects from the preliminary design phase to experimental tests, suggesting a mixed approach able to minimise development time and costs.

Nablawave strongly believes in technology contamination: new ideas and concepts coming from traditional industries can bring relevant advantages to the Aerospace sector providing smart, cost-effective solutions. Our expertise can be valuable on several points: 
1.	We know how to decrease space propulsion development costs by widely adopting commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) components. Often small variations on the propulsion system layout can have large impacts on development, safety, operational costs, as well as time to market.
2.	We know how to assess propulsion concepts in the most efficient way: a mix of design, numerical simulation, and testing, that permits to strongly reduce the development time. 
3.	We know how to exploit experimental facilities, increasing the number of tests per day and reducing testing costs. In our experience it is possible to design, build, and organize flexible and fast testing facilities with low budgets, respecting safety requirements. Our team successfully designed and tested different lab-scale rocket engines (from less than 1 kN up to 10 kN). We carried out more than 500 tests on different propulsion system configurations using a lot of COTS and industrial equipment. 

At the heart of Nablawave there is a team of passionate professionals (researchers, engineers, Ph.Ds) with transversal skills, capable of providing simple and unique solutions. Optimization algorithms and machine learning are seamlessly integrated with advanced analysis and design tools to handle the most complex modelling problems; the result is a drastic acceleration of the R&D process and an important reduction in costs. Our services include:
-	Mechanical design 
-	Structural, fluid-dynamic, vibro-acoustic simulations, combustion and fluid-structure interaction; all the simulations can be coupled with our in-house optimization software 
-	Development of tailor-made engineering software and algorithms, digital twins, optimization and machine learning 
-	Assistance with experimental testing

entityDescription: The National Observatory of Athens (NOA) is a national organization operating under public law rules and procedures and is supervised by the appropriate Directorate of the General Secretariat for Research and Technology of the Ministry of Development. entityDescription:
Human Design Group, a pioneer and expert in ergonomic consulting.
In 1975, Bertin stood as a precursor by creating its Ergonomics Department (formerly called Bertin Ergonomics), the very first private consulting structure in France in this field. Our clients (in aerospace and nuclear industries) seek to control human factor risks for reliability, whether in the functioning of their organizations or for the development (emerging at the time) of computerization solutions for work situations.
40 years later, Bertin Ergonomics becomes Human Design Group. With nearly 120 collaborators (coming from backgrounds in ergonomics, human factors, and cognitive engineering) who support Project Owners, Engineering for major projects (fixed-price and on a contract basis), and Research and Development services.
Our solutions allow us to offer a range of consulting and design ergonomic services to meet each of our clients' demands:
- Integration of human factors in programs (management)
- Ergonomics of digital systems (supervision, business applications, embedded, mobile, voice-activated)
- Reliability of organizations and risk-driving systems
- Ergonomics and layout of spaces and workstations
- Ergonomics and innovation of future products and services (ideation, modeling, and user testing)
The development of Human Design Group is explained by the permanence of values. On the teams' side, there is a client-oriented organization, unwavering motivation, and a friendly and innovative "startup" spirit. On the clients' side, the coherence of the offer and the quality of achievements.

entityDescription:
Heureka, the Finnish Science Centre introduces the public to science and technology in an engaging and interactive way. Visitors can experience the joy of discovery through spectacular exhibitions, planetarium films, educational programmes and events.
Located in the Tikkurila area of Vantaa, Heureka first opened its doors to the public in 1989. Heureka is one of Finland’s most popular recreational centres, attracting an average of nearly 300,000 visitors each year. Heureka’s operations are subsidized by the Ministry of Education and Culture and the City of Vantaa.

Heureka's history
The roots of Heureka, the Finnish Science Centre can be traced back to the University of Helsinki and scientists, who had become acquainted with different science centres located around the world. The initial spark was lit by Adjunct Professors Tapio Markkanen, Hannu I. Miettinen and Heikki Oja.
It all began with the Physics 82 exhibition held at the House of the Estates in Helsinki on 20–26 May 1982. During autumn of that same year, the science centre project was launched with the initial support of the Academy of Finland, the Ministry of Education, and various foundations. The project led to the establishment of the Finnish Science Centre Foundation during 1983-1984. The original founding members of the foundation included the University of Helsinki, the Helsinki University of Technology, the Federation of Finnish Learned Societies, and the Confederation of Industries.
In 1984, the City of Vantaa offered to be the host city and partial financier for the Science Centre, and also designated a property lot located in the southern end of Tikkurila as the future site of the centre. An architectural competition, held in 1985, turned out two first prizes from which the winning design was selected; namely the “Heureka” design submitted by Mikko Heikkinen, Markku Komonen and Lauri Anttila. That’s how the Finnish Science Centre Heureka got its apt name!
Before the building was completed, a number of test exhibitions were set up at other sites. The interior plan for the Science Centre was completed in 1986. The foundation for the building was laid in October 1987, and the construction work was completed one year later. The overall area of the building is 8,200 m², of which 2,500 m² is exhibition space. The Finnish Science Centre Heureka opened its doors to the public on 28 April 1989.

Huld s.r.o is a software engineering company specialized in safety-critical software and complex data processing. In former days, Space Systems Czech (SSC) was established in Czech Republic as a sister company of Space Systems Finland (SSF) fully adopting its culture, practices and quality standards. After succeeding a Merge in the Q4 of 2019,between the former Space Systems Finland, Space Systems Czech and RD Velho; the new brand and name of the company is Huld. Our success is based on the ability to maximise the added value to the customers by providing superior and cost-effective solutions. Working together with our customers, Huld can ensure that risks are managed and products fulfill safety and market demands. 
At the beginning of its existence, Huld has attracted the best experts experienced with providing high-reliability software solutions for many of Europe’s most ambitious space missions. Huld focuses on mission-critical solutions for demanding environments, such as satellite on-board software, Software Verification Facilities and processing control environments. The company aims to enter domestic, European, US and Asian markets and is active in the fields of on-board software, embedded Hard Real Time software, ground processing software, testing and validation, quality, augmented GPS navigation systems and the creation of software- development tools. 
Moreover, Huld office in Prague was established to deliver cutting-edge technology to their customers, exploring latest concepts and trends, which promises to introduce new products with potential to become market disruptors. Beside other activities, we are exploring opportunities in prospecting of asteroids and also dealing with distributed ledger technology. When seeking new products based on the very latest technology advancements, we combine experience with criticality products, ability to criticize proposed solutions, and strong goal-oriented approach. Thus, we can prepare a solution packed with the latest features, but also with viability in mind. 
Approaching almost five years of operation in the Czech Republic, we are proving that the concept is correct and Huld is on the track becoming biggest safety-critical software provider in the space domain in the Czech Republic. entityDescription:
Qfluidics is a young French startup developing its breakthrough “liquid tube” technology. In short, we use magnetic liquids to transport other liquids. Our technology allows us to transport various fluids without any solid contact granting unique advantages over conventional pumping/valving technologies: 
• Abrasive insensitivity (to transport slurries without damaging the pump) 
• Up to 99% pressure drop reduction (very useful to transport viscous fluids at a low energy cost) 
• A very soft pumping action (low-shear) to transport fragile biological fluids (cells, whole blood, etc.)

At the moment, Qfluidics is focused on collaborative projects to introduce and adapt its liquid tube technology to solve issues of various industries.

entityDescription:
Eurecat (www.eurecat.org) is the leading technology centre in Catalonia and the second largest private research organisation in southern Europe.
Eurecat furnishes the business and industrial sector with unique technology and advanced knowledge to address the innovation needs of companies and make them more competitive. The added value provided by Eurecat fast-tracks innovation, cuts outlay on scientific and technological infrastructures, minimises risks and delivers specialised expertise tailored to each company’s requirements. It brings standout solutions to unlock the value chain with initiatives which leverage innovation and business to build capabilities, streamline resources and drive profitability. 
Eurecat is also committed to working with other players in the domestic innovation system. It has partnership agreements in place with other centres which enable technology research and development calling for skills and teams available at other facilities to be conducted jointly and cost-effectively for businesses. We are a member of 22 technology platforms, 12 Digital Innovation Hubs and 37 European associations.
As part of its global outlook Eurecat pursues an internationalisation strategy anchored in three key objectives: supporting companies in their expansion abroad through technological innovation, driving cross-border strategic partnerships and marketing its product and services portfolio.
Eurecat’s key figures are summarised below:

Workforce: > 650
Parity (W/M): 42%/58%
Customers: > 1.700
Patents: 153
Annual income: 49,2 million euros
Sites: 11
Spin-offs: 8
Consortium R&D projects: 200+
Ongoing H2020 projects led: 33
Ongoing H2020 projects: 86

Sixty-seven percent of Eurecat’s customers are Catalan SMEs, and in general 90% of its customers hire R&D&I services which in turn underpin the centre’s operations in harnessing multi-technological solutions to meet specific challenges and needs.
Eurecat’s technological specialisation is split into four Technology Areas: Industrial, Digital, Biotechnology and Sustainability. Taken together these areas have extensive knowhow and expertise in over 20 scientific and technological fields including artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, advanced manufacturing, smart materials, printed electronics, robotics and automation, medical devices, circular economy, climate change and nutrition and health.
These multi-technology and multidisciplinary capabilities enable Eurecat to systematically address complex challenges as a world-class partner for businesses in domains such as Industry 4.0, the digital transformation of production sectors, the circular economy, smart cities, personalised nutrition, predictive medicine and the digital economy. It also has state-of-the-art scientific and technological facilities and laboratories including its Omic Sciences Centre, its Plastronics pilot plant which is a groundbreaker in Europe, and its regional 3D manufacturing laboratory network.
Eurecat’s operations target a range of key business sectors which are significant due to their footprint in the region and their contribution to its GDP. They include the automotive industry, food, tourism, health, energy and resources, construction, railways and aeronautics, cultural and creative industries, industrial systems and processes, textiles and ICT.

CYENS CoE is the Research Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Cyprus in the area of Information and Communication Technologies focusing on Interactive media, Smart systems and Emerging technologies. The Centre of Excellence fosters world-class research activities and at the same time aims to serve as a paradigm for bridging scientific research with innovation outside academia. It is a joint venture between the three public universities of Cyprus (University of Cyprus, Cyprus University of Technology, Open University of Cyprus), the Municipality of Nicosia, and two renowned international partners, the Max Planck Institute for Informatics (Germany) and University College London (UK).

CYENS CoE is designed to act as an integrator of academic research and innovation, towards the sustainable fuelling of scientific, technological and economic growth of Cyprus and Europe, empowering knowledge and technology transfer in the region.
 
CYENS CoE consists of three Research Pillars (RP) representing the three main research areas of Visual Sciences, Human Factors and Design, and Communication and Artificial Intelligence:
· The RP of Visual Sciences: includes the research areas of Computer Graphics, Computer Vision, Imaging and Virtual/Augmented Reality. 
· The RP of Human Factors and Design: includes the research areas of human-computer interaction, applied perception and cognition.
· The RP Communication and Artificial Intelligence: incorporates the research areas of machine learning models, cognitive models of natural language, psychological models of attention, common sense reasoning, analysis of interaction in social networks, distributed/networked systems, mechanisms for ensuring multimedia application support, controlled network performance and quality of experience, and the integration of embedded systems and sensors in the data stream.

entityDescription:
Institute of Educational Policy (IEP) was established in 2011 under Public Law 3966 (Government Gazette Α’ 118/24-05-2011). It is a Public Entity under Private Law supervised by the Ministry of Education and Religious Affairs. IEP operates for the benefit of public interest as an executive scientific body that supports the Ministry of Education and Religious Affairs on issues related to primary and secondary education as well as the transition from secondary to higher education. IEP is also responsible for the in-service teacher training, the formal curriculum development, the educational material as well as the assessment tools used at national level. IEP’s primary mission is the scientific research and study of issues related to all levels of education, the contribution to the design and implementation of educational policy issues and the implementation of co-funded projects. According to Law 4763/2020 (Government Gazette A’ 254/21-12-2020), there are three Scientific Departments:
· Department A: Educational Innovation and Inclusive Education
· Department B: School Curricula and Educational material
· Department C: In-service training & Evaluation, European and International Educational Policy.
Moreover, the Department of Projects and Actions is responsible for coordinating IEP participation, either as project coordinator or partner, in both Partnership Agreement 2014-2020 and EU (co)funded programmes (Erasmus+ etc).

Picosun provides equipment and solutions for conformal coating with ALD (Atomic Layer Deposition) method. Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) is an advanced thin film coating method which is used to fabricate ultra-thin, highly uniform and conformal material layers for several applications. ALD uses sequential, self-limiting and surface-controlled gas phase chemical reactions to achieve control of film growth in the nanometer/sub-nanometer thickness regime. Due to the film formation mechanism – the gases won’t react until in touch with the surface which means the film growth proceeds by consecutive atomic layers “up” from the surface – the ALD film is dense, crack, defect and pinhole-free and its thickness along with structural and chemical characteristics can be precisely controlled on atomic scale.

entityDescription: IHP is a European Research and Innovation Center member of the Leibnitz association, performing research and development in the fields of silicon-based systems, highest-frequency integrated circuits and technologies for wireless and broadband communication, aiming to strengthen the competitiveness of the German and European microelectronic industry. The focus of research at the institute is oriented towards issues relevant for business, resulting in applications for telecommunications, semiconductor and automotive industries, aerospace, telemedicine, and automation technologies. The institute has developed into an internationally recognized competence center for silicon-germanium microelectronic technologies. IHP has with its core competences in materials research, semiconductor technology, circuit design and system design development, has a long-term experience cooperating in many national and international projects with Universities, research institutions and with industry. Besides providing important bridge between academia and industry, IHP provides access to its 0.25 µm and 0.13 µm SiGe:C BiCMOS technologies processed on 8" (200mm) wafer in its own pilot line for chip manufacturing via the Low Volume & Multi Project Wafer (MPW) Service. IHP technologies are especially suited for applications in the higher GHz bands (e.g. for wireless, broadband, radar). They provide integrated HBTs with cut-off frequencies of up to 500 GHz and integrated LDMOS devices with breakdown voltages of up to 22 V, including complementary devices.

entityDescription: VZLU AEROSPACE (VZLU) is a national centre for research, development and testing in aeronautics and space, with turnover more than 250 million CZK and more than 220 employees. Our main mission is to generate invention, transfer it into industrial practice and to provide its partners with the maximum support in the process of new products development. As a multi-discipline research organisation, VZLU exploits synergic effects and also contributes to progress of automotive, rail, defence, security and power industry. The major multidisciplinary fields of VZLU include aerodynamic, structure strength and durability, material and corrosion engineering, composite materials and technologies. In the field of product development, VZLU is focused on rotor blades, industrial fans aircraft engines orsatellite equipment. VZLU collaborates closely with similar organisations throughout Europe to provide feedback necessary for its continuous development. The history of VZLU dates back to 1922, a year when the Institute for Air Navigation Studies under the auspices of the Ministry of Defence was founded. More than 80 Czechoslovak aircraft types have passed through the VZLU’s gates since then. In the pre-war years VZLU was focused mainly on aerodynamics and strength-of-structure calculations. Aircraft made in LETOV, AVIA, AERO and PRAGA factories were tested here. After the war VZLU came under the civil administration and took over design work from many aviation factories. VZLU gave rise to a number of successful aircrafts such as the first jet aeroplane L-29 Dolphin, the L-13 Blanik sailplane, sporting planes and helicopters. From the mid-sixties, VZLU participated in the developments of new airplanes like the L-39 Albatros jet, the L-410 small transport aircraft and sporting planes. For most of the airplanes new engines, an ejection seat, propellers and other systems were developed jointly with other manufacturing plants. Since 1993 VZLU has been largely engaged in national scientific and research programmes financed by ministries of the Czech Republic aimed at supporting domestic industries. Since 1999 VZLU has been participating in more than 40 international projects supported by the EU. VZLU engagement in projects beyond aviation has increased to a large extent over the last couple of years. VZLU is working for a number of customers coming from various industries like turbo-set engineering, car industry, rail vehicles, civil engineering and textile industry, and others. In 2005 VZLU has been awarded by Microaccelerometr contract for the ESA SWARM mission by EADS Astrium. Since then the VZLU expands its activities in the Space domain. VZLU contributed on several ESA missions/projects like SWARM, JUICE, EUCLID, PROBA-3, ARIANE 6 as well as on non-ESA projects like EADS Astrium Spaceplane. VZLU is also engaged in the development of small space instruments and small satellites of the CubeSat type. The VZLUSAT-1 CubeSat (http://vzlusat1.eu) was launched in LEO orbit in June 2017, successfully commissioned and is presently taking data from its payloads (more than 3 years in operation).

entityDescription:
RHIPTO is a non-profit center established to support and supply the UN with a rapid response capacity in the field of environment, development, peace and security. RHIPTO is supported by the UN and was established in response to UNSecurity Council resolution S/RES 2195 (19DEC2014). It became a formal UN collaborating center on May 3rd, 2016 through a Memorandum of Understanding with UNEP, signed by UN Under-Secretary General Achim Steiner, Executive Director of UNEP. In 2019, RHIPTO entered a formal collaboration agreement also with UN Office on Drugs and Crime and INTERPOL, the Worlds largest police organisation with over 190 member states. RHIPTO supports a number of UN agencies, committees and councils on peace, security and development issues.

RHIPTO undertakes analytical, assessment, training or other forms of support to the UN.RHIPTO or collaborating UN agencies publishes and releases a wide range of publications, from non-public briefs on acute threats to environment or security development, threat finance, environmental crime, counter-terrorism, natural resources, training manuals, popular articles or general development and peace issues.
​RHIPTO works through field investigations, analyses and wide networks across United Nations agencies and programmes, through public, humanitarian, research, private and security sectors with networks and contacts throughout most countries in the World.RHIPTO undertakes field missions bringing together lead experts from around the World and works through UN agencies. RHIPTO has offices in Norway, London and Paris.

entityDescription: AAC Hyperion, formerly known as Hyperion Technologies, is based in Delft, the Netherlands, and specializes in high performance components for CubeSats and SmallSats. It is renowned for its attitude determination and orbit control subsystems, and DTE laser communications. Founded in 2013, Hyperion Technologies joined AAC Clyde Space in 2020 and is now part of the international group. With over 200 employees worldwide, AAC Clyde Space is stretched across business locations in Sweden, the United Kingdom, The Netherlands, South Africa and the United States, and Group specializes in advanced nanosatellite spacecraft, mission services, and reliable subsystems. Its market-leading New Space solutions and services enable government, commercial, and educational organizations. In the AAC Clyde Space Group we deliver three main pillars of offerings: Subsystems for CubeSats and SmallSats, CubeSat missions, and Space Data as a Service. At AAC Hyperion, we specialize in subsystem technologies such as: Star trackers, sun sensors, magnetometers, IMUs, reaction wheels, magnetorquers, payload processors, imagers, and laser communication terminals for CubeSats and SmallSats capable of very high speed and secure downlink. Across the Group, we furthermore serve clients with subsystems for Power Conditioning and Distribution Units, Command and Data Handling, RF solutions, batteries as well as GNSS for various sizes of spacecraft.

description: Argotec is an Italian aerospace engineering company whose activities concern the production of small sats for deep space and the development of innovative solutions to support the astronauts’ comfort. Thanks to Argotec’s facilities and know-how, the company activities follow the “all in-house concept” which includes design, development, integration, qualification and operation services. The company’s small sat platforms suitable also for deep space (6U or 12U version) offer high reliability, rad-hardness, large volume for payloads and integrated propulsion systems. Argotec can directly monitor sats in space using its Mission Control Centre certified by NASA JPL Deep Space Network. Moreover, Argotec produces custom OBC (including on-board SW and processing algorithms) and EPS for its platforms.
entityDescription: ARGOTEC is an Italian engineering and software company, providing a wide range of professional and engineering services. Argotec provides Training, Systems, Software, Communications Engineering and technical support services, as well as IT consulting services to the engineering markets, including the aerospace industry and its related agencies and organizations. Argotec has professional capabilities in engineering, informatics (system integration and software development) and a long and recognised experience in Human Space Flights and Operations. Our personnel supported a wide range of Human Space Flight missions including the International Space Station (ISS) operations. Our experience also encompasses astronauts training and ISS flight controller training and certification. Argotec carries on research activities in various aerospace areas, including thermal and control systems. The capability of transferring and removing heat is a critical requirement of many industrial applications. Argotec, carrying out research activities on passive heat transfer technology, addresses this need providing real solutions which have also an immediate application on Earth. Over recent years, the European Space Agency (ESA) contracted Argotec as the unique European responsible of the space food development and supply for the European astronauts on the International Space Station (ISS). To meet this ambitious technological challenge, Argotec developed independently a new research area for the study of nutritional food dedicated to the astronauts, the so-called Space Food Lab.

entityDescription:
The Cyprus Space Exploration Organisation (CSEO) is a non-governmental, non-profit, science organisation and research institution, based in Cyprus, with a global scope of service and activities.

Its main pillars are outreach, education, research, development, space advocacy, and international cooperation in the field of space exploration, astronautics and astronomy. The organisation promotes and facilitates international scientific collaboration in space exploration, and fosters domestically collaboration with other space-faring nations in science, space and planetary missions.

It was founded in 2012, with the goal of “Launching Cyprus into the Space Era” and building the next generation of scientists, that would see Cyprus as a niche player in global space exploration initiatives, and would build an international collaboration with other space-faring nations in scientific, space and planetary missions.

Today it has over 1000 registered researchers, scientists, educators and volunteers and over 250,000 followers on social media. CSEO has multiple spinoffs and subsidiary companies, and supports and promotes startups and technological innovation.

CSEO's Space Cluster of companies is involved in over 10 funded space research programmes (Horizon, ESA, domestic and international).

CSEO’s Space Cluster, companies, researchers and teams are skilled in Earth Observation, ICT, Robotics, Electronics, Computer Vision, Aerospace Engineering, Astrophysics, Planetary Sciences, Environmental and Climate Sciences, Energy, Mechanical, Structural, Materials, Optics, Medicine, Bioengineering, etc. 

CSEO is the official representative of Cyprus to:
- the International Committee on Space Research (COSPAR),
- the International Astronomical Union (IAU),
- the International Astronautical Federation (IAF),
- the Global Experts Group on Sustainable Lunar Activities (GEGSLA),
- the Moon Village Association (MVA),
- the Mars Upper Atmosphere Network (MUAN),
- the Mars Society,
and many other international bodies.

CSEO's International Council comprises some of the world’s most distinguished individuals that are highly decorated for their contribution to space exploration and astronomy.

entityDescription:
Demcon contributes to solutions for contemporary social issues. Be it delivering medical solutions, contributing to security or providing sustainable solutions and high-tech innovations relating to themes like water and energy: Demcon contributes to a better world.
The DEMCON group consists of over thirty companies that jointly focus on three important main activities: Projects, Products and Production. Under the heading of projects, the DEMCON Advanced Mechatronics (DAM) companies jointly together and each independently implement innovative developments. The own product companies each have their own product(s) that they market, sell and service worldwide. This includes, for example, Macawi Respiratory Systems and Finapres Medical Systems. The production branch of the DEMCON focuses on producing high-quality technology, both for its own product companies and for third parties.
In this way, DEMCON can fulfil its mission: to develop, produce and supply technology and innovative products and systems that offer solutions for technical and social customers and end users worldwide. 
The focus areas are high-tech systems, medical systems, industrial systems, opto-mechatronic systems and robotic systems. Markets that are served include: aerospace, agri & food, high-tech systems & materials, life sciences & health, smart industry and water & maritime. As a system supplier, Demcon can fully meet the needs of its customers, from proof-of-principle, prototype and pre-production to series production, building on mechatronic system engineering as its core competence, combined with a wide range of engineering disciplines. This enables the group to undertake challenging projects and meet exacting specifications, delivering the technological innovations to a variety of markets. Thanks to this strong foundation, the DEMCON group has grown into a high-quality development, industrialization and production partner.
Demcon also develops its own products and invests in start-ups and established companies through an innovation program. Recent investments have been made in medical, water, security and energy technology.
Demcon’s ambition is to continue increasing its positive impact. We want to grow further by accepting new and challenging projects, exploring new international markets and expanding our production expertise and capacity.
Demcon is certified for ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 13485:2016

entityName: ISTITUTO NAZIONALE DI GEOFISICA E VULCANOLOGIA - INGV
entityDescription: The National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology (INGV) was established by Legislative Decree of 29 September 1999, n. 381, from the merger of five institutes already operating in the field of geophysical and volcanological disciplines: the National Institute of Geophysics (ING), the Vesuvian Observatory (OV), the International Institute of Volcanology of Catania (IIV), the Institute of Fluid Geochemistry of Palermo (IGF) and the Research Institute on Seismic Risk in Milan (IRRS). The mission and the research objectives of the Institute are indicated in Article 2 of the Statute (G.U.Serie Generale No. 27 of 02-02-2018). The institutional mandate of the Entity includes the pursuit of objectives of observation of the phenomena and of the development of scientific knowledge on the Earth System as a whole, in strong interaction with the technological activity, the management and development of research infrastructures and the realization of activities with potential significant impact on the population and on the different components of the Company. All the aforementioned activities need an administrative action that is supportive and facilitated to INGV researchers and technologists. As a member of the National Civil Protection Service, as well as the Competence Center of the Civil Protection Department, pursuant to the law of 24 February 1992, n. 225, and of the Prime Ministerial decrees of 27 February 2004 and DPCM of 17 February 2017, the INGV is entrusted with the surveillance of the seismicity of the entire national territory and of the activity of the Italian active volcanoes and of the tsunamis in the Mediterranean area, through the management of networks of observation with technologically advanced instrumentation, distributed throughout the country or concentrated around active volcanoes and through the 24-hour guard of n. 3 operating rooms in Rome, Naples and Catania. INGV's primary objective is to contribute to the understanding of the dynamics of the Earth System, in its various phenomena and solid and fluid components, and to the mitigation of associated natural risks. In particular, the activities of the Entity can be subdivided into three broad categories: • Scientific and technological research in the field of Geosciences, with particular regard to Seismology, Volcanology and environmental issues. • Institutional and service research for the Company, for Public Administrations and Industry; in particular, we highlight the activities carried out in the Annual Convention, within the framework of a 10-year Framework Agreement with the Civil Protection Department, regarding seismic, volcanic and tsunami risk, and seismic monitoring and soil deformation activities. in areas where georisources are exploited, on behalf of the Ministry of Economic Development. The institutional research activities also include those relating to the design, development and maintenance of research infrastructures, some of which are of international prestige and of European dimension. • Third Mission activities, including training, dissemination, technology transfer, spin-offs and patents, museum centers and public engagement.

entityDescription:
Weather Flare is a mobile application that helps people with long-term health conditions take back control of their illness whatever the weather. It tracks the effects of weather conditions on medications and illnesses, then presenting useful information back to the user of how-to best plan their day, week or a future holiday.
Integration of the weather makes Weather Flare unique; it takes the users' symptoms and personal medications they may have and cross-references the information to accurate knowledge and up-to-date research of how the weather may affect them. This then translates back to the user via the app in the Traffic Light and Tips functions, so the user does not spend endless amounts of time trying to figure out whether they need to take extra care of the weather and can get on with their day.
 
These functions are all simple, understandable, and personalised to make Weather Flare a breeze to use for anyone, any day and night.
 
HOW WEATHER FLARE WORKS
1.You download the app and tell Weather Flare about your chronic pain. For example:
vDo you have a diagnosed condition?
vWhat other symptoms do you experience?
vIs there anything that triggers your pain or other symptoms?
vDo you take medication?
2.Whenever you experience a symptom or a pain flare-up, you enter the information into Weather Flare (optional).
3.Weather Flare cross-references your symptoms against the weather forecast and looks for patterns. For example:
vDoes your pain get worse when it rains?
vDo your joints ache before a storm?
vDo you have stomach problems when it gets too hot?
4.Weather Flare monitors the weather in your location and sends you reminders, alerts and advice tailored to your weather triggers, allowing you to take action to minimise your pain. For those who don’t want to track their symptoms, Weather Flare will send general symptoms management tips based on the local forecast.
 
We have discovered over 50+ conditions that are affected by weather, we are carrying on from the University of Manchester’s Cloudy with a chance of pain study which showed 75% of people of people with an Arthritis were affected by the Weather. Weather Flare goes beyond this study and adds conditions such as Asthma, Diabetes and Migraines to name a few.In the UK there are About 15 million people in England have a long-term condition and they all fit can be helped by this application by to helping manage their condition. This app can be deployed worldwide via Google and Apple application stores to help up to a potential 2 billions people worldwide.

entityDescription:
Waag is a Future Lab for technology and society.
Technology is not neutral. Waag reinforces critical reflection on technology, develops technological and social design skills, and encourages social innovation.
Waag works in a trans-disciplinary team of designers, artists and scientists, utilising public research methods in the realms of technology and society. This is how Waag empowers as many people as possible to design an open, honest and inclusive future.
As of January 2021, Waag has been assigned the role of Future Lab by the Minister of Education, Culture and Science. This role can be described as follows: ‘A Future Lab is a centre for the future-oriented development of design and for the use of design and technology to solve social challenges.’ Waag was awarded this position due, in part, to the organisation’s 25 years of experience in design and artistic research in the field of technology and society.
Waag's activities primarily take place in research labs, where research and development are carried out on technological and social issues. As part of its public programme, Waag organises workshops, exhibitions, and debates. Additionally, Waag offers educational courses on creative technology and society with its Waag Academy programme. As Future Lab, Waag will be organising expeditions to planet B over the next four years, seeking an answer to the social, technological, and ecological challenges of our time.
