entityDescription:
Since 2014 weAR, an innovative Italian SME, supports companies that are investing in the digital transformation 4.0, proposing digital platforms that allow the creation of innovative user manuals, which can be viewed with smartphones, tablets and smartglasses, offering advanced user experiences thanks to augmented and mixed reality.One of the main use cases is related to the support for maintenance activities, which aim to keep (or restore) an object (plant, component, ...) in a state where it can perform its required function. A Maintenance, Repair and Operation (MRO) market that will reach 774 billion Dollars in 2020, according to a study by Technavio.To increase business productivity, reducing errors, and optimizing staff training, weAR created MARKO, a process-oriented and totally codeless cloud platform that leverages augmented reality as a visual support for maintenance tasks.MARKO has been adopted by several international players in the energy and manufacturing sector, with great benefits in the timing and accuracy of execution, simplicity of use and intuitiveness compared to traditional paper-based and on-screen instructions.Our customers’ request to have a "digital twin" of their products on which overlap layers of content (coming from multiple information sources, such as IoT and EPR systems) and develop predictive maintenance activities, prompted the team to look for new solutions to improve the platform's user experience and increase its potential..MARKO, proposed as SaaS, has been adopted by electric companies (ENEL Group), and manufacture and conbsultancies enterprises (Ericsson, Indra, DS Group).weAR’s Augmented and Mixed reality solution has been tested as POC by Terna Spa, Vodafone Italia, Italian Air Force (AMI) and Leonardo Group and several SME in Italy.
Products and Services
1)MARKO, one of the first content management system / browser for instruction manual in augmented reality, is used by several international Enterprises. The main user is ENEL Group, the largest electric utility in Italy and one of the biggest utility worldwide. MARKO is used in Italy, Brazil and Spain. The use of augmented/mixed reality is a form of disruptive innovation in B2B field. Mainly, weAR's platform has competitive advantage due to his user friendliness. KPI's obtained from the first panel of users demonstrated the validity of the tool, especially in the presence of unskilled personnel. This simplicity-in-use is one of the main winning feature for market penetration. After 1,5 years in development, MARKO tool was proposed to the market since the end of 2016. It has generated revenue for more 500k€ until mid 2020.
2)DIGITAL TWIN EXPERIENCE IN VIRTUAL, AUGMENTED AND MIXED REALITY
The digital twin is a virtual copy of a real item. Using a smarglass, user can manipulate digital twin with the same user experience of the real product.The digital twin allows user to better know the correct usage of a product,with a real feel experience also without the presence of the real item. In addition, it can record user behavior in order to improve design and avoiding misuseWith the digital twin, maintenance and repair operations are very simple to illustrate, with step by step procedures to follow in real time.IoT, Ai, big data can support predictive maintenance, with a dynamic digital twin suggesting the user the correct procedure to better keep the product at top performance.

description:
Biodiversity loss is happening at an accelerated rate, seeing more marine and land ecosystems affected by ocean acidification and human activities, as well as wildfires, flash floods, and natural disasters.
AVINTERRA team aims to act for the protection, restoration and promotion of sustainable use of Earth’s marine and terrestrial ecosystems, offering digital mapping consultancy services based on geospatial and Earth Observation technologies. We help and support local, regional, national and international authorities, as well as private businesses, to extract actionable information based on assets they possess. 
AVINTERRA offers further management consultancy services to respond to business strategy development, data management and community engagement for geo-related projects. Driven by the mission to shape an innovative, creative and sustainable world for the Next Generation, the AVINTERRA team creates and supports STEAM educational projects worldwide, delivering train-the-trainer courses that have the power to enhance career prospects for space and geospatial sectors. The Future We Want for everyone worldwide, needs to address the critical role the Earth’s Sustainability plays and how important it is to cross-collaborate for the Beauty of our planet. We use efficient scientific communication to deliver our ambitious goals.

description:
DTM since 1994 is operating in many industrial sectors: aerospace, biomedical, marine and automotive. The company was born in the late ‘90 as spin-off of Ferrari SpA Space Division (former Ferrari Engineering). All the design and development activities are carried out in Modena premises and laboratories where are available many tools and facilities for design, manufacturing and testing. 
DTM main core-business is the design, development and qualification of aerospace structures and GSE for satellites, launchers and ISS/sub-orbital flight experiments and infrastructures. DTM facilities include CAD, structural, thermal and CFD software tools, clean rooms, autoclave, tools and NDI/test equipments, TVCs, static and fatigue test jigs, shaker and acquisition systems.
entityDescription: DTM is an engineering company working since 1994 in design (3D, structural, thermal, CFD) and MAIT of aerospace structures for satellites (primary, secondary, tertiary structures and instrument mechanical parts) and launchers as well as their ground support equipments (mechanical, fluidic, thermal). DTM is also involved in the development of micro-gravity infrastructures and experiments for parabolic flights, sounding rockets and International Space Station. DTM facilities include autoclave, tools and test equipments for manufacturing, qualification and testing of composite and sandwich parts. DTM capabilities include design and MAIT of thermal control systems as well as Mechanical-GSE, MT-GSE (thermal vacuum chambers) and Fluidic-GSE with special reference to extra high purity systems. Several test facilities are available in the 1000 m2 integration areas available at DTM integration sites like vacuum thermal chambers (also for cryogenic tests), static and fatigue test jigs, shaker, ISO 6 and ISO 8 clean rooms, acquisition systems, fluidic testing apparatus. DTM is an accredited laboratory of Emilia Romagna High Technology Network. Our quality management system is certified according to UNI-EN-ISO-9001 and UNI-EN-9100 international aerospace standard.

The team inherits an experience of over 40 years of research in the development, production, characterization, management and use of metal and non-metal powders.

The company develops and produces highly innovative materials through mechanical, chemical and mechano-chemical activation. entityName: H-ION Kutató, Fejlesztő és Innovációs Kft.
entityDescription:
Since its establishment in 2011, our company has been engaged in materials science and technology R&D and innovation. The R&D and application of new and specialised materials and the technological development induced by industrial problems are together the basis for achieving good results.
Our scientific and engineering team is made up of young, talented scientists, engineers and experienced managers who take an innovative approach to solving unique frontier problems with a systems approach.
We have also taken our R&D results into the space sector, and with the help of our partners, we have tested special insulating materials in a real space environment on the ATL-1 2PQ satellite (5cmx5cmx10cm). We tested the insulation of on-board batteries during the 10-month orbital lifetime. In Hungary, this was the first privately built PQ satellite operating during its full orbital lifetime and the results were successful. It was the SMOG-P 1 PQ satellite and ours was the smallest operational, active smallest PQ satellite. The test of the insulators was successful, confirming the space qualification, and continuing the journey, further testing is currently underway aboard MRC-100. Several research and development projects are currently underway in the areas of special materials, energy storage and propulsion for 2PQ-16U scale applications.
Examples of our Science Department's areas of expertise in general and space:
- R&D of Li-ion and Na-ion batteries with increased volumetric energy density
- Li-ion and Li-ion based Li-ion and Li-ion based Li-ion alloys
- Development of nanoporous insulating materials for low and high temperature alumina applications
- Development of high efficiency thermoelectric materials
- Development of Cube satellite RCS actuator (0.1 - 1 N thrust) with water propellant
- Development of special heat-pipe solutions
- Hydrogen production, storage R&D
The main areas of expertise of our Technology Department are:
- Development of unique flow chemistry technologies,
- Custom equipment development up to TRL9
- Technology consulting, validation, feasibility studies, risk analysis,
- New generation energy storage systems,
In addition to our existing tasks, space and aerospace projects are playing an increasing role. This is another way of enriching the knowledge base of the international professional community in the long term.

description:
University College Dublin [UCD] is home to the UCD Centre for Space Research [C-Space: www.ucd.ie/space]. 
UCD C-Space is a university-wide centre for space-related research, innovation and education. 
Our purpose is to build partnerships that advance the use of space to address global scientific and societal challenges. 

We undertake internationally significant research in the following thematic areas: 
- Nanosatellites and Payloads [including EIRSAT-1 Ireland's first satellite]
- Space Structure Dynamics and Control 
- Earth Observation [data analysis and applications] 
- Ground- and Space-based Astrophysics
- Space Materials 
- Gamma-Ray Detectors 

We provide space-relevant university-based education and industry training courses [including Doing Business with ESA and Winning ESA proposals]. We further support industry through consultancy, collaborations, internships and access to facilities. 
C-Space builds national and global partnerships to deliver major space projects for Europe.
entityDescription: University College Dublin has its origins in the mid-nineteenth century under the leadership of the renowned educationalist John Henry Cardinal Newman. Since its foundation in 1854, the University has flourished and made a unique and substantial contribution to the creation of modern Ireland, based on successful engagement with Irish society on every level and across every sphere of activity. UCD is one of Europe's leading research-intensive universities; an environment where undergraduate education, masters and PhD training, research, innovation and community engagement form a dynamic spectrum of activity. The international standing of UCD has grown in recent years; it is currently ranked within the top 1% of institutions world-wide. UCD is also Ireland's most globally engaged university with over 30,000 students drawn from over 120 countries, and includes 5,500 students based at locations outside of Ireland. The University's main Dublin campus occupies an extensive parkland estate of more than 130 hectares and offers world-leading facilities including the UCD O'Brien Centre for Science, UCD Sutherland School of Law, UCD Lochlan Quinn School of Business and UCD Student Centre. As Ireland's largest university, with its great strength and diversity of disciplines, UCD embraces its role to contribute to the flourishing of Ireland; through the study and discussion of people, society, business, economy, culture, languages and the creative arts, as well as through research and innovation. The University's Strategy 2015-2020 outlines the objectives and major strategic initiatives set in place in order to accomplish UCD's mission and vision for this era.

entityDescription:
One3D s.r.o. is a Czech company that has been successfully operating on the Czech and international market. It offers its customers comprehensive support in the production of plastic and metal parts using SLS, SLM, DMLS, Polyjet, FDM and PU technologies in silicone molds.
The company's main specialization is the Selective Laser Sintering technology, which can be used for every phase of the product development cycle, from prototyping to the production of functional parts in piece or small series volumes. One of the main industries using SLS technology in the areas of rapid prototyping in the country is the automotive and aerospace industries. One3D therefore cooperates with leading companies in the field of automotive and aircraft technology and is one of the leaders in the market. Thanks to this company, designers and test engineers can have the entire product on the table in just a few days. In addition to the production itself, the company also provides a wide range of final surface treatments of parts, which are most used for prototype parts and components.

entityDescription:
Senso4s Company is a high-technology company creating advanced solutions for the global market, by merging different knowledge and experience. 
The heart of every modern device are the electronics which manage the processes of the device and help the device to communicate with users. In order to manage all these functionalities, the overall development must be based on a thorough analysis and on explicit goals as to the purpose that must be achieved and the technology that must be used. Our vast knowledge of PCB design and basic electronics offer us an opportunity to design complex systems based on internationally approved components and on the software developed by us due to which the devices are able to accommodate the users with an extensive range of functionalities.
Our team covers different aspects of product development. During the start-up stage, we acquire additional knowledge on planning activities and choosing the right actions for individual development stages. Due to our experiences, we are able to share our knowledge with other companies which are currently trying to combine high end products with new communication protocols. 
Telecommunications environment is one of the fastest developing fields. Quantity of data is growing constantly, and users are looking for ways to manage their data and to obtain a clearer picture. Globally, telecommunications companies must develop new ways of transmitting the data in the most efficient way. This progress has brought us to the point where we must study different protocols and communicate with different providers across the globe. Depending on the product and environment, we are able to choose the optimal communication protocol (LTE-M, NB IoT, Bluetooth, BLE, Wi-Fi etc.) and design the hardware and the software that is appropriated.
Company’s Vision: To become a leading development company in the field of sensor technology, for the general and the industrial environment.

Company’s Mission: To provide an overall solution and support for the customers who want to gain complete control over the processes in various environments.

Kind regards
Senso4s Team

Business Description: The limited liability company will offer bridging service – drone operators on one side, with the Air Navigation Service Providers on other delivering information of the current drone operations in the air to the air traffic controllers and vice versa delivering airspace information to the same operators so that they can comply in real time.
Company Background: Unmanned Systems Bulgaria is registered with the sole purpose to serve drone operators in Bulgaria and expand abroad. Started as a simple blog it now has significant presence in the social media. There is an expressed support from the national air navigation service provider, air force academy and the community itself.
Products/Services: Current drone flight approval and evaluation is frustrating both for authorities and drone operators as well. Every single flight plan consumes roughly 40 manhours to the authorities and spans within week or two limiting scalability. In future where 30000 flights are expected only above Sofia this process is more than archaic.
Fully digitalized cloud-based partially automated flight approvals and flight telemetry data sharing speeding the process to up to minutes relieving both the authorities and the operators. Two-way communication channel between authorities / air traffic controllers / drone operators in case of need. Security and Safety boost sharing flight data with whom has right to view it.
Technologies: A software product will be developed to serve as a UI/UX to the Bulgarian clients. This cloud-based service will be reached without limitation of devices and Operating Systems. However, we will claim intellectual rights on this development. As the time comes and the EU law is published, we intent to be the first to acquire Certification in accordance with this new U-space Implementing Act.
Our chosen law firm has already years of experience in IP cases and even more as being attorneys-at-law. Their law firm is very reputable in that regard. Once Unmanned Systems Bulgaria gets some traction some resources will be spent on registering a trademark.

entityDescription:
About Aerospace Propulsion Products B.V. (APP)
Aerospace Propulsion Products B.V. (APP) develops and manufactures advanced gas generator systems for a wide range of applications. Our gas generators produce either hot or cold gases and are used in demanding environments such as rocket engine ignition, turbo pump start systems, dust explosion suppression, parachute deployment systems, and medical oxygen generation.
Our History
APP was founded in 1985 by TNO, the Netherlands Organisation for Applied Scientific Research. Initially, the company focused entirely on the production of propellant for the igniters and starter systems of the Ariane 5 Vulcain rocket engine.
In 1995, Stork became a shareholder alongside TNO, enabling APP to expand its activities to the full production of Vulcain igniters and starter systems. Since then, APP has continuously broadened its expertise and product portfolio through the development and production of a wide variety of gas generator systems.
Today, APP is a wholly owned subsidiary of ArianeGroup SAS and continues to contribute to major European aerospace and industrial programs.
Our Products and Applications
APP has developed and produced systems for numerous high-profile programs and applications, including:
- Ignition systems for the Vinci upper-stage rocket engine

- Ignition systems for Prometheus and M10 rocket engines

- Igniters for the Vega launch vehicle first three stages (P80, Z23/Z40, and Z9)

- Fast gas generators for dust explosion suppression systems

- Parachute deployment devices for ExoMars and Space Rider missions

Our Organization
APP combines a straightforward and efficient organizational structure with highly specialized expertise. The company consists primarily of two core departments:
- Engineering

- Production

Today, APP employs around 45 highly skilled professionals, and we continue to grow as our activities expand.
Our Capabilities
APP offers complete in-house capabilities for:
- Technology development

- Engineering and design

- Qualification and testing

- Production and assembly

Our operations are performed according to the highest quality standards, including the stringent requirements applicable to the space industry. Safety is a key priority in both our product development and manufacturing processes, ensuring reliable and robust solutions for critical applications.

entityDescription:
Business Unit of Teledyne UK Limited. Based in the historic city of Lincoln UK, with a team of 55 staff the Teledyne Lincoln Microwave business unit pioneers the development and manufacture of innovative microwave technologies, specialising in delivering RF and Microwave components that meet demanding operation requirements. Our products have applications in the Defence, Communications, Space, Automotive and Instrumentation markets. Our research and development focusses on new generation microwave devices that exploit leading-edge physics, including quantum well and heterojunction structures fabricated to atomic layer precision.

description: Institute for Environmental Solutions (IES) is a non-for-profit research institute and an international network of scientists, artists, engineers and practitioners whose goal is to develop applied solutions to prevent the depletion of the Earth's resources and preserve nature's wonders for the enjoyment of future generations. We create ad hoc multidisciplinary teams to design and develop customized innovative environmental solutions. We employ modern technologies, reflective practice and multi-stakeholder involvement. IES has built an advanced airborne surveillance and environmental monitoring system named ARSENAL through which unique sets of data and images are obtained on the terrestrial, marine and freshwater ecosystems, their structure, chemical composition and spatial characteristics. The system is used to analyze the present, to uncover the past and to project the future. The main research themes of IES: mapping, detection and assessment of land cover/ land use, habitats of EU importance, invasive species, forest resources, forest vitality, and archaeological heritage; future satellite simulation; landscape planning and management; holistic assessment and restoration of aquatic ecosystems; mapping and assessment of waterbody depth and sediments; research of fish migration and natural reproduction; wildlife mapping and modeling.

entityDescription:
Our mission is to promote and inspire space-related education. There is enormous excitement and opportunities in space for schools to grasp in terms of related curriculum as well as hands-on space projects for students to be involved with. Space-related education connects curriculum from many areas such as STEM, Coding, Robotics, Trades, Physics, Design Thinking, Maker, Science, Math and more. Our initiative CyprusSpaceFoundationhopes to help bring those connections directly to students in classrooms across Cyprus by providing educators with new space-related projects and opportunities CyprusSpaceFoundation will work to grow and gain supporters and educators to bring exciting new space projects and online presentations for Cypriot students

CyprusSpaceFoundation was born in 2017 as school engineering club with the mission to explore open source space technologies and inspire and educate students to create and complete small space missions. The project was named Pascal Mission To space and was created by Elpidoforos Anastasiou an Information Technology Teacher and Space enthusiast. The space mission in 2017-2018 was for the students to investigate emerging technologies and develop and satellite simulation and create their own satellite station to receive the data, To achieve this , several experts were invited to educated the team ,moreover the students visited universities and research centers as part of the engineering club initiative to enable them to start thing like researches and develop the prototypes .7 months after the club was created in June 2018 the team successfully launch their prototype satellite using High Altitude balloon from the capital of Cyprus Nicosia with the help of the meteorology departments , the satellite traveled for 3 hours and riches 90.00 feet’s and was sending live meteorological data to the ground station using Lora Wan a technology commonly used for Iot .In editions students were able to predict using simulations software were the satellite was going to land 2 weeks before launch , this was a very difficult task due the special geographical location and military bases in almost 35% percent of the island that we had to avoid.

ADDITESS is a scientific, consulting, and research company whose purpose is to conduct theoretical and applied research and to produce studies, at a strategic and tactical level, on issues concerning Security policies, Border Management, Critical Infrastructure Protection, Transportation and Cargo Security, and also to develop state of the art applied Security Solutions hardware or software-based in the above-mentioned areas. ADDITESS also provides advisory, consulting, and solution services to various Government Organizations and to other Public and Private authorities in Cyprus, Europe or Worldwide, on these same issues.

ADDITESS invested in establishing the role of the company through strong participation in EU funded projects, FP7 and Horizon 2020, or various National R&D proposals in the fields of Security, ICT, Aeronautics (UAVs), Communications, Transportation and Environment. ADDITESS is strategically positioned between academia, SME and government, in Cyprus, equally benefiting from all sectors. Outcome of ADDITESS positioning has as a result research on needing areas providing innovative technological solutions with high readiness in applicability. Our company follows the guidelines of the ISO 9001:2015 standard of operations ensuring quality management regarding Consulting, Research and Development Services in Security and Information Technology Fields. ADDITESS is also the owner of a Facility Security Clearance Certificate from CYMOD for Handling EU Classified Information. ADDITESS is also own the ISO/IEC 27001 Information Security Management System.

description:
Baltic Institute of Advanced Technology (BPTI) is a private, high-tech oriented research institute based in Vilnius, Lithuania. BPTI was founded in 2008 and since then it focuses on creating and developing new technologies and providing R&D services to other companies. 

BPTI strength comes from the ability to gather interdisciplinary research teams which can provide efficient solutions to difficult problems. 

Main research topics for BPTI are focused around information technologies and high-tech electronics, we have experience in working within these fields: Radar and Wireless Front-End Systems, RF and mm-Wave measurements, military User experience (UX) and User Interface (UI) developments, virtual and augmented reality systems, Artificial Intelligence and its application in systems control, language technologies and text analytics, computer vision systems (processing, correction, compression, quality control, video analytics). 

In total BPTI employs over 40 people, most of which are involved in research and development.

entityDescription:
At HV Sistemas we are specialized on electronic product design and manufacturing, with three main business areas:

Space, Defense and Aeronautics Custom Equipment: Our extensive capabilities and experience in the conception, design, development, industrialization and manufacturing of electronic equipment enables us to provide particular solutions, particularly in the development of EGSEs for space applications. We have provided ground support equipment for the following programs: Sentinel-3, Seosar/PAZ, Seosat/Ingenio and PARIS. In the custom solutions field, we do not only provide the design, but we also have capabilities for prototyping and series manufacturing as well as to offer installation, system commiting and post-sales support services. Our customers range from OEM companies incorporating electronics inside their products to large engineering firms. Our customers include Jena-Optronik GmbH, Astrium CASA Espacio, Thales Alenia Space, Eurofighter and Indra, among others.

Radiocommunication equipment and accesories: Our main speciality is data transmission over radio, and from 1998 we are providing products and solutions in this field using private mobile radio and license-free radio. Our equipment is currently used in a wide range of applications, as for example large water supply networks management, fleet management, meteorological and environmental data adquisition or remote alarm and remote control systems. We also manufacture other radiocommunication oriented equipment, as voice scramblers and signalling devices.

entityDescription:
ASPIDA is a French company (SAS with a capital of 100 000 �) located near Lyon which has over 25 years’ experience in cleanrooms and containment laboratories. 
Specialised in the design, manufacture and installation of critical air systems, the key differentiators with ASPIDA products is that they are designed as deployable cleanroom or containment systems using either quick-fit/rigid (eg. TRUSS or REXROTH) or flexible/inflatable structures. 
ASPIDA’s solutions go from the highest levels of containment, such as for chemical weapons or class 3 & 4 pathogens (Ebola, Coronavirus, etc), to the highest levels of cleanliness, such as the integration of the InSight seismometer in an interplanetary protection program or the ISO 5 tent currently used by Airbus for the ExoMars project.Thanks to its experience in some of the world’s leading and most notorious projects, such as the Arch of Chernobyl, the Chemical Weapon dismantling facility SECOIA or the world-first genic therapy sterile hospital rooms for children at Paris Necker, the ASPIDA team has one objective : provide the right environment for the application.
This is achieved by using not only their pragmatic approach and experience in air movement systems, but also being able to use technologies that exist across different industries so as to bring a fully packaged solution to the final customer.

entityDescription:
The WAVE BUMPER is an innovative concept of climate change adaptation. It is the first removable, quickly deployable, seawall protection.
Privileged environments in which to live, coastlines are today the focus of many socio-economic assets and have in recent years united all those who wish to protect this exceptional environmental asset.
However, it has considerable assets in terms of lifestyle quality and economic attractiveness. Environmental criteria are evolving, in particular due to climate change. The potential increase in the sea level and increasing rainfall are leading to growing risks of erosion, flooding and marine submersion.
WAVE BUMPER is the answer to an international concern.
To answer this issue, we created the first removable self-ballasted seawall which can be installed in the event of weather alerts, then reused easily for a new weather hazard. This non-aggressive solution respects the ecology of exposed sites.
One of the innovations is a distinctive curve which absorbs the energy of the wave and sends it back towards the ocean.
The WAVE BUMPER curve limits overflow more efficiently than a system equipped with a vertical wall.
Climate change and its consequences in terms of erosion of the coastline and the risk of marine submersion require us to take a new integrated approach in coastal planning.
This crucial issue for the future of coastal areas and numerous associated activities, must be at the heart of action taken by the authorities.
Our technology can be included in all the coastal programs and action plans which encourage flexible management:
- Management of aquatic zones and flood protection (GEMAPI)
- Flood prevention action plans (PAPI)
- Prevention plans against the risk of marine submersion (PPRL)

entityDescription:
Humatects GmbH(HMT) is an IT company developing software and offering services for human-machine interaction (HMI) for safety critical as well as entertainment systems. The employees at HMT are experts in human factors engineering, artificial intelligence i.e. machine learning, human modelling i.e. Bayesian Networks, industrial design and software development.The companywas founded in 2014 by Dr. Andreas Lüdtke as a spin-off (situated in Germany) of the computer science research institute OFFIS.

HMT develops technologies that are targeted to tailoring interactive systems (like medical devises, systems for autonomous driving, training support systems, control room user interfaces, AR/VR applications for museums and tourism) to the needs of the individual end-user. Starting at OFFIS and continued at HMT, more than 15 years of scientific research on how humans interact with machines have been compiled in computational human models. Our human models are used to simulate, to understand and to predict user behavior and user needs in order to derive individualized support. In addition to the application of our own methods and technologies, we have extensive experience and knowledge in the application of common human factors methods and established standards (e.g. ).
This unique combination of our model-based approach with standardized procedures allows to use formal and objective human-centered metrics to ensure a very high user satisfaction that goes beyond the mere compliance with standards. We design and implement systems that are trustworthy, easy to understand, easy to use, and to which users feel personally attached.

entityDescription:
HEATSELF is an industrial SME specialised in the development and production of thermal solutions. 
HEATSELF offers around fifteen different types of self-regulating heating cable solutions for the terrestrial industry applications.
HEATSELF specialises in the transformation of plastic material into electric-powered elements able to emit calories. HEATSELF employs electrically conductive polymers able to emit heat using the surrounding temperature without using any electronic control system.The number of calories spread by the polymers made by HEATSELF depends on the temperature of the environment they are in or of the support on which they are fixed. The material used to for the HEATSELF products is thermo-sensitive and is able to dilate or contract depending on the surrounding temperature. The image below illustrates the power dissipated by the HEATSELF polymers depending on the temperature.
This result is obtained thanks to HEATSELF’s know-how in the production of polymers with an electrical impendence varying with temperature.

HEATSELF activities focus on the production of heating elements used to regulate the temperature of industrial equipment. The advantage of using HEATSELF’s technology for industrial applications is the use of materials able to adjust the amount of energy needed to maintain industrial processes.Today HEATSELF sells more 100km by year of self regulating heating cable with PTC effect for industry.

HEATSELF certificate ISO 9001 (V2015) demonstrates the HEATSELF capacity to manage Research projetcs.
Another HEATSELF activity is the development of new PTC (Positive Temperature Coefficient) materials for cutting edge applications.
R&D activities represent more than 50% of HEATSELF’s activity. HEATSELF is able to formulate polymers on a dedicate line. HEATSELF can produce strips, wires, cables on two other production lines. A production line will be tailored to the needs of ELECTRAS. In order to monitor R&D and production, HEATSELF set up an electro-thermal characterization laboratory and a performance test bench to assess products over time. HEATSELF now also has the necessary tools to simulate temperature variations between -30°C and +50°C in a 16 m³ climatic chamber.
HEATSELF is also involved in the development of solutions for the automotive industry.

entityDescription:
RedCat Devices (RCD) is a fabless semiconductor company devoted to design semiconductor memories and analog devices for aerospace and nuclear science taking the best from standard and well consolidated CMOS technologies using radiation hardening by design (RHBD) proprietary methodologies to enhance resistance both to total ionizing dose (TID) and single event effects (SEE). The expertise of RCD is focused on semiconductor memories and ADCs/DACs coming from its founders whose experience have been matured in the academy (University of Pavia, University of Milan) and large corporates (ST Microelectronics).
RCD is based in Milano and its capability spreads from project management to physical simulation and layout design of complete silicon devices for customers who can be helped on silicon process choosing too. RCD works mainly on CMOS processes with different fabs like X-FAB, TowerJazz, IHP, LFoundry and others.
RCD is organized in three units: 1) APG, Analog Product Group, 2) MPG, Memory Product Group, 3) SSG, Scientific Software Group. APG and MPG are devoted to the development of rad-hard products (ADCs, DACs, SRAM, NVMs), SSG supports APG and MPG in software maintenance and development of internal tools (rad-hard libraries, testing tools, etc…) required for all phases of chip development.
RCD designs everything from scratch starting from the selected silicon foundry PDK (Process Design Kit), from I/O up to the single logic port, making leverage on more than ten years of rad-hard developments in several research projects (RiFLASH, RAMSES, CISSA, ATENA, SkyFlash, RAISP, R2RAM, EuroSRAM4Space) and customer oriented case studies.
RCD is member of AIPAS association (www.aipas.it).

Company Profile METAPROJECTS

METAPROJECTS Private Research Body was born in 2007 on the initiative of a group of engineers and professionals from the Bolognese industry. It mainly operates in research and technological innovation for electronic engineering. The advanced skills acquired in motion control and power electronics, in sensors, in miniature GPS tracking systems for wildlife trackers, in radio frequency and IoT, were the basis for the implementation of the EXADRONE project http://www.exadrone.it/ in partnership with ENEA Brasimone Research Center.

In the new Automation and Control Laboratory at the ENEA Brasimone Research Center https://www.enea.it/it/centro-ricerche-brasimone/ , mechatronics design relies on skills in technical physics, aerodynamic design with CFD simulation (Computational Fluid Dynamics), advanced electronic design, and advanced SAPR (Remote Piloted Aircraft System) are implemented for monitoring of relevant structures in reinforced concrete and / or nuclear sites.
METAPROJECTS has been active since 2018 in the research and application of "metamaterials" for power radio frequency.

To achieve and support the research objectives, METAPROJECTS carries out electronic design activities with predictive simulation, hardware - firmware and software development, product industrialization, certification support.

entityDescription:
Founded in 2014 as a spin-off from the University of Trieste, PICOSATS is a company committed to the research, development and commercialisation of cutting-edge telecommunications systems for the small satellite market and beyond.
The increasing use of small satellites in low orbits for satellite communications and the spectrum congestion has demanded the development of high-frequency, miniaturized telecommunications systems, and PICOSATS has seized the opportunity to enter this rapidly expanding market. PICOSATS is currently testing in an operational environment two transponders designed for CubeSats and small satellites, one in K/Ka and one in Ku band for applications in LEO and GEO. The development of these products makes use of the know-how acquired by the company through various opportunities provided by the European and Italian Space Agencies. Along with the transponders, PICOSATS has also developed K/Ka band and Ku-band horn antennas, and a V-band double reflector antenna for small satellites. 
Products:

- K/Ka and Ku-band transponder. A miniaturized non regenerative transponder designed for CubeSat and Small Satellites, with a volume of 1 U and a mass of 1.2 kg. The transponder is available in the K/Ka-band and in the Ku-band and it allows two signal bandwidths, 400 kHz or 700 kHz. Telemetry and Telecommand functions are available over the common standards.

- Modem and transceivers. A miniaturized modem/SDR designed for CubeSat and Small Satellites for LEO and GEO applications. With a volume < 0.5 U and a mass < 500 g, it can reach up to4 Gbps in transmission and 1 Gbps in reception making it unique in size and performance ratio. 
- K/Ka and Ku-band horn antennas. BEAMSAT is a horn antenna available in two different bands, Ka-band and Ku-band.With a volume of 2 U, BEAMSAT offers excellent matching and sufficient gain to cover missions both in GEO and LEO.

- V-band ADE antenna. The antenna is an ADE type double reflector operating in the 59.3-71 GHz frequency range. The gain ranges between 30 and 32.5 dB. The antenna fabrication process involves both CNC and L-PBF manufacturing techniques giving the antenna a mass of about 82 g and a high compactness (occupied volume < 0.5 U).
- K, Ka and X band patch antennas. The high-gain Ka-band 8x8 patch antenna, is designed for nano, micro and small satellites. It can be supplied with or without an enclosure weighing 75 g (with enclosure), offering a simple and efficient mounting solution to the satellite’s external structure occupying less than 1 U surface. Its peak gain of 22 dBi and its compact design make it ideal for a wide range of missions ensuring high data rate transmission with no compromises.

entityDescription:
The "Galliera Hospitals" Institution (established as Opera Pia De Ferrari Brignole Sale) owes its origins to the munificence of the Duchess of Galliera who had it built between 1877 and 1888. Presidential Decree of the Council of Ministers 14/07/1995 established it as a high-specialisation hospital of national importance.

In line with its guiding principles and the most recent acquisitions in the area of health care, the Galliera is characterised as the realisation of a hospital model open to the territory and to citizens. It is capable of responding effectively to health care demand with a capacity of 450 beds (data updated at 31.12.2018
www.galliera.it/galliera-live).
The health care aspect, from a standpoint of an integrated diagnostic-therapeutic-rehabilitative process, scientific research, training, and technological and organisational innovation, constitutes the strategic core of activities performed daily by each of the professionals in their own sphere of competence.

The reorganisation process, defined as "for the intensity of care", was implemented in 2013. This is a model that provides a more effective and efficient management of hospital care. The innovative health care organisation involves taking charge of the patient in homogeneous areas which accommodate the patient on the basis of "the intensity" of the case and, therefore, the level of health care complexity:First Level- High Intensity(Pav. mezzanine floor A), an organisational model inaugurated in December 2018: intensive and sub-intensive hospitalisation (resuscitation, Coronary Intensive Care Unit [UTIC], Post-Operative Intensive Therapy [TIPO]) and Stroke Centre;
Second Level- Average Intensity: acute-care hospitalisation (medicalandsurgicalarea);
Third Level- Area for Fragile Patients: hospitalisation for post-acute care patients (stabilisation and rehabilitation) and theACI(Nursing Care Area) launched in May 2017 with 15 beds. The activation of the nurse-managed inpatients area was established by the Galliera Hospitals Institution, in accordance with the regional guidelines of the Decree of Regional Government No. 328 of 28/04/2017, which also envisages institutional cooperation between the Galliera Hospitals Institution and Azienda S.P.E. Brignole, according to nurse-managed areas of 12 beds in order to facilitate ongoing hospital and regional health care.
Inpatient areas work alongside theServices areawhich includes departments dedicated to diagnostic imaging, laboratories and genetics.The hospital is also equipped with a latest-generation Technological Medical Centre with 1 PET/CT scanner, 3 CT scanners, 2 Magnetic Resonance Imaging machines, 2 Linear Accelerators, and 1 MID (Metal Iron Detector).

TheItalian National Registry of Bone Marrow Donors- I.B.M.D.R. is owned by the Galliera (I.B.M.D.R.).

One of the important projects which the Genoese hospital is currently engaged in concerns the construction of aNew Hospital. An innovative facility equipped with large diagnostic outpatients and areas dedicated to hospitalisation (intensity of care), technological and "green" levels (at low environmental impact, with reduced pollutant emissions and energy consumption). The historic building, which dates back to 1888, will be transformed into a multi-centre hub with areas dedicated to administration and research.

entityDescription:
Allerayde SAB Oy (ASAB) is an SME developing emergency solutions in anaphylaxis, starting with AAA Alert, a GNSS enabled automatic emergency service summoning device based on GNSS (Galileo).
In t he 2020 Galileo Masters competition, ASAB was the Finnish Regional winner with "Saving Lives and Optimising Patient Outcome with Galileo" and a My Galileo Solution finalist with "Improving Anaphylaxis Management With AAA Alert Using Galileo".
ASAB has completed proof of concept on the AAA Alert device and has developed a working prototype.
The objective is to move to a final product and launch in key European markets by the end of 2021 early 2022.
Further product development is now underway to develop a drone based solution in medical emergencies based on GNSS (Galileo).
On triggering a field based device a drone will be auto summoned to deliver the required emergency back up (such as an adrenaline auto-injector).
The work already performed by ASAB, in co-operation with GSI Limited, will be used in the new project with the addition of expertise from Krattworks (drone specialist), Estonia to deliver a new concept in emergency medical services which will save lives and money.

By participating in high-profile projects with ESA and the EU, Cloud Signals ensures that its solutions are not only innovative but also aligned with the latest industry standards and requirements.
Cloud Signals generates revenue through various streams, including project management, technology implementation, and product development services. The company supports its clients from the initial concept stage through to the successful market introduction of their products, ensuring a comprehensive and seamless experience.

entityDescription: The Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft zur Förderung der angewandten Forschung e.V. (FhG) is a link between science and industry, that is between the research and the application of its results. It was founded in Munich in 1949 as a non-profit registered association. The organization takes its name from Joseph von Fraunhofer (1787-1826), the successful Munich researcher, inventor and entrepreneur. The Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft is an autonomous organization with a decentralised organisational structure, which currently maintains 60 research institutes and a patent office in locations throughout Germany. Whilst the administrative headquarters are in Munich, the legally non-independent research institutes operate from different locations in 15 of the German Länder, where they carry out their respective work in close partnership with industry. A staff of approximately 18.000, the majority of whom are qualified scientists and engineers, work with an annual total budget of about 1.65 billion Euro. Today Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft is the leading organization of institutes of applied research and development in Europe. The employees carry out research and development projects on a contract basis on behalf of industry, the service sector and government. Future-oriented strategic research commissioned by the government and public authorities are carried out with the aim of promoting innovations in key technologies with an economic and social relevance in the next five to ten years. Working within the framework of the European Union's research and technological development programs, the Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft collaborates in industrial consortia on technical issues ultimately destined to improve the competitiveness of European industry. Commissioned by customers in industry, Fraunhofer scientists provide rapid, economical and immediately applicable solutions. Work focuses on specific tasks across a wide spectrum of research fields including communications, energy, microelectronics, manufacturing, transport and the environment. When required, several institutes collaborate on an interdisciplinary basis to develop system solutions with a wide range of applications. The clients receive advanced technical know-how and very exclusive services.

description:
Lens R&D is a Dutch SME specialized in high reliability Sunsensors for space applications.

The company has a limited offering of analogue fine Sunsensors that are optimised for volume manufacturing and offer some unique properties not to be found in any competing product.
The sensors are designed to allow the volume production required for high reliability constellations.

The BiSon64-ET is an ESA ESCC qualified product that has the widest temperature range available known to date. -125°C to +125°C
The BiSon64-ET-B is the only ESA ESCC qualified Sunsensor with an integrated baffle and based on the BiSon64-ET
The MAUS Sunsensor is the first true radiation hardened Cubesat Sunsensor available worldwide.

Currently the company is also leading the design and development of the first radiation hardened single chip true digital Sunsensor that is expected to be affordable.

entityDescription:
The roots of the Estonian Aviation Academy (EAVA) go back to 1993 and since then we have trained aviation specialists for all main branches of the industry – airline management, aircraft piloting, air traffic control, aircraft maintenance and communication, navigation, and surveillance systems (CNS). We are certified by the Ministry of Education and Research and by the Estonian CAA, because training corresponds to both higher education requirements and EASA requirements. In order to become a full-time student at the Estonian Aviation Academy, one needs to possess a diploma of completed secondary education. After graduation, the students will receive a BSc degree. In addition to the knowledge and skills required for the BSc diploma, the toolbox of the fresh specialist may include professional qualifications as per EASA regulation, in the above-mentioned areas. EAVA currently has close to 60 employees, with over half of them directly involved with student instruction (including 16 dedicated faculty members). On average, about 60 students enrol in full-time studies every year, distributed across our four main full-time study programmes (delivered mainly in Estonian). Additionally, there are attractive options beyond the regular programmes. As a bright example, EAVA (in cooperation with Magnetic MRO, a maintenance organisation with a global reach) is providing a workplace-based aircraft maintenance technician training programme, which has recently received a quality award from the European Commission. EAVA has recently passed the regular institutional accreditation process, the issued accreditation is valid until January 2024. On 7 May, a cooperation agreement was signed between the Estonian Aviation Academy and the International Air Transport Association (IATA), making the Academy the first IATA Authorized Training Center in Estonia. This autumn, EAVA will launch a 3-year Commercial Aviation Management (CAM) programme, with English as the language of instruction. 10-15 top-qualifying students will be invited to join the programme each year.
Although EAVA is small in numbers, our professional scope is wide and strategic plans for the upcoming years are ambitious, including developments regarding UAS, UTM, U-Space, digitalisation in aviation, as well as increasing our international presence.

In addition to the knowledge and skills required for the BSc diploma, the toolbox of the fresh specialist may include professional qualifications as per EASA regulation, in the above-mentioned areas. EAVA currently has close to 60 employees, with over half of them directly involved with student instruction (including 16 dedicated faculty members). On average, about 60 students enrol in full-time studies every year, distributed across our four main full-time study programmes (delivered mainly in Estonian). Additionally, there are attractive options beyond the regular programmes. As a bright example, EAVA (in cooperation with Magnetic MRO, a maintenance organisation with a global reach) is providing a workplace-based aircraft maintenance technician training programme, which has recently received a quality award from the European Commission. EAVA has recently passed the regular institutional accreditation process, the issued accreditation is valid until January 2024. On 7 May, a cooperation agreement was signed between the Estonian Aviation Academy and the International Air Transport Association (IATA), making the Academy the first IATA Authorized Training Center in Estonia. This autumn, EAVA will launch a 3-year Commercial Aviation Management (CAM) programme, with English as the language of instruction. 10-15 top-qualifying students will be invited to join the programme each year.
Although EAVA is small in numbers, our professional scope is wide and strategic plans for the upcoming years are ambitious, including developments regarding UAS, UTM, U-Space, digitalisation in aviation, as well as increasing our international presence.

description:
NHAZCA (Natural HAZards Control and Assessment), Spin-off Company of “Sapienza” University of Rome, is an international leader in the analysis and monitoring of natural hazards and large infrastructures for the management and mitigation of risks. 

Through innovative technologies such as the Terrestrial (TInSAR) and Satellite (DInSAR & A-DInSAR) SAR Interferometry, NHAZCA is able to perform the measurement and the control of surface displacements of the ground and structures with millimeter accuracy. 

NHAZCA has also developed the PhotoMonitoring technology which allows to monitor with extreme precision, thanks to specific hardware and software, changes and surface movements of structures and terrain through the use of images acquired from different platforms (terrestrial, aerial, satellite) and sensors (optical, multispectral, infrared, radar).
entityDescription: NHAZCA is a spin-off company of Sapienza Università di Roma providing innovative services and consultancies addressed to entities in charge of land management and planning, oil&gas companies, mining companies, large infrastructure companies and entities in charge of conservation of architectural heritages. NHAZCA takes advantage of a large network of partners from both the research and industrial fields such as international firms dealing with structural monitoring and geophysics like IMG S.r.l. Services and consultancies provided by NHAZCA are based on innovative techniques customizable to address customers needs. Among the main solutions provided by NHAZCA, the following can be mentioned: i) real time displacement monitoring of both natural and manmade elements by Terrestrial SAR Interferometry; analysis of past and future displacement of both large and small areas by Satellite SAR Interferometry; iii) analysis of the thermal behaviour of rock masses and concrete walls by Infrared Thermography; iv) numerical simulation of landslides, avalanches and floods by innovative proprietary models. Furthermore, thanks to the strong technical expertise of its employers, NHAZCA organizes national and international courses for the spreading of new technologies for the analysis and the control of natural and anthropic hazards.

entityDescription:
Semmelweis EGYETEM University is a leading institution of higher education in Hungary and the Central European region within the area of medicine and health sciences. Its main commitment is based on the integrity of education, research and healing, which make Semmelweis University an internationally renowned centre of knowledge.As a specialist university, it holds a unique place within the country; its prominent role is demonstrated by the fact that approximately 42 percent of Hungary’s doctors, 70 percent of its dentists, 50 percent of its pharmacists and 27 percent of its health care professionals are Semmelweis graduates.A truly international community, programmes are offered in three languages (Hungarian, English, German), and foreign students account for nearly a third of the around 11,000 students studying at the University’s six faculties.

In addition to teaching, Semmelweis University is the largest provider of health care services in Hungary. Even though practical teaching takes place at the university’s clinics and hospitals, they provide the highest quality patient care services at the same time. Most of the departments cater for the most serious cases and patients requiring complex treatment, thus making the university a national health care provider.

Research, development, and innovation comprise an important part of the University’s three-fold mission. The target of research at the university are early diagnostics and therapy, disease prevention and active ageing. Currently, there are 300 research groups at the university including 31 international and 94 Hungarian research grants. Many of its professors are members of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, with close collaboration between the two institutions in numerous areas. Semmelweis University received the prestigious Research University title for the second time in 2013.

Semmelweis University is an employer of nearly 8,500 employees and is involved in higher education vocational training, specialist postgraduate training, higher education vocational training, the cultivation of the next generation of scientists, and nurturing talent. The University organises international conferences and is represented on numerous international scientific boards. Its academic reputation is well-regarded around the world.

description:
STAR-Dundee is a leading supplier of spacecraft on-board data-handling technology with expertise in SpaceWire and SpaceFibre technology. We supply a comprehensive range of SpaceWire and SpaceFibre test and development equipment, and IP cores to the international aerospace industry.
Our highly experienced engineers were instrumental in the development of SpaceWire, writing the ECSS standard with inputs from international spacecraft engineers. Our SpaceWire IP is now widely used and integrated in spaceflight systems monitoring the Earth, exploring our Solar System, studying the universe and supporting commercial space applications.
Our engineers have led the research, development and standardisation of SpaceFibre, the next generation of SpaceWire. SpaceFibre is a substantial leap forward, offering much higher data rates, quality of service, fault detection, isolation and recovery, deterministic data delivery, low latency time-synchronisation and event signalling. SpaceFibre is backwards compatible with SpaceWire at the packet level allowing simple interconnection of SpaceWire devices into a SpaceFibre network.
We have worked on many ESA projects since our formation in 2002, most recently leading the development of a SpaceFibre Interface Chip.
entityDescription: STAR-Dundee is an aerospace engineering company focused on spacecraft on-board data-handling and processing technology. The company delivers a comprehensive range of test and development equipment, chip designs and IP cores to the world’s space agencies and international aerospace industry. STAR-Dundee is a world leader in SpaceWire and SpaceFibre technology. SpaceWire is a spacecraft on-board data-handling network which connects instruments to the mass-memory, data processors and control processors. SpaceWire has some specific characteristics that make it ideal for many space missions: high-speed, low-power, simplicity, relatively low implementation cost, and architectural flexibility. SpaceFibre is a multi-Gbits/s, on-board network technology for spaceflight applications, which runs over electrical or fibre-optic cables. It complements the capabilities of SpaceWire: improving the data rate by a factor of 10, reducing the cable mass by a factor of two and providing quality of service (QoS) and fault detection, isolation and recovery (FDIR) capabilities.

entityName: LABORATORIO DI MONITORAGGIO E MODELLISTICA AMBIENTALE PER LO SVILUPPO SOSTENIBILE - LAMMA
entityDescription:
On 20 December 2007, the Region of Tuscany, the Italian Research Council and the Foundation for Climate and Sustainability established the LaMMA Consortium - Environmental Modelling and Monitoring Laboratory for Sustainable Development, which is incorporated, and autonomous in terms of administration, organisation and accounts (Regional Law n°. 35 dated 23/02/2005).
The Consortium was born out of the project "Laboratorio di Meteorologia Modellistica Ambientale" (LaMMA), which was in turn formed in 1997 by the Region of Tuscany (General Direction for Economic Development, Department of Production Activities) in cooperation with the Italian Research Council (Institute of Biometeorology), with the aim of creating a point of contact between officialdom, the bodies of scientific and technological excellence, industry and the various public services.
Its main offices are hosted at the premises of IBIMET, in the Sesto Fiorentino Research Zone (Florence), with two other satellite offices located in:
- Livorno, the centre for marine meteorology and modelling, serving maritime transport and coastal production businesses;
- Grosseto, the centre for the study of soil erosion and water resources.
The LaMMA Consortium performs two types of closely interrelated activities: technical services, and comprehensive research and innovation activities, thus constituting a centre of excellence.
The main sectors in which the LaMMA Consortium specialises are meteorology, climatology, geographic information systems (GIS) and geology. The Consortium has also acquired considerable experience in the field of atmospheric pollutant dispersion modelling, anemological studies for the purposes of exploiting wind energy, marine and oceanographic modelling, monitoring of pollutants and the state of health of the sea, and monitoring of vegetation.
The research projects and technical services developed by the consortium often involve the use of territorial information systems for the management of resources and environmental risks. We use advanced modelling, and process data from a wide range of sources, but principally from satellite.

entityName: Global Open Data for Agriculture and Nutrition (GODAN)
entityDescription:
The Global Open Data for Agriculture and Nutrition (GODAN) initiative seeks to support global efforts to make agricultural and nutritionally relevant data available, accessible, and usable for unrestricted use worldwide. The initiative focuses on building high-level policy, and public and private institutional support for open data.
The initiative encourages co-operation among existing agriculture and open data activities, bringing stakeholders together to solve long-standing global problems. On a practical level, GODAN lends its expertise to advising on open data policy and funding proposals and, where appropriate, submitting joint proposals with members and partners. GODAN is in a position to use its credibility and expertise to support initiatives that aim to make positive impact in the fields of agriculture and nutrition through the use of open data, helping advise on applications, assembling partner network technical, policy and legal expertise, and acting as a facilitator.
Open access to research, and open publication of data, are vital resources for food security and nutrition; driven by farmers, farmer organisations, researchers, experts, policy makers, governments, and other private sector and civil society stakeholders participating in "innovation systems" and along value chains. Lack of institutional, national, and international policies and openness of data limit the effectiveness of agricultural and nutritional limiting research potential and slowing the introduction of innovations in to the market.
Making open data work for agriculture and nutrition requires a shared agenda to increase the supply, quality, and interoperability of data, alongside action to build capacity for the use of data by all stakeholders.

The GODAN initiative is a voluntary alliance of partners brought together around a shared purpose. The initiative welcomes all those who share this purpose to join as partners and to participate in shaping co-ordinated activities that can deliver on the potential of open data for agriculture and nutrition.

entityDescription:
DataReady exists to help the sustainable development and humanitarian sectors navigate the complexities of data governance. As a result, we can better understand, apply and track the value that data generates for society as a whole.
Around the world, policymakers are engaged in a balancing act between the benefits of data use, individuals’ rights and ethical considerations. In many parts of the world, principles and laws informed by the public and social conventions are desperately needed to inform this balancing act.
Within private companies, non-governmental and civil society organisations, the need to know how data use should be balanced against possible risks and rights is now a management issue. It requires executive attention and robust data management strategies and policies.
These issues aren’t just important for our clients and partners, but for society as a whole. There is significant potential for data to improve the quality and effectiveness of development and humanitarian support that people receive. Moreover, when properly managed and made accessible, data can help empower people, combat mis- and dis-information, and improve trust in public bodies.

entityDescription:
Geoprospectors is one of the leading suppliers of Electrical Conductivity (EC) soil sensors for precision farming. The flagship product Topsoil Mapper is a contact less sensor using electromagnetic induction and was especially developed for the use in agriculture. It can easily be mounted on a tractor or a pickup and can be used in any weather or field condition. The collected data (on soil texture, water content and compaction) are processed in real time over the cloud and provide valuable information about agricultural soils in the form of management zone maps. The resulting knowledge can be used in real time to improve and automate processes such as soil sampling or tillage operations.
All maps can be imported into common farm management tools. The
Topsoil Mapper is designed for easy application without expert knowledge. The entire data acquisition and data evaluation is therefore completely autonomous.

Our mission is to develop powerful and effective strategies, processes, and tools, in order to:
- Facilitate knowledge and technology transfer between organizations
- Convert knowledge into innovative products and services

In this process, we aim for ecologically and socially balanced and economically viable solutions with a global perspective.
Founded as the Center for Central and Eastern Europe MOEZ in 2006, the institute consolidated its expertise and range of services in internationalization and the knowledge economy under a new name in 2015, becoming the Fraunhofer Center for International Management and Knowledge Economy IMW.

entityName: NTUA - Laboratory of Hydrology and Water Resources Development (HWRM)
entityDescription: The Laboratory of Hydrology and Water Resources Development (HWRM) of the Department of Water Resources Management and Environmental Engineering of the School of Civil Engineering is a centre of excellence on water resources and environmental management with an active role at national and European levels. Of interest to HWRM is the domain of hydroinformatics and the design and modelling of complex water systems. HWRM is actively involved in stochastic hydrological analysis and simulation, water resources assessment, extreme event modelling (floods, droughts) and assessment of their consequences, climate and its interactions with water, development of advanced machine learning analytics and multi-objective optimization models, critical water infrastructure protection, cyber-physical security for water systems, water in the circular economy, reuse and recycling and water-energy systems. Of particular interest to the Lab are issues of immersive visualisation of model results for improved decision making. HWRM is a member of several European Networks, such as Watershare and Water Europe and is an active participant in EU R&D developing research and innovation services within H2020, EDA and Horizon Europe.

entityName: RIF Institut für Forschung und Transfer e.V.
entityDescription:
RIF Institute for Research and Transfer in Dortmund was founded in 1990 by university lecturers from different technology oriented university areas united as "Dortmund’s Initiative for computer-integrated manufacture (RIF e.V.)" to stimulate the transfer of research. 
As one of North Rhine-Westphalia “Johannes Rau research institutes”, RIF progresses interdisciplinary understandings of basic research to practically useful methods and improvements for companies. In the area of robotics RIF puts the latest research findings from simulation and virtual reality technology into products. Findings from microstructure technology, material technology and –testing support the improvement and sustainable design of products. Innovative tools from quality management, ergonomics and logistics, as well as automation-related technical solutions help companies in various industries to improve their productivity, quality of products and to reduce production costs. The institute’s holistic approach is completed by projects in the field of industrial marketing, innovative controlling concepts and modern methods of personnel development as well as change management. Furthermore, RIF is founding member of a nationwide, cross-industry network with more than 60 German extramurally, non-profit research institutes united by the membership in the “Konrad Zuse-Forschungsgemeinschaft”. RIF employs 130 scientific staff in the office close to the Technology Park Dortmund in Joseph-von-Fraunhofer-Straße 20.

entityDescription:
NEIKER-BRTA a technological center specialized in the research and creation of innovative solutions for the agri-food and forestry sectors. As an entity under the Department of Economic Development and Infrastructure of the Basque Government,NEIKER works to bring knowledge and value to these sectors, developing new technologies aimed at improving productivity and management of farms, to meet the requirements of quality and safety that the agri-food industry and the final consumer demand.
To achieve this, it maintains a proactive dialogue with the different stakeholders and collaborates in the resolution of the challenges of the primary sector and agrifood companies, among which are: 
the improvement of the profitability and sustainability of the agro-livestock farms.
the generation of new productive activities that create wealth and employment.
the control of food security.
the reduction of the impact of global warming.
All this working in terms of scientific excellence. We train professionals recognized by the international scientific community, capable of generating knowledge that contributes to improving the competitiveness and sustainability of the agri-food sector. We aim to become a global reference in innovation and contribute to the dissemination of knowledge through scientific publications, the participation of our researchers in forums and congresses and the organization of dissemination days.

GeoKapti was established in The Netherlands in 2019 specializing in scientific computing, mathematical modeling, data science and artificial intelligence. We implement our solutions in the form of highly specialized software products to solve challenging problems. Our experience includes: 
* Big data cloud environment for processing, visualizing and analyzing TROPOMI (Sentinel-5P) atmospheric composition data. 
* Co-development of the EUCLID Space Telescope Attitude/Orbit/Control System Software. 
* Development of the GOCE Satellite Data Processor & Toolbox to analyze and calculate quantities for applications in Geodesy, Oceanography and Solid Earth Physics.
* Command and Data Handling communication software and protocols for nanosats and cubesats. 
* Agricultural monitoring platforms using Earth Observation data (Sentinels-2) for european investment funds and seed exporters in South America.
* Countrywide Damage assessment for the Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources of El Salvador after Hurricane Amanda (2020) using SAR (Sentinel-1) 
* Artificial intelligence for cloud detection in optical satellites and land classification for multispectral EO data.
* Plasma Leak detection algorithms for the ITER Tokamak plasma confinement chamber.
* Training and courses in Data science and Machine Learning.

entityDescription:
Eurisy is a non-profit association founded in 1989 by Hubert Curien, then France’s Minister of Education.
Eurisy’s unique membership structure include most space agencies or governmental offices in charge of space affairs in Europe, and international organisations dealing with space matters. Eurisy’s unique membership structure of institutional organisations acting collectively as a non-governmental, non-profit organisation, guarantees Eurisy’s independence and neutrality – therefore the valuable legitimacy needed when facilitating cooperation across professional sectors.
 
The mission of Eurisy is to bridge space and society. To fulfil its scope, Eurisy stimulate and support dialogue and collaboration between public institutions at any level, SMEs, industry and academia from the space and non-space sectors. The goal is to build solid relations with communities, new to space, encouraging early adopters to share experiences creating a common ground for professionals from different backgrounds. 
Aiming at maximising the impact of space-derived innovation and the resulting benefits for society, as well as economy and environment, Eurisy developed a User Programme implemented in several ways:
- by raising public awareness on the benefits of satellite applications, in particular deriving from technology innovation in satellite navigation, communication and Earth Observation;
- by surveying users’ needs in their working context and provide our Members, partners and decision makers at local, national and European level with bottom-up feedback;
- by supporting the take-up of satellite applications and by facilitating dialogue between professional end-user communities and the space community.
 
Eurisy has an extensive experience in engaging with user communities to promote the benefits of satellite-based applications. In over 30 years, Eurisy has built a vast network among space and non-space professional communities. Eurisy design and manage events as platforms to teach, learn and innovate across sectors. Eurisy adds value to innovation projects by involving users, championing their needs and facilitating the dialogue between them and the space stakeholders. Eurisy has been working also to provide its Members and decision makers with specific policy recommendations deriving from research work based on quantitative and qualitative analysis and processing of large surveys’ data as well as individual interviews.

description:
Ceit is a private multidisciplinary non-profit RTO closely connected to TECNUN, the School of Engineering of the University of Navarra (Spain). Its missions are to provide industry with services through the development of technical research projects and to promote the dissemination of knowledge through the training of young researchers and PhD students and scientific publications. Regarding our first mission, more than 100 research projects between TRL4 and TRL7 are carried out at Ceit per year. Moreover, Ceit has participated in 15 FP6 projects, 32 FP7 projects, 18 RFCS projects, 3 LIFE projects and 48 H2020 projects, out of which 12 have been coordinated. In terms of our second mission, in the last 5 years Ceit has produced more than 30 PhD thesis per year, published 100 papers in scientific journals, and participated in 80 international conferences. Since 1996 Ceit has created 15 technology-based spin-offs, which currently employ more than 300 people. 
 Ceit brings value to the aerospace industry by developing technologies in the following areas: •	Advanced manufacturing technologies. •	Mechanical design of flexible mechanisms (Flexures) for couplings and manipulators. •	Cognitive robotics. •	Energy management systems and power electronics. •	Cybersecurity communications, resilient data transmission and processing systems. •	Design of ad-hoc electronic and communication systems. •	Design of highly integrated multi-standard transceivers. •	Global positioning technologies. •	High performance processing platforms.
entityDescription:
