Its missions are to provide industry with services through the development of technical research projects and to promote the dissemination of knowledge through the training of young researchers and PhD students and scientific publications. 
Since 1996 Ceit-IK4 has created 14 technology-based spin-offs, which currently employ more than 300 people. Four of these have been purchased by companies which are listed on NASDAQ, NYSE, the Madrid Stock Exchange and the Paris Stock Exchange. 
Ceit-IK4 has a staff of 249 employees and 51 PhD students, and an annual budget over 15.3 M€. In February 2016, Ceit-IK4 modified its internal structure in order to adapt to the industrial sector and market challenges, which require greater multidisciplinary capacity. This new structure organizes Ceit-IK4’s expertise and capacities in a way that allows the major challenges in industry to be addressed from a more advantageous position.
The new structure is composed of four divisions, which are organised internally in groups:
The Materials and Manufacturing Division at Ceit-IK4 offers solutions to transform industry challenges into value. The assets of the Division rely on an integrated structure based on the Industry 4.0 holistic approach. The former Materials and Mechanical Engineering Departments merged, together with some ICT groups, to achieve a multidisciplinary division fitted to the current integrated industrial reality. This structure allows for a better understanding of material composition and process optimization technologies incorporating Industrial Monitoring, Vision and Robotics knowledge, as well as an advanced Mechanical Design approach. The well-established Thermomechanical Processing and Powder Metallurgy groups are complemented with disruptive technologies such as Additive Manufacturing and Surface Laser treatments. 
The Transport and Energy Division is focused on four main areas; railway transportation (including research lines in railway dynamics, signalling systems, efficient driving assistance system and infrastructure maintenance), aircraft transportation (including on-board devices for structural prognostic health monitoring and electrical component) and road transportation (electrical vehicle components and Intelligent transportation system) and smart grid and energy sensing components. 
The research activity of the Water&Health Division at CEIT-IK4 is funded in three main pillars. The first one relies on the development of urban and industrial water control and monitoring systems and covers the applications in the Water sector. The other two provide the Health sector with a double approach: on one hand research is focused on the design, fabrication and testing of biomedical devices and biosensors for biophysical parameter monitoring and medical diagnosis support, whereas on the other one modelling and development of bioinformatics tools for drug repositioning, genetic and metabolomic applications constitute the core activity.
ICT Division research is focused in monitoring and communications systems. The research ranges from advanced sensors, discrete and integrated analogue electronics up to mmWave, digital electronics, signal processing, algorithms, communication networks, data analysis and visualization among others. All these technologies cover the whole value chain of any monitoring and communication system that can be applied to a number of applications such as ICT, industry, manufacturing, transport, energy, water and health. 
Additionally, Ceit-IK4 is member of the IK4 Alliance, which covers a total of 1,400 people and has a turnover of around 100 M€. The IK4 Alliance was formed in 2005 in line with a federal model, whereby its members share strategies and combine capacities without giving up their sovereignty.

entityDescription: The National Institute for Nuclear Physics (INFN) is the Italian research agency dedicated to the study of the fundamental constituents of matter and the laws that govern them, under the supervision of the Ministry of Education, Universities and Research (MIUR). It conducts theoretical and experimental research in the fields of subnuclear, nuclear and astroparticle physics. All of the INFN’s research activities are undertaken within a framework of international competition, in close collaboration with Italian universities on the basis of solid academic partnerships spanning decades. Fundamental research in these areas requires the use of cutting-edge technology and instruments, developed by the INFN at its own laboratories and in collaboration with industries. Groups from the Universities of Rome, Padua, Turin, and Milan founded the INFN on 8thAugust 1951 to uphold and develop the scientific tradition established during the 1930s by Enrico Fermi and his school, with their theoretical and experimental research in nuclear physics. In the latter half of the 1950s the INFN designed and built the first Italian accelerator, the electron synchrotron developed in Frascati, where its first national laboratory was set up. During the same period, the INFN began to participate in research into the construction and use of ever-more powerful accelerators being conducted by CERN, the European Organisation for Nuclear Research, in Geneva. Today the INFN employs some 5,000 scientists whose work is recognised internationally not only for their contribution to various European laboratories, but also to numerous research centres worldwide.

entityName: Athena Research and Innovation Center in Information, Communication and Knowledge Technologies
description:
Athena Research Centre was founded in 2003 as the “IRIS – Integrated Research for the Information Society” to consolidate and further expand the Greek R&D activities and initiatives in the area of ICT. The new Center initially comprised of the following existing institutes: the Institute for Language and Speech Processing (ILSP), the Cultural and Educational Technology Institute (CETI) and the Industrial Systems Institute (ISI). The founding act provided for the creation of new institutes that would cover vibrant areas of digital technology as well as of units that would incubate knowhow development activities that may lead to new major development directions. In 2006 IRIS was renamed to “Research and Innovation Center in Information, Communication and Knowledge Technologies”, with the name designation “Athena”.

The vision of Athena is to serve the full spectrum of the research lifecycle, starting from basic and applied research, continuing on to system & product building and infrastructure service provision, and ending with technology transfer and entrepreneurship. The fundamental role of Athena is to build knowledge and devise solutions and technologies for the digital society. Its value lies in the unique collection of skills and know-how of its researchers and professional staff and its national and international reputation.

The overall strategy and research values of Athena are developing along these axes: a) A research plan that targets fundamental and applied challenges with high potential impact, aiming at high-quality, novel, and deep results, with informatics at the core of synergies with other sciences, b) A technology transfer plan with a global focus and special attention to the Greek environment, c) A young researcher development plan based on identifying and supporting original talent, d) A strategic co-operations plan aiming at key industrial companies, governmental agencies, regional authorities, and international research and higher-education organisations, e) An educational plan that targets at designing and participating in local and international graduate programs.

Athena is organised today in the following Institutes and Units: a) Information Management Systems Institute (Maroussi), b) Institute of Language and Speech Processing (Maroussi), c) Industrial Systems Institute (Patras), d) Corallia (Maroussi), e) Space Programmes Unit (Maroussi), f) Robotics Perception and Interaction Unit (Maroussi), g) Environmental and Networking Technologies and Applications Unit (Xanthi), h) Pharma Informatics Unit (Maroussi).

Athena has premises and infrastructures in three geographical regions of Greece: Attica - Athens, Western Greece - Patras and Thrace - Xanthi. The Central Administration is located in Athens. This gives Athena a wider, country-wide role and offers unique advantages: a) closer and stronger connections to the regional, academic and industrial environment, b) employee engagement in regional resources and activities, c) enhancing regional competitiveness by providing immediate access to the innovation created, d) taking advantage of the initiatives, funding schemes and other opportunities provided exclusively to regions.

Its value lies in the unique collection of skills and know-how of its researchers and professional staff, and its national and international reputation.

The Central Administration is located in Athens. entityDescription:
Planetek Italia s.r.l. is an Italian Benefit Company established in 1994, headquartered in Bari, part of D-Orbit Group since 2025.
Planetek Italia s.r.l. is a leading Italian company specializing in geospatial data solutions, with a presence in both national and international markets. 
The company owns Planetek Hellas EPE, located in Athens, Greece, and two Italian university spin-offs: GAP s.r.l. and GEO-K s.r.l.

Planetek Italia delivers comprehensive solutions for harnessing the value of geospatial data across the entire data life cycle—ranging from acquisition and storage to management, analysis, and dissemination. 
The company operates in a wide array of application domains, including environmental and land monitoring, open government, smart cities, defense and security, space exploration, and Earth Observation (EO) satellite missions.With extensive expertise in Earth Observation technologies, Planetek develops solutions that utilize optical and radar data from satellites, aircraft, and drones. Its innovations include software for both on-board edge computing and ground segment operations, along with geo-analytics products and value-added services for environmental monitoring.
The company integrates artificial intelligence into its remote sensing data processing workflows and provides EO-based services—such as geo-analytics, dynamic visualizations, and automated reporting—through its proprietary Rheticus® cloud-based platform.

Planetek Italia employs over 130 professionals and reported a financial turnover of approximately €18 million in 2023.

In November 2022, Planetek was among the first 22 European space companies to sign the “Statement for a Responsible Space Sector” initiative promoted by the European Space Agency (ESA). This commitment supports the sustainable development of the space sector and promotes the positive impact of space activities on society.The company adheres to the principles of SDesign Thinking to ensure the development of user-centric solutions, leveraging the best available technologies while maintaining a strong commitment to economic, social, and environmental sustainability.In 2022, Planetek Italia became a member of Assobenefit, the Italian Association of Benefit Corporations, and released its first Sustainability Report, which demonstrated outstanding performance, ranking among the highest in the ICT and Aerospace sectors. In 2023, the company was recognized with the Sustainability Hero award for Italy under the SME EnterPRIZE initiative, a European program that highlights businesses with sustainability-driven models.

Planetek Italia operates under a structured model based on Corporate Functions and Strategic Business Units (SBUs). Each SBU functions with a high degree of autonomy and includes dedicated teams for design, sales, and production.

The company also maintains rigorous quality and compliance standards:It operates an Information Security Management System certified under ISO/IEC 27001:2013.It is certified for remote sensing services in line with the ISO 9001 standard.It applies an Environmental Management System compliant with ISO 14001:2015 and EU Regulation No. 1221/2009 (EMAS III).It holds SA8000 certification for social accountability, which includes a strong commitment to gender equality and ethical labor practices.

entityDescription:
The company started in the field of servicing cutting tools in 1998.
After the very beginnings, MASAM s.r.o. was founded in 2001. Its primary focus was servicing cutting tools. In a short period requirements and customer expectations increased, and consequently it was necessary to reconsider the focus and plans for the future in terms of investment and development of the company.
Between the years 2001 and 2006 the company invested in development through the purchase of new CNC technologies, which allowed us to provide not only services but also the production of cutting tools. This has resulted in the expansion of our production. We supplemented technology, construction, entry and exit checks. For full qualitatively managed processes in the company, during this period we introduced an information management system and certification according to ISO 9001:2008. In 2006, the entire company moved into the newly built premises.
Since 2006 the company has experienced the next period of development and expansion. First there was just an idea of expanding the company with the chip machining and tool room. We were able to test the cutting tools we produced and, of course, also use them for our chip machining needs. During the years 2006 – 2009 it was decided to extend MASAM s.r.o. by two divisions: The Manufacture and Sharpening of Cutting Tools Division and the Chip Machining, Tool Room Division. We started expanding our commercial department, aimed at discovering new markets and new customers for both divisions.
In 2013, the new manufacturing plant in the Vráble industrial park was completed. It is a modern hall, which offers the perfect base for further development. Our goal is to have the most modern machinery permitting us to meet the most demanding requirements of our customers.

LKR Leichtmetallkompetenzzentrum Ranshofen GmbH is a subsidiary of AIT and a part of AIT's Center for Transport Technologies. LKR's business focus is centred around new aluminium and magnesium alloys and their application with steel parts and composites on automotive, aeronautic and space applications. 

When developing lightweight components, one of the main challenges lies in the ability to reduce weight while also ensuring passenger safety during a crash. The use of lightweight materials is a permanent increasing need in theautomotiveindustry, which is reflected in the increased use of this technology in vehicle design. The application of light metals provides a huge weight reduction potential, which in turn has a positive effect on the energy efficiency and CO2 emissions of vehicles.

Striving to rise to these challenges, the LKR team of more than 50 specialists has both cutting-edge simulation tools as well as a unique research infrastructure at its disposal. This allows new metal alloys and customized processes for casting of lightweight components and metal forming to be developed and prototyped.

entityName: Chair of Flight Vehicle Dynamics, Laboratory for Flight Vehicle Dynamics and Multibody Systems
entityDescription:
Scientific and teaching activities as well as collaboration with industry in the area of aerospace dynamics, mechatronical systems and space robotics is conducted at the Chair of Flight Vehicle Dynamics, and related Laboratory for Flight Vehicle Dynamics and Multibody Systems. To this end, special research focus of the Chair and Laboratory is on the mathematical and numerical modelling of multibody/multi-physical systems, computational dynamics as well as flight mechanics and control, including advanced machine/deep learning algorithms and data-driven surrogate models. The Chair established successful international collaboration with several research groups, including scientists at the universities ETH Zürich, TU München, Politecnico di Milano, TU Delft and NASA-JPL, and was involved in chairing of prominent scientific events and editorial activities of the relevant journals.

Any-Shape SA is a company dedicated to Additive Technologies for industry. Our ambition is to be a leading industrial actor in Europe and beyond by providing our customers with the whole value chain in Additive Manufacturing, with a specific focus on engineering for AM and quality assessment. Any-Shape's organisation lies on three main pillars :

- Engineering design for additive manufacturing : Any-Shape provides its customers with a professional support to exploit the full possibilities of industrial 3D printing while properly accounting for manufacturing constraints from the concept to the detailed design phase. 
- Metal, plastic and composite parts production : Any-Shape manufactures high value functional parts in plastic, composite & metal for highly competitive industries. Consistent state-of-the-art technologies are available (SLM, SLS, MJP and FDM Composite).
- Quality assessment : Providing our customers with the best quality standards is our main concern as a way to favour the rapid introduction of 3D printed parts in highly demanding industrial applications. GIS4Mobile is providing software in the field of mapping, geodata, GIS and GNSS.
The primary focus has been registration of various subjects using mobile devices, but also publishing geo enabled data for mobile users, making access to data easy and intuitive using a map, overlayered with information.
Lately we have evolved into building lightweight GNSS receivers that enables users with RTK (tapas) access to work in the field with great accuracy, using a mobile device and this lightweight GNSS receiver.

The latest product we have put to the market is a SAAS solution we call LedningsInfo (PipeInformation).
With this construction companies and professionals are able to view the location of the underground infrastructure as pipes and cables belonging to water-supply, power-supply, telecomunications and other companies.
The purpose is to reduce the risk for damage to the pipes and caples.
This solution depends on the danishLER.DKsystem, where the construction professional is required to make a registration before the work starts, and owners of the infrastucture in turn is obligated to inform about the position of the pipes and cables. For more see this:https://www.gis4mobile.dk/produkter/ledningsinfo/

with international offices in: England | Kenya | Cyprus (HQ)

Silensec covers:
IT Governance – Silensec assists organizations in complying with security best practice and international standards such as ISO27001, ISO22301 and PCI DSS.
Security Audits and Assessments – Silensec carries out compliance audits up to technical security assessments such as penetration tests, source code reviews and Web applications assessment.
Value-Added Security Systems Integration – Silensec specializes in the deployment and integration of a range of security controls such as WAFs, DAMs, SIEMs as well as data classification and DLP solutions.
Managed Security – Silensec runs an ISO27001-certified SOC through which it provides managed security to its clients.
Security Training – Silensec has developed a portfolio of over 30 training courses across the different categories of awareness, proaction, prevention, detection, reaction and compliance.

Silensec is also actively participating as a key member-organisation in the European Cyber Security Organisation (ECSO), as co-chair of the SWG 5.1 Cyber Ranges and Cyber Exercises) and a Premium Partner of the Global Cyber Alliance.

entityName: Consorzio Nazionale Interuniversitario per le Scienze del Mare - CoNISMa
entityDescription: CoNISMa comprises 36 Italian Universities, including about 900 researchers and technicians, it has a recognized legal status and it is under the surveillance of the Ministry of University and Research. CoNISMa entered in the EU Marine Board, being a unique super-organism in Europe, since it merges scientific and capacity building activities. Through CoNISMa, the Italian University-based research and capacity building system working on marine sciences became a single entity and reached international size and reputation as such. CoNISMa covers all fields of marine sciences, with both research and capacity building activities ranging from physics to chemistry, geology, biology, ecology, engineering, economics, and legal sciences. It carries out its activities worldwide. The administrative offices are located in Rome, but the bulk of the "staff" and "infrastructures" is in the associated Universities.

entityName: DLR - INSTITUTE OF AERODYNAMICS AND FLOW TECHNOLOGY (DLR AS)
entityDescription:
The Institute of Aerodynamics and Flow Technology is a leading research Institute in the field of aerodynamics/aeroacoustics of airplanes and aerothermodynamics of space vehicles. It has two main sites at Braunschweig and Göttingen and a division at Cologne. Today a total personal of about 350 employees is engaged in numerical and experimental investigations on air- and space vehicles. Experiments are performed in wind tunnels and in flight experimental aircraft.
The Institute can look back on a long history: After the first “Modellversuchsanstalt für Aerodynamik“ was founded in Göttingen in 1907, the Institute for Aerodynamics and the Institute for Gas Dynamics of the "Deutsche Forschungsanstalt für Luftfahrt” (DFL) were succeeded by today's DLR Institute of Aerodynamics and Flow Technology.
As a leading research institute in the fields of aerodynamics, aeroacoustics and aerothermodynamics, it is subdivided into nine departments. The Institute is acting as a link between basic research at the universities and industrial application. This results in a large number of cooperative national and international research projects.
Environmental policy conditions are playing an increasingly major role in air traffic. The DLR Institute of Aerodynamics and Flow Technology therefore researches how future aircraft and space transportation systems can be designed and operated more efficient, ecological, comfortable, economical and secure. A further core competence is the development of software products used for aerodynamic and aeroacoustic simulations.

description:
Luxembourg is a country with its eyes on the stars - and the Interdisciplinary Centre for Security, Reliability and Trust (SnT) is helping it turn its science-fiction dreams into an economic reality. Our researchers explore the challenges and opportunities of space, hand-in-hand with industry leading partners. From Earthbound satellite receivers - to state-of-the-art nanosatellites and autonomous lunar robots, researchers at SnT infuse Luxembourg's vibrant space industry with new perspectives and innovative solutions. We are proud to be part of the most dynamic ecosystem for applied space innovation in Europe.
SnT conducts internationally competitive research in information and communication technology (ICT) with high relevance creating socio-economic impact. In addition to long-term, high-risk research, SnT engages in demand driven collaborative projects with industry and the public sector. Therefore, the centre has set up a partnership program with now over 55 members, where it develops strategic areas addressing challenges confronting the industry and the public sector in ICT. These resulting concepts present a genuine, long-lasting competitive advantage for companies in Luxembourg and beyond.

entityDescription:
GAIKER, member of Basque Research and Technology Alliance, BRTA, is a Technology Centre devoted to the technological innovation. From its beginnings in 1985, it uptakes, develops and transfers technology to the industry.
GAIKER has carried out close to 567 projects and has leaded or taken part in 132 European Projects framed in Programmes of the Europe acting as partner to gather new advance knowledge for further industrial application. GAIKER’s activity is focused on the transfer to its customers of the technology and the know-how acquired during the up-taking process. From its foundation, the Centre has carried out close to 1,550 R&D projects “under contract” for customers coming from a wide range of sectors (Pharmaceutical Industry, Chemical Industry, Human and Animal Health, Engineering and Consultancy Firms, Public Administrations, Automotive Industries, Construction, Packing and Packaging and Home Appliances, amongst others). This wide offer is possible thanks to its highly qualified staff; nowadays 95 employees. Furthermore, the 8,750 m2of premises -located in the Technological Park of Bizkaia (Zamudio)- include an extensive network of laboratories, as well as pilot plants where processes are optimised, and prototypes developed. GAIKER is a Centre of Innovation dedicated to offer quality solutions to the technological needs of its customers. The certification of its R&D&i Management System in accordance with UNE 166002:2014 standard in 2019.
· In the BIOTECHNOLOGY Area, the Centre carries out in vitro and ex vivo preclinical studies aimed at the toxicological, pharmacokinetic and functional evaluation of compounds (including active ingredients, drugs, cosmetics, functional ingredients and nanocomposites), for which it has the GLP (Good Laboratory Practice) Certificate of Compliance. It is also an expert in the development of biodetection systems of biological targets for applications in human, animal, plant or environmental health. It works in industrial biotechnology focused on improving industrial processes through the selection and production of microorganisms and/or enzymes.
· In the SUSTAINABLE COMPOSITES AND FUNCTIONAL POLYMERS' Area, the Centre develop more sustainable polymeric materials with better functional and structural performance addressing the entire life cycle of the product: from its design and processing to its recycling and reuse. We formulate thermoplastics/thermosets by incorporating bio-based, recycled and biodegradable materials in their conception to adjust their properties to the product/process and optimize their processing conditions in pilot plants as well as their sustainability.
In the same way, the area works on extending the potential of additive manufacturing to new range of materials and functionalities. We either make the materials have sensor performance, or incorporate sensors in the product and the process, to bolster the concept of “Industry 4.0” from the materials' technology perspective. We functionalise the materials to give them new performance with respect to their electrical and durability properties (anti-scratch, self-repairing, fungicide, ...) and develop films and active packaging. 
GAIKER is deeply involved in Recycling and Circular Economy: on the characterisation and treatment of post-consumer waste flow from every origin as well as industrial scraps, using innovative identification and separation systems; We develop ad-hoc chemical recycling processes to obtain monomers, chemical blocks, and fuels derived from plastic waste.

description:
The Centre for Innovation in Polymer Engineering (PIEP) is a private non-profit association, of a technological and scientific matrix, with a business management model.
Founded on December 13, 2000, at the initiative of the industry and in collaboration with the Department of Polymer Engineering at the University of Minho (DEP-UM) and the Support Institute for Small and Medium Enterprises and Innovation (IAPMEI), PIEP intends to provide an excellent response in the delivery of products and services promptly, oriented to the R&D+i needs of companies in the plastics and related sectors, through innovation activities, technology transfer, technical-scientific consultancy, and service provision.
In general, PIEP acts in terms of the provision of testing and testing services and failure diagnoses, the development of new materials and products, processing technologies, and productive tools, based on the promotion of the principles of sustainable development (Circular Economy and Environment). 
PIEP also contributes to training, supporting the development of human resources with capacity and experience in industrial innovation in the field of polymer engineering.
entityDescription:
CENTRE FOR INNOVATION IN POLYMER ENGINEERING

PIEP is a private non-profit research and development organisation providing consultancy, materials, product and processing technology development, as well as testing services for the polymer industry worldwide and related sectors.

Established in 2001 by some of the leading national plastic companies, UMinho and with the national government support through IAPMEI, PIEP holds a wide range of associated members, the majority of plastic industry affiliates (plastics converters, machinery suppliers, mould making companies, compounders, and material suppliers). Based in Guimarães (Portugal) and strategically located in UMinho Campus, close to the Polymer Engineering Department (DEP), PIEP currently employs over 30 people with relevant academic background and applied R&D experience in a wide range of polymer science and engineering domains.

Its 3,000sq meter state-of-the-art facilities (an investment over 6.5 million Euros from private and public sector) provides extensive capabilities for polymer characterisation and testing (mechanical, thermal, rheological, chemical and thermo-physical), thermoplastic materials development and processing (conventional and multi-material injection moulding, single and twin screw extrusion, co-extrusion, blow moulding, thermoforming), thermoset materials processing (vacuum infusion, RTM) and advanced computational modelling tools for product and process design and engineering.

Commitment to industry: PIEP, in cooperation with the academic staff from the Polymer Engineering Department of UMinho, provides research with up to date scientific knowledge, ensuring the best and innovative problem-solving approaches to industry’s innovation challenges and needs.

Our mission: To be a Polymer Engineering Innovation Center, with a regional, national and international scope that efficiently formalizes the link between the industry and the University, capable to respond, on time, the R&D companies needs (in the case of SMEs, even constituting their valence in this field), promoting and supporting the human resources training with experience in industrial innovation activities, aimed to convert ideas into products.

Our Vision: To be a reference partner in applied research, development, and innovation for the polymers and composites industry at the national and international level, promoting the materialisation of new ideas and concepts that serve as a basis for sustainable economic development and industrial competitiveness.

Relevant skills/experience: With its core knowledge and competencies based on materials science – engineering - processing technologies - testing, PIEP is actively engaged in the development of research projects, bringing together a set of integrated and interconnected capabilities that serve the fundamental purpose of its existence: to support the national and international industry in the development of materials, engineering, production technologies and tests applied to polymer materials, products, and systems.

entityDescription:
The Telecom-network R&D Team has been working in the network development and satellite systems for more than 15 years for industrial and R&D purposes. It has recognized skills in the satellite telecommunication area through collaboration with French Spatial Agency (CNES), Marlink (Leading satellite operator for maritime market), Airbus Defense & Space or Thales Alenia Space.

Since 2009, the R&D team is the official maintainer of the open-source satellite emulator OpenSAND, as well as the creator and main contributor of the open-source metrology tool OpenBACH since 2016. Since 2018, the team is the main developer of the Satellite-NS3 (SNS3) open-source simulator.

Since 2007 Viveris has carried out more than 30 R&T projects funded by the French spatial agency (CNES), and in collaboration with academic and industrial partners. Most of project deal with SATCOM (GEO/LEO) and hybrid systems (terrestrial),and in particular the performance evaluation of services/applications in these networks and the optimisations at different levels (access, network, transport and service). Some of the topics addressed during these projects are listed herein: hybrid ADSL/Satellite/cellular/IoT network architectures, IPTV, evaluation of TCP and new transport protocols (QUIC/HTTP3) on SATCOM, evaluation of PEP proxies, CDNs caching, traffic engineering and load balancing (including MPTCP), FEC performances, ROHC header compression, DPI and Machine Learning techniques applied to satellite networks and SDN/NFV Virtualization.

entityDescription:
Neptune is an innovative SME established in 2014, founded by a team of experts in water loss, satellite image analysis, data transmission and remote sensing applications. Water leakage is a paramount worldwide problem because the subsoil pipelines are old and lose an average between 30 to 40% of potable water, with a peak up to 60%. Our idea is to enhance the water loss research system with a "disruptive technology" using EO data to analyse the soil moisture content (SMC) to identify small and big water leaks. Actual trends, analysed by the European Environment Agency (source https://www.eea.europa.eu/) shows the world water consumption doubles every 20 years, more than twice as fast as population growth with the risk in the future that part of the citizens will not have access to drinking water. Saving water resources through the timely identification of leaks is fundamental for users to have guaranteed supply of drinking water, but it is also important for operators in order to lower their operating costs and guarantees of service.
Neptune’s team was looking for a new space-derived technology to apply to daily water leaks issues, with a TTP (Technology Transfer Project), from space technologies to terrestrial applications. Research and a passion for space have led to the identification of the possibility of monitoring soil moisture through the analysis of L-band SAR satellite images, which due to its wavelength is able to penetrate the ground.
The idea, born in 2014, is to innovate the water loss research system with a "disruptive technology" and not by simply improving existing techniques. The main issue that we wanted to address is the amount of water purified and lost during the network source to users. To solve this problem, each year players in the industry issue contracts for millions of Euros for leakage research. The detection service is paid by the kilometre checked and, normally, with the existing technology, a team composed of 2 people can only assess 5 km of water network each day. With NE.P.T.UN.E. Water Leaks Sat (Satellite Network Project To Uncover Extended Water Leaks) we can increase the daily km checked from 5 to 30 because operators are able to go directly to POIs (points of interest) generated by processing satellite images. This way, we can check in 1 day what other competitors check in 1 week, with a great decrease in costs.

entityName: University of Ljubljana, Faculty of Computer and Information Science
entityDescription:
The Faculty of Computer and Information Science of the University of Ljubljana is Slovenia’s leading educational and research institution for computer and information science.
The Faculty’s main function is educating undergraduate and graduate computer science experts of various profiles, as well as engaging in research work which generates new knowledge and uncovers solutions to contemporary problems. The Faculty also offers additional educational activities in computer and information science for several professional profiles by hosting lectures and workshops to increase the level of computer literacy in the country. Its public events also serve to popularise ideas about computers, especially among young people.
The Faculty was founded in 1996, when the Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science split into two separate faculties. The study of computer science itself began at the University of Ljubljana back in 1973, first as an elective programme after the 2nd year of electrical engineering study, and has been an independent study programme since 1982. In 2014, the Faculty moved to a new building in Brdo at the outskirts of Ljubljana.
The Faculty is a full member of theUniversity of Ljubljana. The University was founded in 1919 and is the oldest and largest higher education and scientific research institution in Slovenia.

entityDescription:
Tracasa Global is a public technological company owned by the Government of Navarre, whose headquarters are located in Sarriguren (Spain). It was founded in 1982 with the objective of assisting the Government of Navarre in the creation and implementation of the cadastre of the region. Since its inception, and based on its founding core competencies, Tracasa Global has worked extensively undertaking projects for the development and deployment of cadastral solutions for government agencies in Spain and around the world. Tracasa Global evolved through the years with the creation of new business units and the provision of services to the government of Navarre and new clients, expanding its areas of operation. 

Our main business units include:
· Territorial and Spatial Engineering Area. Group specialized in the generation and analysis of geographic information, designing flows that incorporate the most up-to-date remote sensing techniques (optical and radar) and GIS analysis. Its multidisciplinary team can offer a wide range of studies that require thematic knowledge of the territory (land use and vegetation, hydrology and hydraulics, risk maps, emergencies, security and climate change adaptation...). They are also specialized in the development of products in the downstream segment and the exploitation of Copernicus data for applications such as environment or security.
· Software Engineering and Spatial Data Analytics Area. Most of the exponentially growing collected data has a spatial component. The area is focused on helping organizations making the most of that data by applying the latest IT technologies. Our key expertise relies on extracting, transforming, storing and applying quality controls to huge volumes of spatial data and designing and implementing software and products related to them. These include data visualization, dissemination and analytics.
· Software Engineering and GIS Area, specialises in the implementation of GIS solutions, mainly in water utility companies. These implementations have made us experts in the creation of data models, geographic data migration (loading and validation), development of maintenance tools, exploitation and integration with other systems through APIs. We also have extensive experience in implementing GIS for cadastre and cartography.
· Cadastre, Land Administration and Services to Local Government Area. These services are part of our origins and Tracasa Global continues to provide services and develop solutions for local, regional and national governments in the field of land and cadastral management.

Our corporate mission aims to bolster people’s quality of life and the sustainability and security of our planet, through an ongoing commitment to innovation and digital transformation and leveraging Data Science and Artificial Intelligence as enabling elements. We work both at Spanish national level and internationally for private companies as well as public administrations. Our customers include EEA, JRC, ECMWF or SatCen. We are also active in EU-funded programs such as Horizon Europe, EDF or Erasmus+.

entityDescription: diondo GmbH is a developer, manufacturer and operator of industrial CT systems for non-destructive testing. The range of products extends from high-resolution systems for small test objects to extremely powerful CT systems with linear accelerator (LINAC-CT) for particularly large objects or those made of highly absorbing materials. Despite its small size compared to international competitors, the diondo team has established itself in the global market over the past 25 years as the technologically leading supplier of customized industrial computed tomography systems. The service division sees itself as a partner of the customer for small quantities or individual studies. Feasibility studies of a fundamental nature are regularly carried out for new components or materials. While for recurring applications near-standard systems can be configured from an extensive construction kit of components and functional modules, for special or novel tasks completely new methods and designs are developed and realized. diondo GmbH is independent and can therefore freely select from all imaging components available on the market those that are ideally suited to the task at hand. Many companies from the aerospace industry are already successfully using CT systems from diondo GmbH, for example, for investigations of new materials or for quality assurance of innovative manufacturing processes, such as additive manufacturing. Together with companies and research institutes from the aerospace industry, diondo GmbH is a partner in funded projects and networks, for example in metallic additive manufacturing or the development of series technologies for ceramic composites.

entityDescription: An essential problem when treating cancer is the selective access and controlled destruction of tumour cellsin the patient’s body. After tumours have been surgically removed, individual tumour cells often remain in the body, out of which new tumours could develop.The traditional follow-up treatments of chemotherapy and radiation are often unable to destroy these cancer cells in a controlled manner. Besides, these therapies come along with untold side effects and the destruction of healthy cells might cause more harm to the patient.Based on current diagnostic methods, the possibility now exists of combining biotechnology and physics to come up with a more effective and gentle way to treat cancer. To this end, antibodies endowed with special iron nanospheres are used, as well as alternating magnetic fields,which generate a force through a physical coupling that destroys the abnormal cell without harming the surrounding healthy tissue. MIRA, the Magnetic-field-based Immunotherapy for Remission using endowed Antibodies is a unique cancer therapy, highly selective, efficient, side-effect free and derived from MOA², a pulsed plasma thruster, used for space applications.The procedure’s physical foundation is based on alternating magnetic fields whose effects were described as early as 1942 by Hannes Alfvén, a Swede who would later win the Nobel Prize. During this process, the disruption of a magnetic field generates a force effect on magnetic conductive material that lies in close proximity to it. In nature, such effects can be seen in solar eruptions and in northern lights. In the case of MIRA, the coupling is enabled by iron nanospheres with which the antibody is endowed. The force effect on the antibodies is great enough to destroy the cell membrane, thereby irreversibly damaging the cancer cell.This facilitates gentler treatment, since its effect can be switched on and off in a targeted manner. MIRA therefore functions like a light switch, except instead of light, a therapeutic treatment is switched on and off, precisely targeting the right spot at the right time. Depending on the treatment method, this allows the tumour to be destroyed in one or more carefully planned sessions. MIRA method’s high efficiency is also manifested in its short treatment duration. Experiments performed so far have shown that 30 seconds is enough time for the selected cells to be destroyed. First in-vitro tests are foreseen to start in the 4th quarter of 2019 –if MIRA functions well, the first complete healing of surface-near cancer types (like breast, skin and prostate) is close at hand.MIRA, the Magnetic-field-based Immunotherapy for Remission using endowed Antibodies, is at the centre of the MIRA Companythat is currently in its start-up phase and soon to be founded in Austria. Led bya team of experts with diverse backgrounds in science, engineering, medical operations, legal and financial aspects, the MIRA Company is set to become a leading player in developing and marketing innovative technologies in the area of medicinal applications based on the MOA² technology.

entityName: INSTITUTO POLITÉCNICO DE VIANA DO CASTELO
entityDescription:
The Viana do Castelo Polytechnic Institute (IPVC) was founded in 1980. Is a regional institution, whose aims are a qualified human, cultural, scientific, technical and professional training, to carry out necessary research to accomplish its mission and to cooperate with the regional community of Alto-Minho, particularly with its productive and entrepreneurial sectors.
The IPVC is made up of six Schools offering undergraduate and postgraduate degree courses, these last very often in collaboration with national and international polytechnics and universities. Also promotes Master courses and specialization courses.
The IPVC is a community of students and qualified professionals, located in the northwest of Portugal, aware that the progress of society ensures the harmonious development of persons and their performance. Joined together in the same mission: to create, manage and disseminate knowledge and culture, through processes of education/learning, research, transfer of technology and knowledge.
The IPVC has implemented its existence on the regional, national and international levels. The evolution of this process is based, on two fronts: firstly through the continuous search for quality of training and, secondly, into its involvement in projects in several areas as a tool for building links with the natural partners and other national and international institutions.
The IPVC has, since its creation, bet in the development of research projects and offers services to the community as the way to continue its mission. Due to its extensive experience in the management of EU funds, IPVC has a technical support team fully aware of regulations and guidelines on national and European structural funds and, specially, with regard to issues of eligibility of expenditure, government procurement, environment, information and advertising and equal opportunity between men and women.
On the Viana do Castelo town campus, the IPVC provides a range of facilities, including five residences, six refectories, 4 bars, a 320-seat library and a cultural and Sports Centre. All six schools making up the IPVC are covered by a wireless internet network.

The Institute of Space Sciences and Technologies of Asturias (Instituto de Ciencias y Tecnologías Espaciales de Asturias - ICTEA - https://ictea.uniovi.es/acerca) was created by the Governing Council of the University of Oviedo on March 1st, 2019. It is formally conformed by members of two recognized research groups at the University of Oviedo:
- Applied Mathematical Modelization (MOMA)
- High Energy Physics (FPAUO).

ICTEA team members are dedicated to research, education, innovation and technological development in space and fundamental matter science and technology. The institute has the objective to foster scientific and technological collaboration among interdisciplinary areas in the fields of physics, geology, mathematics, or medicine; focused on the following cooncrete knowledge areas:

- Mineralogy of asteroids
- Planetary geology, with field research in the Antarctica
- Discovery and carachterisation of exoplanets
- Cosmology: study of the large-scale structure of the Universe through gravitational lensing to understand both dark matter and energy
- Adaptative optics using machine learning techniques
- Experimental high energy physics: study and carachterisation of physical observables of the standard model of particle physics (SM), search of new particles, etc.
- Theoretical high energy physics: string theory, extra dimensions and dualities, supersymmetric quantum field theories, supergravity, holography, etc.
- Analysis of type M red dwarf stars' rotation
- Medicine: use of machine learning techniques for diagnostic and prevention

FIBRobotics Ltd. is a company founded in 2019 by a group of materials experts from The Tampere University of Technology. FIBRobotics develops and offers solutions for micromechanical testing of composite materials and material interfaces. The solutions are based on proprietary test devices and software developed and manufactured by Fibrobotics. With the help of these solutions, research institutes and companies developing new materials are able to test the mechanical properties of new materials faster and get more accurate data about the properties of the materials. 

FIBRobotics' current customers are divided into three segments: 
1. Research organizations and universities conducting research on composite materials. Typically, these organizations focus their resources on research and development of new materials. 
2. Companies producing raw materials for composite materials, such as glass and carbon fibre manufacturers, natural fibre processors and resin manufacturers. 
3. Manufacturers of composite products, such as composite components, prepreg manufacturers, tire manufacturers, and composite filament manufacturers for 3D printers Through customers and through contacts at research organizations, it has become clear that FIBRobotics’ solutions are unique and could offer significant value for companies developing new materials for use in aerospace applications such as space shuttles, rockets and satellites.

entityDescription:
The National Statistics Institute is a legally independent administrative Autonomous institution assigned to theMinistry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation, via the Secretary of State for the Economy and Business Support. It is basically governed by 12/1989 of 9 May, Law on the Public Statistical Function that regulates Statistics activity for state purposeswhich is the exclusive competence of the State and by the Statute approved by Royal Decree 508/2001 of 11 May.
The Law assigns the National Statistics Institute an important role in public statistic activity, expressly placing it in charge of large scale statistical operations (demographic and economic censuses, national accounts, demographic and social statistics, economic and social indicators, coordination and maintenance of company directories Electoral Census training...)
Moreover, the law attributes the INE with the following functions: formulation of the National Statistics Plan with the collaboration of Ministerial Departments and the Bank of Spain; the proposal of common regulations on concepts, statistical units, classifications and codes; and relations on statistics with specialised International Institutions and in particular, with the European Union Statistics Office (EUROSTAT).Moreover, there are other collegiate bodies with significant competences in statistical matter as: the Higher Statistics Council, the Interministerial Statistics Commission and the Interterritorial Statistics Committee. In all of them the INE plays an important role.
The INE is also responsible for compiling the Electoral Census, pursuant to Organic Law 5/1985, of 19 June, on the General Electoral Regime, and on the ongoing and computerised coordination and management of the Municipal Register, as set out in Law 7/1985, of 2 April, Regulating the Local Regime Bases, and in Royal Decree 2612/1996, of 20 December, modifying the Regulation on Population and Territorial Demarkation of the Local Entities passed by Royal Decree 1690/1986, of 11 July.

entityDescription: The International Laser Centre is an interdisciplinary research organization formed to foster collaborative research in the areas of progressive methods and technologies of photonics; and their application in industry and health care. The Centre was created by the Ministry of Education of the Slovak Republic in January 1997, as an independent research and educational institution, on the basis of the Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Information Technology, the Slovak University of Technology and the Faculty of Mathematics and Physics, Comenius University, in cooperation with the Moscow State University. The creation of the Centre was aiming at building an excellent research centre equipped with up-to-date sophisticated laser and optoelectronic technologies. The Centre provides a cross- and inter-disciplinary research infrastructure for the high-level interdisciplinary research and development in all fields of laser-based and photonic technologies in cooperation with Slovak universities, academic institutions and industry. We implement this mission by fostering scientific, engineering and biomedical talents. Specifically, the Centre: conducts actual scientific and technological projects, and co-operates with associated institutions; provides a platform for technology transfer and create contacts among scientists, engineers and other specialists sharing interest in the field of photonics, presentation of scientific and technical results, consulting and information services cooperates with universities in under-gradual and post-gradual education covering applications of lasers and optoelectronics in microelectronics, biomedicine, industry, organization of training and courses, workshops, etc.

entityDescription:
Optec4Life is a Medical Device Company, newly founded, with the mission to develop non-invasive systems for monitoring and prediction of physiological parameters to diagnose critical health conditions and classify specific disease stages. The first indication targeted by the new company is the real-time prediction and monitoring of ischemic hypoxia in babies in perinatal and neonatal stage.
The technology is further aiming at non-invasive diagnostics and monitoring of metabolic and respiratory acidosis/alkalosis in real-time, in patients with acute respiratory syndromes in the neonatology intensive care units.
Optec4Life owns an exclusive license for this technology from the nanotechnology research center “nanoGUNE” and “Biodonostia health research center” in Spain for further development and entry to the market. This is a transfer of technology from a private research laboratory to Optec4Life.
The current technology/device called “New Co” is based on a machine learning-assisted photonic system. Proof of concept was realized invitro and ex vivo on various body fluids, and a validation study was done invivo in animal models.
Optec4Life has defined a clear roadmap for the go-to-market strategy, timelines and budget for CE Mark and commercialization of the New Co Device.

entityName: Società Agricola Italian Cricket Farm S.r.l.
entityDescription:
The Italian Cricket Farm S.r.l. is an insect farm born in 2017 in Piedmont (Italy). The company was founded by two investing partners employed in the Italian food sector. To date, it is the largest insect farm in Italy and specializes in cricket (Acheta domesticus (L. 1758)) and mealworm (Tenebrio molitor (L. 1758)) breeding. The bred insects will be destined for the future European protein market, as this food matrix is one of the most important sustainable food resources of the future. This is because, according to a multitude of LCA-based studies, the insect consumes few environmental resources and produces a food with very high protein values, both in terms of quantity (up to 70% of dry weight) and quality (with all 9 essential amino acids). 
The company's development is focused on the design of independent breeding modules to enable a system of protein self-production by the circular economy policies promoted by the European Union.
In addition, from 2020 the company is increasingly specializing in projects related to the engineering development of insect breeding; through application in a European CoRoSect project (Horizon 2020) and the continued development of insect breeding modules for future human space colonies.

entityDescription:
The Bambino Gesù Paediatric Hospital (OPBG) is a Scientific Institute for Research, Hospitalization and Health Care and an Academic Medical Center. It is Italy’s main paediatric Hospital and provides third level health care for children while performing basic, clinical and translational research activities. OPBG is part of the Italian National Healthcare System and is widely recognized as referral centre for all paediatrics specialties at national and international level. 
The Hospital provides a complete range of healthcare services to children. OPBG has a total permanent staff of aprox 2,500, of which 550 physicians, 45 biologists and pharmacists, involved both in clinical and in research activities. OPBG has a research staff on a non-permanent position of 180. There are also aprox 50 post-graduate trainees (medical and surgical) and over 100 students and interns. 
The hospital has developed a true "Bambino Gesù System" that stretches beyond the regions of Rome and Lazio, establishing itself as a national and international centre of excellence. The historical location at Gianicolo, in Rome, has become the hub of a new multi-centred hospital extending beyond regional boundaries to meet the healthcare needs of children from all over southern Italy.Equally important are the international missions in developing countries. Today the Bambino Gesù is active in 12 countries, with the goal of providing care and passing on its experience in the poorest areas of the world.

Clinical activities consist of aprox 29.000 inpatient admissions, over 44,000 day hospital admissions, more than 4,800 day surgery treatments and more than 2,100,000 outpatient visits. 
Clinical activities are organised around 10 departments:
- University-Hospital Paediatric Department
- Specialist Paediatric Department
- Department of Laboratories 
- Medical-Surgical Department of Paediatric Cardiology
- Department of Medical and Surgical Neonatology
- Department of Neurosciences and Neurorehabilitation
- Oncohaematology and Cellular and Gene Therapy
- Surgical Department
- Imaging Department 
- Department of Emergency Admissions and Anaesthesiology/Resuscitation/Operating Rooms

entityDescription: Three o’clock is a service design company specialized in the mobility and energy sectors in urban areas. Cities were not originally designed with users in mind. More collaborative approaches need to be applied to reduce cities’ complexities, reimagine its services (be it mobility, housing, education or health) and to tackle climate change and inequalities. To succeed today, we need to understand and listen to people's needs to create the best experience for them. We do this in 3 steps:​ 1. ​We help organisations design and test products and services that create the most value for their users and are as efficient as possible for their business.​ How? By co-creating value propositions, business models and experiences based on user and market​ insights. We also help them boost their market uptake and support the scaleup to enter new markets.​ 2. We get the right messages out to engage users and build strong communities through communication, outreach, dialogue and shared decision-making.​ 3. We help organisations learn methods and apply tools to ideate and design new products & services with a new mindset through challenges, innovation camps, intrapreneurship programs. All supported with our very own Sprintbox.​ We are a social enterprise. entityDescription:
Established in November 2018, D-Flight, the Italian Public Private Partnership constituted by ENAV S.p.A. and Leonardo S.p.A., Telespazio S.p.A. for the development and deployment of U-space services. Through D-Flight, ENAV aims to bring together traditional air traffic with the specific needs of a new type of air traffic, allowing the use of drones for a growing number of services, while guaranteeing maximum safety standards at the same time.D-Flight staff includes operational and technical skills and expertise in UAS Traffic Management and ATM. 
D-Flight already deployed services in Italy to support an initial Italian U-space implementation. Primary goal of D-Flight platform is to bridge authorities and operators to enable safe and secure drone operations into the airspace.D-flight already developed U-space solutions that allow spacing among all drone operations in strategic manner (i.e. planning and strategic deconfliction) and monitoring of compliance of drone operation with authorized volume (tracking and monitoring). Moreover, it is possible to inform/alert in case of contingency/emergency situations the involved actors (tactical geofencing, emergency management, collaborative interface with ATC). D-Flight platform is available on the market as a product that can be customized or ready to further developments to meet relevant and specific regulations or innovation.

entityDescription:
The Italian National Institute of Statistics, a public research organisation, is the main producer of official statistics in the service of citizens and policy-makers. It operates in complete independence and continuous interaction with the academic and scientific communities.
The history of Istat starts in 1926, when the Central Institute of Statistics was created under law n. 1162: the idea of statistics as a tool for understanding phenomena started to grow along with the conviction that all surveys should be carried out by a single independent body.
Since 1989 Istat has been performing the role of directing, coordinating, and providing technical assistance and training within the National Statistical System (Sistan).
The modernisation programme, launched in 2016, aims to enrich the supply and quality of the information produced, while improving the effectiveness and efficiency of overall activity.

entityName: Budapest University of Technology and Economics - Department of Aeronautics and Naval Architecture
entityDescription:
The Department of Aeronautics and Naval Architecture was established more than 70 years ago as Department of Aircraft. Today it has 19 full time teaching-researcher staff of which 12 has PhD degrees. The Department delivers lecture on BSC, MSc and PhD levels including the fundamental sciences (fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, numerical methods, numerical optimisation, etc.) and the professional subjects on specialisation in aeronautics, air transportation,
ATM, pilot training, naval architecture and railway vehicles. There research and teaching infrastructure includes several laboratories (fluid and thermal machines, UAS lab and workshop, CFD lab and training centre, advanced instrumentation lab) and is also equipped with full size flight simulators for scientific purposes (with B737 and A320 controls in left and right seats), Mechatronix Ascent FNTP II flight simulator applied in the pilot training program, small computer controlled gas turbine, small water channel, load and test bench, track qualification vehicles, thermal cameras, motion capture system, and several others.
The Department has been involved in more than 25 EU supported projects including the SESAR and CleanSky megaprojects, the EPATS, SAT-Rdmp, Sinbad, Pplane, Esposa, Neli, Innovate, SmartPolis, several national projects, including SafeFly – developing small 4 seater aircraft, and Idea-e, working on the conceptual design of small 4-seater electric aircraft and large cargo hybrid UAV. The Department was also involved in developing design for various yachts (such as the special demonstration yacht Penelope), and aircraft including the leading advisory role in the development of the Corvus Racer for the Red Bull AirRace.
The leading staff members served as project coordinators and project managers for the L1 level Gabriel project which developed the maglev supported take-off and landing of undercarriage-less aircraft. This project was managed to finish in the planned time frame without any changes in the
defined description of work. The Department members have significant experience in international conference organisation, and work with high level international bodies, such as the International Forum for Aviation Research (IFAR). The department has a long term and successful working relationship many European universities, institutions and companies, including DLR, ONERA, CIRA, NLR, TU München, Aachen, Delft, HungaroControl, Knorr-Bremse, Siemens, and several
others. The department has strong skills in concept exploration, operational concept development, developing disruptive technologies and solutions and the combination of engineering solutions with economic and innovation aspects. Staff members are publishing 35 – 40 articles yearly.

entityName: TUM - CHAIR OF SCIENTIFIC COMPUTING IN COMPUTER SCIENCE (SCCS)
entityDescription: “The most scientifically important and economically promising research frontiers in the 21st century will be conquered by those most skilled with advanced computing technologies and computational science applications.” This central statement from the 2005 President’s IT Advisory Committee report from the US also outlines the chair’s focus fields in research and teaching: the algorithmics of scientific and high-performance computing as well as applications of numerical simulation. The spectrum extends from efficient numerical algorithms (discretization of partial differential equations, fast linear solvers, high-dimensional numerics, sparse grids, image processing, adaptivity, and hardware-awareness) via parallel and distributed computing (parallel algorithms, parallelization, load balancing, and Grid computing) as well as the embedding of simulation tasks up to simulation scenarios from various fields (fluid dynamics, fluid-structure interaction, chemical engineering, traffic, finance, or quantum chemistry). Our research projects, due to the tasks’ complexity, are typically tackled in multi-disciplinary cooperation and, thus, cover almost the entire simulation pipeline.

entityDescription:
Applied Science International, LLC is dedicated to “Changing the Known Built World” by bringing an advanced level of scientific inquiry to the examination, analysis, and study of structures for a safer world. During the past decade ASI has been arduously working to bring a new, more advanced method of structural analysis to the forefront. Called The Applied Element Method(AEM) , the approach is superior to its predecessor, the Finite Element Method (FEM). By allowing for the automatic initiation of cracks and the separation of elements, AEM provides a crucial, unparalleled capability for analyzing the safety and security of structures subjected to a catastrophic load. 
Born out of this effort, one that would allow engineers to more clearly analyze the stability of structural designs, ASI proudly introduces Extreme Loading® Technology (ELT). Positively affecting the design and analysis of structures, ELT is the culmination of the combined efforts of leading scientists and engineers in the implementation of AEM. entityDescription:
Bauhaus Luftfahrt e.V. has been founded in 2005 as an independent non-profit research institution for long term research in aviation by the three aerospace companies EADS (today Airbus Group), Liebherr-Aerospace and MTU Aero Engines as well as the Bavarian Ministry for Economic Affairs. In January 2012, IABG-Industrieanlagen-Betriebsgesellschaft became the latest member of the institution.
The non-profit institution is an internationally-oriented think tank. The team of around 35 scientists deals with the future of mobility in general and with the future of air travel in particular. The goal of the research work is to consider the complex system of aviation from different points of view. Reserach projects are aimed to consider technical, economic, social and ecological aspects holistically. Researchers from a variety of domains and expertise areas are jointly working on novel technologies, concepts and processes which could change the way aviation is operated in the coming decades.
The current strategy has put the focus on strengthening the five leading themes:
 „Visionary Aircraft Concepts“,
 „Ecological Perspectives of Aviation, Sustainability and Alternative Energies“,
 „Future Technologies and Innovation PotentialsInnovation Potentials“,
 „Socio-economic and Political Drivers of Future Aviation“, and
 „Knowledge Management“.
Along those leading themes, Bauhaus Luftfahrt achieved worldwide recognition and to became a nucleus for international research networks with the main focus on the first three themes.
The following key objectives were pursued in the research work at Bauhaus Luftfahrt in the past years:
- Development of concepts for innovative solutions and their implementation roadmaps,
- Publication of results in the form of conference contributions and journal articles as well as
- Organization of scientific conferences, seminars and workshops
- Generation of intellectual properties and patents.

entityDescription:
The IDF is a public/private partnership led by the insurance industry and supported by international organisations. The IDF was conceived and proposed at a meeting of the Political Champions Group for Disaster Resilience (PCG) on the margins of the UN General Assembly in 2013. A Task Force was formed and produced a detailed Concept Note that outlined its need, purpose and potential operation. It was first announced at the United Nations Conference of the Parties (COP21) Paris Climate summit in 2015 and was officially launched by leaders of the United Nations, the World Bank and the insurance industry in 2016.

The IDF is on a mission to optimise and extend the use of insurance and its related risk management capabilities to build greater resilience and protection for people, communities, businesses, and public institutions that are vulnerable to disasters and their associated economic shocks. Having started as a forum with membership from all sectors, in June 2020 it also launched a legal entity (registered in the UK) to conduct its operational activities. Most notably these activities include the Tripartite Agreement, a joint programme with the German government and UNDP through which access to risk understanding and risk transfer mechanisms will be accelerated in 20 vulnerable countries. 
The role of insurance in the Sustainable Development Goals: Evidence proves that countries with greater penetration of insurance coverage have faster economic recoveries from disasters, and rebuild with greater resilience to future disasters. Research shows that a 1% increase in insurance penetration can reduce the disaster recovery burden on taxpayers by up to 22%. A key goal of the UN Agenda 2030 is to take a risk-based approach to manage the risks of extreme events and climate. Within the frameworks that form the UN Agenda 2030, including the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), insurance is explicitly recognised as a key vehicle to enable the risk sharing and transfer solutions required for greater global resilience.

entityDescription:
Founded in 1971, theCNA di Brescia– the Italian Confederation of Craft Trades and Small- and Medium-Sized Enterprises –hasover 4,000members in Brescia. The CNA represents artisans, business owners, professionals, the self-employed and small and micro businesses in the tourism, services and industrial sectors. T
A presence that guarantees services, consultancy and information with credibility and professionalism, fully aware of the active role it plays in the success of small businesses and the development of a segment which continues to create jobs and new businesses on its own. The CNA comprises10 national unions: CNA Food, CNA Artistic and Traditional trades, CNA Wellbeing and Health, CNA Communication and Advanced Services, CNA Construction, CNA Federmoda (Fashion), CNA FITA (Transport), CNA Installation and Systems, CNA Production, CNA Community Services. There are45 subcategoriesand 5 interest groups: CNA Youth Enterprise and CNA Women’s Enterprise. 
CNA represents and protectsthe interests of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises operating in the manufacturing, construction, services, transport, trade and tourism sectors, small and medium-sized industries, and in general the world of businesses and relative associated forms, with particular reference to the crafts sector; of artisans, self-employed, different types of professionals, male and female entrepreneurs, and of those who have retired.
The CNA works to raise the profile of the craft industry and small and medium-sized businesses, proposing itself as a partner for their development and promoting economic and social progress. This goal is pursued through a structured and widespread organisation, a system of companies that offers integrated services and personalised consultancy to businesses, a modern structure that provides its members with assistance, information and innovative solutions.
In addition, through its own DIH (Digital Innovation Hub) CNA supports SMEs in the digital transformation path through advices, training, opportunities for experimentation, and tools for the realization of innovative solutions
Promote the development of digital innovation with initiatives and projects to reinforce the level of knowledge and understanding of digital maturity in the Industry 4.0 reality. Building the future of SMEs, making it present. Raising awareness of the change towards the new digital era.
At national level the CNA represents the craft industry in numerous associations, bodies and institutions, including: CNEL (National Council for Economics and Labour), ICE (National Institute for Foreign Trade), INAIL (National Institute for Insurance against Accidents at Work), INPS (National Social Security Institute), Artigiancassa (credit institute for craft industry businesses), the National Register of Constructors, the National Register of Hauliers; it also forms part of committees and government ministry working groups. The CNA is also a founding member of:Fondartigianato(Inter-professional fund for continuous training),SANARTI(Supplementary Healthcare Fund For Craft Workers),EBNA(Bilateral national crafts association),Artifond(Supplementary pension fund for employees of the crafts sector) andPrevedi(Supplementary Pension Fund for Employees of Industrial and Artisan Businesses in Construction and Similar Sectors).

description:
O.C.E. Technology is a European company setup to develop products and services for high-reliability embedded systems. Its founders bring together many years’ engineering, academic and business experience developing successful hardware and software products. The company is supported by the Irish government and has strong cooperation with the European Space agency in the development of unique innovative products to improve productivity of embedded software developers.
The management team has an established track record in the successful development and sales of processor ICs and boards to large OEMs (Siemens, Intel) and the associated software and operating systems.
Located in south Dublin OCE’s products include software productivity tools for SPARC and ARM embedded processors, high-reliability system-on-chip (SOC) devices, system-in-package (SIP) memories, and satellite subsystems.
OCE, in cooperation with the European Space Agency (ESA), developed a SOC debug software tool and high-reliability category B operating system for the Space market. The requirements of this market are similar to those of other embedded system markets such as automotive and medical. The company has setup a global distribution network and is pursuing an aggressive expansion programme.
OCE’s quad-core rad-hard SPARC chip is the highest performance of its type commercially available and is already successfully flying on 15 satellites. In 2021 OCE launched a high performance rad-tolerant AI chip with quadcore ARM, and octa core GPU and neural network accelerator cores. OCE’s SIP process is one of only two similar processes in the world. OCE offers a custom SIP design service for companies wishing to produce proprietary OBCs or systems housed in a SIP package. OCE also offers a range of satellite subsystems with many years heritage.
