entityDescription:
STAM is a private engineering SME headquartered in Genoa, Italy, specializing in delivering advanced engineering services to industries worldwide. Initially supported by seed funding from the European Space Agency’s (ESA) Technology Transfer Programme to develop an innovative gearbox system, STAM has since expanded its expertise across multiple sectors, including defense, robotics, security and transport, energy, and environmental technologies. The company boasts a highly qualified workforce, with 90% holding at least a master’s degree and over 70% possessing an MSc in Engineering.
STAM has been a trusted collaborator of ESA since 1999, actively contributing to initiatives such as the Innovation Triangle Initiative and the Technology Transfer Programmes. Notable projects include its role as the main subcontractor in the ADRiNET project, which focused on developing a parametric simulator for active debris removal (ADR) using nets. This effort culminated in a successful parabolic flight campaign in Ottawa, Canada, validating the ADR concept. The technology was further enhanced through the EU’s H2020 ADR1EN Project, encompassing upscaling activities, thermal-vacuum testing at Thales Alenia Space Italy, full-scale ground experiments, and the creation of a comprehensive business plan for ADR systems.
STAM has also led ESA projects like “Hermetic Sealing for Rotating Shaft,” where it developed and tested innovative mechanical sealing solutions. More recently, STAM was named ESA’s National Technology Broker for Italy, tasked with driving technology transfer initiatives. This role involves technology scouting, promotional campaigns, and developing business models for high-potential use cases, helping research centers unlock the value of their intellectual property and facilitating spin-in and spin-off technology transfers between terrestrial and space applications. Through this role, STAM also manages ESA’s Spark Funding in collaboration with the Italian Space Agency (ASI).
As part of its contributions to ESA’s Space Rider program, STAM developed a business model emphasizing microgravity research in advanced materials, pharmaceuticals, and biotechnologies. The model bridges the current cost gap for space missions by leveraging intellectual property to attract private and institutional investors, fostering a venture-builder approach to innovation.
Thanks to its extensive portfolio of R&D projects, STAM has forged strong partnerships with hundreds of international companies and research institutions, including leading organizations and key stakeholders in the space sector.

entityDescription:
Terma provides mission-critical solutions for the aerospace, defense, and security industries, guided by one overarching purpose: Securing People through Advanced Technology. Our strength lies not only in engineering and manufacturing, but in our ability to apply these capabilities in complex operational environments, tailored to the specific needs of our customers. We are recognized for our expertise in mission-critical software, systems integration, and secure data transfer across domains. BUSINESS AREAS: Space designs and delivers electronics, software, and support services for satellites, control centre's, and testing systems. With strong heritage in European institutional programs, the Business Area is expanding into global New Space markets with increasing focus on defense. Terma continues to develop and deliver advanced Star Trackers and other critical satellite technologies, serving customers across Europe, the U.S., Asia Pacific, and the Middle East. Surveillance & Mission Systems delivers advanced radar and command-and-control (C2)technologies for single-domain operations – such as air defense and naval missions – as well as multi-domain scenarios involving intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance. The SCANTER radar family remains a core offering, particularly in coastal surveillance and port and airport traffic control. Radar applications for naval vessels continue to grow, including a milestone contract in 2024/25 with the Canadian Coast Guard for anew class of multi-purpose vessels. Terma also advanced its drone detection and classification capabilities using artificial intelligence, attracting strong interest from customers worldwide. The Business Area secured a key order from the Danish Ministry of Defence Acquisition and Logistics Organization for the BMD-Flex C2system and was appointed system integrator for Denmark’s new Very Short-Range Air Defense (VSHORAD) system. The growing demand for Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) further strengthens this Business Area’s strategic position. As the protection of vital infrastructure becomes an increasingly urgent priority for governments and private operators alike, Terma’s integrated radar and software solutions are uniquely suited to securing critical assets against evolving threats, from conventional intrusions to emerging challenges. This positions Surveillance& Mission Systems as a key enabler in the safeguarding of essential societal Infrastructure across land, sea, under water and air.
Self-Protection Systems provides integrated electronic warfare solutions for military aircraft, enhancing survivability through systems such as the ALQ-213 controller and Advanced Threat Displays. The Business Area also delivers Terma’s operationally proven 3D-Audio solution, improving aircrew situational awareness and reducing fatigue. In 2024/25, demand was at a record high, with continued traction across fighters, helicopters, mobility aircraft, and collaborative combat systems. Support & Services ensures high availability and lifecycle support for Terma solutions across civil and defense applications. With scalable maintenance offerings and the Terma Lifecare service portfolio, the Business Area provides everything from unit-level service to countrywide solutions. In 2024/25, Support & Services expanded its presence in the Middle East and Asia, introduced cyber-hardened radar solutions, and launched a new cybersecurity subscription model. The Business Area also initiated OEM support activities to meet growing regional demand and support defense procurement across Denmark and the Nordics.

entityDescription:
TeSA Lab (www.tesa.prd.fr ) is a private non-profit organisation, aiming at performing Research studies and PhD in Telecommunications for Space and Aeronautics, and in related domains.
This non-profit organisation acts as a Research Lab, with a Scientific Committee, wellcoming research engineers, academics from partner members, together with around 20 PhD students and post-docs. This collaborative Research Laboratory includes academic members from French universities (engineer schools) ENAC, ISAE-Supaero, INPT and IMT Atlantique, as well as industrial partners (Thales Alenia Space and Rockwell Collins France) and institutional partners as the French Space Agency (CNES), the Institute of Technology (IRT) Saint Exupery and the Air Navigation Services (DSNA).
TeSA is a structure unique in France, around which revolve various industrial, institutional and academic organizations. This has allowed it to develop for more than 10 years a practice in collaboration for applied research, with high efficiency and, whenever necessary, a guarantee of confidentiality.
The expertise of TeSA covers: 
•	digital communications: synchronisation, equalization, waveform modulation, source and channel coding, spectrum surveillance, MIMO systems,…
•	networks : transmission techniques, architectures, routing, multiple access, security,… 
•	signal and image processing : navigation and positioning, radar signal processing, estimation, detection and classification, fusion,…
in application domains such as 
•	space and aeronautical communication systems, 
•	Earth observation, 
•	localization and navigation.

entityDescription:
Avia-GIS NV is a Belgian SME founded in 2001 that specializes in spatial risk mapping and modelling as a basis for the development of tailored spatial decision support systems (SDSS) and software packages applied to public-, animal- and crop health in general and integrated pest and disease management (IPM) in particular. We focus on the development of state-of-the-art techniques that broaden the scope of conventional analyses, convert data into new insights and bridge the gap between research and decision-making including: mathematical and spatio-temporal modelling, monitoring via earth observation through satellites and drones, wireless IoT sensor networks, and satellite navigation. In addition to our Software Products for risk mapping and integrated pest management, we offer a range of Consulting and Contract Research services to the industry, international organisations, governmental agencies, and research teams. These include: development of vector and disease transmission models to test what-if scenarios and support clinical trials, development of tailored SDS Systems and mobile applications; coordination of multidisciplinary research projects and networks, and à la carte on-site / on-line training and capacity building. Avia-GIS was growing steadily since 2001 and invested most of its increasing resources in human capital. Our experts are specialised in environmental engineering, biology, entomology, meteorology, spatial epidemiology, spatial modelling and ICT. The company has a unique market position. Only few companies operate in our domain and none developed such close contacts with the academic, decision support and industrial world. As a result we have a clear view on user needs and requirements, on the state of the art, and on how this can be translated into cost-efficient operational tools.
Avia-GIS NV is a Belgian company that employs 15 highly skilled collaborators from five nationalities of which one is a resident entomologist in Guadeloupe.
In addition Avia-GIS is owner of an independent daughter company in South Africa, Avia-GIS RSA Ltd. This company is specialized in eco-friendly integrated pest management for the hospitality industry.

EFTAS is based in Muenster, Germany, and is recognized since its foundation in 1988 among the German leading companies providing services in the following domains: • EFTAS.geoinformation Remote Sensing, Photogrammetry, Geostatistics, Mapping and Field observations • EFTAS.gis IT-Architecture, GIS- and Interface Development • EFTAS.webmapps Routing, Web Services, Web portal- and App-Programming • EFTAS.evolution Research, Studies, Technology- and Market development • EFTAS.consult Process Optimization, Knowledge Transfer and Training. Its clients comprise communal, national and international authorities as well as those from private industry. Whether for small communes, international government institutions or up to international or European institutions, EFTAS realizes special solutions adapted to the need of its clients by means of Geospatial information technologies (GeoIT). The success of EFTAS is based on the high quality of its products and services as well as the performance of the interdisciplinary team of EFTAS. EFTAS has managed projects in many countries all over the world and is since 2002 the leading service provider in Germany for the IACS Control with Remote Sensing (CwRS) framework and since 2007 in Europe for EC LUCAS Area Frame Survey applications. Based on its key staff of 66 employees at the headquarter in Muenster, more than 100 freelance experts, and a wide network of longstanding cooperation’s with professional partners abroad EFTAS disposes on a network of knowledge with its sectoral, regional and technical competences which constitute a service company of international format. EFTAS has established since 1997 its Quality Management System, which has been certified according to the standard DIN EN ISO 9001:2008 under the registration number 041009574 by TÜV CERT of the RWTÜV association in Essen, Germany.

entityDescription: Axcon is an independent, privately owned development house located in Denmark. We focus on advanced electronics, programmable logic (FPGA), and embedded software - in simple terms, we work with electronics and the software that runs inside of electronic devices. Axcon has history of successful cooperation with ESA/ESTEC/ESOC with the LISA phase meter development and the LLCD/LLOCL/LADEE laser communication/ranging development. We have four main revenue streams: * On-site consulting. Our consultants work onsite for our clients to assist in various tasks. * Outsourced development. We take over a project for the client and return the full development package and working products ready for production. * Technical courses for developers, engineers, and project managers. * Modules for rapid prototyping. These modules are produced by English Sundance Multiprocessor Technologies. The Customers Our customers range from large, multinational corporations to small, enterprising startups. Most of our customers are Danish companies with a focus in electronics development or require electronics development for their products. We have contracts throughout Denmark as well as in neighboring countries and abroad. We have worked for companies in Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Germany, Austria, the USA, and we have even sent consultants to work abroad as far away as Korea. Products Axcon does not focus on developing our own products; rather, we focus on development contracts with regional and international corporations to create advanced solutions. Through a distribution agreement, we supply a range of advanced modules with FPGA, DSP, AD/DA technology. These modules are well-suited for rapid prototyping and small production series. Additional products provided include specific IP cores, software, and development systems. History Axcon was founded in 2004. We currently employ 12-15 predominatly engineers and we have partnerships with a large network of freelancers. Our employees work with our customers throughout Denmark as well as Denmark's neighboring countries. In 2009 Axcon was awarded the Danish "Gazelle Award" for exceeding 100% growth over a 5 year period. Management Axcon is owned by Anders Enggaard, who also is one of the two founders. Axcon was founded by two engineers with extensive backgrounds in electronics development and the international electronics community. Their expertise is focused in the American and Danish industries. Axcon is 100% self-financed and run without external ownership shares. Axcon is a private limited company.

entityDescription:
Top Modal is a Limited Liability Company (LLC) that offers studies, expertise, training and software tools in the field of structural dynamics since 2003. The goal of Top Modal is to provide solutions and know-how to the engineer so that he may solve his problems in the most efficient manner. As a small specialized company, Top Modal enjoys working in a close partnership with its customers – whether universities, engineering firms or industrial companies – spanning the aerospace, automotive, and marine fields
Top Modal is headed by Dr. Nicolas Roy, an expert in structural dynamics, optimization and robust design with over 30 years of industrial experience. With a M.S. from Caltech and Ph.D. from Penn State University, Dr. Roy worked at Lockheed Martin (Sunnyvale, CA) , ONERA (Toulouse) and Intespace (Toulouse) before founding Top Modal in 2003. Dr. Roy is also an instructor and lecturer at several universities and training centers in Europe and Asia, as well as co-author of the book Structural Dynamics in Industry available in English and French.

entityDescription:
EVOLEO Technologies, Lda. is a SME created in Jan 2007, investing in skills related to the design of critical and complex electronic systems. EVOLEO embraces four areas of activity:
•	Space (flight Hi-Reliability development, HW/SW, test and validation support activities)
•	Infrastructures (monitoring, knowledge extraction for decision support – railways/roads/energy)
•	Industry (quality control, test and automation systems)
•	Technology (specialized development of subsystems for 3rd party integration)

These four activity areas harmonise into three business areas:
•	Quality Support Systems (testing units for quality assessment labs, production lines)
•	Tangible Assets Management Support Solutions (solutions to monitor different kind of assets, providing management tools to the End User, to aid the decision-making process of investment or maintenance)
•	Technology (internal products for 3rd party integration or to embed into the other EVOLEO areas)

EVOLEO includes a skilled multidisciplinary engineering team seeking and promoting partnerships and networking between centres of knowledge and industry players, cooperating, among others, with European Space Agency (ESA), industry players and R&D groups, either National or International.

EVOLEO key skills are related to the design, build and integration of electronic embedded systems solutions for monitoring and data processing (Remote Interface Units). Those include integrated intelligence SW (embedded) for local data pre-processing or simply as transmitters of collected data to a central server.

EVOLEO has also skills in the implementation of multi-core systems (e.g. on FPGA) and has developed under an ESA project its own Computer Unit and its on-board controlling SW for a satellite payload control with LEON3 processor and real time OS RTEMS, involving key players of the computing solutions such Aeroflex Gaisler in Sweden. In other areas (framework of FP7 or national programs) the company integrates multiple data systems (vibrations, GPS, communications, data bases), apply data fusion to create operational SW tools to deal with the overall system and algorithms.

As fields of expertise one can refer:
On-Board Data Systems - Payload Data Processing, On Board Data Management, Microelectronics for digital and analogue applications
Space System Software (Space Segment Software, Ground Segment Software, Ground Data Processing)
Spacecraft Electrical Power (Power conditioning and distribution)
System Design & verification (Collaborative and Concurrent Engineering, System Analysis and Design, Verification & AIT)
Quality, Dependability and Safety (System Dependability and Safety)

EVOLEO provides engineering services covering a wide range of needs in the electronics design, embedded and systems engineering.
Design and Implementation of Analogue HW(Project, CAD, WCA, PSA, FMEA/FMECA)
Design and Implementation of Digital HW (Project, CAD, FPGA, µC/µP 8-32 bit - simple and multi-core over FPGA, VHDL and C)
SW Implementation for Embedded Systems (Real time operating systems, NI LabView platform, Windows or Linux environment)
Instrumentation, Automation and Control (PLCs, National Instruments technology)
Systems Engineering (Support to systems integration & validation)
Quality and Development Process (Support to ESA-ECSS standards)

entityDescription:
The Centro Studi Demetra (Development of European Mediterranean Transportation) is the Association born in 2006 by the commitment of exponents of the academic, entrepreneurial and institutional world with the aim to encourage, in Italy, initiatives regarding formative, legal, administrative and economic aspects in the transport sector, with particular regards to the civil aviation.
The experience matured in these first four years of activity has run the Association to elaborate on the new frontier of the community politic in the innovation technology and ecologic sector, main themes of great interest and in continuous evolution. These themes have to be analyzed with particular attention to the security and have to be matched with the evolution of others sectors as the aerospace and the microlight.
Demetra establishes oneself as authoritative cultural reference of the civil aviation environment, that extends from the microlight to the space, achieving important recognitions, among which, the actual audition within the cognitive investigation on the Italian airport system conducted by the transports, mails and telecommunications Committee of the Chamber of the deputies.
The Centro Studi Demetra performs specialist popularization activities and, for this goal, it organizes conferences, seminars and lectures tense to promote the debate on the aerial transport politic, creating occasions of comparison among the political and academic referents, the maximum institutional authorities, the entrepreneurial vertexes, the most accredited experts to deepen, in particular, the problems of the sector connected to the consequential transformations derived by the liberalization and privatization of the system and the relative adjustment of the community legislation rules. 
Besides, for several months now the Centro Studi Demetra entertains, near its head office in Rome, the meetings of the work plan on the "Regulation" that the Agusta Westland, with the collaboration of The European House Ambrosetti, has started, within the study on "The development of the aerial transport to vertical take-off in the context of a state-of-the-art mobility system for the Country", with the final purpose to define, in sight of the future EXPO 2015, the premises normative for a middle-long term plan of infrastructures and heliports able to allow the necessary development of the mobility through the means vertical take-off.
Within its activities, Demetra also occupy oneself with the education and the refresher training of its members representatives besides the meetings that are periodically held near its center.
The Demetra publishing project will lead to the publication of a "Aerial transport code¿, consistent in a selection of the national and community legislation, of extreme utility for the sector stakeholders they daily have to consult the numerous and various normative sources that discipline the aerial transport.

entityDescription: UHI North West and Hebrides is an institute of further and higher education which offers both full time and part time programmes. The three main college campuses are located in Thurso, Fort William and Stornoway with a number of smaller campuses around the region providing access for students and staff across a large geographical area. In addition a network of electronically linked learning centres allows UHI North West and Hebrides to reach learners in remote areas, meet the needs of employers, and support local economic activity and development. UHI North West and Hebrides is an academic partner of the University of the Highlands and Islands (UHI), a unique partnership of colleges and research institutions across the Highlands and Islands of Scotland. Each college and research institution has its own distinctive character and strengths. This means that students of UHI can share in the educational advantages of a larger institution whilst benefiting from the personal attention which a smaller college, like UHI North West and Hebrides, can provide. UHI North West and Hebrides hosts three prestigious research centres - the Environmental Research Institute (Thurso) and the UHI Centre for History (Dornoch) and the Centre for Recreation and Tourism (Fort William). All centres support the educational and economic development of the area, with research focussed on contemporary environmental and societal issues, and the role of heritage tourism. The UHI North West and Hebrides is a registered charity for purposes of 'advancing education'. Scottish Charity registration number SC02125

entityDescription: TreeMetrics has developed a faster, more accurate and more effective forest measurement and harvest optimisation system. The company offering is aimed at forest owners and sawmillers to enable more efficient harvest operations resulting in greater timber yields and improved profits. This innovative technology based system provides a better method of matching standing forest areas to sawmills requirements. This significantly reduces the volume of trees that need to be felled, thus reducing wastage and increasing profits. From 2007 and 2009 the company completed paid proving trials with major forests owners around Europe. These trials have proved the accuracy and value proposition of the TreeMetrics system. Numerous resultant scientific papers have been published in industry journals by the project partners. From 2010 the company began industrial level contract with 3 major forest growers to prove the ability of the company to deliver consistent accuracy and value over large harvest areas. entityDescription: S.A.B. Aerospace Srl is a private and independent SME operating in the Space Business since 2004. The company core business is focused in the development of mechanical systems, sub-systems and mechanisms related to Launchers, Satellites and Payloads. SAB has been and is currently involved in several projects related to launchers through contracts awarded by ELV, ESA and ARIANESPACE for the development of items such as Adapters, Systems for Payload Multiple launch, Separation Systems and Test apparatus for shock testing. SAB is currently responsible (on behalf of Arianespace) for the Shock testing services executed with the VESTA (VEga Shock Test Apparatus) tool on the payloads to be embarked on the VEGA launcher. Moreover SAB has participated to launch campaigns and is familiar with rules implemented by ESA in the launch space port in French Guyana. Satellite activities performed by SAB Aerospace are linked to the partnership established in 2010 with OHB System AG and they range from Platform Mechanical Design Development to Mechanical Integration of Satellites including as well MGSE Design and Manufacturing. SAB Aerospace is performing activities for the development of Optical Payloads and Equipments sub-system in terms of Thermo-mechanical Design, Structures manufacturing, Integration and Environmental Testing. The above mentioned activities are supported by research program developed in cooperation with a network of research centers for the study of technologies such as Laser Welding Technology, Separation System Technologies, Thermal Control Systems, Advanced Ceramics and Light Alloys. The company headquarter is in Benevento, an area considered one of the Italian poles concerning aeronautical and aerospace business. In the headquarter S.A.B. Aerospace concentrates all the activities related to Manufacturing, Assembly/Integration and Testing. All the engineering and R/D activities are based in the Ancona office, while a third office is in Milan for Business Development and Marketing. The SAB internal facilities comprises: - An Integration facility built inside a 100000 class clean room facility and equipped with a 1ton lifting crane for the handling of the different parts and assembled systems. - The Vibration test facility is composed by a 49KN electrodynamics shaker mounted in the clean room described above. - A four axes milling machines used to manufacture space components made up of Aluminum, Invar and Peek. In addition SAB can rely on a manufacturer network for manufacturing of complex mechanical structures.

entityDescription:
The University of Nova Gorica is an institution of higher education that provides undergraduate and graduate study programs and conducts scientific research.

It started in 1995 as the School of Environmental Sciences, the first international graduate school in Slovenia, founded by the Municipality of Nova Gorica and the Jozef Stefan Institute of Ljubljana. Due to the introduction of new study programs and the expansion of scientific research activities, the School was reorganized in 1998 and renamed Nova Gorica Polytechnic. In 2006 the institution changed its status and became the University of Nova Gorica. Its founders are the Municipality of Nova Gorica, the Municipality of Ajdovscina and Jozef Stefan Institute from Ljubljana. 

Today the University of Nova Gorica provides education at seven schools: School of Science, School of Environmental Sciences, School of Engineering and Management, School of Humanities, School of Viticulture and Enology, School of Arts, and the Graduate School, which offers the following doctoral study programs: Environmental Sciences, Physics, Karstology, Comparative Studies of Ideas and Cultures, Linguistics, Molecular Genetics and Biotechnology and Economics and Techniques for the Conservation of the Architectural and Environmental Heritage.

Research is conducted at twelve laboratories and centers (Center for Astrophysics and Cosmology, Laboratory for organic matter physics, Laboratory for multiphase processes, Laboratory for Environmental Research, Materials research laboratory, Laboratory for quantum optics, Center for Atmospheric Research, Center for Biomedical Sciences and Engineering, Center for Cognitive Science of Language, Center for Systems and Information Technologies, Research Center for Humanities and Wine Research Center.

entityDescription:
Istituto Superiore per la Protezione e la Ricerca Ambientale (ISPRA, eng: Italian Institute for Environmental Protection and Research), has been established by Legislative Decree no. 112 of 25 June 2008, converted into Law no. 133 (with amendments) on 21 August 2008. is a Public research body acting under the vigilance of the Italian Ministry of Environment and Energy Security, and provided with technical, scientific, organizational, managerial, administrative and financial autonomy. ISPRA performs scientific and technological research applied to environmental protection as well as assessment, monitoring, control, communication, training and education activities. The main activities are related to environmental characterization, monitoring and reporting with respect to prevention, evaluation and mitigation of impacts, quality of the environment, habitats and biodiversity; stainable use of resources.
ISPRA coordinates the National System of Environment Protection Agencies (SNPA -21 environmental agencies of the Italian regions and autonomous provinces), ensuring the exchange of information and expertise on environmental monitoring, control and inspections, connecting scientific knowledge communities with environmental administrators and policy makers at national and local level.
ISPRA performs the function of the Geological Service of Italy, of National Focal Point of EEA/EIONET and of UNEP/MAP INFO-RAC.
ISPRA experts are fully engaged, in support of the Italian Ministry of the Environment, in several technical working groups for the implementation of EU directives and regulations (e.g. Habitats, Birds, Invasive Alien Species, Water, MSFD, INSPIRE, Air Quality, Waste, REACH and others).

entityDescription: The Consorzio Futuro in Ricerca (CFR) was established in 1993. It is a private non-profit organization, with public and private participation, aimed at the promotion, development and enhancement of human, scientific, technological and economic resources .The CFR promotes and manages research and innovation through projects carried out in collaboration with universities, research centres, public entities, industrial companies, in Italy and abroad, as well as linking know-how generators, industrial organizations and the working world.CFR chiefly activates in the field of precompetitive research and technological transfer for industrial application. Its activity is complementary to the institutional actions taken by the University of Ferrara, member of the consortium, evaluating its technical-scientific and human competences.The institutional activities assumed by CFR consist in the conclusion and technical-administrative management of research contracts, the coordination of scientific manifestations, and the organisation of educational events on behalf of public and private companies on a local, national or international scale.During its more than twenty years of business, the CFR has received orders with more than 800 national and international public and private buyers, subscribing to more than 5000 contracts for a total value of over 145 million Euros.CFR is committed to promoting and activating research contracts and agreements with companies, industry, small and medium-sized businesses and public administration regarding the following areas: protection of the environment, food technologies and biotechnology; architectural innovation, urban economics, and restoration technology; technology of polymers and innovative materials; innovations in engineering, data processing, electronic, energetic, pharmaceutical, physical, chemical, mathematical, geological, mineralogical and biological technologies; linguistic innovations, musical and multimedia technologies; economic, juridical, and organisational analysis.CFR provides information on current research programmes run by the laboratories of the members of the consortium, it provides information and support for the realisation of tests, analysis and certification at the laboratories of members of the consortium or of third parties, it provides support to draft contracts and agreements with public or private institutions, support for the organisation and management and/or immediate organisation and management of Master courses, courses of further education, of vocational retraining and professional further training, also by means of specific scholarships, doctoral research scholarships and post-doctoral scholarships.CFR provides support to the companies in terms of advanced technologies by offering advice and services; it creates and/or participates in auxiliary societies which may also be profit societies in order to carry out certain activities (organisation of conferences, technical-administrative spin-off management, etc.); it promotes cooperation agreements also on an international scale between research institutions and industrial companies.CFR takes care of coordinating all the activities involved in the participation and management of the various types of intervention, from the administrative part to the entire organisation of the project itself. In particular, it not only takes care to identify the opportunities of participation at the various financing programmes, but it is also committed to: communicating the information gathered; preparing the required documentation and finally forwarding it to the determined institutional organs; writing the necessary press coverage.In order to promote and evaluate research results and in order to develop scientific and business culture CFR plans and organizes events on a national and international scale.

Its activity is complementary to the institutional actions taken by the University of Ferrara, member of the consortium, evaluating its technical-scientific and human competences.The institutional activities assumed by CFR consist in the conclusion and technical-administrative management of research contracts, the coordination of scientific manifestations, and the organisation of educational events on behalf of public and private companies on a local, national or international scale.During its more than twenty years of business, the CFR has received orders with more than 800 national and international public and private buyers, subscribing to more than 5000 contracts for a total value of over 145 million Euros.CFR is committed to promoting and activating research contracts and agreements with companies, industry, small and medium-sized businesses and public administration regarding the following areas: protection of the environment, food technologies and biotechnology; architectural innovation, urban economics, and restoration technology; technology of polymers and innovative materials; innovations in engineering, data processing, electronic, energetic, pharmaceutical, physical, chemical, mathematical, geological, mineralogical and biological technologies; linguistic innovations, musical and multimedia technologies; economic, juridical, and organisational analysis.CFR provides information on current research programmes run by the laboratories of the members of the consortium, it provides information and support for the realisation of tests, analysis and certification at the laboratories of members of the consortium or of third parties, it provides support to draft contracts and agreements with public or private institutions, support for the organisation and management and/or immediate organisation and management of Master courses, courses of further education, of vocational retraining and professional further training, also by means of specific scholarships, doctoral research scholarships and post-doctoral scholarships.CFR provides support to the companies in terms of advanced technologies by offering advice and services; it creates and/or participates in auxiliary societies which may also be profit societies in order to carry out certain activities (organisation of conferences, technical-administrative spin-off management, etc.); it promotes cooperation agreements also on an international scale between research institutions and industrial companies.CFR takes care of coordinating all the activities involved in the participation and management of the various types of intervention, from the administrative part to the entire organisation of the project itself. In particular, it not only takes care to identify the opportunities of participation at the various financing programmes, but it is also committed to: communicating the information gathered; preparing the required documentation and finally forwarding it to the determined institutional organs; writing the necessary press coverage.In order to promote and evaluate research results and in order to develop scientific and business culture CFR plans and organizes events on a national and international scale.

Our high standard of interdisciplinary research and education respond to global challenges and build a sustainable future. Our research is ranked among the best in the world in several fields. Our campuses are located in the cities of Joensuu and Kuopio.

entityDescription:
TRANSVALOR S.A. was created in 1984 to transfer to the industry and valorise the research results of the Mines ParisTech science labs. Transvalor´s main shareholder is ARMINES.
Initially, Transvalor specialized as a scientific software editor and obtained an international commercial success with software in the material forming simulation domain. In early 2009, Transvalor created Transvalor Innovation, a department to promote further the transfer and valorisation activity for all the research labs of MINES ParisTech. One dedicated 5-person team (of which three are doctors) in Transvalor Innovation is working with the O.I.E. (Observation Impacts Energy - http://www.oie.mines-paristech.fr) MINES ParisTech research lab on the industrialisation, valorisation and commercialisation of the HelioClim solar irradiation databases, the SoDa web site and all type of value added activity in the solar resource domain.
Today, the SoDa web site (www.soda-pro.com) registers more than 76 000 unique visitors per year. Over 135 millions of requests of irradiation data through WGET service were fulfilled in 2018. The SoDa web site hosts also the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) solar radiation products access.
Transvalor Innovation has participated and continues to participate to several R&D programs with the Mines ParisTech-ARMINES/O.I.E centre and/or the DLR. Within these R&D programs, its main role is to integrate products as web services (WFS and WPS) or as value added services, to build and maintain the hardware/software infrastructure needed to operate these services and to disseminate/distribute these services to a large panel of customers/stakeholders.
More than 70 customers have an annual subscription service with Transvalor to obtain solar irradiation data from the SoDa web site. In the recent years, we have delivered various services and/or data to several hundreds of different companies.

entityName: CZECH UNIVERSITY OF LIFE SCIENCES PRAGUE
entityDescription:
Czech University of Life Sciences Prague (CZU) is a public higher education institution offering study programs at the Bachelor, Master, and Doctoral levels. At present, 20,500 students, including 10,229 females and 5,660 international students, are enrolled in daily and combined forms of study across 297 study programs, with 155 taught entirely in English. CZU employs approximately 1,600 staff members, including more than 800 academic staff, such as professors, associate professors, senior researchers, and lecturers.
Research at CZU focuses on environmental, biological, agricultural, socio-economic, and technical topics, with faculties and departments actively participating in research projects funded by Czech national grant agencies such as the Czech Science Foundation, The National Agency for Agriculture Research, and the Technology Agency of the Czech Republic, as well as international grant agencies such as Horizon Europe, Erasmus, LIFE, COST, and OECD. CZU manages around 400 research projects annually, with approximately one-third being international collaborations. The university is currently implementing up to 50 Horizon Europe projects, further strengthening its role in European research and innovation.
As a leading institution in life sciences, CZU is an active member of several prestigious international organizations, including the Euroleague for Life Sciences (ELLS), the Association for European Life Science Universities (ICA), the Danube Rector’s Conference (DRC), the Central and South Eastern Europe ICA Regional Network (CASEE), AGRINATURA – The European Alliance on Agricultural Knowledge for Development, and the European University Association (EUA).
CZU maintains a gender-balanced environment in accordance with EU requirements, as established in its Gender Equality Plan (GEP) and supported by the HR Award, ensuring an inclusive and diverse academic and research environment.

The university is currently implementing up to 50 Horizon Europe projects, further strengthening its role in European research and innovation.
As a leading institution in life sciences, CZU is an active member of several prestigious international organizations, including the Euroleague for Life Sciences (ELLS), the Association for European Life Science Universities (ICA), the Danube Rector’s Conference (DRC), the Central and South Eastern Europe ICA Regional Network (CASEE), AGRINATURA – The European Alliance on Agricultural Knowledge for Development, and the European University Association (EUA).
CZU maintains a gender-balanced environment in accordance with EU requirements, as established in its Gender Equality Plan (GEP) and supported by the HR Award, ensuring an inclusive and diverse academic and research environment.

entityDescription: Łukasiewicz Research Network - Krakow Institute of Technology (in Polish: Sieć Badawcza Łukasiewicz - Krakowski Instytut Technologiczny) was established on April 1, 2020 as a result of the merger of two Krakow institutes included in the Łukasiewicz Research Network: the Foundry Research Institute and the Institute of Advanced Manufacturing Technologies. Together, the two institutes, with decades of tradition and experience, have created a strong unit capable of taking on new challenges in development directions crucial for the Łukasiewicz Research Network, i.e. health, intelligent mobility, sustainable economy and energy, and digital transformation of strategic importance for the Polish economy. The headquarters of Łukasiewicz - Krakow Institute of Technology is located at ul. Zakopiańska 73. The Institute employs 208 employees, including research department employees, engineers and support department employees. The Institute has specialized equipment for conducting research on a laboratory scale as well as on a semi-industrial scale. There are four Centers in the structure: the Center for Casting Technology, the Center for Advanced Manufacturing Technologies, the Material Processing Center and the Material Research Center, in which the key team of the research department responsible for generating innovative solutions for the Polish economy is concentrated. The recipients of solutions developed at the Institute are representatives of the foundry, tooling, aviation, medical, energy and many other industries. The Institute also offers commercial services carried out mainly at the Center of Research Laboratories (including Accredited Laboratories), as well as by the Certification and Standardization Bureau. The Institute also has a production department focusing on the design and manufacture of production lines for the packaging industry. Łukasiewicz - Kraków Institute of Technology conducts interdisciplinary research covering both classical and modern technologies of material production and processing. The Institute develops 3D printing technologies based on metals, plastics and ceramics, and also manufactures materials and tools for the advanced technology industry. Other research areas of the Institute include the design and manufacture of materials for electromobility, including fuel cells, the production and processing of composite and nanocomposite materials for special applications, and the development of robotization and automation of processes in line with the assumptions of Industry 4.0. In the near future, scientists of the Łukasiewicz - Krakow Institute of Technology will also undertake work in the field of designing material solutions and production technology for the renewable energy industry, including offshore wind energy and the domestic photovoltaic sector, and the corrosion research area will be expanded to include biocorrosion and corrosion in the chloride environment. The high level of work carried out at the Institute guarantees cooperation with numerous scientific and research centers in the world, including joint research projects, participation in scientific conferences, exchange of personnel and valuable experience in the field of research and implementation.

entityDescription:
Hertz Systems has been operating for over 34 years (including ownership transformations) providing end to end solutions – from design to manufacturing, assembly, integration, testing and training. We provide hardware and software solutions for the military, government and European institutions, and the as well as private sector. Hertz Systems is located in western part of Poland (Zielona Góra, close to Berlin).
For almost 20 years the company has been active on the military market developing satellite navigation receivers integrated with crypto modules. Hertz Systems devices are dedicated for various combat vehicles and other military platforms requiring precise and reliable PVT. More than 2,000 of our receivers have been delivered to the Polish Armed Forces. Work is currently underway on receivers integrated with M-Code and GALILEO modules.
Hertz Systems also executes space projects related to, among others, GNSS systems for downstream applications as well as sensors for space. The entity holds Security Accreditation Board authorization to access PRS technology and aims to manufacture PRS receivers in Poland. Furthermore, the entity provides testing and validation services for satellite modules, it is also equipped with SimPRS software enabling generation of real PRS signals.
Hertz Systems also specializes in systems ensuring safety of critical infrastructure (Hawk system for detection and neutralization of drones) and critical data (TEMPEST equipment). The aim of the Hawk system is to detect the drone before invading the protected area, track it in real time and bring it to the ground or neutralize it in the air. The system generates and automatic alert in the event of intrusion into the guarded zone and effectively neutralizes the intruder.
The company declares its expertise in project management at all TRL levels and project phases (from design through manufacturing till market introduction), practical knowledge in software and hardware for GNSS applications, access to Electromagnetic Compatibility Laboratory and professional equipment/software.
Hertz Systems is a highly trusted partner, which is confirmed by various licenses and certificates. Implemented Quality Management System complies with standards of PN EN ISO 9001 and AQAP 2110 and 2210. Moreover, the company holds Concession, issued by the Ministry of the Interior and Administration for manufacturing and sales of products and technology dedicated for military and police use. 
Hertz Systems has its own, in-house R&D department located in Science and Technology Park close to company HQ.

The system generates and automatic alert in the event of intrusion into the guarded zone and effectively neutralizes the intruder.

Hertz Systems is a highly trusted partner, which is confirmed by various licenses and certificates. Implemented Quality Management System complies with standards of PN EN ISO 9001 and AQAP 2110 and 2210. Moreover, the company holds Concession, issued by the Ministry of the Interior and Administration for manufacturing and sales of products and technology dedicated for military and police use. 
Hertz Systems has its own, in-house R&D department located in Science and Technology Park close to company HQ.

entityDescription: Ciência Viva, created in 1996, is the National Agency for the promotion of scientific culture and technology. It is a non-profit association and its members are national research laboratories and science policy institutes. Its main goal is to promote public awareness of Science and Technology among the general public, with a particular focus on young people. To reach this goal, Ciência Viva develops its activities along three strategic axes: a) Science education (teacher training, science projects for schools, summer internships for secondary school students in research centres and institutions); b) Science communication events for the general public (Science in Summer, Science and Technology Week, World Space Week, talks and debates); c) A national network of Ciência Viva Science Centres, in collaboration with local authorities and universities. Presently there are 20 Ciência Viva Science Centres nationwide. Ciência Viva has been actively promoting, supporting and developing science education activities in the area of Space Science and Technology since 1999 and has been an active promoter of ESA¿s educational projects since then. These activities and projects include the development of projects with schools (e.g. participation in ESA¿s project ¿Greenhouse in Space¿, and ¿Astrobiology: other worlds, other lives? - 2010/2011, and ¿Mission-X¿ ¿ 2011/2012), the yearly coordination and dissemination of the World Space Week, the organization and coordination of Astronomy in Summer, a national campaign of astronomical observations and activities and the organization of talks and debates. Over the last years, the Ciência Viva Science Centre Network has gained considerable experience in training through teacher development courses organised in the centres that are already certified as teacher training centres. Participation in the European projects Fibonacci, Pollen and SciencEduc, amongst others, has also strongly enriched Ciência Viva¿s experience.

entityDescription:
G & A Engineering S.r.l. is a small company operating for over 45 years in military and space sector.
The company is located in a modern plant in Oricola (AQ), in a land of 18,000 square meters, divided into different buildings and structured to meet the needs arising from research, design, engineering, experimentation, prototyping and series construction, that the company carries out in military, space, industrial, medical and professional sectors.
The company has several workshops with tools, machines and equipment of the latest generation that, together with the company know-how and qualified and multidisciplinary staff, have allowed to consolidate high-level technologies and processes that allow it to operate in sectors very challenging and that make it independent in passing from an idea to a finished product.
The company workshop includes: Microelectronic Workshop, Metrologic Workshop, Electronic Workshop with Laboratory Instrumentation, Mechanic Workshop.
Over the years the company has consolidated high-level technologies, processes and know-how that allow to operate in very challenging sectors and has a structure that guarantees the sale of services/products at all stages of their "Life Cycle", carrying out research, design, engineering, industrialization, manufacturing and logistics activities, integrated with the continuous application of all the standards typical of space, military and industrial sectors. Unique and peculiar characteristic of the Company is the ability to design and build "Special Equipment", ie custom designed devices built with criteria that make a prototype comparable, for finishes and construction features, with an industrialized product; these special equipment typically include electronic, microelectronic and electrical technologies as well as mechanical, pneumatic, hydraulic, vacuum, etc ...; beyond that, the company is known on the market for its ability to cooperate with the world of research and the ability to make experimental systems indistinguishable from industrial systems.

entityDescription:
Thales Alenia Space brings over 40 years of experience to the design, integration, testing and operation of innovative space systems for telecommunications, navigation, Earth observation, environmental management, exploration, science and orbital infrastructures. A joint venture between Thales (67%) and Leonardo-Finmeccanica (33%), Thales Alenia Space also teams up with Telespazio to form the parent companies’ “Space Alliance”, which offers a complete range of services and solutions. Thales Alenia Space has built up unrivaled expertise in dual (civil-military) missions, constellations, flexible high-throughput payloads, altimetry, meteorology, and high-resolution radar and optical observation, as well as space exploration. The company capitalizes on its strong legacy, while also making innovation a key to its strategy. By offering a continuous stream of new products and expanding its global footprint, Thales Alenia Space has established its leadership in today’s fast-evolving space sector. Thales Alenia Space posted consolidated revenues exceeding 2.3 billion Euros (2023) and has over 8000 employees at fourteen sites in 8 countries.

Thales Alenia Space UK is focused on propulsion systems (Electrical Propulsion, Chemical propulsion) including development of complex thruster mechanisms.
The centre of competence for propulsion (both electrical and chemical) is based in Harwell and utilising the Thales UK facilities in Belfast for assembly integration and test. The Harwell facility is next to the ESA facilities and houses the UK programme management, systems engineering, mechanical/thermal engineering and propulsion engineering for multiple programmes.
The growth of Thales Alenia Space UK relies on close partnerships with Thales UK R&T, UK Academics and UK SMEs.

Leadbitter is owned by Bouygues UK which is evolving to become the next leader in UK construction. entityDescription:
The Copernicus Science Centre is one of the largest science centres in Europe. Its exhibition is divided into six interdisciplinary parts with over 450 exhibits. Music is combined here with biology, and mathematics with architecture. Science enters the realm of feelings, and the visitors themselves may become the object of observation.

The variety of exhibits gathered at several thousand square meters creates an area in which everyone can make own discoveries. 

The Centre features the only Robotic Theatre in the world. The moves of its leading actors ¿ RoboThespians ¿ are controlled by compressed air, and their heartbeats are produced by a 40-Watt loudspeaker. 

In the CSC, everyone may feel like a real scientist bent over slides and test-tubes, surrounded by spectroscopes or electropneumatic sets. Our laboratories allow for independent experimenting. The physics, chemistry, biology and robotics labs are equipped with devices used in state-of-the-art laboratories all over the world. 

The building is surrounded with the Discovery Park. Its design was developed together by engineers, artists and greenery designers. Apart from art exhibits presenting sound effects, it also includes an open air gallery and a summer stage. 

The Centre co-organises the Science Picnic ¿ the largest open air event for the promotion of science on our continent. The commitment of scientists and interest of our audience have contributed to impressive achievements that we may be proud of in Europe. In 2005, the Science Picnic held in Warsaw was commended by the European Commission as one of ten model European projects in the "Science and Society" field. 

In June 2011, we opened one of the most modern planetaria in Europe. The Heavens of Copernicus makes it possible to watch over ten million stars. A spherical screen surrounds the auditorium from all sides, and the 3D technology makes the spectators feel immersed in the projected image. The planetarium is a venue of sky presentations, film shows, lectures and meetings. The Heavens of Copernicus Planetarium has its own production studio, where original film shows for our visitors are created. 

We are one of the youngest science centres, yet we are considered one of the most interesting and innovative centres in the world. The attendance rate in the Copernicus Science Centre proves the fundamental need to establish such institutions and bears witness to the considerable developmental ambitions of our society. Less than 2 years after the opening, we have been visited by over 2 million people.

The CSC is a cultural institution established and financed by the Capital City of Warsaw, the Ministry of Science and Higher Education and the Ministry of National Education.

entityDescription:
The Norwegian Institute for Nature Research (NINA) is Norway's leading institution for applied ecological research.
NINA is responsible for long-term strategic research and commissioned applied research to facilitate the implementation of international conventions, decision-support systems and management tools, as well as to enhance public awareness and promote conflict resolution.
Ecological expertise
The institute was established in 1988, employs a staff of approximately 240 and directs well-equipped laboratories and facilities at seven locations in Norway. NINA offers broad-based ecological expertise covering the genetic, population, species, ecosystem and landscape level, in terrestrial, freshwater, and coastal marine environments.
Interdisciplinary issues
In addition, NINA addresses a wide variety of interdisciplinary issues involving both ecologists and social scientists, and plays an important role in European and other international research activities. NINA is experienced in dealing with natural and human aspects of resource and biodiversity management in developing countries and Eastern Europe, and has actively contributed to capacity building and technology transfer by means of research cooperation and consultancy activities.
Services 
NINA's activities encompass resource assessment and monitoring, development of methodologies, environmental impact assessments, community-based resource management, and analysis of natural, anthropogenic and socio-economic aspects of biodiversity and resource management. NINA's staff offers provides comprehensive and up-to-date scientific expertise, and guarantees top-quality services in commissioned research and consultancy tasks.

entityName: Fondazione Centro Euro-Mediterraneo sui Cambiamenti Climatici ( CMCC)
entityDescription: Fondazione CMCC is a non-profit research institution.CMCC’s mission is to investigate and model our climate system and its interactions with society to provide reliable, rigorous, and timely scientific results, which will in turn stimulate sustainable growth, protect the environment, and develop science driven adaptation and mitigation policies in a changing climate. CMCC collaborates with experienced scientists, economists, and technicians, which work together in order to provide full analyses of climate impacts on various systems such as agriculture, ecosystems, coasts, water resources, health, and economics.CMCC supports policymakers in setting and assessing costs, mitigation, and adaptation policies.It involves and links private and public institutions jointly investigating multidisciplinary topics related to climate science research. CMCC benefits from the extensive applied research experience of its members and institutional partners:Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia;Università del Salento;Università Ca’ Foscari Venezia; Università di Sassari; Università della Tuscia;Politecnico di Milano;Alma Mater Studiorum Università di Bologna: Resources for the Future. CMCC research activities are distributed among 3 Research Institutes, each of them grouping the CMCC Research Divisions: Institute for Earth System Predictions (IESP) it has the objective of promoting, organizing, and disseminating forecasts, simulations and scenarios of the Earth system at all scales IESP - Institute for the Forecasting of the Terrestrial System; it includes: ROFS - Regional Ocean Forecasting System;CLIVAP Climate Variability & prediction;ESYDA Earth System Modelling and Data Assimilation; ASC - Advanced Scientific Computing; GOCO - Global Coastal Ocean. Institute for Climate Resilience (ICR)it uses IESP products to develop new methodologies, provide information on risks and adaptation; it includes: IAFES Impacts on Agriculture, Forests and Ecosystem Services; RAAS-Risk Assessment and Adaptation Strategies; REMHI - REgional Models and geo-Hydrological Impacts; ISCD - Information Systems for Climate science and Decision-making.European Institute on Economics and the Environment (EIEE): it aims at supporting environmental, energy and natural resource decisions through economic research and interaction with national and international policies; it includes: Sustainable Earth Modelling Economics (SEME); Economic analysis of Climate Impacts and Policy (ECIP). CMCC acquired portfolio of research projects includes more than 600 funded projects:38 projects in FP6 and FP7, 84 projects in H2020, 73 in Horizon Europe & 420 projects under other EU and international research grants. In about a half of the implemented projects, CMCC acted as the coordinator. In 2022 the annual turnover was equal to 22,9M€ and 173 permanent staff have been working at CMCC. Correspondingly high is the experience and skills in managing international projects. CMCC has developed documented internal quality management system for scientific consultancy, project implementation and advisory service. CMCC Quality Management System is certified according to the ISO 9001:2008 standards (IQNet Certification No. 18049). Since 2008 CMCC operates its own Supercomputing Centre (SCC) located in Lecce at CMCC HQ.SCC is the only computational facility in Italy specializing in Climate Change research.

entityDescription:
Johanniter-Unfall-Hilfe e.V. (Johanniter) is a German non-governmental organization dedicated to excellence in the fields of ambulance service, civil protection and disaster relief. With its more than
13,000 full-time and 22,000 voluntary staff, Johanniter is one of four organizations forming the backbone of the German ambulance and medical civil protection system.

Johanniter is active in the international arena with its branch of Johanniter International Assistance providing assistance in different areas and phases of disaster relief and humanitarian aid, with its core competences in the fields of primary health care, rehabilitation of people with disabilities and disaster preparedness. Johanniter International Assistance is present with field offices and/or cooperating with local partners e.g. in Haiti, Democratic Republic of Congo, Indonesia. Johanniter International Assistance is registered with DG ECHO concerning middle and long term projects as a Partner with status "p" within the Framework Partnership Agreement (FPA).

On the basis of the core competence in disaster preparedness, Johanniter has a long experience in
the international disaster relief environment and is actively involved in the EU Civil Protection
Mechanism: Since 2006, together with the partners, Cyprus Civil Defence (CCD), Bulgarian Chief Directorate for Fire Safety and Civil Protection and German Federal Agency for Technical Relief (THW), Johanniter conduct yet Assessment Mission Courses (AMC) for EU experts in Bulgaria/Cyprus, provides trainers and lecturers for various training courses contributes civil protection/disaster relief experts for missions and can support EUCP missions with its EUTAC TAST, e.g. in November/December 2010 due to the cholera outbreak in Haiti. Johanniter is a co-developer of the communication kits "EU Assessment Mission Kit" and "MIC in a Box" and has an agreement with the European Commission to maintain and provide these tools for EU missions. Furthermore, Johanniter was involved in the first year in the design, organization and conduct of EU module table-top exercises in Slovenia/Croatia.

Planning, managing, conducting and evaluating complex projects on an international level is part of
Johanniter's daily routine, in particular in the unit "International Projects and Cooperation" (IPC), under the auspices of Johanniter International Assistance in the national headquarters of Johanniter in Berlin. Johanniter is/was e.g. the coordinating beneficiary for the Preparatory Action projects EUTAC, EURAMET based on the calls for proposals for the Preparatory Action on an EU Rapid Response Capability of 2008 and 2009 and EURACARE, based on the call for proposals for Prevention and Preparedness 2011 under the Civil Protection Financial Instrument. EUTAC TAST, EURAMET and EURACARE, are registered modules in CECIS and available for EU CP interventions.

As integral part of the Johanniter Disaster Relief Concept, Johanniter has an International
Training Centre which organizes and coordinates trainings mainly of Johanniter volunteers to
train and prepare them for international missions. They cooperate for instance with the Federal Training
Centre of THW in Neuhausen a.d.F. or the Academy for Crisis Management, Emergency Planning and Civil Protection (AKNZ) in Bad Neuenahr-Ahrweiler. The International Training Centre (ITC) is located in Berlin and part of the Johanniter Academy, which is certified according to DIN EN ISO 9001 :2000.

Based on their long experience and activities in the international disaster relief realm, Johanniter has established a network of highly qualified and experienced experts and actors who can be made available for international trainings and exercises. Nevertheless, the experience of the professional qualifications of Johanniter staff members is demonstrated by the permanent staff member, Mr. Harm Bastian Harms as head of the unit for International Projects & Cooperation.

entityName: UNIV DE LAS PALMAS GRAN CANARIA - INSTITUTE FOR APPLIED MICROELECTRON INTEGRATED SYSTEM DESIGN DIVISION
entityDescription: The Institute for Applied Microelectronics (IUMA) started its activities in the late 1980 by coordinating the synergies of a qualified group of scientists and experts from the University of Las Palmas de Gran Canaria (ULPGC) in the fields of microelectronics, communications, computer science and mathematics. Since its conception, IUMA has witnessed changes in its administrative and legal status due to its excellence in research and technology transfer to industries, being partly granted at present by the regional and national governments apart from the incomes obtained from private and public industries as well as from competitive scientific programs. With more than 55 researchers, technicians and administrative support, IUMA is structured in 6 different divisions: Integrated Systems Design; Information Technology; Microelectronics Technology; Control Systems and CAD Tools; Communications; Microsystems. IUMA has a strong presence in diverse initiatives. Some of our members participate in the Steering Committee of international conferences or have been chairing some of them while others are part of the Editorial Board of international journals. IUMA members have published more than 250 papers in well-known journals and conferences. The approval of different submissions presented to european and national programs has lead to the acquisition of state-of-the-art equipment which is employed in the development of new technology products for industries located in USA, Europe and Australia. IUMA is also promoting innovation in the local sector by collaborating with emerging enterprises. Furthermore, during the last 15 years IUMA has participated in the creation of 8 spin-off, being a valuable factor of innovation in the Canary Islands.

Company description: The German Remote Sensing Data Center (DFD) is an institute of the German Aerospace Center (DLR) with facilities in Oberpfaffenhofen near Munich and in Neustrelitz in the state of Mecklenburg – Western Pomerania. DFD and DLR’s Remote Sensing Technology Institute (IMF) together comprise the Earth Observation Center EOC, which has become a center of competence for earth observation in Germany.
DFD supports science and industry as well as the general public. With its national and international receiving stations DFD offers direct access to data from earth observation missions, derives information products from the raw data, disseminates these products to users, and safeguards all data in the National Remote Sensing Data Library (D-SDA) for long term use. Its geoscience research related to the atmosphere, global change and civil security facilitates access to products and approaches based on remote sensing and consolidates their utilization in scientific and commercial domains. DFD operates thematic user services, in particular the World Data Center for Remote Sensing of the Atmospheric (WDC-RSAT), and the Center for Satellite-based Crisis Information (ZKI).
Core competence of DFD
- Design, development, engineering and operation of a multimission payload ground segment including a network of national and international acquisition stations and processing systems;
- Capability of 24/7 operation of complex infrastructure, including satellite ground stations in exposed locations (Arctic, Antarctic), and rapid generation of thematic information for public authorities, European and international users;
- Development and integration of IT systems for processing and managing large amounts of data and for operating the National Remote Sensing Data Library;
- Development of methods and processes for mapping crisis regions, for risk and vulnerability modeling, and for setting-up decision support systems for environmental and crisis-response activities;
- Development and operationalisation of thematic processors, also using models and assimilation methodologies, to generate products, indices and time series for trace gases, aerosols, cloud parameters, irradiance, geo- and bio-physical variables for terrestrial ecosystems, land use, energy, environment, urban areas, and georisks;
- Development of customised visualisation methods and creation of visualisations, animations, apps, and finalized TV and internet productions.
DFD provides opportunities for the next generation of scientists by offering internships as well as jobs for diploma, Master’s, and PhD candidates and guest scientists. Networking with universities is stimulated through comprehensive institutional cooperation with universities in Würzburg (terrestrial ecosystems) and Augsburg (atmosphere). To a high extent the activities of DFD are international and focused on long-term research cooperation with global partners.
The German Remote Sensing Data Center has ISO 9001 certification.

entityName: INSTITUTO SUPERIOR TECNICO - INSTITUTO DE PLASMAS E FUSAO NUCLEAR
entityDescription:
Instituto de Plasmas e Fusão Nuclear (IPFN, Institute for Plasmas and Nuclear Fusion) is a research unit of Instituto Superior Técnico (IST) with the status of Associated Laboratory granted by Fundação para a Ciência e a Tecnologia.
IPFN ensures the Portuguese participation in EUROFusion, the European Consortium for the Development of Fusion Energy.
The role of the research unit at national and international level was recognized in the last FCT evaluation of R&D units, where IPFN was awarded the classification “Exceptional”.
The main activities of IPFN are centered on Research and Education:
Research is organised into two Thematic Areas: Controlled Nuclear Fusion and Intense Lasers and Plasmas Technology, divided into seven scientific groups in total. The research activities of the IPFN are monitored by an External Advisory Panel.
Education encompasses a broad range of activities, including coordination and participation in Doctoral Programs and Master Degrees, training of young researchers in advanced facilities, and outreach activities for pre-university students and teachers. 
Our research programme is carried out in the scope of seven groups, focused in specialized fields of study.
Controlled Nuclear Fusion: Engineering and Systems Integration, Material Processing and Characterisation, Experimental Physics, Theory and Modelling
Intense Lasers and Plasmas Technology: Lasers and Plasmas, N-PRiME, High-Pressure Plasmas.

IPFN is based at the Alameda campus of IST in Lisbon. We operate several experimental facilities both at this campus and at the Tecnologic and Nuclear campus, in Loures.

ISTTOK Tokamak ; L2I Laboratory for Intense Lasers ; PEL Plasma Engineering Laboratory ; MotLab Ultra-cold Atoms Laboratory for Ultra-cold Atoms and Quantum Plasmas ; ESTHER European Shock Tube for High-Enthalpy Research ; LATR Laboratory of Accelerators and Radiation Technologies ; PL Plasma Laboratory ; EPP Computational facility ISTCluster ; VOXEL VOlumetric medical X-ray imaging at Extremely Low dose

entityDescription:
We, the German Space Agency, undertake statutory tasks in the space sector on behalf of the German Federal Government. Under the "Raumfahrtaufgabenübertragungsgesetz" and within the scope of the tasks effectively assigned to us, we implement the space strategy of the Federal Government, develop and manage the national space programme, and represent the interests of the Federal Republic of Germany in space-related international bodies in accordance with the tasks assigned to us. We advise the Federal Government and develop initiatives and strategic approaches for space policy. All of our activities are based on the guidelines laid down by the Federal Government in its space strategy.
With our missions and projects, we strengthen Germany’s scientific excellence and expand the technological expertise and global competitiveness of German industry. Promoting the commercialisation of space technologies, the innovation potential of German SMEs and technology transfer are essential tasks of our industrial policy mandate. Space technologies and applications are intended to benefit people on Earth and improve the quality of life in Germany, Europe and the rest of the world.
Our space missions make a significant contribution to solving global and societal challenges. Examples include providing information on climate change and climate protection, the further development of digitalisation and communications technologies, and contributions to national security.We make the results of our missions and projects publicly available. We inform the public about new scientific findings and promote awareness of the relevance of space for everyday life. Last but not least, we strive to spark interest and enthusiasm among young people for the natural sciences in general and space in particular.

entityName: DLR - INSTITUTE OF AERODYNAMICS AND FLOW TECHNOLOGY (DLR AS) Göttingen
entityDescription:
The Institute of Aerodynamics and Flow Technology is a leading research Institute in the field of aerodynamics/aeroacoustics of airplanes and aerothermodynamics of space vehicles. It has two main sites at Braunschweig and Göttingen and a division at Cologne. Today a total personal of about 350 employees is engaged in numerical and experimental investigations on air- and space vehicles. Experiments are performed in wind tunnels and in flight experimental aircraft.
The Institute can look back on a long history: After the first “Modellversuchsanstalt für Aerodynamik“ was founded in Göttingen in 1907, the Institute for Aerodynamics and the Institute for Gas Dynamics of the "Deutsche Forschungsanstalt für Luftfahrt” (DFL) were succeeded by today's DLR Institute of Aerodynamics and Flow Technology.
As a leading research institute in the fields of aerodynamics, aeroacoustics and aerothermodynamics, it is subdivided into nine departments. The Institute is acting as a link between basic research at the universities and industrial application. This results in a large number of cooperative national and international research projects.
Environmental policy conditions are playing an increasingly major role in air traffic. The DLR Institute of Aerodynamics and Flow Technology therefore researches how future aircraft and space transportation systems can be designed and operated more efficient, ecological, comfortable, economical and secure. A further core competence is the development of software products used for aerodynamic and aeroacoustic simulations.

entityName: DLR - INSTITUTE FOR SOFTWARE TECHNOLOGY (DLR SC)
entityDescription:
The mission of the Institute for Software Technology is research and development in software engineering technologies, and the incorporation of these technologies into DLR software projects. Current activities focus on software for distributed systems and intelligent systems, artificial intelligence, software technologies for embedded systems, visualization, data science, and high-performance computing.

Software development costs account for an increasing fraction of the overall labor cost in R&D projects. For DLR, this fraction amounts to about a quarter of its personnel. As compared to manual techniques which still prevail in software development, the use of state-of-the-art software engineering technologies leads to better project results and more efficient development processes. In cooperation with DLR’s engineering institutes, the DLR Institute for Software Technology takes part in demanding software development projects where it complements the application know-how of the other project partners.
Through its cooperation with world-wide leading partners as well as its collaboration in international forums and standardisation bodies, the Institute for Software Technology takes an active role in the development of new software technologies and builds up corresponding expertise at DLR for future projects.
The Institute for Software Technology is located at the DLR sites in Cologne, Braunschweig, Berlin and Oberpfaffenhofen. It is divided into the departments "Intelligent and Distributed Systems", "Software for Space Systems and Interactive Visualization" and "High-Performance Computing".
