entityDescription: The Hungarian Astronomy Nonprofit Ltd. (HANLtd.) aims to provide an independent economical-legal entity for the balanced emergence of the institutional representatives of Hungarian astronomy and astrophysics science. The HANLtd. aims to work as the highest level economic representative of Hungarian astronomy. The HANLtd. was registered on 13rd June 2017, its founder and majority owner is the Research Centre for Astronomy and Earth Sciences of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, Hungary’s largest astronomical research institute. Other owners are the Hungarian Astronomical Association (MCSE), and the Observatory Foundation of Baja. The Ltd. is open and has already invited other Hungarian actors of astronomy, astrophysics, space science and technology domain. Goals and activities cover three fields: scientific research, related technology development and education plus outreach: We perform space research and space industry activities, and participate in European Space Agency projects. Successful project performed by our colleagues are: Astrobiological analysis of Mars related to Mars Express spacecraft (Co. 4000105405), pipeline development and data exploitation for ESA Herschel Space Telescope, instrument development for Earth-based field analogies related to ExoMars rover (Co. 4000119270) and planning activities for exoplanet oriented next ESA missions including TESS and CHEOPS. Other successful space research projects are the COST TD1308 international cooperation on astrobiology, and the Europlanet H2020 RI project for the solid-state spectroscopy of cosmic materials. HANLtd. organises the educational and science promotional activities of Svábhegy Observatory, Hungary's largest, and Central-Europe's almost largest visual observatory. The 0,6 m Zeiss Cassegrain telescope, and its monumental dome-building is an iconic facility of the Hungarian astronomy. A well-equipped research and educational laboratory is available. Visitors can make observations with Hungary's largest H-alpha solar telescope, and with Hungary's largest (0,3 m) refractor. Using modern educational and demonstrational equipment, interactive daytime and night programs are organised for students and various other groups. Our mission is to bring the breathtaking views of the night sky, the aesthetic beauty of celestial bodies and the unbelievable secrets of the universe directly and in an easy-to-understand way to Hungarian audience. We represent a scientific educational and science promotional activity in Hungarian astronomy. We provide own research and measurement facilities for BSc, MSc and PhD university students with the telescopes and the research and educational laboratory. We support the national university level astronomy education with senior scientists in the Research Centre for Astronomy and Earth Sciences and in cooperation with the Eötvös Loránd University (contributing in courses, practices, student supervising). We support and organise astronomical events, demonstrations and conferences. We are the chief organiser of the 13th International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics. We represent Hungary in a condign, high-standard and memorable way on this 50 nation event. We organise astronomy promotional programs and demonstrations on celestial events, youth camp and company events. Our goal is the coordinated and high-level support of national astronomical communication by expert members of the Ltd., including scientists, engineers and educators. The communication with media is done regularly by TV, radio, newspaper and various online sources in a professionally correct way. We provide a representative environment for astronomical reports and interviews at the telescopes and research laboratories.

Company description: The Italian Red Cross, also known as CRI, is a non-profit organization, which carries out its mandate and activities in the humanitarian field within the framework of the International Movement of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, of which it is member. The CRI plays a unique role in Italy as an auxiliary to the public powers in the humanitarian field, an institutional role that derives from the Geneva Conventions of which the Italian Republic is a signatory. It is also recognized for its task of protecting health and preventing diseases, responding to emergencies and reducing risks related to disasters and spreading a culture of non-violence and peace, through the promotion of Humanitarian Principles and Values and International Humanitarian Law. The organization of the Italian Red Cross is inspired by the principles of subsidiarity, democracy and electivity of the association offices, of separation between the direction and control functions and the autonomous operational functions of the territorial bodies, as well as the criteria of effectiveness, efficiency and economy. The Italian Red Cross can count on the work of about 160.000 volunteers who are involved in implementing actions to achieve the CRI 2030 Strategic Objectives, which are: 
•Fulfilment of humanitarian mandate of Italian Red Cross through organizational capacity building (organizational development, fund raising, projects’ monitoring, planning and evaluation, management of human resources).
•Involvement of volunteers and staff in decision-making process (enhancement of voluntary service and promotion of active citizenship with a special focus on youth) 
•Promotion and dissemination of Red Cross/Red Crescent Principles, humanitarian values andInternational Humanitarian Law (advocacy and promotion of a culture of non-violence and peace); 
•Safeguarding and promotion of health and safety education (first aid activities, blood donation, health education and healthy lifestyle promotion); 
•Promotion of social inclusion and integration of vulnerable people (activities aiming at supporting and promoting the inclusion of marginalized people, such as homeless, poor persons, migrants, elderly, people with disabilities, etc.; social support in hospitals, including clown-therapy and psychosocial support); 
•Disaster risk reduction, raising communities resilience through prevention and preparedness in case of disaster (disaster preparedness and response at national and international level; psychosocial support activities in time of crisis; health assistance at major events; mitigation and resilience to climatic changes, etc.); 
•Cooperation with RC Movement and RC National Societies increasing projects and areas of intervention abroad.

Petroceramics S.p.A. was founded in 2003 as the first spin-off of the University of Milan. Petroceramics S.p.A. has always been committed in turning the outmost recent scientific findings into innovative solutions and industry-ready technologies and cutting edge products. This ongoing commitment has lead to the development of significant know-how , innovative products and solutions.

Petroceramics S.p.A. is now a stand-alone, dynamic company which develops new advanced materials and technological solutions for different technical sectors including automotive, armoured protection of individuals and vehicles, manufacturing industry and aeronautic.

Our leitmotif is to turn the outmost recent scientific findings into innovative materials as well as industry-ready equipment and processes.

Today, Petroceramics S.p.A. relies on several patented technologies and materials. Our state-of-the-art equipments can ensure a rapid and excellent production of small scale, customized parts as well as prototypes and pre-series. Petroceramics S.p.A. has an internal research and development laboratory which enables the rapid characterization of both own and customer's materials including analysis services and consultancy services on ceramics and petrology.

Petroceramics S.p.A. is composed of highly qualified experts in several fields, including geology, materials sciences, physics, nuclear and mechanical engineering and chemistry. Our organizational structure reflects both the customer-oriented attitude, guided by agility, flexibility and efficiency criteria, and our dedication to science and technology development.

Petroceramics S.p.A. is located within the Kilometro Rosso Science & Technology Park in Stezzano (Bergamo) which offers a highly innovative, interdisciplinary environment.

Thanks to the gained long-standing experience in more than a decade, ItalSystem s.r.l. has been able to demonstrate its capacity for creating innovative solutions within several mission types.

entityDescription:
GET is Greek SME developing solutions in Geo-Informatics, geospatial open data applications, environmental geoinformativs and geo-Business Intelligence. GET is member of si clister in Greece. 

We are working on the central management of data and information related to location. Our aim is to support common operational picture, decision making and provision of modern e-services for the professionals and the citizens.
We are developing central spatial data infrastructures (SDIs) in which data access is performed using web services based on open standards (OGC, ISO, Inspire). That way we can support vertical applications in thematic areas like the environment, urban management, cultural heritage and energy.
In our approach we utilize free and open source software and tools (FOSS). Our flagship product GET SDI PORTAL, a framework for the development of Spatial Data Infrastructures, is entirely developed by us and it is also an open source software available under the GPL3 license.

We are the first Geo-Informatics company in Greece developing professional, complex solutions based on Free Software / Open Source Software through contemporary business models (Infrastructure/Software/Data as a Service).
We are the first company in Greece developing business combination solution of Open Data Portals with Spatial Data Infrastructures based on Free Software / Open Source Software (FOSS).
We are the first Geo-Informatics Company in Greece implementing, since 2010, projects, based in software developed and support by the company itself. The mapping platform, GET SDI Portal is FOSS (available in Github under license GPLv3) and it used by more than 50 customers globally (Greece, United Kingdom, Ghana, Ecuador, Spain, China).
We are the first company in Greece which offers innovative solution for Earth Observation open data designed in order to use/reclaim European infrastructures of Sentinel satellite network as well as Copernicus data Repository minimizing software cost since the solution is based on Free and Open Source Software and and provided as Software/Platform as a Service (SaaS / PaaS)
Our solutions are based on open standards (OGC) and compatible to directives and laws governing information management (INSPIRE, PSI).
We prefer to use open & free software, however we can implement, with equal success, solutions with the use of commercial software (ESRI, Intergraph, Oracle, Microsoft)
We believe in data economy and its perspective and this the reason leading us for developing solutions based on and create open data.
We invest in research and innovations and this is represented in our solutions which are modern and based on alternative business models (Cloud based, S / D / I aaS).
We are notable for the high level of Corporate Social Responsibility expressed by a variety of actions.

Archangel Lightworks is building deployable laser communication systems for the high-volume, secure, space-enabled networks of the future.

entityDescription:
It is widely understood that application of conventional design principles cannot guarantee sustainable infrastructure performance throughout its lifecycle. Deterioration is imminent at some point due to unavoidable parameters, be they inherent (e.g. aging, material deficiencies), internal (e.g. installation of new equipment, change of use) or external (e.g. networks, access, nearby structures, earthquake events).Our vision at Grid-Engineers is to provide our clients with resilience-oriented solutions that assist them accommodate the effects of such unavoidable parameters. In this context, we tend to metaphorically think of resilience-based solutions as “pacemakers”, virtually built-in the infrastructure’s “organism” to safeguard the desirable technical, operational and financial performance throughout its lifetime.Our vision is supported by our excitements to connect the latest academic research findings with crucial industry requirements by offering our clients advanced design solutions, modern material applications, and decision-support systems based on efficient financial engineering and smart monitoring of all critical parameters. To this end, we work with all actors responsible for the design, construction, financing and operations of infrastructure including owners, contractors, consultants & designers, network operators, infrastructure investors, insurers and reinsurers.
To be able to deliver high-end services in this exciting domain, we strive to bring under one roof experts in state-of-the-art engineering (including analysis and experimental validation), new technologies for efficient monitoring and data collection, risk analysis and financial assessment. Our international network of highly experienced and deeply respected academic collaborators enables us to connects us with world-class field leaders whenever confronting challenging applications.

Initially a spin-off by researchers from NTUA’s laboratory of Soil-Structure –Systems, Grid Engineers is currently operating as a creative group of experts in several fields joining forces in order to produce out-of-the-box engineering solutions. Having shaped a unique modus operandi during the last decade, our team members are proud for having been able to smoothen the interface between engineering disciplines and form a flexible group of experts in diverse backgrounds. This gives us the ability to efficiently deliver solutions in otherwise resource-demanding projects requiring multi-disciplinary collaboration between academia and practice.

entityDescription:
The history of the Company dates back to 1994 when a group of programmers, who would later become the founders of Pentacomp, started working on the establishment of the system supporting the National Criminal Register.
1990s: Business Intelligence and dedicated systems
In 1995, five founders – who would later become members of the Management Board and shareholders - established the civil law partnership PentaComp. The founders included: Piotr Salata, holding the position of the President twice, Wojciech Chybowski, a long-term President, Dariusz Figura and Michał Kirpluk, members of the Board and Wojciech Kamiński – currently a shareholder of the Company.
From its very beginning Pentacomp engaged new co-workers and partner companies. A master agreement with Digital Equipment Polska (later Compaq Polska) resulted in numerous contracts performed for large enterprises. The first order fulfilled in the 1990s for the National Criminal Register brought about long-term and fruitful cooperation, which still remains the pride of Pentacomp – a solid and reliable partner that can be trusted. The National Criminal Register, as the first Client, uses the company's solution to this day.
At the end of the 1990s the list of Pentacomp's regular Clients included PSE (creation of the energy wholesale trading system), Polskie Koleje Państwowe (carriage and cargo tracking system), Polska Telefonia Cyfrowa (Era GSM) and EuroBIG.

At the end of 1997 Pentacomp was registered as Pentacomp Systemy Informatyczne Sp. z o.o. At that time the company specified its identity. We were experts in designing, implementing and managing data warehouses already and we moved on to specialise in Business Intelligence. Thus, Pentacomp became an experienced company able to deliver its software dedicated to handle strategic business processes in large organisations.
21st century
Security, Flexibility (AGILE methodology) and Development
Since 2000 Pentacomp has been developing on a regular basis. We gained competence in finance and banking. We implemented more and more large projects for state administration – ministries, central offices and institutions appear on the list of our Clients. The Company decides to expand into insurance market, which results in strategic cooperation with one of the Polish insurance companies. We took another step to improve our biometric solutions offer. Pentacomp became the leader in employing biometric technologies in Poland – cooperation with the Ministry of the Interior and Administration and PWPW S.A. in the scope of biometric passports and with the Polish Border Guard and the Police. At that time, Pentacomp, as one of the first companies in Poland, was granted the AQAP certificates, which entitled the Company to offer its solutions and services to the military sector. The Company was awarded also the NATO NCAGE Certificate.
In 2007 Pentacomp was transformed into a joint-stock company. At present, we have 117 employees and we are a stable enterprise of a good name and established position. Every year Pentacomp improves its ranking among IT businesses, demonstrating an above-average growth in the business.
2010 and the future
EMCS PL and EORI – Competence in Customs and Excise Duty
One of the Company's recent successes is the creation of the EMCS PL system to the order of the Ministry of Finance, which supports the register of movement of goods subject to excise duty. The competence gained in the EMCS PL Project translate into successful cooperation with businesses trading in products subject to excise duty: with fuel, tobacco and distilling industries. Pentacomp delivered, also to the order of the Ministry of Finance, the EORI system – the Economic Operators’ Registration and Identification System (part of the E-customs Project).

entityDescription:
Geosparc ("Geospatial Architects") is a software company building geospatial technology, solutions and products. The company commercially supports open source web GIS technology in general and its own open source platform, Geomajas in particular. Geomajas couples the innovative power of open source with the reliability of a true enterprise class application framework. With Geomajas, Geosparc focuses on delivering advanced GIS capabilities in standard web technology and integrate them with existing business applications like ERP, CRM, CMS, BI, BPM, etc. Geomajas showcases very robust security and scalability, while being open and extensible.

Geosparc has several years of experience and expertise in open source geospatial software, web GIS solutions and enterprise integration. Its commercial services and offerings include support contracts with service level agreements, commercial licenses, consulting services, Proof of Concepts, training and support services for web GIS projects (architecture, design, implementation, deployment). 

Geosparc provides developers, industries and governments with reliable products and services and innovative ideas to create and integrate Web GIS solutions. In doing so Geosparc helps its customers unlock the full potential of spatial information on the web.
Geosparc has customers in the private and public sector and is active in several international projects. 

More recently Geosparc has invested in a product pipeline of spatial enabled SAAS solutions such as Issuedoc, Spotbooking and Sleevemonkey. With these products Geosparc provides end-user solutions for (local) governments supporting their business processes for managing spatial information, public infrastructure and safety.

entityDescription:
Aprovec is a company created in February 2017 in the field of Risk Management.
Several activities are already carried out such as regulatory technical checks, prevention by infrared thermographic imaging, endoscopy ...
The interest to participate concerns another sector related to food:
The physical consequences of space travel are mainly caused by weightlessness or by a different gravity from that of the Earth.
Serious problems are a consequence: astronauts have their bones that become fragile after long stays in space, there are also muscle disorders.
After arriving aboard the ISS, most astronauts feel that their head and sinuses are congested. The blood increases in the upper part of the body and the body reacts to decrease the accumulation of blood.
And the consequences appear. The perception of the taste of food is altered.

We believe that these effects can be slowed down by an appropriate diet.
We propose to study the means of limiting them, by a feed capable of reducing them.

Some patients have disorders of taste due to their treatment. Perhaps it is possible to relate these symptoms to those of space?

We suggest working on a nutrition improvement project with transposition into everyday life (osteoporosis for example) with the will to initiate partnerships with industrialists interested in producing these adapted dishes.

entityName: Fachhochschule Aachen - Aachen University of Applied Sciences
entityDescription:
With more than 14,500 students, almost 2,000 graduates a year, ten faculties, more than 90 degree programmes, nine in-house and three affiliated institutes as well as four competence platforms, FH Aachen University of Applied Sciences, with its Aachen and Jülich locations, is one of the biggest and most important universities of applied sciences in Germany. Around 230 professors as well as approximately 900 employees work here, in teaching, in research and in administration. 
FH Aachen offers its students a first-rate course of study that superbly prepares them for jobs in modern and trendsetting professions. Apart from the traditional MINT subjects, such as mathematics, informatics, natural sciences, and technology, the range of courses offered by the university also includes business studies and design. In line with market requirements, more than 90 Bachelor's and Master's degree programmes aren't just offered as full-time courses of study, there is also an ever increasing number of dual study programmes, in line with market requirements. 
The university focuses on modern teaching which is guided by the latest didactic insights and utilises up-to-date methods such as e-learning. Students are provided with individual personal support which allows for an intense exchange of knowledge and experiences with the teaching staff. The incorporation of current research and development findings optimally prepares students for their professional careers after graduation. 
When it comes to research, the FH Aachen strives to be among the strongest universities of applied sciences in Germany. The competences are mainly in the future areas of energy, mobility, and life sciences. The latest research results are directly incorporated into teaching. 
Through the close cooperation with regional businesses, the university and business enterprises collaborate on the development of products and methods which provide added value directly in the region. FH Aachen trains and educates young women and men who assume responsibility in regional businesses and contribute to the development of the local trade and industry by applying their research-related expert knowledge and methodological skills. 
The expansion of regional, national and international networking in teaching and research is an essential part of FH Aachen's plans for the future, especially with regard to the euroregional location of the campuses in Aachen and Jülich, in immediate proximity to Belgium and the Netherlands. A further decisive step is offering international degree programmes. Here, the language of instruction is English which is meant to attract the interest of more foreign prospective students. In this context, the cooperation with numerous and significant foreign partner universities of FH Aachen are particularly attractive. 
FH Aachen's Freshman Institute prepares students from all over the world for a further course of study in Germany. Imparting language skills as well as content competence in a highly focused manner enables students to seamlessly commence a Bachelor's degree programme in North Rhine-Westphalia.

entityDescription: DMAT (Disaster Management Advice and Training) is a registered limited partnership offering services like Advice in preventive measures for disaster management operations; Disaster control, emergency planning and evaluation; Assistance during disasters; Assistance at tenders/preparation of proposals in the field of disaster, crisis and security calls; Assistance in development of EU Civil Protection(EUCP) modules –Table of Organization and Equipment, training, exercises and Standard Operating Procedures like in the EU Civil Protection projects EUTAC, EURETS and EURMET; Individual training and lectures for disaster management for UN (UN OSOCC course, Civil Military Coordination etc..) and EUCP(Assessment Mission Course, Operational Management Course, International Coordination Course etc...); Research and studies in disaster management, leadership, ethical and socio-economic effects of disaster, national and international disaster response laws, legal aspects in Peace Support Operations, Use of Military and Civil Defense Assets in natural disaster and complex emergencies, standardization in disaster management operations etc….). entityDescription: Academic Computer Centre CYFRONET AGH was established 40 years ago, in 1973. Foundation of the Centre was given by the Krakow University Rectors' College members, which in 1971 put forward a proposal to the state authorities to purchase a modern, large and multi-access computer for the Krakow scientific community and create the inter-university computer centre. Formally, the Centre was established on March 23, 1973 by the Minister of Science and Higher Education under the name Community Computational Centre CYFRONET-KRAKOW. Under this name the Centre operated until 1992, when it was renamed to the Academic Computer Centre CYFRONET-KRAKOW. Another name change took place in December 1998. ACK CYFRONET-KRAKOW converted to the Academic Computer Centre CYFRONET of the University of Science and Technology (ACK CYFRONET AGH). The Centre, which is organizationally and financially an autonomous unit of the AGH-UST in Krakow, is now one of the largest supercomputing and networking centers in Poland.

entityDescription:
The Institute of Chemical Methodologies (IMC) belongs to the Department of Chemistry and Technology of Materials.
IMC is situated in Lazio territory with two locations. The executive office is placed within the Roma 1 Research Area of Montelibretti (Rome) and one Supporting Operational Unit is at “La Sapienza” University of Rome.
IMC was established in 2002 by the union among the Institute of Chromatography, the Institute of Nuclear Chemistry and the Service of Nuclear Magnetic Resonance. A year later even the former Study Center on Reaction Mechanisms joined IMC. The union of these four former CNR bodies has founded IMC as a unique reality, with multidisciplinary skills which include general chemistry, organic and metal organic chemistry, analytical chemistry, physical chemistry, radiation chemistry, separation science, mineralogy, biology, supramolecular chemistry and colloid chemistry. In addition to the scientific tradition based on an extended number of chemical and physical disciplines there is the presence of researchers and technologists with competences in the humanities.
Through these competencies IMC personnel generate knowledge, transfer it to applications, and form the young generation within the three thematic areas – Food and Agriculture, Health, Environment and Cultural Heritage – accomplishing the mission of the Institute which consists in the development of sustainable chemical processes and products which aim to improve life quality.

entityDescription:
SERTIT (SErvice Régional de Traitement d'Image et de Télédétection) is a self-funding remote sensing service within the University of Strasbourg, whose legal representative is the President of the University of Strasbourg (UNISTRA) and has recently integrated a large university laboratory ICube as a platform. 
SERTIT is part of ICube Laboratory and Michel de Mathelin is director of both. Hence, SERTIT is now being administered through ICube within the University of Strasbourg. Then, each applications or service domain has an appointed reference leader. SERTIT also has increasing links to other laboratories and departments within the University of Strasbourg.
SERTIT was founded in 1986 with the arrival of the CNES SPOT programme. It is specializes in producing geo-information from Earth Observation data developing image processing methods and delivering geo-information products in natural resources monitoring, land management, urban planning, environmental survey, plus natural disaster and risk management.
SERTIT has a multi-disciplinary team, comprised of 20 specialists in remote sensing, GIS, geology, land surveying, photogrammetry, geography and physics, and proposes professional training for users of Earth Observation Services. SERTIT is both a R&D centre and a service provider. SERTIT has accompanied the development of the whole French EO satellite family (SPOT AVAL projects, Pléiades HR system programmes, ARCTOS system, new CO3D), European Space Agency satellite development (ERS-1, through ENVISAT to the Sentinels) and is Principal Investigator for many space agencies.
SERTIT a rapid mapping pioneer has supported activities within the International Charter “Space and Major Disasters” since 2000. SERTIT is a key player offering rapid mapping to the civil protection, humanitarian communities, insurance actors. Also, in Copernicus EMS Risk and Recovery SERTIT teams with Airbus DS, to provide services.
Otherwise, SERTIT’s work consists of land cover/land use monitoring exploiting EO. Part of this work was focussed on urban growth monitoring and now another part consist in natural resource (grassland and forest) mapping and monitoring in Western Europe: Interreg ForestClim project, forest clearing and logging, storm damage and species mapping.
Since 2002, SERTIT is largely involved in developing EO applications as well as EO training in Asia, particularly in China and Vietnam. SERTIT was PI for the DRAGON I to 3 successful Flood project (2004-2008) and is now working on DRAGON 4. The common word is “water driven landscape” and cover the field of vegetation mapping, biodiversity assessment, water quality, water extent, water resource monitoring and epidemiology.
At last, SERTIT is involved in training activities, participates in Master courses and training. It is also involved in training sessions for European Space agency in Europe (Lisbon Prague Krakow) and China (Wuhan, Lanzhou), training actions funded by the French Foreign office (Catachina in Beijing, 2003, Bulgarisk in 2009), CNES training programmes in Mexico (2014) and Haiti (2015) and for Algerian agencies (2016).
SERTIT is also working on 3D applications involving satellite and drone imagery and is leading the A²S project (Alsace Aval Sentinelle), which focuses on the development and the implementation of a value added production centre exploiting large Sentinel data fluxes.
SERTIT always takes user wishes and needs into account converging user requirements and expectations with EO data potential and processing methods to conceive adapted products and services. As an independent entity, it uses space for Earth’s benefit helping spread Europe’s influence. SERTIT enables the following worlds to converge : space domain technologies and their users; remote sensing research and industrial applications; researchers from all over the world; and political and economic players.

entityDescription: The Parco Archeologico di Ostia Antica is one of the new institution with administrative autonomy of the Italian Ministry of Culture. It is one of the largest archaeological parks of the Country, including the remains of the most important seaport of ancient Rome, the largest harbour of the ancient Mediterranean, practically the “hub” of the Roman empire from the early centuries of the city life, until the late antiquity, on which the Park mainly exercises tasks of protection, promotion and enhancement. The most important archaeological sites of the Park are: the ruins of ancient city of Ostia; the necropolis of Isola Sacra; the complex of the Imperial ports of Claudius and Trajan (Portus), the two basilicas of Portus and S. Ippolito and the Late Antiquity and Medieval Age remains of the city of Portus, the Museum of Roman Ships near the international airport “Leonardo da Vinci” of Fiumicino. The Parco is one of the main research centers on the ancient logistics.

entityDescription: FIDAMC is a Research Center created in 2006 by the Spanish Ministry of Industry, the Regional Government of Madrid and the Airbus Group, focused on the research, development and potential uses of composite materials. The entity is mainly addressed to aerospace activities but widely open to other sectors, having carried out projects in the railway, wind energy and automotive areas. FIDAMC staff number is 80 people, mainly high-skilled engineers, with a strong background on composite materials. FIDAMC facilities are placed in Getafe since 2009, with an area of about 1500 m2 for offices and about 4000 m2 for the physicochemical and mechanical laboratory and the manufacturing workshop. This huge area gives house to the specific state-of-the-art equipment required to carry out all the activities related to the ongoing projects, which will be described below. The main general activities carried out at FIDAMC are: • The improvement of technologies already known and the analysis, test and demonstration of emerging technologies; • The selection of the optimal ways to use those technologies in specific products; • The cooperation to establish specific Design Principles/Stress methods; • The suggestion of new research lines to Universities, R&D Labs or other Technological Centers which can cooperate potentially with FIDAMC. entityDescription:
ElFys, Inc. was founded in the fall 2017 to commercialize the innovation of photodetector technologies invented by a group of university researchers. The team has then been complemented with seasoned professionals in industrial manufacturing, sales and marketing. The technologies are protected by several patents. ElFys is the first in the world to combine the latest developments in solar cell technology with light detection, and thus, successfully apply black silicon to light sensing. The technology allows to significantly improve the performance of any device that uses light detectors as ElFys is the first in the world to capture every single ray of light. See for example Juntunen, et.al., Near-unity quantum efficiency of broadband black silicon photodiodes with an induced junction, Nature Photonics 10, 777-781, (2016)

The company utilizes the state-of-the-art processing facilities at Micronova Nanofabrication Center in Espoo, Finland: 2600 square metersof CMOS compatible facilities suitable for both R&D and semi-mass production. For volume production ElFys is in partnership with commercial foundries, having first full processes succesfully completed end 2023.

entityDescription: Spacemanic is small satellite mission integrator, focused on delivering innovative and reliable nanosatellite solutions, platforms and components. The company is very strong in the field of design, development and testing of fundamental small satellite components, such as onboard computers, power system units and solar panels. Our engineers are very experienced in the field of radio communication, and ground station design and operations. The Spacemanic transciever for UHF and S bands is very reliable and has been working in space for half year and counting, on board the first Slovak satellite skCUBE. Our products have very good and well documented flight heritage from the CubeSat’s space mission. This includes our highly precise and bespoke sun sensors, magnetometers and magnetorquers. The company Spacemanic is based in Bratislava, Slovakia, with two labs equipped for space mission technology design and development, as well as a small testing facility for nanosatellite missions. We are able to perform the basis required environmental tests needed for nanosatellites. Spacemanic is a spin-off company from the Slovak Organisation for Space Activities (SOSA), which has successfully designed, developed, launched and is operating skCUBE.

entityDescription:
EuroUSC Italia is a consultancy company providing services to Manufacturers, Operators, Insurance companies and Authorities operating in the aviation domain. We are leading experts in regulation and safety in the drone field but we cover also other aviation domains such as ATM/ANS and aerodromes. Established in Rome as a joint venture between Deep Blue Srl and Prof. Filippo Tomasello, our strength is to be completely independent from organisations involved in design, production, marketing or maintenance of drones, parts, components or systems, as well as from operators and flying schools, in line with the requirements laid down for “Qualified Entities” in the EASA Basic Regulation.
With a very dynamic and professional team, we can satisfy customers expectations conjugating high quality with competitive fares. Thanks to our involvement in the major regulatory
and standardization bodies at international level (ICAO, JARUS, EUROCAE and ISO) we help our customers with knowledge, methods and techniques that are always at the state-of-the-art and beyond. EuroUSC Italia is also member of the Board of Directors of UVS-International, the leading world association of drone operators and manufacturers. EuroUSC Italia participates to the European Horizon 2020 programme and is involved in several research projects funded by the European Commission, GSA, EDA and SESAR SJU. In these projects we offer our qualified contribution on: analysis of compliance to applicable regulations, safety assessment using state-ofthe-art methodologies, definition of operational procedures, testing and validation. Activities take place in the context of innovative applications for drones, cutting-edge technologies and infrastructures such as the U-Space.
We are also leading experts in the application of the Specific Operations Risk Assessment (SORA) methodology to fly drones in the new EASA “Specific” Category. We have developed an online tool for the Risk Assessment with SORA: www.online-sora.com

entityDescription:
The purpose of the company is the production and distribution of fiber composites of all kinds. Advice, Construction, Prototypes and Batches – INNOcomposites offers everything from one source.

3 key principles we live
•	Rapid processing to keep TIME as your competitive edge!
•	Full commitment to producing highly resilient components with minimum weight. 
•	100% confidentiality and discretion to preserve your recipe for success a secret. 

Our size allows us to respond immediately to your individual needs and requests. To convert your ideas, we work with the autoclave and infusion method. These technologies ensure an economical, high performing manufacturing process to combine the highest quality with economic benefits.

We offer an in-house developed manufacturing method to build complex hollow bodies that show an outstanding smooth inner surface. This process is much more efficient and ecological than the common sand core method. Not to mention that aerodynamics reaches new dimensions. 

We don’t waste, we recycle! Repair work with prepregs and hand-laminate using vacuum-bagging is the key. By applying these methods, existing fibre composite parts can be repaired or adapted to any request.

INNOcomposites, the CTO respectively, can record 12 years of experience working with the composite material, vacuum presses and infusion technology. The speciality is the processing of composite prepregs using autoclave technology.

Materials we work with
•	Carbon fibre, Fibreglass, Hybrid fibre, PP-fibers (e.g. Zylon fibre, Aramid fibre) (Bild von diversen Materialien)
•	Combining mentioned fibres with metals, polyurethane foams or elastomers (e.g. Airpad, Kraibon)
•	Processing of sandwich constructions such as honeycomb and foam materials (e.g. Nomex, Rohacell)

Supplemental work
•	Segmented moulds
•	Applying adhesives to merge composites (preparation, depth of roughness, etc.)
•	Assembly work (drilling, cutting, rivet, sanding etc.)
•	Applying Punctum® method to create hollow bodies, reaching max. cure level up to 40

entityDescription: The Extrapolation Factory is a design-based research studio for participatory futures studies, founded by Elliott P. Montgomery and Chris Woebken. The studio develops experimental methods for collaboratively prototyping, experiencing and impacting future scenarios. Central to these methods is the creation of hypothetical future props and their deployment in familiar contexts such as 99¢ stores, science museums, vending machines and city sidewalks. With this work, the studio is exploring new territories for democratized futures by rapidly imagining, prototyping, deploying and evaluating visions of possible futures on an extended time scale. entityDescription: MetGIS GmbH is a spin-off of the University of Vienna, specialized in the automated operational calculation of ultra high resolution world-wide weather forecasts. In contrast to the common standard, extra precise terrain data are included in the forecast generation process, resulting in a supreme quality of the calculated predictions, especially over mountain areas. MetGIS realtime predictions are available via www.metgis.com, but are also provided in form of APIs (application programming interfaces). These allow providers of foreign information systems (websites, apps, etc.) to access weather predictions not only for individual points, but also as color map overlays, zoomable to resolutions of less than 100 m for many parts of the world. The international customers stem from fields such as tourism, avalanche warning, open-pit mining and wintry road maintenance. Amongst others, they profit from the more cost-effective planning of resources and the possibility to lower the weather-related risk of accidents.

entityDescription:
Gold Mobile Innovation (GMI) Ltd is a small innovation consultancy with deep experience in the mobile and digital industries. Founded in 2007, GMI has been increasingly specialising in Open Innovation, Open R&D, and collaborative product & service development models, leading to the creation of The Mobile Collective (TMC) in 2010. TMC enables and supports the collaborative development of innovative technology-based solutions by bringing the mobile developer & designer communities together with professional scientists and educators in ThinkCamp events. ThinkCamps provide an open and creative environment for developing new products and services. They are designed to support a collaborative approach to generating cross-industry solutions. The events select one area of focus (such as Citizen Science ) and are structured to address problems, rise to challenges, and take advantage of new opportunities. Participants are drawn from a diverse range of disciplines and skill-sets, which they apply in a creative way. The TMC team facilitates the generation of ideas during the ThinkCamp events and then provides support for the organically formed working groups to further develop and implement the solutions, both during and beyond the event. 

The TMC team also has 8 years experience in running Hack Days, primarily Over the Air (www.overtheair.org), which has been the largest and most successful developer event in the Mobile Industry. Over the Air has typically attracted over 600 attendees and the active support of major players in the mobile industry. A key feature of every Over the Air is the Hack Day competition, which attracts over 20 entries each year – many of which win valuable prizes across a wide range of general categories, sponsored categories, and thematic or problem-solving challenges. At the record breaking 2011 event held in Bletchley Park, more than 120 attendees stayed coding overnight. 

Most recently, TMC was a consortium member in the EU FP7-funded Citizen Cyberlab project, whose goals were to to build digital tools and online collaborative platforms for Citizen Science, and to enhance the opportunities for learning and creativity available to Citizen Scientists world wide. Within this project, TMC led the community outreach and engagement activities (including running events such as Hack Days and Code Sprints) across the development of 7 platforms and tools for Citizen Science and 4 pilot projects, led the development of requirements with respect to learning and community building and building community engagement, and supported dissemination and exploitation planning throughout the project.

entityDescription:
Geminali AS

Geminali AS was established in 1998. The goal of the company and its partner company Geminor Inc, USA is to develop and commercialise software tools and instrumentation in the areas of environmental optics, radiative transfer, and remote sensing as well as to market instruments produced by collaborative partners. 

The company has done world wide marketing of instruments developed and produced by the Norwegian Institute for Air Research (NILU) for measurements of UV radiation and visible light together with software for estimating biological dose rates, total ozone column amount, cloud effects, and surface albedo. In addition, the company is actively engaged in the development of algorithms for interpretation of satellite remote sensing data through tight collaboration with the University of Bergen, Norway and Stevens Institute of Technology, USA. 

With funding from the Norwegian Research Council (NRC) and the Norwegian Space Centre (NSC), the company is actively involved in projects to develop retrieval algorithms associated with optical satellite remote sensing of open oceans, icy arctic waters, coastal waters, lakes, and snow-covered surfaces. 

Our partner company, Geminor Inc, USA, has recently developed a software tool (AccuRT) for accurate an efficient computation of radiative transfer in coupled atmosphere-surface systems. This software tool will play an important role in the proposed development of an Inherent Optical Properties algorithm for the Sentinel-3 OLCI sensor.

For the last twenty years Geminali AS and Geminor Inc have been heavily involved in research related to the retrieval of aerosol and marine IOPs with projects involving both theoretical algorithm development and fieldwork to acquire marine in situ data for algorithm validation. Fieldwork has included projects funded by NRC and NSC in Norway, Africa, and China, and algorithm development has included projects for NASA, ESA, JAXA (Japan), and KIOST (South Korea). The work for JAXA is aimed at retrieval of snow properties, while the work for South Korea involves development of algorithms for cloud screening, atmospheric correction, and IOP retrieval using data from the upcoming GOCI-II geostationary satellite.

entityDescription:
Evince Technology is an SME company developing a highly novel new class of devices based on synthetic diamond. Rather than employ conventional semiconductor approaches, Evince has instead developed processes to embed highly enhanced field emission sources within the diamond. This yields a family of patented electron devices (using diamond as a solid-state vacuum) as well as a highly robust cold cathode electron source that does not suffer from the usual degradation mechanisms because the emitters are fully encapsulated within the diamond.
Being based on diamond, the devices will be inherently hard to radiation and robust over a wide temperature range. The technology has multiple near term space applications such as electron sources for TWT’s and ion thrusters, and longer term application in solid-state power electronic and high frequency amplifier components.

entityDescription:
INFALIA is a spin-off company of the MKLab (https://mklab.iti.gr/) group of Centre for Research and Technology Hellas (CERTH) – Information Technologies Institute (ITI), focusing on AI and semantic technologies on images, videos, text and multimodal content. MKLab, for more than 17 years, has machine learning expertise in several domains of application, through its leading role in an extensive list of European projects, where it participates or coordinates (https://mklab.iti.gr/projects). 

In the space domain, MKLab technically coordinates the H2020-EOPEN project (https://eopen-project.eu/), under the H2020-EO-2-2017 EO Big Data shift topic. In EOPEN, MKLab is responsible for the domains of knowledge discovery and knowledge representation. AI and Machine learning methods are followed in change, concept and event detection from EO and non-EO data. Clustering techniques identify and visualise key-players and user communities in the corresponding use case domain. An advanced multimodal fusion approach is also introduced to quantify similarities among heterogeneous multimodal objects to assist information retrieval. In addition, the participating team is responsible for the creation of the EOPEN ontology to provide automatic semantic reasoning for decision making. These tasks also require involvement in the linking of EO data with non-EO data and external open data sources. Furthermore, the MKLab team is responsible for crawling data from the Web and Social Media sources and will also be responsible for the Web presence of EOPEN and other communication activities. The project involves three pilot use case scenarios in monitoring flood, climate change and food security.

entityDescription: ITC S.A. (www.itcnet.gr) is an SME established on 1995. The activities are related primarily in advancing research and development (R&D) in the fields of atmospheric, marine and environmental science and engineering, energy recovery and in applications related to these. Particularly, ITC is aiming at the development of methodologies and data sets related to atmospheric, hydrological and oceanographic processes. Atmospheric model development (related to dust cycle, surface energy exchange and aerosol-radiation-cloud-precipitation interactions) and applications in the area of short-range weather forecasting encompasses the main activities of the company. In addition, model development and applications, are related to several other topics including analysis of extreme weather events, surface hydrology, flooding, desalination and natural based solutions. The gained experience is obtained from the participation in a number of commercial and research projects (e.g. SKIRON, NHREAS, POSEIDON I&II, WASSF-I&II, Earth2Observe, OPERANDUM), funded from various sources (e.g. EU/EC, USA, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Norway, Italy). ITC runs operationally modelling systems for various applications around the world and a number of forecasting systems on a real-time (24/7) basis, providing weather-related forecasts and flood forecasting, including hydrological models for various countries around the globe. Further development (integrated tools) and dissemination of the research results and experience built during the past two decades is the ultimate target to advance the competiveness at the international level. The long-term target of the company is to develop integrated forecasting tools that are cost-efficient and can offer high-resolution weather information tailored to specific stakeholder decision support needs (e.g. local weather information, wind and wave energy, flood forecasting, desalination, agriculture management).

The gained experience is obtained from the participation in a number of commercial and research projects (e.g. SKIRON, NHREAS, POSEIDON I&II, WASSF-I&II, Earth2Observe, OPERANDUM), funded from various sources (e.g. EU/EC, USA, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Norway, Italy). ITC runs operationally modelling systems for various applications around the world and a number of forecasting systems on a real-time (24/7) basis, providing weather-related forecasts and flood forecasting, including hydrological models for various countries around the globe. Further development (integrated tools) and dissemination of the research results and experience built during the past two decades is the ultimate target to advance the competiveness at the international level. The long-term target of the company is to develop integrated forecasting tools that are cost-efficient and can offer high-resolution weather information tailored to specific stakeholder decision support needs (e.g. local weather information, wind and wave energy, flood forecasting, desalination, agriculture management).

entityName: Leibniz Institute for Baltic Sea Research Warnemuende
entityDescription:
The IOW´s mission is to conduct interdisciplinary marine research in coastal seas, with special emphasis on the Baltic Sea. Four departments representing the disciplines of physical oceanography, marine chemistry, biological oceanography and marine geology work jointly on a long-term research programme. It focuses on observations and modelling of ecosystem changes and their underlying processes in marginal seas and shelf regions.
The research programme strives for an in-depth understanding of the functions of the ecosystem with the overall objective to differentiate between natural variability and anthropogenically triggered changes. Past ecosystem states are reconstructed from sediment archives.
Long-term observation data from the Baltic Sea, collected and hosted at the IOW and its predecessor since the 1950s, are a valuable treasure for the entire coastal sea research community, both nationally and internationally. These time series ensure high-quality data support for hydrodynamic and ecosystem models and enable the institute to analyse trends. In addition, the data are used to support "what-if“ model scenarios as future projections.
The IOW contributes significantly to the sound scientific knowledge that is needed to implement the marine strategy for the Baltic Sea. Therefore, the institute cooperates with ministries, agencies and authorities, at both the federal and state level. The Federal Maritime and Hydrographic Agency (BSH) has entrusted the IOW with the Baltic Sea Monitoring Programme, to which Germany and the other countries bordering the Baltic Sea committed themselves in the Helsinki Convention. Besides, the IOW runs for the BSH three autonomous measuring stations in the western Baltic Sea (at Darss Sill, in the Arkona Basin and Odra Bight) which deliver oceanographic data from different water levels around the clock.
The IOW scientists have r/v Elisabeth Mann Borgese (length o.a.: 56.50 m) and r/v Maria S. Merian (length o. a.: 94.80 m) at their disposal.
(source: https://www.leibniz-gemeinschaft.de/en/institutes-museums/einrichtungen/iow/)

entityDescription:
TEKEVER was born from the idea that collective intelligence achieved through the sharing of knowledge anytime, anywhere and by everyone can improve society. Our teams want to push the limits by building technological products that will bring to reality what may seem impossible for most.

TEKEVER was incepted in 2001 and the Group's development strategy relies on competitive technology development, organic growth and having an international reach, operating in areas where innovative ICT and Aerospace products can make a significant impact on organizations activities and people's life. TEKEVER currently has subsidiaries in Europe, Asia, South and North America, focused on developing innovative technology, creating and distributing products, supporting partners and servicing customers around the world. TEKEVER is completely privately owned and counts on around 30 highly skilled, experienced and motivated staff. 95% of the staff have undergraduate (BSc) or graduate (MSc) degrees and backgrounds vary from Engineering disciplines (Electronics and Aerospace) to Computer Science and Marketing and public relations. 
TEKEVER Aeronautics B.V. is the Dutch arm of the TEKEVER group. Building on a combination of existing TEKEVER expertise and local Dutch teams and brainpower, TEKEVER Aeronautics B.V. is currently fully dedicated to activities in the field of space systems. From Space Exploration, Earth Observation and New Technology development, we aim to deliver advanced Space solutions with unique innovation to push the boundaries in Space.

TEKEVER Aeronautics B.V. current areas of activity include:
Satellites
Achieving economies of scale in the world of satellites is quite a challenge: Bringing innovation, standardisation, mass reduction and quick development together into a single package is a difficult nut to crack. Grouping these packages into networks is another ballgame. TEKEVER is working on pushing Nano and Pico Satellites further to achieve these goals. Small is the new Big!

Launchers
Getting into space is tough! Gravity is a drag and anytime you want to leave you need to take everything you need to survive for as long as you’re there, with you. What if you could send things into space as easily as taking a flight from Lisbon to Tokyo? TEKEVER is working towards delivering launch capability at a fraction of the cost for small payloads.

entityDescription: DIET (Department of Information Engineering, Electronics and Telecommunications, http://www.diet.uniroma1.it) is a department of Sapienza University of Rome, recently established after the fusion of the former Department of Electronic Engineering (DIE) and Department of Science and Technique of Information (INFOCOM). It is a governmental organization under the directives of the Italian Ministry of University and Scientific Research. The permanent staff is of about 65 researchers and professors, plus administrative and technical personnel, temporary researchers, contractors, and PhD students. Turnover of staff personnel is related to people retiring and consequent replacing. As for PhD students the turnover is three years whereas for temporary researchers and contractors it is 3-6 years. DIET carries out research and teaching activities covering many aspects of Information and Communication Technology. DIET has an extensive scientific experience in active and passive remote sensing. It has performed activities for analysing and interpreting data (electromagnetic models, inversion techniques), designing radar and radiometric sensors, modelling environment phenomena. Remote sensing of the atmosphere by microwave radiometers (both ground-based and satellite measurements) and radar remote sensing researches for land applications have been developed in the framework of international experiments and projects funded by Italian Ministry of Research, ASI, ESA and Italian Civil Protection. Past experience on inversion schemes include standard regression techniques, as well as Bayesian technique and neural networks.

entityDescription: The University of Nicosia (UNIC for short) is the largest university in Cyprus, with over 12,000 students, from over 70 countries across the globe, coming together in an innovative and transformative learning space. Located in Nicosia, the country’s capital, and with presence in 18 other cities worldwide, we are driven by our pursuit of excellence in teaching and learning, innovation, research, technology, and a continually evolving academic environment. We empower our students and instill in them the confidence to make an impact in the world. Many of our degree programmes and departments were the first of their kind in Cyprus. Over time, several programmes such as Medicine, International Relations, Accounting, Law, and Architecture, have developed into some of the most well-regarded in Cyprus and in the region. Today, UNIC’s new programmes focus on cutting-edge research, making us global leaders in certain fields, such as in our very successful initiative in Digital Currency/Blockchain Technology. Internationalisation is a central component of UNIC’s strategy. This includes partnerships for degree programmes, student mobility, and opportunities for students post-graduation in academia or industry, in order to share knowledge and capabilities across countries. The first and largest medical programme in Cyprus was formed in collaboration with St George’s, University of London. Today, the Medical School attracts over 500 students from around the world. In Greece, we offer several joint Masters degrees with the top Greek universities: Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, University of Patras and the Hellenic Open University. Thereby MindEarth helps to convert data into concrete actionable information that enables scientists, planners and politicians to improve the timeliness, confidence and sustainability of their strategies and decisions. The key concept of MindEarth follows the idea of creative geo-data science that jointly exploits SOA approaches for data sourcing and refining, geospatial analytics, visualization and customization. entityDescription:
Shom (Service hydrographique et océanographique de la marine) has three main missions.
National hydrographic service : Shom performs general hydrography duties for all seafarers to meet France’s international obligations under the international SOLAS Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea and the United Nations convention on the Law of the Sea. SHOM collects, archives and distributes official information necessary for maritime navigation. 
Support to defence : Within its areas of competence, Shom provides all necessary defence expertise and operational support in terms of knowledge of the aero-maritime environment.
Support to government maritime and coastal policies : Shom provides support to government maritime and coastal policies.

Its operationnal missions are to describe and to know about the sea physical environment in relation with the atmosphere, the ocean seabed and the coastal areas, to foresee their evolutions and to diffuse the corresponding data.

entityDescription:
Tyvak Orbital Networks Ltd represents the most advanced and vertically integrated offering of nanosatellite components and services on the market. We provide turnkey nanosatellite solutions and CubeSat space vehicle products and services that target advanced state-of-the-art capabilities for government and commercial customers to support operationally and scientifically relevant missions.
By leveraging on the platforms originally developed by the US parent company, Tyvak Orbital Networks Ltd will develop and deploy a new generation of best-in-class Nano and Microsatellites and increase partnership opportunities in the UK.
Our work helping others to put Nanosatellites and payloads into space has tremendous value as an R&D engine. For the past ten years, our team has focused on building, launching, and operating fully integrated satellite systems that optimize limited resources (i.e. power, volume, processing, bandwidth) to enable the highest performance levels. Tyvak Orbital Networks Ltd aspires to build on its International heritage and position itself at the leading edge of satellite technology, solving specific problems to ensure successful missions with a broad range of objectives.
In addition to R&D consulting services, Tyvak Orbital Networks Ltd has acces to and can deploy a full suite of spacecraft components, modules, mission operations tools and end-to-end launch integration services.

entityDescription:
Østfold University College has around 100 studies taught in new and modern premises.The university college has a total of just under 7,000 students. There are nearly 3,600 ordinary students at campus Halden, nearly 2,400 ordinary students at campus Fredrikstad, and nearly 1,000 students are taking continuing and further education programmes under the auspices of HiØ VIDERE (Centre for Continuing Education) at both campuses.The school has more than 550 members of staff. Students have good opportunities to take parts of their studies abroad.
HiØ offers a number of courses taught in English

The University College Board consists of 11 members and has overall responsibility for the university college's activities.
Østfold University College has an elected rectorate (rector and pro-rector) and a permanently employed university college director.
The HiØ units are headed by deans. 

Research and development
The HiØ staff are engaged in basic research, applied research, professionally oriented and vocationally relevant research and development work in most areas covered by the university college's portfolio of study programmes.
Applied research and development work is often carried out in collaboration with business and industry in the region and with the public sector.
The students' competence is developed through research-based teaching and by introducing them to student-active research and development. The research carried out at HiØ also helps to safeguard and realise a multitude of values and cultures in society, and to develop new knowledge that is communicated to other researchers and users and to society at large.

Partners - International Relations
Østfold University College has many partners, both national and international ones. As for its mission, Østfold University College is a regional institution with the particular responsibility for the local community. In addition to this reginonal focus, HiØ collaborates with over 100 universities world wide and participate in international co-operation programmes such as Erasmus+ and Nordplus.

Student welfare
The welfare of HiØ students is attended to in several ways – including through the considerable efforts of the Foundation for Student Life and the Student Parliament in Østfold.

Among other things, the Foundation for Student Life for Østfold runs the counselling service, student accommodation, bookshops and several canteens at HiØ.

The Student Parliament for Østfold attends to student democracy at HiØ with the help of many student representatives and other active participants from the different programmes and units at the university college.

entityDescription:

Driven by our focus on customer satisfaction, our passion for providing innovative solutions, state of the art tools and highly skilled staff, the company has excelled in supporting organizations of both the private and public sectors in Cyprus and abroad. 
We help the public sector manage environmental resources, reclaim degraded areas and develop sustainable development strategies. entityDescription:
The National Laboratory for Civil Engineering (Laboratório Nacional de Engenharia Civil - LNEC), established in 1946, is a public research institution, devoted to science and technology, with the status of State Laboratory. Located near the centre of Lisbon, in a 22ha campus, LNEC works in all the main fields of civil engineering and related scientific areas, giving it a unique multidisciplinary perspective. It has a staff of about 500 members and 125 research fellows. Researchers represent 30% of the personnel and have got a PhD or equivalent degree. Around 46% of LNEC's annual budget is funded from its own revenue, through scientific and technology contracts, with the balance coming from the National Budget and other sources of income.

The basic missions of LNEC are to contribute to pursue the public policies and to provide expert support to the public authorities in the various Public Administration sectors, particularly in what concerns the quality and safety of works, the protection and re-qualification of both natural and built heritage, as well as the technological upgrading and innovation, namely in the building construction sector.

entityDescription: Idroplan (powered by Farm Technologies SRL) is the smart component of an irrigation systems. Idroplan system monitors the most important parameters of the soil through a low cost, reliable and scalable network of nodes and a dashboard provides actionable insights based on the data gathered. The dashboard suggests timing and quantity of the next irrigation and provides on-time alerts. The core engine elaborates the data gathered through the network of nodes and integrates them with weather forecasts, to give tailored insights to each farmer. The network is configured as a mesh network: only one central node is connected, acting as gateway. This is possible thanks to the unique communication protocol that allows each node to measure and repeat the signal of more distant nodes, hence enabling long distance coverage and reducing the final cost for the user, while achieving best-in-class reliability.

entityName: TUM - CHAIR OF PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT, DESIGN SYSTEMATICS, AND LIGHTWEIGHT DESIGN
entityDescription: The Laboratory for Product Development and Lightweight Design is based at the TUM Department of Mechanical Engineering. Our Laboratory’s research and teaching is about engineering design, i.e., the creation of concrete solutions to specific problems. This is particularly challenging when the solution and its elements are entirely unknown. In so-called top-down approaches, the development focus is on the desired features of the new product rather than on already existing solutions or their elements. Both, methods from product development, such as creativity techniques, and methods from lightweight design, such as physical surrogate modelling, help to explore the unknown and find a way to new solutions to complex problems. For complex problems, it is often important to consider the entire system by adopting a holistic and interdisciplinary view. In both, lightweight design and in product development, all relevant requirements on a product, all aspects of feasibility and constraints on realization, and all interactions of all system components have to be taken into account. How treat the resulting complexity is an important subject of our research and teaching. We cover a large span of different quantitative and qualitative methods ranging, for example, from new numerical optimization techniques from lightweight design to Design Structure Matrices from product development. In order to produce both, applicable and scientifically outstanding results we closely cooperate with many partners from industry and academia.

entityDescription:
Founded in 2014, Faculty Science Ltd (‘Faculty’) is the UK’s largest, independent Applied AI company, with 400 employees, including ~130 PhD+ level qualified data scientists and software engineers, many cleared to SC/DV. We have delivered over 500 AI projects to clients, ranging from small advisory reports to full production-level software used in critical BaU functions. Our services business covers four sectors, (Government, Defence, National Security, Healthcare, Energy Transition, Retail & Consumer) and our product team delivers ‘Frontier’, an AI-enabled supply chain and demand-side forecasting tool for healthcare, commercial and Government clients.
We offer bespoke AI/ML builds, data analytics & visualisation, data strategy, data engineering services and decision intelligence products, helping organisations to understand their data, and take action from subsequent insights. We have links with the AI teams at UCL and Harvard; our own team includes former Front Line users from across all FLCs and domains.
The Defence team formed in Aug 2021, has been the data science partner of Dstl’s ‘Defence AI Centre (Experimentation)’ and the provider of forward-deployed AI/ML expertise and platforms to elements of UKStratCom. We are a member of the RN FASTER programme and are constructing computational digital twins of complex business processes for another FLC, via Dstl. Awaiting List-X accreditation.
We are experienced across a wide range of AI applications, including;
Digital signal processing of acoustic, electric and electromagnetic signals to enable signal detection, conducted for government agencies, Front Line Commands and a UK Defence manufacturer. Includes voice fingerprinting of radio and voice transmission to identify propaganda, or to automate auditing of safety practices involving radio commands.
Intelligence data fusion up to TS, including building ML-specific elements of underlying knowledge platforms, including on MODCloud. Cloud-agnostic development engineering teams have constructed AI platforms for the National Crime Agency, BEIS, Food Standards Agency and elements of UKStratCom. Most experience with AWS, Azure and Palantir Foundry.
Still and moving image object detection, using lightweight models to enable edge-based still image processing Proof of Concept in a harsh-environment Front Line use case. Other examples include an automated trackside maintenance video inspection system for National Rail, an automated nuclear waste sorting and segmentation system for a Civil Nuclear client and a video detector for a sensitive National Crime Agency use case.
NLP tools and platforms for improved intelligence discovery and fast identification of disinformation for UK Government Defence and Security clients, across multiple classifications; often in combination with video and other sources.
Improved route calculation for uncrewed UAVs and USVs, undertaken for multiple clients, combining meteorological, topographical, sensor and vessel performance data.

entityName: AIMPLAS- ASOCIACION DE INVESTIGACION DE MATERIALES PLASTICOS Y CONEXAS
entityDescription: AIMPLAS, Technological Institute of Plastics located in Valencia, is a private, non-profit Association with more than 500 associated companies created in 1990. AIMPLAS is formed by +120 highly skilled professional, more than 65% with a Masters, Engineering or equivalent degree in Chemistry, polymer engineering, materials engineering or equivalent, including 15 PhD. AIMPLAS’ fields of work are related to technological research and development on thermoplastic and thermosetting plastic materials & products, its transformation processes and their recyclability and sustainability. AIMPLAS generates new knowledge and technologies that can be transferred to companies in order to help them to increase their effectiveness and competitiveness. Nowadays, AIMPLAS has participated in 100 EU projects in FP5, FP6, FP7, LIFE+, CIP-EcoInnovation, H2020, among others, coordinating more 30 of them. In H2020, AIMPLAS is participating in more than 18 projects, coordinating most of them. Outstanding LIFE projects were celebrated at the Green Awards ceremony in Brussels on 30 May 2017, BREAD4PLA – with AIMPLAS as a coordinator - was honoured as one of the two most exceptional LIFE projects of the programme's 25-year history. At National and Regional levels AIMPLAS participates in around 100 projects yearly. AIMPLAS, as RO is focused to help companies in the plastic sector to develop new products and increase their competitiveness through innovation, has more than 20 pilot plants representing the most relevant polymer/plastics/composites production technologies present in the industry nowadays and has state-of-the art test facilities for chemical, optical, morphological, mechanical and physical characterisation. These pilot lines and laboratories are used by many customer’s every year allowing them to test new materials, optimize production processes and launch new products to the market, supported by AIMPLAS technical staff, resulting in more than 5000 assays, 170 technical assessments and 120 skills training actions to more than 1500 clients per year. AIMPLAS has state-of-the-art 8500 m2 facilities, including thermoplastics and thermoset pilot plants, analysis and testing laboratories (physical-mechanical, chemical, packaging, automotive and construction) and training areas. Member of any technology platforms, clusters, associations, networks etc. We take part in international and national research networks and technological platforms, with the objective to support the research and competitiveness of enterprises in their use with plastic materials. The interchange of R&D management tools as well as a know-how transfer allow us to be pioneers in the needs of the business field and the latest technologies.

entityName: UNIV FIRENZE - Department of Information Engineering (DINFO)
entityDescription:
Research on informatics, electronics, and telecommunications
The Department of Information Engineering (DINFO), one of the 24 departments of the University of Florence, is the reference Department for ICT (Information and Communications Technology), where it carries out advanced research in control systems, computer science and engineering, electronics systems, electromagnetism, telecommunications, operation research, bioengineering and electrical engineering.
Traditional and advanced researches, designs and implementations are digital signal processing, fixed and wireless telecommunications systems, radar, sensors and electronic devices, advanced software, ultrasound systems, satellite telecommunication/localization/sensing, media content processing and interpretation, decision support , security and protection of information and telematics, ICT for eHealth systems and electrical networks effciency.
DINFO is member of several inter-university centres and consortia, among which CNIT (National Inter-University Consortium for Telecommunications), MECSA (Microwave Engineering Centre for Space Applications), MIDRA (Multidisciplinary Institute for Development Research and Applications) and TICOM (Consortium for Technologies of Information and Telecommunications), which play an important role in the national high-level scientific cooperation between universities and industries.
DINFO also includes MICC (Media Integration and Communication Centre), a centre of excellence established by the Ministry of University and Research in 2001.
DINFO employs a workforce of more than 210 units (including professors, researchers, technical and administrative people, post-doc fellows and PhD students) with success in the acquisition of important public and private research funding. DINFO is in charge of two first-level three-year degree courses (Electronic Engineering and Telecommunications, Computer Engineering), five Master-of-Science two-year courses (Biomedical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Electrical and Automation Engineering, Telecommunications Engineering) and a PhD course in Information Engineering for a total of about 1,400 students.
The main public research funding comes from European Community, the European Space Agency, the Ministry of University and Research, national research programs and the Tuscany Region. More than a quarter of the research budget of the DINFO comes from contracts with private companies that generate a fruitful technological transfer to industry.
